body.translated_text: <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> (Ornament of the Mahāyāna Sūtras)
Oṃ
Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

CHAPTER I
First Section

children.text: arthajño 'rthavibhāvanāṃ prakurute vācā padaiś cāmalair duḥkhasyottaraṇāya duḥkhitajane kāruṇyatas tanmayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The knower of meaning (<s>arthajña</s>) makes clear the meaning through speech and pure words, out of compassion, being absorbed in it, for the deliverance of suffering beings from suffering;

children.text: dharmasyottamayānadeśitavidheḥ satveṣu tadgāmiṣu śliṣṭām arthagatiṃ niruttaragataṃ pañcātmikāṃ darśayan || AMsa_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: showing, with regard to beings who are headed toward that, the well-connected understanding of meaning — unsurpassed in its scope, fivefold in nature — of the <s>Dharma</s> taught in the manner of the supreme vehicle. (AMsa 1.1)

body.translated_text: 'The knower of meaning makes clear the meaning' —

body.text: iti ka upadeśam ārabhya ko 'laṃkarotīti | arthajñaḥ | kam alaṃkāram alaṃkaroti | arthavibhāvanāṃ kurute | kena
body.translated_text: this means: With reference to the teaching, who ornaments it? The knower of meaning (<s>arthajña</s>). What ornament does he produce? He makes the meaning clear. By what means?
'Through speech and pure words' —

body.text: | amalayā vāceti pauruṣayā amalaiḥ padair yuktaiḥ sahitair iti vistaraḥ | na hi vinā vācā padavyañjanair artho vibhāvayituṃ sakyata iti | kasmai
body.translated_text: by pure speech, meaning personal speech; by pure words, meaning connected and coherent — this is the elaboration. For without speech and words, meaning cannot be made clear. For whom?
'For the deliverance of suffering beings from suffering, out of compassion, being absorbed in it' —
the compassion that arises toward suffering beings — from that
compassion,
'absorbed in it' (<s>tanmaya</s>)
means pervaded by compassion. Whose ornament does he produce?
'Of the <s>Dharma</s> taught in the manner of the supreme vehicle' —

body.text: | uttamayānasya deśito vidhir yasmin dharme tasya dharmasya | kasminn alaṃkaroti |
body.translated_text: the method taught as the supreme vehicle — of that <s>Dharma</s> in which this method is taught. Where does he ornament?
'With regard to beings who are headed toward that' —

body.text: | nimittasaptam yeṣām mahāyānagāmisatvanimittam ity arthaḥ | katividham alaṃkāraṃ karoti | pañcavidhaṃ |
body.translated_text: the locative of occasion: those beings for whom the occasion is that they are headed toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — this is the meaning. How many kinds of ornament does he produce? Five kinds.
'Showing the well-connected, unsurpassed in scope, fivefold understanding of meaning' —

body.text: śliṣṭam iti yuktāṃ niruttaragatām ity anuttarajñānagatāṃ | tām idānīṃ pañcātmikāṃ arthagatiṃ dvitīyena ślokena darśyati |
body.translated_text: 'well-connected' means appropriate; 'unsurpassed in scope' means belonging to unsurpassed knowledge. He now shows that fivefold understanding of meaning by the second verse.

children.text: ghaṭitam iva suvarṇaṃ vārijaṃ vā vibuddhaṃ sukṛtam iva subhojyaṃ bhujyamānaṃ kṣudhārtaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Like refined gold, like a water-born lotus that has blossomed, like wholesome and delicious food being eaten by those afflicted with hunger,

children.text: vidita iva sulekho ratnapeṭeva muktā vivṛta iha sa dharmaḥ prītimagryāṃ dadhāti || AMsa_1.2 ||
children.translated_text: like a well-composed letter understood, like a pearl from a jewel-casket — the <s>Dharma</s> thus revealed here bestows the highest joy. (AMsa 1.2)

body.text: anena ślokena pañcabhir dṛṣṭāntaiḥ sa hi dharmaḥ pañcavidham artham adhikṛtya deśitaḥ sādhyaṃ vyutpādyaṃ cintyam acintyaṃ pariniṣpannaṃ cādhigamārthaṃ pratyātmavedanīyaṃ bodhipakṣasvabhāvaṃ | so 'nena sūtrālaṃkāreṇa vivṛtaḥ prītim agrāṃ dadhādati | yathākramaṃ

children.text: | yadā sa dharmaḥ prakṛtyaiva guṇayuktaḥ kathaṃ so 'laṃkriyata ity asya codyasya parihārārthaṃ trtīyaḥ ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: Since that <s>Dharma</s> is by its very nature endowed with qualities, how can it be ornamented? — to address this objection, the third verse:

body.translated_text: By this verse, with five similes: for that <s>Dharma</s> has been taught with reference to five kinds of meaning — what is to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), what is to be elucidated (<s>vyutpādya</s>), what is to be contemplated (<s>cintya</s>), what is inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>), and what is fully accomplished (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) — the meaning of realization, to be personally experienced, whose nature is the wings of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>). When revealed by this <s>Sūtrālaṃkāra</s>, it bestows the highest joy, in the manner of refined gold and so forth, respectively.

children.text: yathā bimbaṃ bhūṣāprakṛtiguṇavad darpaṇagataṃ viśiṣṭaṃ prāmodyaṃ janayati nṛṇāṃ darśanavaśāt |
children.translated_text: Just as a reflected image, endowed with natural qualities of adornment, when seen in a mirror, generates a special delight in people through the power of seeing,

children.text: tathā dharmaḥ soktaprakṛtiguṇayukto 'pi satataṃ vibhaktārthas tuṣṭiṃ janayati viśiṣṭām iha satām || AMsa_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Dharma</s>, though always endowed with natural qualities as described, when its meaning is analyzed, generates a special satisfaction here among the good. (AMsa 1.3)
'Just as a reflected image, endowed with natural qualities of adornment, seen in a mirror' —
'through the power of seeing,'
'generates a special delight.'

children.text: evaṃ sa dharmaḥ subhāṣitaiḥ prajkṛtyaiva guṇayukto 'pi satataṃ
children.translated_text: So too that <s>Dharma</s>, through well-spoken words, though always endowed with natural qualities,
'when its meaning is analyzed, generates a special satisfaction.'

children.text: | buddhimatām atas tuṣṭiviśeṣotpādanād alaṃkṛta iva bhavatīti | ataḥ paraṃ tribhiḥ ślokais tasmin dharme trividham upaśaṃsaṃ darśayaty ādarotpādanārthaṃ |
children.translated_text: For the wise, since it produces a special satisfaction, it becomes as if ornamented. Henceforth, with three verses, he shows a threefold commendation of that <s>Dharma</s>, for the purpose of generating respect.

body.translated_text: What does this show?

children.translated_text: Just as a medicine, pungent when smelled but sweet in taste, so too

children.text: dharmarmo dvayavyavasthāstho vyañjanato 'rtho na ca jñeyaḥ || AMsa_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s>, established in the duality: from its letter, its meaning is not to be known. (AMsa 1.4)
Like a king, difficult to please, this <s>Dharma</s> is vast, deep, and profound;
but once pleased, like that king, it becomes the giver of excellent qualities and wealth. (AMsa 1.5)
Just as a jewel of fine quality and priceless value does not please the common person who cannot appraise it,

children.text: dharmas tathāyam abudhaṃ viparyayāt toṣayati tadvat || AMsa_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: so too this <s>Dharma</s> does not please the foolish; but conversely, like that jewel, it pleases the wise. (AMsa 1.6)

body.translated_text: The threefold commendation: first, being the cause of removing obscurations, by the simile of medicine. 'Established in the duality'

body.text: vyañjanārthavyavasthaḥ | vibhutvahetutvam abhijñādivaiśeṣikaguṇāiśvaryadānād rājopamatvena | āryadhanopabhogahetutvaṃ ca anarthajātyaratnopamatvena | parīkṣakajana āryajano veditavyaḥ | naivedaṃ mahāyānaṃ buddhavacanaṃ kutas tasyāyam anuśaṃso bhaviṣyatīty atra vipratipannas tasya buddhavacanatvaprasādhanārthaṃ kāraṇavibhājyam ārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: means established in the letter and the meaning. Second, being the cause of mastery, by bestowing sovereignty over special qualities such as <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), by the simile of a king. Third, being the cause of enjoying noble wealth, by the simile of a jewel of fine quality and priceless value. 'The person who can appraise' should be understood as the noble person. 'This <s>Mahāyāna</s> is not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>; how then will it have this commendation?' — for one who is confused about this, in order to establish its being the <s>Buddha</s>'s word, the verse beginning with the analysis of reasons:

children.translated_text: Because of non-prediction at the beginning; because of simultaneous arising; because it is beyond the range of reason; because of its establishment,
because of the non-existence of existence and non-existence; because of being an antidote; and because of its different meaning from the letter — (AMsa 1.7)
'Because of non-prediction at the beginning' —

children.text: yady etat saddharmāntarāye paścāt kenāpi utpāditaṃ | kasmād ādau bhavatā na vyākṛtam anāgatabhayavat |
children.translated_text: If this was later produced by someone as an obstacle to the true <s>Dharma</s>, why was it not predicted by the <s>Bhagavān</s> at the beginning, as he did with future dangers?
'Because of simultaneous arising' —

children.text: samakālaṃ ca śrāvakayānena mahāyānasya pravṛtter upalabhyate na paścād iti katham asyābuddhavacanatvaṃ vijñāyate |
children.translated_text: And the arising of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is observed to be simultaneous with the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (vehicle of hearers), not later. How then can its non-being the <s>Buddha</s>'s word be determined?
'Because it is beyond the range of reason' —

children.text: nāyam evam udāro gambhīraś ca dharmas tārkikāṇāṃ gocaraḥ | tīrtikaśāstreṣu tatprakārānupalambhād iti | nāyam anyair bhāṣito yujyate | ucyamāne 'pi tadanadhimukteḥ |
children.translated_text: This <s>Dharma</s>, so lofty and profound, is not within the range of logicians. Because no such kind of teaching is found in the treatises of non-Buddhist schools, it is not proper that it was spoken by others. Even when it is spoken, there is no conviction in it on their part.
'Because of its establishment' —

children.text: athānyenābhisaṃbudhya bhāṣitaḥ | siddham asya buddhavacanatvaṃ | sa eva buddho yo 'bhisaṃbudhya evam bhāṣate |
children.translated_text: But if it was spoken by someone else who was awakened: then its being the <s>Buddha</s>'s word is established. For he himself is a <s>Buddha</s> who, having awakened, speaks thus.
'Because of the non-existence of existence and non-existence' —

children.text: yadi mahāyānaṃ kiṃcid asti tasya bhāva siddhim idaṃ buddhavacanam ato 'nyasya mahāyānasyābhāvāt | atha nāsti tasyābhāve śrāvakayānasyāpy abhāvāt | śrāvakayānaṃ budhavacanaṃ na mahāyānam iti na yujyate vinā buddhayānena buddhānām anutpādāt |
children.translated_text: If the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is something that exists, its existence establishes that this is the <s>Buddha</s>'s word, since there is no other <s>Mahāyāna</s>. But if it does not exist, then in its non-existence, the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> too would not exist. It is not proper to say 'The <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is the <s>Buddha</s>'s word but not the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,' because without the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle), <s>Buddhas</s> would not arise.
'Because of being an antidote' —

children.text: bhāvyamānaṃ ca mahāyānaṃ sarvanirvikalpajñānāśrayatvena kleśānāṃ pratipakṣo bhavati tasmād buddhavacanaṃ |
children.translated_text: And the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, when cultivated, becomes the antidote to afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), because it serves as the basis for all non-conceptual knowledge. Therefore it is the <s>Buddha</s>'s word.
'Because of its different meaning from the letter' —

children.text: na cāsya yathārutam arthas tasmān na yathārutārthānusāreṇedam abuddhavacanaṃ veditavyaṃ | yad uktam ādāv avyākaraṇād ity anābhogād etad anāgataṃ bhagavatā na vyākṛtam iti kasyacit syād ata upekṣāyā ayoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: Its meaning is not to be taken literally. Therefore, following the literal meaning, it should not be considered as non-<s>Buddha</s>'s word. The statement 'Because of non-prediction at the beginning' — if someone might say that the <s>Bhagavān</s> did not predict this because he lacked interest, then regarding the impropriety of indifference, a verse:
<s>Buddhas</s> have the eye of direct perception and are protectors of the teaching;

children.text: adhvany anyanāvṛtajñānā upekṣāto na yujyate || AMsa_1.8 ||
children.translated_text: their knowledge of the future is unobstructed — indifference on their part is not proper. (AMsa 1.8)

body.text: anena kiṃ darśayati | tribhiḥ kāraṇair anāgatasya mahataḥ śāsanopadravasyopkeṣā na yujyate | buddhānām ayatnato jñānapravṛtteḥ

children.translated_text: because they have the eye of direct perception and because the protection of the teaching is

children.text: ca yatnavatvāt | anāgatajñānasāmarthyāc ca sarvakālāvyāhatajñānatayeti | yad uktaṃ bhāvābhāve 'bhāvād iti | etad eva śrāvakayānaṃ mahāyānam etenaiva mahābodhiprāptir iti kasyacit syād ataḥ śrāvakayānasya mahāyānatvāyoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: something they strive for; and because of the capacity of knowledge of the future, their knowledge being unobstructed at all times. The statement 'Because of the non-existence of existence and non-existence' — someone might think: 'This <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> itself is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; through it alone is great awakening attained.' Regarding the impropriety of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> being the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, a verse:

body.translated_text: What does this show? For three reasons, indifference toward a great future danger to the teaching is not proper: because <s>Buddhas</s>' knowledge functions effortlessly,

children.translated_text: Because of incompleteness, because of contradiction, because of being no means, and likewise because of lack of instruction in that regard —

children.text: na śrāvakayānam idaṃ bhavati mahāyānadharmākhyam || AMsa_1.9 ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> cannot be what is called the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>. (AMsa 1.9)
'Because of incompleteness' —

children.text: parārthopadeśasya na hi śrāvakayāne kaścit parārtha upadiṣṭaḥ śrāvakāṇām ātmano nirvidvirāgavimuktimātropāyopadeśāt | na ca svārtha eva pareṣūpadiśyamānaḥ parārtho bhavitum arhati |
children.translated_text: of instruction regarding benefit for others. For in the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, no benefit for others is taught, since the instruction for <s>Śrāvakas</s> is only the means of personal disgust, dispassion, and liberation. And instruction in one's own benefit cannot serve as benefit for others when applied to others.
'Because of contradiction' —

children.text: svārthe hi paro niyujyamānaḥ svārtha eva prayujyate sa ātmana eva parinirvāṇārthaprayukto 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyata iti virodham etat | na ca śrāvakayānenaiva cirakālaṃ bodhau ghaṭamāno buddho bhavitum arhati |
children.translated_text: For when another is directed to his own benefit, he is engaged in his own benefit only. That he, being engaged in his own <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening — this is a contradiction. And one who strives in awakening for a long time through the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone cannot become a <s>Buddha</s>.
'Because of being no means' —

children.text: | anupāyo hi śrāvakayānaṃ buddhatvasya na cānupāyena ciram api prayujyamānaḥ prārthitam arthaṃ prāpnoti | śṛṅgād iva dugdhaṃ na bhastrayā | athānyathāpy atropadiṣṭaṃ yathā bodhisatvena prayoktavyaṃ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> is no means to <s>Buddhahood</s>. And one who applies himself for a long time by a non-means does not attain the desired goal — like milk from a horn, not from a bellows. Even if instruction is given there in some other way regarding how a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should practice,

children.text: tathāpy anupadeśān na śrāvakayānam eva mahāyānaṃ
children.translated_text: 'likewise, because of lack of instruction,' the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone

children.text: bhavitum arhati | na hi sa tādṛśa upadeśa etasminn upalabhyate | viruddham vā cānyonyaṃ śrāvakayānaṃ cety anyonyavirodhe ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: cannot be the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For no such instruction is found therein. Or, the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> and the <s>Mahāyāna</s> are mutually contradictory — regarding their mutual contradiction, a verse:
Because of contradiction in intention, instruction, practice,

children.text: upastambhasya kālasya yat hīnaṃ hīnam eva tat || AMsa_1.10 ||
children.translated_text: support, and time — what is inferior is indeed inferior. (AMsa 1.10)

body.translated_text: How is it contradictory? Through five contradictions:
contradictions of intention, instruction, practice, support, and time.

body.text: | śrāvakayāne hy ātmaparinirvāṇāyaivāśayas tadartham evaupadeśas tadartham eva prayogaḥ parīttaś ca puṇyajñānasaṃbhārasaṃgṛhīta
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, the intention is only for one's own <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the instruction is for that purpose only, the practice is for that purpose only, the support is a limited
accumulation of merit and knowledge,

body.text: cālpena tadarthaprāptir yāvat tribhir api janmabhiḥ | mahāyāne tu sarvaṃ viparyayeṇa | tasmād anyonyavirodhād
body.translated_text: and in time, the attainment of that purpose is achieved quickly — even within three births. In the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, however, everything is the opposite. Therefore, due to mutual contradiction,
whatever
vehicle
is inferior is indeed inferior —

body.text: | na tan mahāyānaṃ bhavitum arhati | buddhavacanasyedaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yat sūtre 'vatarati vinaye saṃdṛśyate dharmatāṃ ca na vilomayati | na caivaṃ mahāyānaṃ
body.translated_text: it cannot be the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. 'The characteristic of the <s>Buddha</s>'s word is that it accords with the <s>Sūtra</s>, is seen in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and does not contradict <s>Dharmatā</s> (the nature of things). But the <s>Mahāyāna</s>

body.text: sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatvopadeśāt | tasmān na buddhavacanam iti kasyacit syād ato lakṣaṇavirodhe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: , because it teaches the essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, is not the <s>Buddha</s>'s word.' — Someone might think this. Regarding the contradiction with the defining characteristics, a verse:

children.translated_text: Because it accords with its own <s>sūtras</s>, because its own <s>Vinaya</s> is seen therein,

children.text: audāryād api gāmbhīryād aviruddhaiva dharmatā || AMsa_1.11 ||
children.translated_text: and because of its vastness and profundity — <s>Dharmatā</s> (the nature of things) is not contradicted. (AMsa 1.11)
This indeed accords
with its own <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras.
And its own
bondage's (<s>śleṣa</s>)
<s>Vinaya</s> (discipline)

children.text: saṃdṛśyate | yo mahāyāne bodhisatvānāṃ śleśa uktaḥ | vikalpaśleśā hi bodhisatvāḥ |
children.translated_text: is seen therein — the bondage that is declared for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are bound by conceptual elaboration.
And because its character is vastness and profundity,
it does
not contradict <s>Dharmatā</s>

children.text: vilomayaty athaiva hi dharmatā mahābodhiprāpataye tasmān nāsti lakṣaṇa
children.translated_text: (the nature of things). For precisely this is <s>Dharmatā</s>, for the attainment of great awakening. Therefore there is no contradiction
with the defining characteristics.

children.text: | agocarād ity uktam atas tarkagocaratvāyoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: The statement 'Because it is beyond the range of reason' — regarding the impropriety of it being within the range of logic, a verse:

body.translated_text: What does this verse show?

children.translated_text: Logic is dependent, uncertain, non-pervasive, limited to conventional truth, and subject to exhaustion;

children.text: bālāśrayo matas tarkas tasyāto viṣayo na tat || AMsa_1.12 ||
children.translated_text: it relies on the immature — therefore this is not its domain. (AMsa 1.12)
scripture (<s>āgama</s>);
it is uncertain,
because understanding changes over time;
it is non-pervasive,
not covering the entire range of the knowable;
it is limited to conventional
truth, not to ultimate truth;
and it is subject to exhaustion,

children.text: ca pratibhānaparyādanāt | mahāyānas tu na niśritaṃ yāvat akhedavat | śatasāhasrikādyanekasūtropadeśāt | ato na
children.translated_text: because intellectual inspiration is exhaustible. The <s>Mahāyāna</s>, however, is not dependent, and so on up to: it is inexhaustible, because of the instruction in numerous sūtras such as the Hundred-Thousand. Therefore
this is not the domain of logic.

children.text: | anupāyatvāt śrāvakayāne na buddhatvaṃ prāptam ity uktam atha mahāyānaṃ katham upāyo yukta ity upāyatvayoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: It has been said 'Because of being no means, <s>Buddhahood</s> is not attained through the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>.' But how then is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> a proper means? Regarding the propriety of its being a means, a verse:

body.translated_text: For logic, relied upon by one who has not seen the truths, is sometimes dependent on

children.translated_text: Because of vastness and profundity, maturation and non-conceptualization —

children.text: deśanā'to dvayasyāsmin sa copāyo niruttare || AMsa_1.13 ||
children.translated_text: the teaching of both is found herein, and this is the means to the unsurpassed. (AMsa 1.13)

body.translated_text: What does this verse show? Through the
teaching of vastness,
the
maturation
of beings, through engaging them by their vast conviction;
through the teaching of profundity,
non-conceptualization — therefore,
of this
twofold teaching,
in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>,
'this is the means to the unsurpassed'
knowledge — through both of these, respectively:

body.text: satvānāṃ paripācanād ātmanaś ca buddhadharmaparipākād iti | ye punar asmāt trasanti tadartham asthānatrāsādīnave kāraṇatvena ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: through maturing beings and through maturing the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> for oneself. Now, for those who are frightened by this, regarding the disadvantage of fear of what should not be feared, as a reason, a verse:

children.text: tadasthānatrāso bhavati jagatāṃ dāhakaraṇo mahāpuṇyaskandhaprasavakaraṇād dīrghasamayam |
children.translated_text: Fear regarding that which is not a ground for fear causes burning for beings, because of generating a great mass of demerit, for a long time.

children.text: agotro 'sanmitro 'kṛtamatir apūrvācitaśubhas trasaty asmin dharme patati mahato 'rthād gata iha || AMsa_1.14 ||
children.translated_text: One without <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), without a good friend, of uncultivated mind, who has not accumulated merit in the past, is terrified of this <s>Dharma</s> and falls from a great purpose, having departed from it. || AMsa_1.14 ||
fear where there is no ground for fear. It causes burning
in the lower realms. For what reason?
Because of generating a great mass of demerit.
For how long?
For a long time.

children.text: | evaṃ paścād ādīnavaḥ | yena ca kāraṇena yāvantaṃ ca kālaṃ tat saṃdarśayati | kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇe tu satīti caturvidhaṃ trāsakāraṇaṃ darśayati |
children.translated_text: Thus, afterwards, the danger. And he shows by what cause and for how long. 'But when there is a cause' — he shows the fourfold cause of fear.
He has no <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage),
or
no good friend,

children.text: vā avyutpannamatir vā bhavati mahāyānadharmatāyāṃ pūrvaṃ vān
children.translated_text: or his mind is undeveloped regarding the nature of <s>Mahāyāna</s>, or he has not previously
accumulated merit.
'Falls from a great purpose'

children.text: iti mahābodhisaṃbhārārthāt | aprāptaparihāṇito 'paramādīnavaṃ darśayati | trāsakāraṇam uktam atrāsakāraṇaṃ vaktavyam ity atrāsakāraṇatve ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: means from the purpose of accumulating the requisites of great awakening. He shows the further danger of the loss of what has not yet been attained. Having stated the cause of fear, the cause of fearlessness should be stated; regarding the cause of fearlessness, the verse:

body.translated_text: Fear where there is a ground for fear —

children.text: tadanyānyānyābhāvāt paramagahanatvād anugamāt vicitrasyākhyānād dhruvakathanayogād bahumukhāt |
children.translated_text: Because of the non-existence of any other alternative, because of its extreme profundity, because of its consistent teaching, because of its variegated exposition, because of its being steadfastly taught from many perspectives,

children.text: yathākhyānaṃ nārthād bhagavati ca bhāvātigahanāt na dharme 'smiṃs trāso bhavati viduṣāṃ yonivicayāt || AMsa_1.15 ||
children.translated_text: because the meaning is not according to the literal expression, and because the nature of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is extremely profound — the wise have no fear of this <s>Dharma</s>, through careful investigation. || AMsa_1.15 ||

body.translated_text: 'Because of the non-existence of any other alternative'

body.text: iti tato 'nyasya mahāyānasthābhāvāt | atha śrāvakayānam eva mahānaṃ syād anyasya śrāvakasya pratyekabuddhasya vābhāvaḥ syāt | sarva eva hi buddhā bhaveyuḥ |
body.translated_text: means because of the non-existence of any <s>Mahāyāna</s> other than this. If the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Vehicle of the Hearers) alone were the great vehicle, then there would be no other — no <s>Śrāvaka</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> — for all would be <s>Buddhas</s>.
'Because of its extreme profundity'
and because of the consistent teaching of the path to omniscient
knowledge,
that is, operating simultaneously.
'Because of its variegated exposition'

body.text: | vicitraś cātra saṃbhāramārga ākhyāyate na kevalaṃ śūnyataiva | tasmād abhiprāyikenānena bhavitavyam iti |
body.translated_text: — here the variegated path of accumulation is taught, not merely emptiness alone. Therefore, this must be taken in its intended sense.
'Because of its being steadfastly taught from many perspectives'

body.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ cātra śūnyatā kathyate bahibhiś ca paryāyais teṣu teṣu sutrānteṣu tasmād bhavitavyam atra mahatā prayogena | anyathā hi sakṛt pratiṣedhamātrakṛtam abhaviṣyad iti |
body.translated_text: — here emptiness is taught repeatedly and through many alternative expressions in various <s>sūtras</s>. Therefore, there must be great purposefulness in this. Otherwise, a mere single negation would have sufficed.
'The meaning is not according to the literal expression'

body.text: na cāsya yathārutam artho 'smād api trāso na yuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: — the meaning of this is not according to the letter; therefore fear is not justified on this account either.
'Because the nature of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is extremely profound'

body.text: atigahanaś ca buddhānāṃ bhāvo durājñeyas tasmān nāsmabhis tadajñānāt trasitavyam iti |
body.translated_text: — the nature of the <s>Buddhas</s> is extremely profound and difficult to know; therefore we should not be frightened out of our ignorance of it.
Thus,

body.text: yoniśaḥ pravicayād viduṣāṃ trāso na bhavati
body.translated_text: through careful investigation, the wise have no fear.
Regarding the object of knowledge being the domain of far-reaching wisdom, the verse:

children.text: śrutaṃ niśrityādau prabhavati manaskāra iha yo
children.translated_text: Based on what is heard, first mental engagement arises here;
from mental engagement arises knowledge whose object is the truth of reality;

children.text: tato dharmaprāptiḥ prabhavati ca tasmin matirato
children.translated_text: from that arises the attainment of <s>Dharma</s>, and in that one whose mind delights,

children.text: yadā pratyātmaṃ sā katham asati tasmin vyavasitiḥ || AMsa_1.16 ||
children.translated_text: when that knowledge is personally experienced — how could there be conviction without it? || AMsa_1.16 ||
'Based on what is heard, first mental engagement arises'

children.text: yoniśa ity arthaḥ | yoniśo manasikārāt tatvārthaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ prabhavati lokottarā samyagdṛṣṭis
children.translated_text: — 'which' means thorough, i.e., thorough mental engagement. From thorough mental engagement arises knowledge whose object is the truth of reality — the supramundane right view.
Then,
the attainment of the <s>Dharma</s> that is its
fruit;
then, when that is attained,
the wisdom —
the knowledge of liberation — manifests. Thus,
when that wisdom is personally experienced,
how, without that,
could this
conviction,

children.text: niścayo bhavati naivedaṃ buddhavacanam iti | atrāsapadasthānatve ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: this certainty, arise — 'this is not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>'? Regarding the ground of fearlessness, the verse:

children.text: ahaṃ na boddhā na gabhīraboddhā buddho gabhīraṃ kim atarkagamyaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'I am not a knower; nor is anyone a knower of the profound. The <s>Buddha</s> knows the profound — but why is it beyond reasoning?

children.text: kasmād gabhīrārthavidāṃ na mokṣa ity etad uttrāsapadaṃ na yuktam || AMsa_1.17 ||
children.translated_text: Why is there no liberation for those who know the profound meaning?' — these are not justified grounds for terror. || AMsa_1.17 ||
'I
am
not a knower of this'

children.text: ty uttrāsapadaṃ tan na yuktaṃ | atha buddho 'pi
children.translated_text: is taken as a ground for terror, that is not justified. Or if 'even the <s>Buddha</s>
is not a knower of the profound
thing,'
then how could he
teach
the profound?
— that ground for terror is unjustified. Or
'why is the profound
beyond
reasoning?'

children.text: ity uttrāsapadaṃ tan na yuktaṃ | atha
children.translated_text: — that ground for terror is not justified. Or
'why is there no liberation for those who know the profound meaning'
in this
way —
but not for mere reasoners?
— that ground for terror is not justified.
Regarding the establishment of that from non-faith alone, the verse:

body.translated_text: If first

children.translated_text: For one of inferior aspiration, of inferior spiritual disposition, surrounded by inferior companions —

children.text: audāryagāmbhīryasudeśite 'smin dharme 'dhimuktir yadi nāsti siddham || AMsa_1.18 ||
children.translated_text: if there is no faith in this <s>Dharma</s> that is well-taught in its grandeur and profundity, that is the proof. || AMsa_1.18 ||
aspiration is inferior,
and whose
spiritual disposition (<s>dhātu</s>)
is
inferior
— that is, the habitual tendency of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) —
surrounded by inferior
com-
panions,
those of the same aspirations and dispositions,
if for such a one there is no faith in this
<s>Dharma</s> well-taught in its grandeur and profundity,
the <s>Mahāyāna</s>
<s>Dharma</s>,
then precisely for that reason
it is proven

children.text: utkṛṣṭam idaṃ mahāyānam iti | aśrutasūtrāntapratikṣepāyoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: that this <s>Mahāyāna</s> is supreme. Regarding the impropriety of rejecting unheard <s>sūtras</s>, the verse:

body.translated_text: One whose

children.text: śrutānusāreṇa hi buddhimattāṃ labdhvā śrute yaḥ prakaroty avajñāṃ |
children.translated_text: One who, having gained a semblance of intelligence by following what he has heard, then shows contempt for what is heard —

children.text: śrute vicitre sati cāprameye śiṣṭe kuto niścayam eti mūḍhaḥ || AMsa_1.19 ||
children.translated_text: when the remainder of what is heard is varied and immeasurable, how can such a deluded one arrive at certainty? || AMsa_1.19 ||

body.text: kāmaṃ tāvad adhimuktir na syād aśrutānāṃ tu sūtrāntānām aviśeṣeṇa pratipakṣo na yuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: Granted that there may be no faith; but a wholesale rejection of <s>sūtras</s> one has not heard is not reasonable.
'By following what is heard'
— as it were,
having gained intelligence — one who shows contempt for what is heard
it-
self — such a deluded one,
when there exists indeed the remainder of what is heard, which is
varied
and
immeasurable —
from what
cause
could he
arrive at certainty

body.text: na tad buddhavacanam iti | na hi tasya śrutād anyad balam asti tasmād aśrutvā pratikṣepo na yuktaḥ | yad api ca śrutaṃ tad yoniśo manasi kartavyaṃ nāyoniśa ity ayoniśomanasikārādhīnave ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: that 'this is not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>'? For he has no other basis of authority than what he has heard; therefore, rejecting without having heard is not reasonable. And even what has been heard should be reflected upon thoroughly, not cursorily. Regarding the disadvantage of careless mental engagement, the verse:

children.text: yathārute 'rthe parikalpyamāne svapratyayo hānim upaiti buddheḥ |
children.translated_text: When the meaning is imagined according to the literal expression, one's own understanding suffers a loss of wisdom;

children.text: svākhyātatāṃ ca kṣipati kṣatiṃ ca prāpnoti dharme pratighāvatīva || AMsa_1.20 ||
children.translated_text: and one casts away the well-taught quality, suffers harm, and experiences an obstruction to the <s>Dharma</s>, as it were. || AMsa_1.20 ||
'One's own understanding'

children.text: iti svayaṃdṛṣṭapraāmarṣako na vijñānām antikād arthaparyeṣṭī |
children.translated_text: means one who grasps by one's own perception, not one who seeks the meaning from the learned.
'Suffers a loss of wisdom'
means through the loss of not attaining knowledge of things as they truly are. And regarding the <s>Dharma</s>'s
'well-taught quality,'
one
casts it away;
and because of the resultant demerit,
one 'suffers harm.' And regarding the <s>Dharma</s>,
one experiences
an obstruction

children.text: āvaraṇaṃ ca dharmavyavasanasaṃvartanīyaṃ karmety ayam atrādīnavaḥ | ayathāvataś cārtham avijānato 'pi pratighāto na yukta iti pratighātāyoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: — an obscuration, a <s>karma</s> that leads to the disappearance of the <s>Dharma</s>: this is the danger here. Regarding the impropriety of hostility even when one does not understand the meaning correctly, the verse:

children.text: manaḥ pradoṣaḥ prakṛtipraduṣṭo 'yathārute cāpi hy ayuktarūpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Mental hostility is inherently faulty and inappropriate when the meaning is not according to the literal expression;

children.text: prāg eva saṃdehagatasya dharme tasmād upekṣaiva varaṃ hy adoṣā || AMsa_1.21 ||
children.translated_text: all the more so for one who is in doubt about the <s>Dharma</s>; therefore equanimity alone is better, for it is faultless. || AMsa_1.21 ||
'Inherently faulty'
means blameworthy by nature.
'Therefore equanimity alone is better.'
Why?
'For it is faultless.'
But hostility is faulty.

body.translated_text: End of the first chapter of the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>: the establishment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

CHAPTER II
Second chapter.
Summary verse on the distinctive characteristics of taking refuge:

children.text: ratnāni yo hi śaraṇapragato 'tra yāne jñeyaḥ sa eva paramaḥ śaraṇaṇagatānām |
children.translated_text: One who has gone to the Three Jewels for refuge in this vehicle is to be known as the supreme among those who have taken refuge,
by virtue of a fourfold distinction of meaning, differentiated by universality, acceptance, attainment, and mastery. || AMsa_2.1 ||

body.translated_text: 'He is the supreme among those who have taken refuge.'
For what reason?
By virtue of a fourfold distinction of meaning.
The fourfold meaning
should be understood through the differentiation of universality, acceptance, attainment, and mastery.

body.text: sarvatragārthaḥ | abhibhavārthaḥ | te punar uttaratra nirdekṣyante | tathāpy atra śaraṇapragatānāṃ bahuduṣkarakāryatvāt kecin notsahante ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The meaning of universality. The meaning of mastery. These will be explained later. Even so, because the task requires much difficult exertion for those who have taken refuge, some lose heart. The verse:

children.text: yasmād ādau duṣkara eṣa vyavasāyo duḥsādho 'sau naikasahasrair api kalpaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Since in the beginning this resolve is difficult, since that goal is hard to accomplish even through thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: siddho yasmāt satvahitādhānamahārthas tasmād agre yāna ihāgraśaraṇārthaḥ || AMsa_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: since the great purpose of establishing beings' welfare has been accomplished — therefore this vehicle is supreme and has the supreme purpose of refuge. || AMsa_2.2 ||

body.text: etena tasya śaraṇagamanavyavasāyasya praṇidhānapratipattiviśeṣābhyāṃ yaśohetutvaṃ darśayati | phalaprāptiviśeṣeṇa

children.translated_text: its great purposefulness.
Regarding the previously introduced meaning of universality, the verse:

body.translated_text: By this he shows that the resolve to take refuge, through the distinctions of aspiration and practice, is a cause of glory. And through the distinction of attaining the fruit,

children.text: sarvān satvāṃs tārayituṃ yaḥ pratipanno yano jñāne sarvagate kauśalyayuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who is engaged in ferrying across all beings, who is skilled in the knowledge that encompasses everything, in the vehicle,

children.text: yo nirvāṇe saṃsaraṇe 'py ekaraso 'sau saṃsṛtiśāntyekaraso 'sau jñeyo dhīmān eṣa hi sarvatraga evam || AMsa_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: who has a single taste in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) — that wise one, having a single taste in cyclic existence and peace, should be known as truly universal. || AMsa_2.3 ||

body.text:
etena caturvidhaṃ sarvatragārthaṃ ...
... asāṃketikaṃ dharmatā
prātilambhikaṃ ceti prabhedalakṣaṇā pravṛttir audārikasūkṣmaprabhedena | śaraṇapratipattiviśeṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text:
By this, the fourfold meaning of universality ... [lacuna]
... conventional and natural,
and that obtained through practice — the characterization of this process, through the differentiation of coarse and subtle. Regarding the distinction of the practice of taking refuge, the verse:

children.text: śaraṇagatim imāṃ gato mahārthāṃ guṇagaṇavṛddhim upaiti so 'prameyām |
children.translated_text: One who has gone to this refuge of great purpose grows in an immeasurable multitude of qualities;

children.text: sphurati jagad idaṃ kṛpāśayena prathayati cāpratimaṃ mahārthadharmam || AMsa_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: he pervades this world with a compassionate mind and proclaims the <s>Dharma</s> of great purpose, incomparable. || AMsa_2.4 ||

body.translated_text: Here,
the great purpose of the state of having taken refuge
is shown through the practices for one's own and others' benefit. The practice for one's own benefit
is of many kinds —
an immeasurable growth of qualities.

body.text: | aprameyatvaṃ tarkasaṃkhyā kālāprameyatayā veditavyaṃ | na hi sā guṇavṛddhis tarkeṇa prameyā na saṃkhyā na kālenātyantikatvāt | parārthapratipattir āśayataś ca karuṇā sphuraṇena prayogataś ca mahāyānadharmaprathanena | mahāyānaṃ hi mahāryadṛśāṃ dharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Immeasurability should be understood through being immeasurable in reasoning, in number, and in time. For that growth of qualities cannot be measured by reasoning, nor by number, nor by time, since it is ultimate. The practice for others' benefit is, in terms of intention, the pervading of compassion, and in terms of application, the proclamation of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s>. For the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the <s>Dharma</s> of those of great noble vision.
End of the second chapter of the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>: taking refuge.

CHAPTER III
Third chapter.
Summary verse on the classification of <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage):

children.translated_text: Supremacy among beings, its nature, its marks, the classification of <s>gotra</s>,
its danger, its benefit, a twofold simile, and fourfold division. || AMsa_3.1 ||

children.text: agratvaṃ svabhāvo liṅgaṃ prabheda ādīnavo 'nuśaṃso dvidhāupamyaṃ
children.translated_text: its supremacy, nature, marks, classification, danger, benefit, and twofold simile

children.text: cety eṣa prabhedaḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ | ete ca prabhedāḥ pratyekaṃ
children.translated_text: — this classification is summarized. And these classifications are each
fourfold.
Regarding the proof of the existence of <s>gotra</s>, the verse:

body.translated_text: By this, the existence of <s>gotra</s>,

children.text: dhātūnām adhimukteś ca pratipatteś ca bhedataḥ |
children.translated_text: Through the difference of dispositions, of aspirations, and of practices,
and through the observation of the difference of fruits — the existence of <s>gotra</s> is established. || AMsa_3.2 ||

body.text: nānādhātukatvānām aparimāṇo dhātuprabhedo yathoktam akṣarāśisūtre | tasmād evaṃ jātīyako 'pi dhātubhedaḥ pratyetavya iti | asti yānatraye gotrabhedaḥ | adhimuktibhedo 'pi satvānām upalabhyate prathamata eva kasyacit kvacid eva yāde 'dhimuktir bhavati so 'ntareṇa gotrabhedaṃ na syāt | utpāditāyām api ca pratyayavaśenādhimuktau pratipattibheda upalabhyate kaścin nirvohā bhavati kaścin neti so 'ntareṇa gotraprabhedaṃ na syāt | phalabhedaś copalabhyate hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭā bodhayaḥ
body.translated_text: The immeasurable differentiation of dispositions of beings of various dispositions, as stated in the <s>Akṣarāśisūtra</s>. Therefore, such a differentiation of dispositions should be acknowledged. There is a differentiation of <s>gotra</s> in the three vehicles. A differentiation of aspirations is also observed among beings — from the very beginning, someone has aspiration only in a certain vehicle; that could not exist without a differentiation of <s>gotra</s>. And even when aspiration has been generated by conditions, a differentiation of practice is observed — some are energetic and some are not; that could not exist without a differentiation of <s>gotra</s>. And a differentiation of fruits is observed — awakenings of inferior, middling, and superior degree;

body.text: so 'ntareṇa gotrabhedaṃ na syāt bījānurūpatvāt phalasya | agratvavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: that could not exist without a differentiation of <s>gotra</s>, since the fruit corresponds to the seed. Regarding the proof of supremacy, the verse:

children.translated_text: Because it is the cause of the excellence of wholesome qualities in their elevation, universality, great purposefulness, and inexhaustibility,
the supremacy of <s>gotra</s> is established. || AMsa_3.3 ||

body.text: atra gotrasya caturvidhena nimittatvenāgratvaṃ darśayati | tad dhi gotraṃ kuśalamulānām udagratve nimittaṃ sarvatve mahārthatve akṣayatve ca | na hi śrāvakāṇāṃ tathodagrāṇi na ca sarvāṇi santi balavaiśāradyādyabhāvāt | na ca mahārthānyaparārthatvāt | na cākṣayāṇy anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇāvasānatvāt | lakṣaṇavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here he shows the supremacy of <s>gotra</s> through its being the cause in a fourfold manner. For that <s>gotra</s> is the cause of the elevation, universality, great purposefulness, and inexhaustibility of wholesome roots. For the wholesome roots of <s>Śrāvakas</s> are not elevated to the same degree, nor do they encompass all — because of the absence of the powers, the fearlessnesses, and so on; nor are they of great purpose — because they do not benefit others; nor are they inexhaustible — because they culminate in <s>Nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. Regarding the analysis of the characteristics, the verse:

children.text: prakṛtyā paripuṣṭaṃ ca āśrayaś cāśritaṃ ca tat |
children.translated_text:
It is innate and nurtured,
and it is both support and supported;

it should be known as both existent and non-existent,
for the purpose of bringing forth qualities. // AMsa_3.4 //

body.text: etena caturvidhaṃ gotraṃ darśayati | prakṛtisthaṃ samudānītam āśrayasvabhāvam āśritasvabhāvaṃ ca tad eva yathākramaṃ | tatpunarhetubhāvena sat phalabhāvenāsat | guṇottāraṇārthana gotraṃ veditavyaṃ guṇā uttaranty asmād uddhavantīti kṛtvā | liṅgavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this he shows the fourfold <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage): innate, cultivated, of the nature of a support, and of the nature of being supported — in that order. Furthermore, it is existent as a cause and non-existent as a result. The <s>gotra</s> should be understood as serving to bring forth qualities, because qualities arise and emerge from it. On the division of characteristics, one verse:

children.translated_text: Compassion, faith, patience, and from the very first endeavor,

children.text: samācāraḥ subhasyāpi gotre liṅgaṃ nirupyate || AMsa_3.5 ||
children.translated_text: good conduct — even of the virtuous — are indicated as the marks of the <s>gotra</s>. // AMsa_3.5 //

body.text: caturvidhaṃ liṅgaṃ bodhisatvagotre | ādiprayogata eva kāruṇyaṃ satveṣu | adhimuktir mahāyānadharme | kṣāntirduṣkaracaryāyāṃ sahiṣṇutārthena | samācāraś ca pāramitāmayasya kuśalasyeti | prabhedavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: There are four marks of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>gotra</s>: compassion toward beings from the very first endeavor; faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s>; patience in the sense of forbearance in difficult practices; and good conduct consisting of wholesome actions based on the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). On the division of types, one verse:

children.text: niyatāniyataṃ gotram ahāryaṃ hāryam eva ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>gotra</s> is determined and undetermined, unshakable and shakable;
this division of the <s>gotra</s> according to conditions is, in summary, fourfold. // AMsa_3.6 //

body.text: samāsena caturvidhaṃ gotraṃ niyatāniyataṃ tadeva yathākramaṃ pratyayairahāryaṃ hāryaṃ ceti | ādīnavavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: In summary, the <s>gotra</s> is fourfold: determined and undetermined, which are respectively unshakable and shakable by conditions. On the division of defects, one verse:

children.translated_text: Habitual afflictions, bad companionship, lack of resources, and dependence on others —
these should be known as the fourfold defect of the <s>gotra</s>, in summary. // AMsa_3.7 //

body.text: bodhisatvagotre samāsena caturvidha ādīnavaḥ yena gotrastho 'guṇeṣu pravartate |
body.translated_text: There are, in summary, four defects of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>gotra</s>, by which one established in the <s>gotra</s> engages in non-virtuous activities:

body.text: kleśabāhulyaṃ | akalyāṇamitratā | upakaraṇavidhātaḥ | pāratantryaṃ ca | anuśaṃsavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: abundance of afflictions; association with unwholesome friends; lack of requisites; and dependence on others. On the division of benefits, one verse:

children.text: cirād apāyagamanam āśumokṣaś ca tatra ca |
children.translated_text: One goes to the lower realms only after a long time, and one is quickly liberated from them;
one experiences suffering only mildly, and one matures beings with urgency. // AMsa_3.8 //

body.text: caturvidho bodhisatvasya gotre 'nuśaṃsaḥ | cireṇāpāyān gacchati | kṣipraṃ ca tebhyo mucyate | mṛdukaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ teṣūpapannaḥ pratisaṃvedayate | saṃvignacetās tadupapannāṃś ca satvān karuṇayamānaḥ paripācayati | mahāsuvarṇagotrāupamye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: There are four benefits for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the <s>gotra</s>: one goes to the lower realms only after a long time; one is quickly liberated from them; when reborn there, one experiences suffering only gently; and with a mind filled with urgency, one matures beings born there through compassion. On the analogy with a great gold mine, one verse:

body.text: Comparaison avec une grande Famille d'or, en un vers.

children.translated_text: Like a gold mine, it should be known as the support of immeasurable virtue,
and as the support of knowledge, purity, and powers. // AMsa_3.9 //

body.text: mahāsuvarṇagotraṃ hi caturvidhasya suvarṇasyāśrayo bhavati | prabhūtasya prabhāsvarasya nirmalasya karmaṇyasya ca | tatsādharmyeṇa bodhisatvagotram aprameyakuśalamūlāśrayaḥ | jñānāśrayaḥ | kleśanairmalyaprāptyāśrayaḥ | abhijñādiprabhāvāśrayaś ca | tasmān mahāsuvarṇagotropaṃ veditavyaṃ | mahāratnagotrāupamye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: For a great gold mine is the support of four kinds of gold: abundant, luminous, pure, and workable. By analogy, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>gotra</s> is the support of immeasurable roots of virtue; the support of knowledge; the support for the attainment of purity from afflictions; and the support of powers such as the supernatural knowledges. Therefore it should be understood as analogous to a great gold mine. On the analogy with a great jewel mine, one verse:

children.translated_text: Like a precious jewel mine, it should be known from the standpoint of great awakening,
because it is the support of great knowledge, noble <s>samādhi</s>, and the welfare of great beings. // AMsa_3.10 //

body.text: mahāratnagotraṃ hi caturvidharatnāśrayo bhavati | jātyasya varṇasaṃpannasya saṃsthānasaṃpannasya pramāṇasaṃpannasya ca | tadupamaṃ bodhisatvagotraṃ veditavyaṃ mahābodhinimittatvāt mahājñānanimittatvād āryasamādhinimittatvāt cittasya hi saṃsthitiḥ samādhiḥ mahāsatvaparipākanimittatvāc ca bahusatvaparipācanāt | agotrannasthavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: For a great jewel mine is the support of four kinds of jewels: those of fine quality, those endowed with good color, those endowed with good shape, and those endowed with good measure. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>gotra</s> should be understood by this analogy: because it is the cause of great awakening, the cause of great knowledge, the cause of noble <s>samādhi</s> — for <s>samādhi</s> is the stability of the mind — and the cause of maturing great beings, since it matures many beings. On the state of being without <s>gotra</s>, one verse:

children.translated_text: Someone is exclusively devoted to misconduct; someone has eradicated the white <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: amokṣabhāgīyaśubho 'sti kaścin nihīnaśuklo 'sty api hetuhīnaḥ || AMsa_3.11 ||
children.translated_text: someone lacks the virtue leading to liberation; and someone has diminished virtue and is devoid of the cause. // AMsa_3.11 //

body.text: aparinirvāṇadharmaka etasminn agotrastho 'bhipretaḥ | sa ca samādato dvividhaḥ | tatkālāparinirvāṇadharmā atyantaṃ ca | tatkālāparinirvāṇadharmā caturvidhaḥ | duścaritaikāntikaḥ samucchinnakuślamūlaḥ | hīnakuśalamūlaś cāparipūrṇasaṃbhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, one who is by nature incapable of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is meant as one without <s>gotra</s>. And that is, in summary, of two kinds: one who is temporarily incapable of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, and one who is permanently so. The temporarily incapable is fourfold: one exclusively devoted to misconduct; one whose roots of virtue have been eradicated; one with diminished roots of virtue and incomplete accumulation;

body.text: atyantāparinirvāṇadharmā tu hetuhīno yasya parinirvāṇagotram eva nāsti | prakṛtiparipuṣṭagotramāhātmye ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: and the permanently incapable of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> is one who is devoid of the cause — one in whom the <s>gotra</s> for <s>parinirvāṇa</s> simply does not exist. On the greatness of the innate and nurtured <s>gotra</s>, one verse:

children.text: gāmbhīryāudāryavāde parahitakaraṇāyodite dīrghadharme ajñātvaivādhimuktir bhavati suvipulā saṃprapattikṣamā ca |
children.translated_text:
In the profound and vast teaching, in the <s>Dharma</s> that is extensive for the sake of benefiting others,
there arises, even without learning, a vast faith capable of commitment;

children.text: saṃpattiś cāvasāne dvayagataparamā yad bhavaty eva teṣāṃ tajjñeyaṃ bodhisatvaprakṛtiguṇavatas tatprapuṣṭāc ca gotrāt || AMsa_3.12 ||
children.translated_text:
and there is, at the end, a supreme twofold attainment — this should be known
as arising from the natural qualities of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and from the nurtured <s>gotra</s>. // AMsa_3.12 //

body.text: yadgābhīryāudāryavādini parahitakriyārthamukte vistīrṇe mahāyānadharme gāmbhīryāudāryārtham ajñātvaivādhimuktir vipulā bhavati | pratipattau cotsāhaḥ | saṃpattiś cāvasāne mahābodhirdvayagatāyāḥ saṃpatteḥ paramā tatprakṛtyā guṇavataḥ paripuṣṭasya ca bodhisatvagotrasya māhātmyaṃ veditavyaṃ | dvayagatā iti dvaye laukikāḥ śrāvakāś ca | parameti viśiṣṭā | phalato gotraviśeṣaṇe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: When, regarding the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s> that teaches the profound and vast, that is taught for the purpose of benefiting others, that is extensive — when, even without learning the meaning of profundity and vastness, a vast faith arises, and when there is enthusiasm in practice, and when at the end there is the supreme attainment of great awakening, surpassing the twofold attainment — this should be understood as the greatness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>gotra</s> that is naturally endowed with qualities and that is nurtured. 'Twofold' refers to worldly beings and <s>Śrāvakas</s>. 'Supreme' means surpassing them. On the characterization of the <s>gotra</s> from the standpoint of its fruit, one verse:

children.translated_text:
For the growth of the tree of awakening with its vast and excellent qualities,
and for the attainment of the pacification of wealth, happiness, and suffering,

children.text: svaparahitasukhakriyāphalatvād bhavati samudagrasamūlam udagragotram etat || AMsa_3.13 ||
children.translated_text:
because it bears the fruit of creating well-being for oneself and others,
this <s>gotra</s> is lofty, having a deep and eminent root. // AMsa_3.13 //

body.text: svaparahitaphalasya bodhivṛkṣasya praśastamūlatvam anena bodhisatvagotraṃ saṃdarśitaṃ |
body.translated_text: By this, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>gotra</s> is shown to be the excellent root of the tree of awakening whose fruit is the welfare of self and others.
End of the third chapter on <s>gotra</s> in the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>.

CHAPTER IV
Fourth Chapter.
On the characteristics of the generation of the mind, one verse:

children.translated_text: Of great enthusiasm, of great undertaking, of great purpose, and of great fruition —
the volition of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having a twofold aim, is the arising of the mind. // AMsa_4.1 //

body.translated_text: Of great enthusiasm:
through the heroic energy of resolution, because of the capacity to endure what is profound, difficult, and of long duration.
Of great undertaking:
through the energy of practice corresponding to that resolution.
Of great purpose:
because of the governance of benefit for self and others.
Of great fruition:
because it culminates in great awakening.

body.text: so 'yaṃ trividho guṇāḥ paridīpitaḥ puruṣakāraguṇo dvābhyāṃ padābhyām arthakriyāguṇaḥ phalaparigrahaguṇaś ca dvābhyāṃ |
body.translated_text: These three qualities are elucidated: the quality of effort by two phrases, the quality of purposeful action, and the quality of result-acquisition, each by two phrases.
Having a twofold aim:
because it takes as its object the purposeful action for the welfare of great beings. Thus, with three qualities and a twofold object,
this volition
is called the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>). On the division of <s>cittotpāda</s>, one verse:

children.translated_text: The generation of the mind is first that of conviction, then that of pure superior intention,
that of maturation on the stages, and likewise that free from obstructions. // AMsa_4.2 //
generation of the mind
is fourfold:
That of conviction
on the stage of the practice of aspiration.
That of pure superior intention
on the seven stages.
That of maturation
from the eighth stage onward. That free from obstructions on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. On the ascertainment of <s>cittotpāda</s>, four verses:

body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattvas</s>'

children.translated_text: It has compassion as its root, and the constant intention of benefiting beings;
faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise the search for that knowledge as its object. // AMsa_4.3 //
It is a vehicle of ever-higher aspiration, established in moral discipline;
the rousing of the adversary is its obstacle; forbearance is its support. // AMsa_4.4 //
The increase of virtue is its benefit, for it consists of merit and knowledge;

children.text: sadā pāramitāyoganiryāṇaś ca sa kathyate || AMsa_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: it is said to always have the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> as its way out. // AMsa_4.5 //
Its culmination is the stages; by the respective practice at each stage,
the ascertainment of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' generation of the mind should be understood. // AMsa_4.6 //

body.text: tathāyaṃ viniścayaḥ | kiṃmūla eṣa caturvidho bodhisatvānāṃ cittotpādaḥ kimāśayaḥ kimadhimokṣaḥ kimālambanaḥ kiṃyānaḥ kiṃpratiṣṭhaḥ kimādīnavaḥ kimanuśaṃsaḥ kiṃniryāṇaḥ kiṃparyavasāna iti | āha |

children.translated_text: Its root is compassion.
Its intention is the constant welfare of beings.
Its faith is in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>
<s>Dharma</s>.
Its object is the search for that knowledge,
that is,
because it takes that knowledge as its object.
Its vehicle is ever-
higher aspiration.
Its foundation is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>
moral discipline.
Its obstacle
is its defect. And what is that obstacle?
The rousing of the adversary —
the arousing of the mind of another vehicle,
or forbearance
toward it.
Its benefit is the increase of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>
consisting of merit
and knowledge.
Its way out is the constant practice
of the <s>pāramitās</s>
(perfections).
And its culmination is the stages,
according to each respective
stage's
practice.

children.text: | yasyāṃ bhūmau yaḥ prayuktas tasya tadbhūmiparyavasānaḥ | samādānasāṃketikacittautpāde ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whoever is engaged in whichever stage, for that person the culmination is that stage. On the conventional and formal generation of the mind, one verse:

body.translated_text: The ascertainment is thus: What is the root of this fourfold generation of the mind of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? What is its intention? What is its faith? What is its object? What is its vehicle? What is its foundation? What is its defect? What is its benefit? What is its way out? What is its culmination? He says:

children.translated_text:
Through the power of a friend, through the power of a cause, through the power of a root,
through the power of learning, and through the cultivation of virtue —
the generation of the mind is said to be of unstable and stable arising, through the instruction of another. // AMsa_4.7 //

body.text: yo hi parākhyānāc cittotpādaḥ paravijñāpanāt sa ucyate samādānasāṃketikaḥ | sa punar

children.translated_text: through the power of a friend —
through the influence of a spiritual friend;
through the power of a cause —
through the capacity of the <s>gotra</s>; through the power of the root
of virtue —
through having been nurtured in the past;
through the power of learning —

children.text: vā tatra tatra dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe bahūnāṃ bodhicittotpādāt |
children.translated_text: through the arising of the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening mind) of many, when this or that <s>Dharma</s> discourse is being taught;
through the cultivation of virtue —

children.text: vā dṛṣṭa iva dharme satataśravaṇodgrahaṇadhāraṇādibhiḥ | sa punar mitrabalād
children.translated_text: in this very life, through constant hearing, grasping, retaining, and so forth. Furthermore, that arising through the power of a friend is
of unstable arising —
it should be understood. That arising through the power of a cause and so forth is
of stable arising.
On the ultimate generation of the mind, seven verses:

body.translated_text: The generation of the mind that arises through the instruction of another — through being informed by another — is called conventional and formal. And that is:

children.translated_text: When the <s>Buddha</s> has been well served, and the accumulations of knowledge and merit well gathered,
from the arising of non-conceptual knowledge regarding <s>dharmas</s>, its supremacy. // AMsa_4.8 //

children.text: dharmeṣu ca satveṣu ca tatkṛtyeṣūttame ca buddhatve |
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>dharmas</s> and beings and their duties, and regarding the supreme <s>Buddhahood</s>,
from the taking up of equal-mindedness and non-apprehension, its distinction of delight. // AMsa_4.9 //
The grandeur of its birth therein, the enthusiasm, the purity of intention,

children.text: kauśalyaṃ pariśiṣṭe niryāṇaṃ caiva vijñeyam || AMsa_4.10 ||
children.translated_text: the skill in the remaining, and the way out — should be understood. // AMsa_4.10 //
Born from the seed of faith in the <s>Dharma</s>, from the excellent mother of the <s>pāramitās</s>,

children.text: dhyānamaye sukhagarbhe karuṇā saṃvardhikā dhātrī || AMsa_4.11 ||
children.translated_text: in the womb of happiness which is the meditative absorption, compassion is the nurturing nurse. // AMsa_4.11 //
Grandeur should be understood from the accomplishment of the ten great aspirations;
enthusiasm should be understood from the unfatigued engagement in what is difficult, lengthy, and extensive. // AMsa_4.12 //
From the awakening that is close to full awakening, and from the attainment of knowledge of its means,

children.text: āśayaśuddhir jñeyā kauśalyaṃ tv anyabhūmigatam || AMsa_4.13 ||
children.translated_text: the purity of intention should be understood; skill, however, pertains to the other stages. // AMsa_4.13 //
The way out should be understood through the mental attention corresponding to the established stages;
from the conceptual knowledge of that, and through non-conceptualization of that very thing. // AMsa_4.14 //

body.text: prathamena ślokenopadeśapratipattyadhigamaviśeṣaiḥ pāramārthikatvaṃ cittotpādasya darśayati | sa ca pāramārthikaś cittotpādaḥ pramuditāyāṃ bhūmāv iti |
body.translated_text: By the first verse, he shows the ultimacy of the generation of the mind through the distinctions of instruction, practice, and realization. And that ultimate generation of the mind is on the stage of <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful).
Of that distinguished by delight —
he shows the reason. Therein,
equal-mindedness regarding <s>dharmas</s>
arises from the realization of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>;
equal-mindedness regarding beings
arises from the understanding of the non-distinction between self and other;
equal-mindedness regarding the duties toward beings
arises from aspiring for the cessation of their suffering just as for one's own;
equal-mindedness regarding <s>Buddhahood</s>

body.text: samacittatā taddharmadhātor ātmany abhedapratibodhāt | tasminn eva ca pāramārthikacottotpāde ṣaḍarthā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: arises from the realization of the non-difference of that <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) in oneself. And in that very ultimate generation of the mind, six aspects should be understood:

body.text: janma audāryam utsāha āśayaśuddhiḥ pariśiṣṭakauśalyaṃ niryāṇaṃ ca
body.translated_text: birth, grandeur, enthusiasm, purity of intention, the remaining skill, and the way out.
Therein,
birth
should be understood through the distinctions of mother, womb, and nurse.
Grandeur
through the accomplishment of the ten great aspirations.
Enthusiasm through the unfatigued engagement in what is difficult over a long period of time.
Purity of intention through the knowledge close to awakening
and from the attainment of knowledge of its means.
The remaining
skill
is the skill on the other stages.
The way out is through the mental attention corresponding to the established
stage.
How through mental attention? Through the conceptual knowledge of that stage-establishment,
and
This is mere conceptualization.
And of that very
conceptual cognition,
due to the absence of conceptualization.
Regarding the greatness through similes, there are six verses:

children.translated_text: The arising is like the earth; another is like refined gold;
another resembles the waxing new moon; another is said to be like fire, [characterized by] growth. || AMsa 4.15 ||
Again, another is like a great treasure; another is like a jewel-mine;
another should be known as resembling the ocean; another like a thunderbolt; another resembling the mountain-king (<s>Indra</s>). || AMsa 4.16 ||
Another resembles the King of Medicines; another should be known as resembling a great friend;
another has the brilliance of a wish-fulfilling gem; another should be known as resembling the sun. || AMsa 4.17 ||
Another is like the sweet music of a <s>Gandharva</s>; another should be known as resembling a king;
another is like a storehouse; another is like a great highway. || AMsa 4.18 ||
Another should be known as resembling a vehicle; another resembles a <s>Gandharva</s>, being the source of both willow and consciousness;
another resembles the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss); and another resembles the current of a great river. || AMsa 4.19 ||

children.text: meghasadṛśaś ca kathitaś cittotpādo jinātmajānāṃ hi |
children.translated_text: And the arising of the mind of the heirs of the Conquerors is said to resemble a cloud.

children.text: tasmāt tathā guṇāḍhyaṃ cittaṃ muditaiḥ samutpādyam || AMsa_4.20 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, such a mind, rich in virtues, should be generated with joy. || AMsa 4.20 ||

body.translated_text: The first arousing of
the mind
of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>
is like the earth,
because it is the foundation for the production of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> and their requisites. The arousing of the mind accompanied by intention
resembles refined gold,
because the intention for benefit and happiness does not undergo alteration. Accompanied by endeavor,
it resembles the white
fort-
night's new moon,
because of the increasing growth of wholesome qualities. Accompanied by superior intention,
it resembles

body.text: sadṛśa indhanākaraviśeṣeṇevāgnis tasyottarottaraviśeṣādhigamanāt | viśeṣādhigamāśayo hy adhyāśayaḥ | dānapāramitāsahagato
body.translated_text: fire, because just as fire grows with special fuel, so too one attains progressively higher distinctions; for superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is the intention toward attaining distinctions. Accompanied by the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>),
it is like a great treasure,
because through the enjoyment of material goods it satisfies immeasurable beings, and because it is inexhaustible. Accompanied by the perfection of moral discipline (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>),
it is like a jewel-mine,
because all jewels of virtue are produced from it. Accompanied by the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>),
it is like the ocean,
because it is unshakable by all unwanted adversities. Accompanied by the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>),
it is like a thunderbolt,

body.text: pamo dṛḍhatvād abhedyatayā | dhyānapāramitāsahagataḥ parvatarājopamo niṣkampatvād avikṣepataḥ | prajñāpāramitāsahagato
body.translated_text: because of its firmness and indestructibility. Accompanied by the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), it is like the king of mountains, because of its immovability and non-distraction. Accompanied by the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>),
it is like the King of Medicines,
because it pacifies all the illnesses of the obstructions of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). Accompanied by the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>),
it resembles a great friend,
because it does not abandon beings in any circumstance. Accompanied by the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>),
it resembles a wish-fulfilling gem,
because of the fulfillment of its fruit in accordance with each being's aspiration. Accompanied by the means of gathering disciples (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>),
it resembles the sun,
because it ripens the harvest of those to be trained. Accompanied by the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>),
it is like the sweet music of a <s>Gandharva</s>,
because it attracts those to be trained through its <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. Accompanied by the refuges (<s>pratiśaraṇa</s>), it is like a great
king,
because it is a cause of non-destruction. Accompanied by the accumulations of merit and wisdom (<s>puṇyajñānasaṃbhāra</s>),
it is like a storehouse,
because it is the repository of abundant accumulations of merit and wisdom. Accompanied by the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>),
it is like a great
royal
high-
way, because it is traversed and followed by all noble beings.
Accompanied by calm abiding and insight (<s>śamatha</s>-<s>vipaśyanā</s>),
it is like a vehicle,
because it conveys one comfortably. Accompanied by <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) and ready eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>),
it is like a <s>Gandharva</s>,

because, by analogy with the retention of water and its inexhaustible outpouring, there is the retention and exposition of the meaning of <s>Dharma</s> both heard and unheard. Accompanied by the summary of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmoddāna</s>),
it resembles the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss),
because it is delightful to hear for those to be trained who desire liberation. Accompanied by the one-way path (<s>ekāyanamārga</s>),
it resembles the current of a river,

body.text: samaḥ svarasavāhitvāt | anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhe ekāyanatvaṃ tadbhūmigatānāṃ bodhisatvānām abhinnakāryakriyātvāt | upāyakauśalyasahagato
body.translated_text: because it flows of its own accord. On the one-way path, when the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) is obtained, there is one-wayness for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on that stage because their activity is undivided. Accompanied by skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>),
it is like a cloud,

CHAPTER V
The Fifth Chapter
On the characteristic of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: The practice of the heirs of the Conquerors is understood as having a great basis, great undertaking, and great fruition.

a great basis,

CHAPTER VI
The sixth chapter.
On the analysis of the characteristics of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), a verse:

children.text: na san na cāsan na tathā na cānyathā na jāyate vyeti na cāvahīyate |
children.translated_text: 'It is neither existent nor non-existent, neither thus nor otherwise; it is neither born nor ceases nor diminished;

children.text: na vardhate nāpi viśudhyate punar viśudhyate tatparamārthalakṣaṇaṃ || AMsa_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: it neither increases nor is purified, yet it is purified — that is the characteristic of ultimate reality.' // AMsa_6.1 //

body.text: advayārtho hi paramārthaḥ | tam advayārthaṃ pañcabhir ākāraiḥ saṃdarśayati |

children.translated_text: 'Not existent'
with respect to the characteristics of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>);
'nor non-existent'
with respect to the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>);
'not thus'
because of the non-identity of the perfected with the imagined and the dependent;
'nor otherwise'
because of the non-difference from those very two;
'it is neither born nor ceases'
because the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is unconditioned;
'it neither diminishes nor increases'
because it remains in the same state regarding the cessation and arising in the aspects of defilement and purification;
'it is not purified'

children.translated_text: because it is by nature undefiled; yet it is purified, because of the removal of adventitious afflictions. This fivefold non-dual characteristic
is the characteristic of ultimate reality,
to be understood thus. On the refutation of the perversion of the view of self, a verse:
