for they are
different

children.text: ātmalakṣaṇāt parikalpitāt | sā punaḥ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ kleśadauṣṭhulyaprabhāvitatvāt | nāpy ato
children.translated_text: from the imagined self-characteristic. They are the five aggregates of clinging, being produced by the propensity of affliction. Nor does any
other self-characteristic apart from these two
obtain. Therefore there is no self.
This delusion

children.text: eṣa tūtpanno yeyam ātmadṛṣṭis tasmād eva cātmābhāvān
children.translated_text: has arisen — this view of self — and therefore, because of the very non-existence of self,
liberation too should be understood as merely the exhaustion of delusion,

children.text: veditavyo na tu kaścin muktaḥ | viparyāsaparibhāṣāyāṃ dvau ślokau |
children.translated_text: not that anyone is liberated. On the characterization of perversion, two verses:

body.translated_text: To begin with,

children.text: kathaṃ jano vibhramamātram āśritaḥ paraiti duḥkhaprakṛtiṃ na saṃtatām |
children.translated_text: 'How can a person, relying on mere delusion, not perceive the continuous nature of suffering?

children.text: avedako vedaka eva duḥkhito na duḥkhito dharmamayo na tanmayaḥ || AMsa_6.3 ||
children.translated_text: Without knowing, he is a knower — indeed afflicted, yet not afflicted; consisting of <s>dharmas</s>, yet not consisting of them.' // AMsa_6.3 //
'How can a person, when things arise dependently in plain sight, resort to the idea of other-causation?

children.text: tamaḥ prakāraḥ katamo 'yam īdṛśo yato 'vipaśyan sadasan nirīkṣate || AMsa_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: What kind of darkness is this, whereby, not seeing clearly, one looks for the existent and the non-existent?' // AMsa_6.4 //
How
is it that this world,
relying on the mere delusion

children.text: ātmadarśanaṃ niśritya satatānubaddhaṃ duḥkhasvabhāvaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ na paśyati |
children.translated_text: of seeing a self, does not see the constantly attending nature of suffering in conditioned things?
'Without knowing'

children.text: jñānena tasyā duḥkhaprakṛteḥ | vedako 'nubhavena duḥkhasyāduḥkhito duḥkhasyāprahīṇatvāt |
children.translated_text: — through knowledge, of that nature of suffering; 'a knower' through experience of suffering — 'not freed from suffering' because suffering has not been abandoned;
'not afflicted'
because of the non-existence of a self conjoined with suffering;
'consisting of <s>dharmas</s>'
because there is only <s>dharmas</s>, through the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>); but not
consisting of <s>dharmas</s>

children.text: dharmanairātmyena | yadā ca loko bhāvānāṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ pratyakṣaṃ paśyati taṃ taṃ pratyayaṃ pratītya te te bhāvā bhavantīti | tat katham etāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ
children.translated_text: through the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>). And when the world directly sees the dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) of entities — that those entities come into being depending on this and that condition — then how can one
resort to the view of other-causation,
that seeing and so forth are not dependently arisen?
What kind of

children.text: tamaḥprakāro lokasya yad vidyamānaṃ pratītyasamutpādam avipaśyan na vidyamānam ātmānaṃ
children.translated_text: darkness is this of the world, that, not seeing the existent dependent origination, one looks at
a non-existent self?

children.text: | śakyaṃ hi nāma tamasā vidyamānam adraṣṭuṃ syān na tvavidyamānaṃ draṣṭum iti | asaty ātmani śamajanmayoge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: For it is indeed possible through darkness not to see what exists, but not to see what does not exist! On the connection between peace and birth when there is no self, a verse:

children.text: ta cāntaraṃ kiṃcana vidyate 'nayoḥ sadarthavṛttyā śamajanmanor iha |
children.translated_text: 'There is no difference whatsoever between these two — peace and birth — when considered in terms of ultimate reality;

children.text: tathāpi janmakṣayato vidhīyate śamasya lābhaḥ śubhakarmakāriṇām || AMsa_6.5 ||
children.translated_text: yet, from the cessation of birth, the attainment of peace is accomplished for those who perform virtuous deeds.' // AMsa_6.5 //

body.text: na cāsti saṃsāranirvāṇayoḥ kiṃcin nānākaraṇaṃ paramārthavṛttyā nairātmyasya samatayā |

children.translated_text: Yet, from the cessation of birth,
the attainment of liberation does occur
for those who perform virtuous deeds —

children.text: ye mokṣamārgaṃ bhāvayanti | viparyāsaparibhāṣāṃ kṛtvā tatpratipakṣapāramārthikajñānapraveśe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: those who cultivate the path of liberation. Having characterized perversion, four verses on entering the knowledge of ultimate reality, which is its antidote:

body.translated_text: There is no difference whatsoever between <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> in terms of ultimate reality, because of the sameness of selflessness.

children.text: saṃbhṛtya saṃbhāram anantapāraṃ jñānasya puṇyasya ca bodhisatvaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having accumulated a boundless shore of provisions — of knowledge and merit — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

children.text: dharmeṣu cintāsuviniśriś citatvāj jalpānvayām arthagatiṃ paraiti || AMsa_6.6 ||
children.translated_text: through being well-established in reflection on <s>dharmas</s>, reaches the understanding of meaning that follows conceptual elaboration.' // AMsa_6.6 //

children.text: arthān sa vijñāya ca jalpamātrān saṃtiṣṭhate tannibhacittamātre |
children.translated_text: 'Having understood that objects are mere conceptual elaboration, he abides in mere mind that resembles it;

children.text: pratyakṣatām eti ca dharmadhātus tasmād viyukto dvayalakṣaṇena || AMsa_6.7 ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> becomes directly perceived — freed from the characteristic of duality.' // AMsa_6.7 //

children.text: nāstīti cittāt param etya buddhyā cittasya nāstitvam upaiti tasmāt |
children.translated_text: 'Having gone beyond the mind with understanding — "there is nothing [external]" — one then arrives at the non-existence of mind itself;

children.text: dvayasya nāstitvam upetya dhīmān saṃtiṣṭhate 'tadgatidharmaghātau || AMsa_6.8 ||
children.translated_text: having arrived at the non-existence of both, the wise one abides in the realm of reality, free from both.' // AMsa_6.8 //
'By the power of non-conceptual knowledge of the wise one, following equally everywhere, always,

children.text: tadāśrayo gahvaradoṣasaṃcayo mahāgadeneva viṣaṃ nirasyate || AMsa_6.9 ||
children.translated_text: that basis — the deeply embedded accumulation of faults — is expelled like poison by a great remedy.' // AMsa_6.9 //
provisions

children.text: tvaṃ dharmacintāsuviniśritatvaṃ samādhiniśrityabhāvanāt manojalpāc ca teṣāṃ dharmāṇām arthaprakhyānāvagamāt tatpraveśaṃ darśayati | asaṃkhyeyaprabhedakālaṃ pāramasya paripūraṇam ity
children.translated_text: and the being well-established in reflection on <s>dharmas</s> — through the cultivation based on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and through understanding the revelation of meaning of those <s>dharmas</s> from mental elaboration — he shows the entry. 'Boundless shore' means the fulfillment of innumerable divisions of time.
By the second: having understood that objects are mere
mental elaboration,

children.text: narthān viditvā tadābhāse cittamātre 'vasthānamiyaṃ bodhisatvasya nirvedhabhāgīyāvasthā | tataḥ pareṇa
children.translated_text: the abiding in mere mind that appears as their reflection — this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s stage of the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). Beyond that,
in the direct realization of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,

children.text: gamane dvayalakṣaṇena viyukto grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇena iyaṃ darśanamārgāvasthā | tṛtīyena yathāsau dhamadhātuḥ pratyakṣatām eti tad darśayati | kathaṃ cāsau dharmadhātuḥ pratyakṣatām eti |
children.translated_text: being freed from the characteristic of duality — the characteristic of the grasped and the grasper — this is the stage of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). By the third: he shows how that <s>Dharmadhātu</s> becomes directly realized. And how does the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> become directly realized?
Having understood that apart from mind

children.text: anyadālambanaṃ grāhyaṃ nāstīty avagamya buddhyā tasyāpi cittamātrasya nāstitvāvagamanaṃ grāhyaṃbhāve grāhakābhāvāt | dvaye cāsya nāstitvaṃ viditvā dharmadhātau avasthānam atadgatir grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇābhyāṃ rahita evaṃ dharmadhātuḥ pratyakṣatām eti | caturthena bhāvanāmārgāvasthāyām aśrayaparivartanāt pāramārthikajñānapraveśaṃ darśayati | sadā sarvatra samatānugatenā
children.translated_text: there is no external apprehended object, through understanding the non-existence of that very mind-only too — because in the absence of the apprehended, the apprehender is also absent. Having known the non-existence of both, abiding in the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> — the 'going beyond both' means being free from the characteristics of the apprehended and the apprehender — thus the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> becomes directly realized. By the fourth: he shows the entry into knowledge of ultimate reality through the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivartana</s>) at the stage of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). By the power of
non-conceptual knowledge,
which follows equally everywhere in the dependent nature (<s>paratantra svabhāva</s>),
that basis —
the deeply embedded accumulation of faults, characterized by the propensity of affliction, is expelled like
poison by a great remedy.
On the greatness of the knowledge of ultimate reality, a verse:

body.translated_text: By the first verse: the accumulation of

children.translated_text: 'Well-established in the good <s>Dharma</s> set forth by the Sage, having directed the mind to the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> at the root,

children.text: smṛtim agatim avagamya kalpamātrāṃ vrajati guṇārṇavapāramāśudhīraḥ || AMsa_6.10 ||
children.translated_text: having understood that all recollection is merely conceptualization, the quick-witted one swiftly reaches the far shore of the ocean of virtues.' // AMsa_6.10 //
<s>Buddha</s>, well-established —
that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered the knowledge of ultimate reality, having directed the mind to the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>
of the root-mind which has the collected <s>dharmas</s> as its object,

children.text: yā smṛtir upalabhyate tāṃ sarvāṃ smṛtipravṛttiṃ kalpanāmātrām avagacchaty evaṃ
children.translated_text: understands that whatever recollection is obtained — all that activity of recollection — is merely conceptualization; thus
he swiftly reaches the far shore of the ocean of virtues —
<s>Buddhahood</s>.
This is the greatness of the knowledge of ultimate reality.

In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the sixth chapter on reality (<s>tattva</s>).

CHAPTER VII
The seventh chapter.
On the analysis of the characteristics of supernatural power (<s>prabhāva</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: 'With respect to the birth, speech, mind, good and bad [deeds], their basis, the way out, and the unseen of others —

children.text: jñānaṃ hi sarvatragasaprabhedeṣv avyāhataṃ dhīr agataḥ prabhāvaḥ || AMsa_7.1 ||
children.translated_text: knowledge, unobstructed in all its pervasive categories, is the wisdom of the one who has gone beyond; that is supernatural power.' // AMsa_7.1 //
knowledge regarding

children.text: jñānaṃ divyaśrotrābhijñāyāṃ vācaṃ tatra gatvopapannā bhāṣante |
children.translated_text: speech is through the superknowledge of the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotrābhijñā</s>) — they speak having gone there and been reborn;
knowledge regarding
mind is the superknowledge of reading others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāyābhijñā</s>); the former
good and bad [deeds]

children.text: dhāne jñānaṃ pūrvanivāsābhijñā | yatra vineyās tiṣṭhanti
children.translated_text: knowledge regarding [previous] abodes is the <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) of recollection of former lives. Knowledge of going to the place where those to be trained dwell
— knowledge of going to that place —
is the <s>abhijñā</s> of the domain of supernatural power.
Knowledge regarding

children.text: jñānam āsravakṣayābhijñā yathā satvā upapattito niḥsarantīti | eṣu ṣaṭsvartheṣu sarvatra lokadhātau sapramedeṣu
children.translated_text: escape is the <s>abhijñā</s> of the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) — how beings escape from rebirth. With regard to these six objects, in all world-systems, including the limited ones,
the knowledge that is unmediated and unobstructed regarding the levels (<s>pada</s>)

children.text: jñānaṃ sa prabhāvo bodhisatvānāṃ ṣaḍabhijñāsaṃgṛhītaḥ | prabhāvalakṣaṇavibhāge svabhāvārtha uktaḥ | hetvartham ārabhya ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: is the power (<s>prabhāva</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, comprised under the six <s>abhijñās</s>. In the analysis of the characteristics of power, the essential meaning has been stated. Regarding the meaning of the cause, a verse:

body.translated_text: Knowledge regarding others' rebirth is the superknowledge of the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutopapādābhijñā</s>);

children.translated_text: Having entered the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), perfectly pure, with the embrace of non-conceptual knowledge,
through mental application (<s>manasikāra</s>) in accordance with each particular state, one attains the supreme accomplishment of power. (AMsa 7.2)

body.text: yena niśrayeṇa yena jñānena yena manasikāreṇa tasya prabhāvasya samudāgamas tatsaṃdarśayati | phalārtham ārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows by what basis, by what knowledge, and by what mental application the attainment of that power comes about. Regarding the meaning of the fruit, a verse:

children.text: yenāryadivyāpratimair vihārair brāhmaiś ca nityaṃ viharaty udāraiḥ |
children.translated_text: By noble, divine, and incomparable modes of dwelling, and by sublime <s>Brahma</s>-dwellings, one constantly abides;

children.text: buddhāṃś ca satvāṃś ca sa dikṣu gatvā saṃmānayaty ānayate viśuddhim || AMsa_7.3 ||
children.translated_text: and having gone to <s>Buddhas</s> and beings in the directions, one honors them and brings about purification. (AMsa 7.3)

body.text: trividhaṃ phalam asya prabhāvasya saṃdarśayati | ātmana āryādisukhavihāram atulyaṃ cotkṛṣṭaṃ ca lokadhātvantareṣu gatvā buddhānāṃ pūjanaṃ satvānāṃ viśodhanaṃ ca | karmārthaṃ ṣaḍvidham ārabhya catvāraḥ ślokāḥ | darśanakarma saṃdarśanakarma cārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows the threefold fruit of this power: for oneself, an incomparable and exalted dwelling in noble and other modes of happiness; and having gone to other world-systems, the worship of <s>Buddhas</s> and the purification of beings. Regarding the sixfold meaning of activity, four verses. Regarding the activity of seeing and the activity of showing, a verse:

children.text: māyopamān paśyati lokadhātūn sarvān sasatvān savivartanāśān |
children.translated_text: One sees all world-systems with their beings, with their evolution and dissolution, as illusion-like;

children.text: saṃdarśayaty eva ca tān yatheṣṭaṃ vaśī vicitrair api sa prakāraiḥ || AMsa_7.4 ||
children.translated_text: and one shows them as one wishes, being master, by various means as well. (AMsa 7.4)
world-systems with their beings, with their evolution
and dissolution,
seeing them as illusion-like;
and for others,
showing them as one wishes;
and by other
various
means such as shaking, blazing, and so forth,

children.text: | daśavaśitālābhāt | yathā daśabhūmike 'ṣṭabhyāṃ bhūmau nirdiṣṭāḥ | raśmikarmārabhya ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: due to obtaining the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>), as taught in the <s>Daśabhūmika</s> at the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). Regarding the activity of rays, a verse:

body.translated_text: Oneself, of all

children.translated_text: Activity of emitting rays; one verse.

children.text: raśmipramokṣair bhṛśaduḥkhitāṃś ca āpāyikān svargagatān karoti |
children.translated_text: By emitting rays, one causes those greatly suffering in the lower realms to be reborn in heaven;

children.text: mārānvayān kṣubdhavimānaśobhān saṃkampayaṃ srāsayate samārān || AMsa_7.5 ||
children.translated_text: and one makes <s>Māra</s> and his hosts, shaking their disturbed celestial palaces, tremble and fall. (AMsa 7.5)

body.text: dvividhaṃ raśmikarma saṃdarśayati | apāyopapannānāṃ ca prasādaṃ janayitvā svargopapādanaṃ | mārabhavanānāṃ ca samārakāṇāṃ kampanodvejanaṃ | vikrīḍanakarma cārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows the twofold activity of rays: generating faith in those born in the lower realms and causing them to be reborn in heaven; and shaking and terrifying <s>Māra</s>'s hosts together with their abodes. Regarding the activity of sport, a verse:

children.translated_text: One displays immeasurable sport of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) in the midst of the foremost assembly;

children.text: sakarmajanmottamanirmitaiś ca satvārtham ātiṣṭhati sarvakālam || AMsa_7.6 ||
children.translated_text: and through supreme emanations with their deeds and births, one constantly carries out the benefit of beings. (AMsa 7.6)
Through displaying immeasurable sport of <s>samādhi</s>

children.text: buddhaparṣanmaṇḍalamadhye trividhena nirmāṇena sadā satvārthakaraṇāc ca | trividhaṃ nirmāṇaṃ śilpakarmasthānanirmāṇaṃ | vineyavaśena yatheṣṭopapattinirmāṇaṃ | uttamanirmāṇaṃ ca tuṣitabhavanavāsādikaṃ | kṣetrapariśuddhikarma ārabhya ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: in the midst of the <s>Buddha</s>'s assembly-circle, and through constantly benefiting beings by means of threefold emanation. The threefold emanation is: emanation through craft and skill, emanation of birth at will in accordance with those to be trained, and supreme emanation such as dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and so forth. Regarding the activity of field-purification, a verse:
Through mastery of knowledge, one attains the purification of the field, for showing it as one wishes;

children.text: abuddhanāmeṣu ca buddhanāma saṃśrāvaṇāt tān kṣipate 'nyadhātau || AMsa_7.7 ||
children.translated_text: and in world-systems where the <s>Buddha</s>'s name is not heard, by making them hear the <s>Buddha</s>'s name, one transfers them to other realms. (AMsa 7.7)

body.translated_text: Through twofold purification of evil: through purification of the vessel-world,
through mastery of knowledge,
by showing <s>Buddha</s>-fields made of crystal, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), and other materials as one wishes; and through purification of beings, by causing those born in
world-systems devoid of the <s>Buddha</s>'s name to hear
the <s>Buddha</s>'s name,

body.text: prasādaṃ grāhayitvā tadavirahiteṣu lokadhātuṣūpapādanāt | yogārtham ārabhya ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: generating faith in them, and causing them to be reborn in world-systems that are not devoid thereof. Regarding the meaning of application, a verse:

children.text: śakto bhavaty eva ca satvapāke saṃjātapakṣaḥ śakunir yathaiva |
children.translated_text: One becomes capable in maturing beings, like a bird whose wings have grown;

children.text: buddhāt praśaṃsāṃ labhate 'timātrām ādeyavākyo bhavati prajānām || AMsa_7.8 ||
children.translated_text: one receives the highest praise from the <s>Buddha</s> and becomes one whose words are accepted by the people. (AMsa 7.8)

body.text: trividhaṃ yogaṃ pradarśayati | satvaparipācanaśaktiyogaṃ praśaṃsāyogam ādeyavākyatāyogaṃ ca | vṛttyartham ārabhyaṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: He shows the threefold application: application of the capacity to mature beings, application of praise, and application of one's words being accepted. Regarding the meaning of mode of operation, a verse:

children.text: ṣaḍdhāpy abhijñā trividhā ca vidyā aṣṭau vimokṣā 'bhibhuvas tathā'ṣṭau |
children.translated_text: The six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the threefold knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the eight bases of mastery (<s>abhibhu</s>) likewise,

children.text: daśāpi kṛtsnāyatanāny ameyāḥ samādhayo dhīragataḥ prabhāvaḥ || AMsa_7.9 ||
children.translated_text: the ten spheres of totality (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>), and the immeasurable <s>samādhis</s> — the power is of one who has gone far. (AMsa 7.9)

body.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ prabhedair bodhisatvasya prabhāvo vartate | abhijñāvidyāvimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanāpramāṇasamādhiprabhedaiḥ | evaṃ ṣaḍarthena vibhāgalakṣaṇena prabhāvaṃ darśayitvā tanmāhātmyodbhāvanārthaṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> operates through six categories: the categories of <s>abhijñās</s>, knowledges, liberations, bases of mastery, spheres of totality, and immeasurable <s>samādhis</s>. Having thus shown the power through the analysis-characteristic of six meanings, to reveal its greatness, a verse:

children.text: sa hi paramavaśitvalabdhabuddhir jagadavaśaṃ svavaśe vidhāya nityam |
children.translated_text: For he, having obtained supreme mastery of mind-wisdom, always places the world — which is not self-mastered — under his own mastery;

children.text: parahitakaraṇaikatābhirāmaś carati bhaveṣu hi siṃhavat sudhīraḥ || AMsa_7.10 ||
children.translated_text: delighting solely in benefiting others, he moves through existences like a lion, with great courage. (AMsa 7.10)

body.text: trividhaṃ māhātmyaṃ darśayati | vaśitāmāhātmyaṃ svayaṃ paramajñānavaśitvaprāptyā kleśāsvavaśasya jagataḥ

children.translated_text: under his own mastery;
greatness of delight — always
delighting solely in acting for the benefit of others;
and greatness of fearlessness in existences.

body.translated_text: He shows the threefold greatness: greatness of mastery — by personally attaining supreme mastery of knowledge, placing the world, which is not self-mastered due to afflictions,
The section on power (<s>prabhāva</s>) is the seventh in the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>.

CHAPTER VIII
Eighth Section
Regarding the maturation of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a summary verse:

children.text: rūciḥ prasādaḥ praśamo 'nukampanā kṣamātha medhā prabalatvam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Interest, faith, tranquility, compassion, patience, intelligence, strength,

children.text: ahāryatāṅgaiḥ samupetatā bhṛśaṃ jinātmaje tatparipākalakṣaṇam || AMsa_8.1 ||
children.translated_text: and unshakability — being endowed with these qualities intensely — in the child of the conqueror, that is the characteristic of maturation. (AMsa 8.1)
Interest (<s>ruci</s>):
in the <s>Dharma</s> taught as the <s>Mahāyāna</s>;
faith (<s>prasāda</s>):
in the teacher thereof;
tranquility (<s>praśama</s>):
of afflictions;
compassion (<s>anukampā</s>):
toward beings;
patience (<s>kṣamā</s>):
in difficult practices;
intelligence (<s>medhā</s>):
in grasping, retaining, and penetrating;

body.translated_text: By this he shows the classification of maturation. Ripening through the removal of afflictions is

Universal ripening through the three vehicles is

Eminent ripening, distinguished by surpassing external maturation, is
<s>prapācanā</s> (forth-ripening).

<s>anupācanā</s> (following-ripening).

<s>supācanā</s> (good ripening).

<s>adhipācanā</s> (superior ripening),
in the sense of unerring meaning.
Constant ripening is
<s>nipācanā</s> (constant ripening),
in the sense of non-decline. Progressively higher ripening is
<s>utpācanā</s> (progressive ripening).

children.translated_text: Having performed wondrous difficult deeds, having accumulated all merit through hundreds of exertions, through an excellent long period of time and aeons, through the destruction of all coverings,

children.text: sūkṣmasyāvaraṇasya bhūmiṣu gatasyotpāṭanād buddhatā ratnānām iva sā prabhāvamahatāṃ peṭā samuddhātitā || AMsa_9.3 ||
children.translated_text: through uprooting the subtle obscuration traversed through the stages — <s>Buddhatva</s> (Buddhahood) is that, like a casket of jewels of great radiance, revealed. || AMsa_9.3 ||

body.text: samudāgamataḥ svabhāvata aupamyataś ca buddhatvam udbhāvitaṃ | yāvadbhir
body.translated_text: <s>Buddhatva</s> (Buddhahood) is set forth in terms of its attainment, its nature, and its analogy. Through as many
hundreds of difficult deeds
and through as many
accumulations of merit
and through as much
time,
and through the abandonment of as much afflictive and cognitive
obscuration —
it is attained. This is the attainment.
The attainment of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects), purified of all obscurations —
this is the nature.
Like a revealed jewel
casket —

body.text: tadaupamyaṃ | tasyaiva buddhatvasyādvayalakṣaṇe sānubhāve dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: this is its analogy. Regarding the non-dual characteristic together with the potency of that very <s>Buddhatva</s>, two verses:

children.text: sarvadharmāś ca buddhatvaṃ dharmo naiva na kaścana |
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Buddhatva</s> — <s>Dharma</s> is indeed neither nothing nor something;

children.text: śukladharmamayaṃ tac ca na ca tais tannirūpyate || AMsa_9.4 ||
children.translated_text: it consists of pure <s>dharmas</s>, yet it is not defined by them. || AMsa_9.4 ||
Because it is the cause of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, it has been likened to a jewel mine;
because it is the cause of what is wholesome, it has been likened to a rain cloud. || AMsa_9.5 ||
All <s>dharmas</s> are <s>Buddhatva</s> —

children.text: tathatāyā abhinnatvāt tadviśuddhiprabhāvitatvāc ca buddhatvasya na ca kaś ciddharmo 'sti parikalpitena dharmasvabhāvena
children.translated_text: because of the non-difference of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and because <s>Buddhatva</s> is brought about by the purification of that; yet no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever exists in the nature of an imagined entity.
<s>Buddhatva</s> consists of pure <s>dharmas</s> —

children.text: ca buddhatvaṃ pāramitādīnāṃ kuśalānāṃ tadbhāvena parivṛtteḥ | na ca tais tān nirdiśyate pāramitādīnāṃ pāramitādibhāvenāpariniṣpatter idam advayalakṣaṇaṃ | ratnākarameghopamatvam anubhāvaḥ | deśanā dharmaratnānāṃ tatprabhavatvāt kuśalasasyānāṃ ca vineyasaṃtānakṣetreṣu |
children.translated_text: because of the transformation of wholesome qualities such as the <s>pāramitās</s> into that state. Yet it is not defined by them, because the <s>pāramitās</s> and so forth are not ultimately established as <s>pāramitās</s> and so forth. This is the non-dual characteristic. Being like a jewel mine and a cloud is the potency: because it gives rise to the jewels of <s>Dharma</s> teaching, and because it is the cause of wholesome harvests in the fields of trainees' continuums.

children.text: buddhatvaṃ sarvadharmaḥ samuditam atha vā sarvadharmavyapetaṃ prodbhūter dharmaratnapratatasumahato dharmaratnākarābham |
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhatva</s> is all <s>dharmas</s> assembled, or again, devoid of all <s>dharmas</s>; because of producing the vast and great jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, it resembles a jewel mine;

children.text: bhūtānāṃ śuklasasya prasavasumahato hetuto meghabhūtaṃ dānād dharmāmbuvarṣapratatasuvihitasyākṣayasya prajāsu || AMsa_9.6 ||
children.translated_text: because of being the cause of the vast production of the wholesome harvest for beings, it is like a cloud, through the giving of the vast, well-arranged, inexhaustible rain of <s>Dharma</s> upon the people. || AMsa_9.6 ||

body.text: anena tṛtīyena ślokena tam evārthaṃ nirdiśati | sumahataḥ pratatasya dharmaratnasya

children.translated_text: producing

children.text: nimittatvād ratnākarābhaṃ bhūtānāṃ mahataḥ śuklasasya prasavahetutvān meghabhūtaṃ | mahataḥ
children.translated_text: the vast and great jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, it resembles a jewel mine. Because it is the cause of producing the great wholesome harvest for beings, it is like a cloud — through the giving
of the vast, well-arranged, inexhaustible rain of <s>Dharma</s>

children.text: prajāsv ity ayam atra padavigraho veditavyaḥ | tasyaiva buddhatvasya śaraṇatvānuttarye pañca ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: upon the people — this is the analysis of the words to be understood here. Regarding the unsurpassed quality of <s>Buddhatva</s> as a refuge, five verses:

body.translated_text: By this third verse he expounds that very meaning. Because it is the cause of

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhatva</s> is indeed protection from the entire host of afflictions, always,
from all wrongdoing, and from birth and death as well. || AMsa_9.7 ||
protection
from the defilement of afflictions, <s>karma</s> (action), and birth.

body.translated_text: By this, in summary, he shows that it is a refuge through

children.translated_text: From all calamities, from lower realms, from wrong methods,

children.text: satkāyād dhīnayānāc ca tasmāc charaṇam uttamam || AMsa_9.8 ||
children.translated_text: from the <s>satkāya</s> (personality view) and from the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (lesser vehicle) — therefore it is the supreme refuge. || AMsa_9.8 ||

body.translated_text: By this second verse,
through protection from
calamities, in detail. Therein, being protection from all calamities:

body.text: yad buddhānubhāvena andhāś cakṣūṃṣi pratilabhante badhirāḥ śrotraṃ vikṣiptacittāḥ svasthacittamītayaḥ śāmyantīty evam ādi |
body.translated_text: that by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, the blind obtain eyes, the deaf obtain hearing, the distracted obtain sound minds, and diseases are calmed — and so forth.
Being protection from

body.text: paritrāṇatvaṃ buddhaprabhayā tadgatānāṃ mokṣaṇāt tadagamane ca pratiṣṭhāpanāt |
body.translated_text: lower realms — through liberating those who have gone there by the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>, and through establishing them so that they do not go there again.
From wrong methods —

Its being a protection means rescuing from the views of <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). Its being a protection for <s>satkāya</s> (the embodied self) means causing <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the two vehicles.
Its being a protection from the <s>Hīnayāna</s>
means converting those of indeterminate <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage) to the single path of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text: śaraṇam anupamaṃ tacchreṣṭhabuddhatvam iṣṭaṃ jananamaraṇasarvakleśapāpeṣu rakṣā |
children.translated_text: 'The incomparable refuge is that supreme <s>Buddhahood</s> — protection in the evils of birth, death, and all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);
the vehicle of total protection for those beset by various fears, the path of means for removing extended and various sufferings.' // AMsa_9.9 //

body.text: anena tṛtīyena tasyaiva śaraṇatvasyānupamaśreṣṭhasya cānuttaryaṃ tenaivārthena darśayati |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows the unsurpassability of that very refuge-nature, which is incomparable and supreme, through that very meaning.

children.text: bauddhair dharmair yac ca susaṃpūrṇaśarīraṃ yat saddharme vetti sa satvān pravinetum |
children.translated_text: 'That which has a body perfectly endowed with <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, which knows how to guide beings in the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: yātaṃ pāraṃ yatkṛpayā sarvajagatsu tad buddhatvaṃ śreṣṭham iha eṣyaṃ śaraṇānām || AMsa_9.10 ||
children.translated_text: which has gone to the far shore, and which through compassion [acts] toward all worlds — that <s>Buddhahood</s> is the supreme and sought-after among refuges.' // AMsa_9.10 //

body.text: anena caturthena yaiḥ kāraṇais tat tathānuttaraṃ śaraṇaṃ bhavati tat saṃdarśayati |

children.translated_text: '<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>' —
the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and so forth —
'perfectly endowed'

children.text: svabhāvatvāt | svārthaniṣṭhām adhikṛtya saddharmasatvavinayopāyajñānāt karuṇāpāragamanāc ca parārthaniṣṭhām adhikṛtya |
children.translated_text: because of being their very nature. With respect to the accomplishment of one's own purpose: through knowledge of the true <s>Dharma</s> and the means of disciplining beings; and with respect to the accomplishment of others' purpose: through having gone to the far shore of compassion.

body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows the reasons by which that is thus an unsurpassed refuge.

children.text: ālokāt kālāt sarvasatvānāṃ buddhatvaṃ śaraṇaṃ mahat |
children.translated_text: 'From the time of seeing, for all beings, <s>Buddhahood</s> is the great refuge;
it is regarded as [effecting] the reversal of all calamities and the prosperity of well-being.' // AMsa_9.11 //

body.text: anena pañcamena ślokena yāvantaṃ kālaṃ yāvatāṃ satvānāṃ yatrārthe

children.translated_text: it is a refuge.

children.text: bhavati tat samāsena darśayati | yatrārthe iti
children.translated_text: He shows that. 'For what purpose' means
for the reversal of all calamities and for the prosperity of well-being.
On the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), six verses:

body.translated_text: By this fifth verse, he shows in summary for how long a time, for how many beings, and for what purpose

children.text: kleśajñeyavṛtīnāṃ satatam anugataṃ bījam utkṛṣṭakālaṃ yasminn astaṃ prayātaṃ bhavati suvipulaiḥ sarvahāniprakāraiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The seed of the veils of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) and <s>jñeya</s> (the knowable), which has followed [beings] continuously for a long time — in which [Buddhahood] that [seed] has gone to destruction through all the exceedingly vast modes of abandonment;

children.text: buddhatvaṃ śukladharmapravaraguṇayutā āśrayasyānyathāptis tatprāptir nirvikalpād viṣayasumahato jñānamārgāt suśuddhāt || AMsa_9.12 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> — the otherwise-becoming of the basis, endowed with the foremost qualities of pure <s>dharmas</s> — its attainment is from the supremely pure path of knowledge, whose object is immeasurably vast, free from conceptualization.' // AMsa_9.12 //

body.translated_text: By this [verse], the transformation of the basis is illuminated through separation from the seed of the opponent and through connection with the endowment of the antidote.

body.text: yathā ca tatprāptir dvividhamārgalābhāt | suviśuddhalokottarajñānamārgalābhāt | tatpṛṣṭhalabdhānantajñeyaviṣayajñānamārgalābhāc ca |
body.translated_text: And its attainment is through obtaining two kinds of path: through obtaining the supremely pure supramundane path of knowledge, and through obtaining the path of knowledge of the boundless object of the knowable, which is subsequently obtained.
'For a long time'
means from beginningless time.
'Through all the exceedingly vast modes of abandonment'
means through the modes of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages).

children.text: sthitaś ca tasmin sa tathāgato jagan mahācalendrastha ivābhyudīkṣate |
children.translated_text: 'And standing therein, that <s>Tathāgata</s> looks down upon the world as if standing upon the king of great mountains;

children.text: śamābhirāmaṃ karūṇāyate janamaghābhirāme 'nyajane tu kā kathā || AMsa_9.13 ||
children.translated_text: he has compassion for the people delighting in peace, and what to speak of other people delighting in evil!' // AMsa_9.13 //

body.text: anena dvitīyenānyāśrayaparāvṛttibhyas tadviśeṣaṃ darśayati | tatstho hi

children.translated_text: 'as if standing upon the king of great mountains,'

children.text: dūrāntaranikṛṣṭaṃ lokaṃ paśyati | dṛṣṭvā ca karuṇāyate śrāvakapratyekabuddhān api prāg eva tadanyān |
children.translated_text: sees the world far below at a great distance. And having seen, he has compassion even for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, how much more for others.

body.translated_text: By this second [verse], he shows the distinction of that [transformation] from other transformations of the basis. For one standing therein,

children.text: pravṛttir ūddhittir avṛtir āśrayo nivṛttir āvṛttir atho dvayādvayā |
children.translated_text: 'Activity, elevation, non-activity, the basis, cessation, perpetuity, and that of duality and non-duality,

children.text: samāviśiṣṭā api sarvagātmikā tathāgatānāṃ parivṛttir iṣyate || AMsa_9.14 ||
children.translated_text: equal and distinguished, and all-pervading — the transformation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is regarded [as tenfold].' // AMsa_9.14 //

body.text: anena tṛtīyena taddaśaprabhedaṃ darśayati | sā hi tathāgatānāṃ parivṛttiḥ parārthavṛttir iti

children.translated_text: 'activity' (<s>pravṛtti</s>).
Because of being distinguished among all <s>dharmas</s>, it is an elevated activity, hence
'elevation' (<s>udvṛtti</s>).
In the cause of defilement,
'non-activity' (<s>avṛtti</s>).
'Basis' (<s>āśraya</s>)

children.text: iti yo 'sau parivṛttyāśrayastaṃ darśayati | saṃkleśān nivṛttito
children.translated_text: — this shows the basis that is transformed. Through the cessation of defilements,
'cessation' (<s>nivṛtti</s>).
Because of being ultimate, it is an extended activity, hence
'perpetuity' (<s>āvṛtti</s>).
Through the activity of displaying awakening and <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
it is the activity of 'duality' (<s>dvayā</s>).
Because of being unestablished in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>, being of both the conditioned and the unconditioned,
it is the activity of 'non-duality' (<s>advayā</s>).
Through the commonality of liberation with <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,
it is an 'equal' (<s>samā</s>)
activity. Because of being unequaled by the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> such as the powers and fearlessnesses,
it is a 'distinguished' (<s>viśiṣṭā</s>)
activity. Because of being present in the instruction of all vehicles,
it is an 'all-pervading' (<s>sarvagatā</s>)
activity.

body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows the tenfold classification of that [transformation]. For that transformation of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is activity for the benefit of others, hence

children.text: yathāmbaraṃ sarvagataṃ sadāmataṃ tathaiva tat sarvagataṃ sadāmatam |
children.translated_text: 'Just as space is all-pervading and ever regarded [as such], so too that [Buddhahood] is all-pervading and ever regarded [as such];

children.text: yathāmbaraṃ rūpagaṇeṣu sarvagaṃ tathaiva tat satvagaṇeṣu sarvagam || AMsa_9.15 ||
children.translated_text: just as space pervades all groups of forms, so too that [Buddhahood] pervades all groups of beings.' // AMsa_9.15 //

body.text: anena caturthena tatsvabhāvasya buddhatvasya sarvagatatvaṃ darśayati | ākāśasādharmyeṇoddeśanirdeśataḥ pūrvāparārdhābhyāṃ |

children.translated_text: 'All-pervasiveness in groups of beings' —
this should be understood as being fulfilled through the going to all beings as their self, which is the <s>ātman</s> (selfhood) of <s>Buddhahood</s>.

body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows the all-pervasiveness of <s>Buddhahood</s>, which is the nature of that, through the analogy with space, by way of statement and explanation in the first and second halves.

children.translated_text: 'Just as, when a water-vessel is broken, the reflection of the moon is not seen,

children.text: tatha duṣṭeṣu satveṣu buddhabimbaṃ na dṛśyate || AMsa_9.16 ||
children.translated_text: so in corrupted beings, the image of the <s>Buddha</s> is not seen.' // AMsa_9.16 //
the non-seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>-image
is established through an analogy.

body.translated_text: By this fifth [verse], though it is all-pervading, in beings who are unfit vessels,

children.translated_text: 'Just as fire blazes in one place and is extinguished in another,

children.text: buddheṣv api tathā jñeyaṃ saṃdarśanamadarśanam || AMsa_9.17 ||
children.translated_text: so too with <s>Buddhas</s> — one should understand their appearing and disappearing.' // AMsa_9.17 //

body.text: anena ṣaṣṭhena buddhavineyeṣu satsu buddhotpādāt tad

children.translated_text: 'appearing';
when [beings] have been disciplined, through <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — that is
'disappearing.'
This is established through the analogy of fire blazing and being extinguished. On the effortless and unrelenting nature of <s>Buddha</s>-activity, four verses:

body.translated_text: By this sixth [verse]: when there are beings to be disciplined by <s>Buddhas</s>, there is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> — that is

children.translated_text: 'Just as from instruments not struck together there would be the arising of sound,

children.text: tathā jine vinābhogaṃ deśanāyāḥ samudbhavaḥ || AMsa_9.18 ||
children.translated_text: so too in the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), without effort, there is the arising of teaching.' // AMsa_9.18 //
'Just as from a jewel, without effort, there is the manifestation of its own radiance,

children.text: buddheṣv api vinābhogaṃ tathā kṛtyanidarśanam || AMsa_9.19 ||
children.translated_text: so too with <s>Buddhas</s>, without effort, there is the manifestation of [their] activity.' // AMsa_9.19 //
the sound of unstruck instruments
and the radiance of a jewel.

body.translated_text: By these two verses, he establishes <s>Buddha</s>-activity without effort, through the analogy of

children.translated_text: 'Just as in space, uninterrupted activities of the world are seen,
so too in the undefiled element, the activities of the <s>Jinas</s> are uninterrupted.' // AMsa_9.20 //

children.text: yathākāśe kriyāṇāṃ hi hānir abhyudayaḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: 'Just as in space there is always the decline and prosperity of activities,
so too in the undefiled element there is the arising and passing of <s>Buddha</s>-activity.' // AMsa_9.21 //
like space
— just as the world's
activities
are uninterrupted, yet various activities have their
arising and passing —
so too. On the depth of the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), sixteen verses:

body.translated_text: By these two also, the unrelenting nature of <s>Buddha</s>-activity is [shown] through the uninterruptedness of <s>Buddha</s>-action,

children.translated_text: 'Though not distinguished by before and after, [yet] free from all obscurations,

children.text: na śuddhā nāpi cāśuddhā tathatā buddhatā matā || AMsa_9.22 ||
children.translated_text: neither pure nor impure — <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is regarded as <s>Buddhahood</s>.' // AMsa_9.22 //

body.text: paurvāparyeṇa viśiṣṭatvān na śuddhā | paścāt sarvāvaraṇanirmalatvān nāśuddhā malavigamāt |
body.translated_text: Because of not being distinguished by before and after, it is not pure. Because of being subsequently free from all obscurations, it is not impure — due to the removal of defilement.

children.translated_text: 'In purified <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), through non-self, from the attainment of the path,
<s>Buddhas</s>, being those who have attained a pure self, have gone to the greatness of the self.' // AMsa_9.23 //

body.text: tatra cānāsrave dhātau buddhānāṃ paramātmā nirdiśyate | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | agranairātmyātmakatvāt | agraṃ

children.translated_text: non-self is purified

children.text: tathatā sā ca buddhānām ātmā svabhāvārthena tasyāṃ viśuddhāyām agraṃ nairātmyam ātmānaṃ buddhā labhante śuddhaṃ | ataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and that is the <s>ātman</s> (self) of <s>Buddhas</s> in the sense of essential nature. In that purified [suchness], <s>Buddhas</s> attain the supreme non-self as [their] self, the pure [self]. Therefore,
'being those who have attained a pure self' —

children.text: buddhā ātmamāhātmyaṃ prāptā ity anenābhisaṃdhinā buddhānām anāsrave dhātau paramātmā vyavasthāpyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhas</s> have attained the greatness of the self. With this intention, the supreme self of <s>Buddhas</s> is established in the undefiled element.

body.translated_text: And therein, in the undefiled element of <s>Buddhas</s>, the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) is taught. For what reason? Because it has the nature of the supreme <s>nairātmya</s> (non-self). The supreme

children.text: na bhāvo nāpi cābhāvo buddhatvaṃ tena kathyate |
children.translated_text: '<s>Buddhahood</s> is said to be neither existence nor non-existence;
therefore, regarding the question of the <s>Buddha</s>'s thus-ness, the method of the undeclared (<s>avyākṛta</s>) is regarded [as appropriate].' // AMsa_9.24 //
is not called 'existence'
— because it has the characteristic of the absence of a person (<s>pudgala</s>) and <s>dharmas</s>, and because <s>Buddhahood</s> has that [absence] as its nature.
It is not called 'non-existence'
— because it has the nature of the characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Therefore, regarding the question of the <s>Buddha</s>'s existence or non-existence —
the question

children.text: bhavati tathāgataḥ paraṃ maraṇān na bhavatīty evamādir
children.translated_text: 'Does the <s>Tathāgata</s> exist after death or not?' and so forth —
the method of the undeclared (<s>avyākṛta</s>) is regarded [as appropriate].

body.translated_text: For that very reason, <s>Buddhahood</s>

children.text: dāhaśāntir yathā lohe darśane timirasya ca |
children.translated_text: 'Just as there is the extinguishing of burning in iron, and [the cessation] of blindness in vision,

children.text: cittajñāne tathā bauddhe bhāvābhāvo na śasyate || AMsa_9.25 ||
children.translated_text: so too in <s>Buddha</s>-mind and -knowledge, existence and non-existence should not be predicated.' // AMsa_9.25 //

children.text: yathā ca lohe dāhaśāntir darśane ca timiram etasya
children.translated_text: Just as in iron the extinguishing of burning, and in vision the blindness — this

children.text: śāntir na bhāvo dāhatimirayor abhāvalakṣaṇatvāt | nābhāvaḥ śāntilakṣaṇena bhāvāt | evaṃ buddhānāṃ
children.translated_text: cessation is not existence, because it has the characteristic of the absence of burning and blindness. Nor is it non-existence, because there is the entity characterized by cessation. So too with <s>Buddhas</s> —
in mind and knowledge,
the cessation of desire and ignorance, which correspond to burning and blindness,
should not be called 'existence'

children.text: tadabhāvaprabhāvitatvāc cetaḥprajñāvimuktyā nābhāvas tena tena vimuktilakṣaṇena bhāvāt |
children.translated_text: — because it is produced by the absence of those [defilements], through the liberation of mind and wisdom. Nor [should it be called] non-existence, because of the entity characterized by that particular liberation.

children.text: buddhānām amale dhātau naikatā bahutā na ca |
children.translated_text: 'In the stainless element of <s>Buddhas</s>, there is neither oneness nor multiplicity,
like space — because of bodylessness, [yet] in accordance with previous bodies.' // AMsa_9.26 //
In the
undefiled
element of <s>Buddhas</s>, there is no oneness
— in accordance with previous bodies. There is no multiplicity — because of the absence of body,
like space.
'In the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> such as the powers, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is regarded as like a mine of jewels;
in the wholesome crops of the world, it is regarded as like a great cloud.' // AMsa_9.27 //
'Because of being perfectly full of merit and knowledge, it is regarded as like the full moon;
and because of producing the light of knowledge, it is regarded as like the great sun.' // AMsa_9.28 //
and the likeness to the full moon and the great sun,
are self-explanatory.

body.translated_text: These two verses on the likeness to a mine of jewels and a cloud,

children.translated_text: 'Just as immeasurable rays, intermingled in the disc of the sun,

children.text: sadaikakāryā vartante lokam ālokayanti ca || AMsa_9.29 ||
children.translated_text: always perform a single function and illuminate the world —' // AMsa_9.29 //
'So too in the undefiled element, the immeasurability of <s>Buddhas</s>,
intermingled and performing a single function in [their] activities, are regarded as producing the light of knowledge.' // AMsa_9.30 //
intermingled rays
performing a single function, he shows their common activity. The
'single function' of rays

children.text: pācanaśoṣaṇasamānakāryatvād veditavyaṃ | dvitīyenānāsrave dhātau miśraikakāryatvaṃ nirmāṇādikṛtyeṣu |
children.translated_text: should be understood through their common activity of ripening and drying. By the second [verse], in the undefiled element, the intermingled single function in activities such as emanation.

body.translated_text: By the first [verse], through the analogy of

children.translated_text: 'Just as from the emission of a single ray, all rays are emitted

children.text: bhānos tathaiva buddhānāṃ jñeyā jñānaviniḥsṛtiḥ || AMsa_9.31 ||
children.translated_text: from the sun, so too should the emission of knowledge of <s>Buddhas</s> be understood.' // AMsa_9.31 //
through the emission of all rays —

children.text: sa ca buddhānām ekakāle jñānapravṛttiṃ darśayati |
children.translated_text: this shows the simultaneous operation of knowledge of <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.translated_text: At a single time,

children.translated_text: 'Just as in the functioning of the sun's rays there is no sense of "mine,"

children.text: tathaiva buddhajñānānāṃ vṛttau nāsti mamāyitam || AMsa_9.32 ||
children.translated_text: so too in the functioning of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge there is no sense of "mine."' // AMsa_9.32 //
'Just as the world is illuminated by rays released at once from the sun,

children.text: sakṛt jñeyaṃ tathā sarvaṃ buddhajñānaiḥ prabhāsyate || AMsa_9.33 ||
children.translated_text: so too all that is knowable is illuminated by <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge at once.' // AMsa_9.33 //

body.text: mamatvābhāve jagajjñeyaprabhāsena ca | yathākramaṃ ślokau gatārthau |
body.translated_text: On the absence of possessiveness and on the illumination of all that is knowable in the world — the verses are self-explanatory, in order.

children.translated_text: 'Just as clouds and the like are regarded as obscurations of the sun's rays,
so too the corruption of beings is the veiling of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.' // AMsa_9.34 //
obscuration of clouds and the like
[prevents] the rays' illumination, so too
the veiling of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge —
the corruption of beings through being unfit vessels, due to the extreme prevalence of the five degeneracies (<s>pañcakaṣāya</s>).

body.translated_text: Just as the

children.translated_text: 'Just as due to the condition of dust, there is varied coloring and non-coloring of cloth,
so too, due to the condition of [prior] penetration, there is varied coloring and non-coloring of knowledge in liberation.' // AMsa_9.35 //

body.translated_text: Just as due to the specific condition of dust, there is varied coloring of cloth,
and in some cases
non-coloring,
so too, due to the specific power of previous aspirations and practice
, for <s>Buddhas</s>
there is varied coloring of knowledge in liberation.
For <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, in liberation there is
non-coloring [of knowledge].

children.translated_text: 'The depth in the stainless element — in characteristics, abodes, and activities —

children.text: buddhānām etad uditaṃ raṅgair vākāśacitraṇā || AMsa_9.36 ||
children.translated_text: this has been declared for <s>Buddhas</s>; like coloring or painting space.' // AMsa_9.36 //
depth

children.text: evam uktaṃ | lakṣaṇagāmbhīryaṃ caturbhiḥ ślokaiḥ | sthānagāmbhīryaṃ pañcamenaikatvapṛthaktvābhyām asthitatvāt | karmagāmbhīryaṃ daśabhiḥ | tat punar lakṣaṇagāmbhīryaṃ viśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ paramātmalakṣaṇam avyākṛtalakṣaṇaṃ vimuktilakṣaṇaṃ cārabhyoktaṃ | karmagāmbhīryaṃ bodhipakṣādiratnāśrayatvakarma satvaparipācanakarma niṣṭhāgamanakarma dharmadeśanākarma nirmāṇādikṛtyakarma jñānapravṛttikarma avikalpanakarma citrākārajñānakarma jñānāpravṛttikarma vimuktisāmānyajñānaviśeṣakarma cārabhyoktaṃ | seyamanāsrave dhātau niṣprapañcatvād ākāśopame gāmbhīryaprabhedadeśanā yathā
children.translated_text: Thus it has been stated. The depth of characteristics is [shown] by four verses. The depth of abode by the fifth, because of non-abiding in either unity or separateness. The depth of activity by ten [verses]. Furthermore, the depth of characteristics is stated beginning with the characteristic of purification, the characteristic of the supreme self, the indeterminate characteristic, and the characteristic of liberation. The depth of activity is stated beginning with the activity of being the support for the jewels of the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) and so forth, the activity of maturing beings, the activity of reaching the final goal, the activity of teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, the activity of creating emanations and so forth, the activity of the operation of knowledge, the activity of non-conceptualization, the activity of knowledge of variegated forms, the activity of the non-operation of knowledge, and the activity of the special knowledge common to liberation. This teaching of the divisions of depth in the undefiled realm, which is free from conceptual elaboration and like space, should be understood as
painting space with colors —
[impossible].

body.translated_text: This is the threefold

children.translated_text: 'Though <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is undifferentiated for all, it has come to purity;

children.text: tathāgatatvaṃ tasmāc ca tadgarbhāḥ sarvadehinaḥ || AMsa_9.37 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood [consists in that], and all embodied beings have that as their essence (<s>tathāgatagarbha</s>).' // AMsa_9.37 //
The <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) that is undifferentiated for all —

children.text: tadviśuddhisvabhāvaś ca tathāgataḥ | ataḥ sarve satvās tathāgatagarbhā ity ucyate | vibhutvāvibhāge ślokā ekādaśa |
children.translated_text: and the <s>Tathāgata</s> has the nature of its purification; therefore all beings are said to have <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> (the embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>). On the distinction of sovereign power (<s>vibhutva</s>), eleven verses:
'The sovereign power of <s>Śrāvakas</s> is surpassed by worldly [power];
over <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the [power] of <s>Śrāvakas</s> is surpassed by that of the mind-born <s>Buddha</s>-stage.' // AMsa_9.38 //
'The sovereign power of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> does not reach even a fraction of that;
the sovereign power of <s>Tathāgatas</s> does not reach even a fraction of that.' // AMsa_9.39 //

body.text: ābhyāṃ tāvad dvābhyāṃ prabhāvotkarṣaviśeṣeṇa buddhānāṃ vibhutvaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: By these two [verses], he shows the sovereign power of <s>Buddhas</s> through the distinction of the excellence of supernatural power.

children.text: aprameyam acintyaṃ ca vibhutvaṃ bauddham iṣyate |
children.translated_text: 'The sovereign power of the <s>Buddhas</s> is held to be immeasurable and inconceivable —

children.text: yasya yatra yathā yāvat kāle yasmin pravartate || AMsa_9.40 ||
children.translated_text: for whom, where, how, to what extent, and at what time it operates.' // AMsa_9.40 //

body.translated_text: By this third [verse], through the distinction of the depth of the varieties of modes, how
is it immeasurable,
and how
is it inconceivable?
He says: for the sake of which person it
operates,
in which world-realm, by what kinds of modes,
to what extent —
little
or much,
at what time.
By the remaining verses, he shows the distinctions of sovereign power through the distinctions of mental transformation:

children.translated_text: 'In the transformation of the five sense faculties, supreme sovereign power is obtained —
in the operation regarding all objects of all [faculties], with the arising of twelve hundred qualities.' // AMsa_9.41 //
In the transformation of the five sense faculties,
twofold
supreme sovereign power is obtained.
Of all five sense faculties,
all
five
objects' operation —
therein, for each individually,
with the arising of twelve hundred
qualities.
'In the transformation of mind too, supreme sovereign power is obtained —
in the non-conceptual, perfectly pure knowledge that accompanies sovereign power.' // AMsa_9.42 //
accompanying sovereign power,
in the non-conceptual, perfectly pure
knowledge,
supreme
sovereign power is obtained,
together with which all knowledge of sovereign power operates.

body.translated_text: In the transformation of mind,

children.translated_text: 'In the transformation of the apprehension of objects, supreme sovereign power is obtained —
in the purification of the field, for the display of enjoyments as one wishes.' // AMsa_9.43 //
In the transformation of
objects,
in the transformation of apprehension,
and
in the purification of the field,
supreme sovereign power is obtained, by which
the display of enjoyments as one wishes
is accomplished.

body.translated_text: 'In the non-obstruction of all activities of knowledge, at all times.' // AMsa_9.44 //

children.translated_text: In the transformation of conceptualization, of all knowledges and activities,
at all
times,
in non-obstruction, supreme sovereign power is obtained.
'In the transformation of the basis, supreme sovereign power is obtained —

children.text: apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ buddhānām acale male pade || AMsa_9.45 ||
children.translated_text: the non-abiding <s>Nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, in the unmoving, pure state.' // AMsa_9.45 //
In the transformation of the basis, the non-abiding <s>Nirvāṇa</s> —
supreme sovereign power is obtained
of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
in the undefiled realm.
'In the transformation of sexual union, supreme sovereign power is obtained —
in the blissful abiding of the <s>Buddha</s>, and in the perception of the non-defilement of consorts.' // AMsa_9.46 //
In the transformation of sexual union,
twofold:
in the blissful abiding of the <s>Buddha</s>,
and
in the perception of the non-defilement of consorts.
'In the elimination of the perception of space, supreme sovereign power is obtained —
in the fulfillment of desired aims and in the manifestation of movement and form.' // AMsa_9.47 //
In the elimination of the perception of space,
twofold indeed:
in the fulfillment of desired aims,
whereby one becomes a 'womb of space' (<s>gaganagarbha</s>);
and in the manifestation of movement and form,
through going as one wishes and through mastery over space.
'Thus, in the immeasurable transformation, immeasurable sovereign power is acknowledged;
through the performance of inconceivable deeds of the <s>Buddhas</s>, in the undefiled basis.' // AMsa_9.48 //

body.text: ity anena mukhenāprameyā parāvṛttiḥ | tatra cāprameyaṃ vibhutvam

children.translated_text: the performance of inconceivable deeds of the <s>Buddhas</s>

children.text: anāsrave dhātau veditavyaṃ | tasyaiva buddhasya satvaparipākanimittatve sapta ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: is to be understood in the undefiled realm. On that very <s>Buddha</s>'s being the cause of the maturation of beings, seven verses:

body.translated_text: Thus, by this method, the transformation is immeasurable; and therein the sovereign power is immeasurable —

children.text: śubhe vṛddho loko vrajati suviśuddhau paramatāṃ śubhe cānārabdhvā vrajati śubhavṛddhau paramatām |
children.translated_text: 'The world, increased in virtue, goes to the supreme in thorough purification; and without having commenced virtue, goes to the supreme in the increase of virtue;

children.text: vrajaty evaṃ loko diśi diśi jinānāṃ sukathitair apakvaḥ pakvo vā na ca punar aśeṣaṃ dhruvam iha || AMsa_9.49 ||
children.translated_text: thus the world goes in every direction through the well-spoken teachings of the Conquerors — whether unripened or ripened — yet not completely and permanently here.' // AMsa_9.49 //

body.text: anena yādṛśasya paripākasya nimittaṃ bhavati taddarśayati | upacitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca vimuktau paramatāyām anupacitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca kuśalamūlopacaye | apakvaḥ

children.translated_text: goes to the supreme in the increase of virtue —
this ripening he goes to; the ripened one
goes to the supreme in thorough purification.

children.text: | evaṃ ca nityakālaṃ vrajati na ca niḥśeṣaṃ lokasyānantatvāt |
children.translated_text: And thus [the world] goes perpetually, yet not exhaustively, because of the infinity of the world.

body.translated_text: By this [verse], he shows the cause of what kind of maturation it is: of those who have accumulated roots of merit, toward the supreme in liberation; and of those who have not accumulated roots of merit, toward the accumulation of roots of merit. The unripened one

children.text: tathā kṛtvā caryāṃ kṛcchrāvāpyāṃ paramaguṇayogād bhutavartī mahābodhiṃ nityāṃ dhruvam aśaraṇānāṃ ca śaraṇam |
children.translated_text: 'Having performed the conduct that is difficult to attain, through the possession of supreme qualities, abiding in truth, [they reach] the great awakening — permanent, stable, and the refuge of the refugeless;

children.text: labhante yaddhīrā daśadig sadā sadā sarvasamayaṃ tad āścaryaṃ loke suvidhacaraṇān nādbhutam api || AMsa_9.50 ||
children.translated_text: that which the steadfast ones attain in the ten directions, always, at all times — that is a wonder in the world, yet not surprising from those of good conduct.' // AMsa_9.50 //

body.translated_text: By this second [verse], the maturation of the ripened <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —
a wonder,
yet not a wonder.
Its characteristic:
'always, at all times'

body.text: iti nityaṃ nirantaraṃ ca tad anubhūya mārgacaraṇaṃ
body.translated_text: means permanently and uninterruptedly, having experienced that path-conduct —
conduct of good method.

children.text: kvaciddharmāñ ca kaṃ dharmyaṃ cakraṃ bahumukhaśatair darśayati yaḥ kvacij janmāntardhiṃ kvacid api vicitrāṃ janacarīm |
children.translated_text: 'He who shows the <s>Dharma</s> wheel to a certain person worthy of <s>Dharma</s>, with hundreds of approaches — somewhere birth, somewhere disappearance, somewhere varied life-stories,

children.text: kvacitkṛtsnāṃ bodhiṃ kvacid api ca nirvāṇam asakṛt na ca sthānāt tasmād vicalati sa sarvaṃ ca kurute || AMsa_9.51 ||
children.translated_text: somewhere complete awakening, and somewhere <s>Nirvāṇa</s> again and again — yet he does not move from that station, and he accomplishes everything.' // AMsa_9.51 //

body.text: anena tṛtīyena yugapadbahumukhaparipācanopāyaprayoge nimittatvaṃ darśayati | yathā yatrasthaḥ satvān vinayati | vicitrā janacarī jātakabhedena |

children.translated_text: 'Does not move from that station'
means from the undefiled realm.

body.translated_text: By this third [verse], he shows being the cause through the simultaneous application of means of maturation with many approaches: as, wherever stationed, he disciplines beings. 'Varied life-stories' means through the varieties of <s>Jātakas</s>.

children.text: na buddhānām evaṃ bhavati mama pakvo 'yam iti cāprapācyo 'yaṃ dehī api ca adhunāpācyata iti |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddhas</s> do not think thus: "This one is ripened by me" or "This embodied being is unripenable" or "This one is now being ripened";

children.text: vinā saṃskāraṃ tu prapacam upayāty eva janatā śubhair dharmair nityaṃ diśi diśi samantāt trayamukham || AMsa_9.52 ||
children.translated_text: yet, without deliberate effort, humanity proceeds to maturation through wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, perpetually, in every direction, all around, through three approaches.' // AMsa_9.52 //

body.text: anena caturthena tatparipākaprayoganimittatvam anabhisaṃskāreṇa daśayati | trayamukham iti yānatrayeṇa |
body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], he shows being the cause of that maturation-practice without deliberate construction (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>). 'Three approaches' means through the three vehicles (<s>yānatraya</s>).

children.text: yathāyatnaṃ bhānuḥ pratataviṣadair aṃśavisaraiḥ prapākakaṃ sasyānāṃ diśi diśi samantāt prakurūte |
children.translated_text: 'Just as the sun, with its extended, brilliant beams of rays, without effort, ripens the crops in every direction all around,

children.text: tathā dharmārko 'pi praśamavidhidharmāṃśuvisaraiḥ prapākaṃ sasyānāṃ diśi diśi samantāt prakurūte || AMsa_9.53 ||
children.translated_text: so too the sun of <s>Dharma</s>, with its beams of rays of the <s>dharmas</s> of the method of pacification, ripens the crops in every direction all around.' // AMsa_9.53 //

body.translated_text: By this fifth [verse], he shows the simile for the maturation without deliberate construction.

children.text: yathaikasmād dīpād bhavati sumahān dīpanicayo 'prameyo 'saṃkhyeyo na ca sa punar eti vyayamataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as from one lamp arises a great, immeasurable, innumerable mass of lamps, and that [first lamp] does not thereby undergo destruction;

children.text: yathaikasmād buddhād pākābhavati sumahān paripākapākanicayo 'prameyo 'saṃkhyeyo na ca punar eti punar upaiti vyayamataḥ || AMsa_9.54 ||
children.translated_text: so too from one <s>Buddha</s> arises a great, immeasurable, innumerable mass of matured ones, and [the <s>Buddha</s>] does not thereby again undergo destruction.' // AMsa_9.54 //

body.translated_text: By this sixth [verse], the sequential maturation [is shown].

children.text: yathā toyais tṛptiṃ vrajati na mahāsāgara iva na vṛddhiṃ vā yāti pratataviṣadāmbu praviśanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as the great ocean does not become satiated by waters, nor does it increase when the extended, brilliant waters enter;

children.text: tathā bauddhau dhātuḥ satatasamitaiḥ śuddhiviśanair na tṛptiṃ vṛddhiṃ vā vrajati paramāścaryam iha tat || AMsa_9.55 ||
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Buddha</s>-realm, with the constant, continuous entries of purification, neither becomes satiated nor increases — this is the supreme wonder here.' // AMsa_9.55 //

body.text: anena saptamena paripakvānāṃ vimuktipraveśe samudrodāharaṇena dharmadhātor atṛptiṃ cāvakāśadānād avṛddhiṃ dhyānādhikatvāt | dharmadhātuviśuddhau catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: By this seventh [verse], with the illustration of the ocean regarding the entry of the ripened into liberation, [he shows] the non-satiation of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> — through giving space — and its non-increase, because of the predominance of meditation. On the purification of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, four verses:

children.translated_text: 'Having the characteristic of the purification of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) through the exclusion of the duality of all <s>dharmas</s>;
having the characteristic of the inexhaustible mastery of the object, knowledge, and its support.' // AMsa_9.56 //

body.text: eṣa svabhāvārtham ārabhyaikaḥ ślokaḥ | kleśajñeyāvaraṇadvayāt sarvadharmatathatāviśuddhilakṣaṇaś ca | vastutadālambanajñānayor akṣayavaśitālakṣaṇaś ca |
body.translated_text: This is one verse with regard to the meaning of the intrinsic nature. Having the characteristic of the purification of the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> from the twofold obscuration of afflictions and of the knowable (<s>kleśajñeyāvaraṇa</s>). And having the characteristic of inexhaustible mastery regarding both the object and the knowledge that takes it as its support.

children.translated_text: the inexhaustible placing of all beings in the twofold [benefit] in every way is the fruit.' // AMsa_9.57 //

body.translated_text: 'The full accomplishment of the cultivation of the knowledge of <s>tathatā</s> in every way;

body.text: eṣa hetvarthaṃ phalārthaṃ cārabhya dvitīyaḥ ślokaḥ | sarvatastathatājñānabhāvanā dharmadhātuviśuddhihetuḥ |

children.translated_text: 'In every way'
means through all the approaches of the <s>Dharma</s>-teachings.
The inexhaustible placing of all beings in the twofold benefit and happiness in every way is the fruit.

body.translated_text: This is the second verse with regard to the meaning of the cause and the fruit. The cultivation of the knowledge of <s>tathatā</s> in every way is the cause of the purification of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Having the activity of the application of means through the emanation of body, speech, and mind;
endowed with the immeasurable twofold gateway of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention).' // AMsa_9.58 //

body.text: eṣa karmārthaṃ yogārthaṃ cārabhya tṛtīyaḥ ślokaḥ | trividhiṃ kāyādinirmāṇaṃ karma samādhidhāraṇīmukhābhyāṃ dvayena cāprameyeṇa puṇyajñānasaṃbhāreṇa samanvāgamo yogaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the third verse with regard to the meaning of activity and practice. The threefold emanation of body and so forth is the activity; and the practice is the endowment with the immeasurable twofold accumulation of merit and knowledge through the two gateways of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Through the intrinsic-nature [body], the <s>Dharma</s> [body], the enjoyment [body], and the emanation [bodies], having distinct functions —
this purified <s>Dharmadhātu</s> has been proclaimed by the <s>Buddhas</s>.' // AMsa_9.59 //

body.text: eṣa vṛttyartham ārabhya caturthaḥ ślokaḥ | svābhāvikasāṃbhogikanairmāṇikakāyavṛttyā bhinnavṛttikaḥ | buddhakāyavibhāge sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fourth verse with regard to the meaning of function. Having distinct functions through the functions of the <s>svābhāvika</s> (intrinsic-nature), <s>sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment), and <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation) bodies. On the analysis of the <s>Buddha</s>-body, seven verses:

children.translated_text: 'The intrinsic-nature body, then the enjoyment body, and the other — the emanation body;

children.text: kāyabhedā hi buddhānāṃ prathamas tu dvayāśrayaḥ || AMsa_9.60 ||
children.translated_text: these are the divisions of the body of the <s>Buddhas</s>; the first, however, is the basis of the [other] two.' // AMsa_9.60 //

body.text: trividhiḥ kāyo buddhānāṃ | svābhāviko dharmakāya āśrayaparāvṛttilakṣaṇaḥ | sāṃbhogiko yena parṣanbhaṇḍaleṣu dharmasaṃbhogaṃ karoti | nairmāṇiko yena nirmāṇena satvārthaṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: The body of the <s>Buddhas</s> is threefold: the intrinsic-nature body (<s>svābhāvikakāya</s>) is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, characterized by the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>); the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s>) is that by which he performs the enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s> in the assemblies; the emanation body (<s>nairmāṇikakāya</s>) is that by which he accomplishes the welfare of beings through emanation.

children.translated_text: 'The enjoyment [body] in all realms is differentiated by assemblies and retinues,

children.text: kṣetraiś ca nāmabhiḥ kāyair dharmasaṃbhogaceṣṭitaiḥ || AMsa_9.61 ||
children.translated_text: by fields, by names, by bodies, and by the activities of the enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s>.' // AMsa_9.61 //

body.text: tatra sāṃbhogikaḥ sarvalokadhātuṣu parṣanmaṇḍalabuddhakṣetranām aśarīradharmasaṃbhogakriyābhir bhinnaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the enjoyment body is differentiated in all world-realms by the activities of assemblies, <s>Buddha</s>-fields, names, bodies, and the enjoyment of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: samaḥ sūkṣmaś ca tacchiṣṭaḥ kāyaḥ svābhāviko mataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The intrinsic-nature body is considered equal, subtle, and connected with those [enjoyment bodies];
it is the cause of the sovereign power of enjoyment, for the display of enjoyments as one wishes.' // AMsa_9.62 //

body.text: svābhāvikaḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ samo nirviśiṣṭatayā | sūkṣmo durjñānatayā | tena sāṃbhogikena kāyena saṃbaddhaḥ saṃbhogavibhutve ca hetur yatheṣṭaṃ bhogadarśanāya |
body.translated_text: The intrinsic-nature body of all <s>Buddhas</s> is equal, through non-differentiation; subtle, through being difficult to know; connected with that enjoyment body; and the cause of the sovereign power of enjoyment, for the display of enjoyments as one wishes.

children.translated_text: 'The immeasurable emanation of the <s>Buddhas</s> is considered the emanation body;
the complete accomplishment of the purpose of both [self and others] by the two [bodies] is established in every aspect.' // AMsa_9.63 //

body.text: nairmāṇikas tu kāyo buddhānām aprameyaprabhedaṃ buddhanirmāṇaṃ sāṃbhogikaḥ svāthasaṃpattilakṣaṇaḥ | nairmāṇikaḥ parārthasaṃpattilakṣaṇaḥ | evaṃ dvayārthasaṃpattir yathākramaṃ dvayoḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ sāṃbhogike ca kāye nairmāṇike ca |
body.translated_text: The <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation) body of the <s>Buddhas</s> is the immeasurably manifold <s>buddhanirmāṇa</s> (Buddha-emanation). The <s>sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment) body has the characteristic of one's own attainment (<s>svārthasaṃpatti</s>). The <s>nairmāṇika</s> body has the characteristic of the attainment for others (<s>parārthasaṃpatti</s>). Thus the twofold attainment is established in the two bodies respectively — in the <s>sāṃbhogika</s> body and in the <s>nairmāṇika</s> body.

children.translated_text: Through displays of craft, birth, great awakening, and perpetual <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
this <s>buddhanirmāṇakāya</s> (Buddha-emanation body) is a great illusion, a great means for liberation. // AMsa_9.64 //

body.text: sa punar nirmāṇakāyaḥ sadā vineyārthaṃ śilpasya vīṇāvādanādibhiḥ | janmanaś cābhisaṃbodheś ca
body.translated_text: Furthermore, that <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body) is always for the benefit of those to be trained — through crafts such as playing the <s>vīṇā</s> and so forth, through birth, through perfect awakening, and

body.text: nirvāṇasya ca darśanair vimocane mahopāyatvāt parārthasaṃpattilakṣaṇo veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: through displays of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — it should be understood as having the characteristic of the attainment for others, because it is a great means for liberation.

children.text: tribhiḥ kāyais tu vijñeyo buddhānāṃ kāyasaṃgrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: The collection of bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s> should be known through three bodies;

children.text: sāśrayaḥ svaparārtho yas tribhiḥ kāyair nirdarśitaḥ || AMsa_9.65 ||
children.translated_text: that which has a basis and serves one's own and others' purposes has been shown through the three bodies. // AMsa_9.65 //

body.text: tribhiś ca kāyair buddhānāṃ sarvakāyasaṃgraho veditavyaḥ | ebhis tribhiḥ kāyaiḥ sāśrayaḥ svaparārtho nidarśitaḥ | dvayoḥ svaparārthaprabhāvitatvāt dvayoś ca tadāśritatvād yathā pūrvam uktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Through the three bodies, the entirety of all bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s> should be understood. Through these three bodies, that which has a basis and serves one's own and others' purposes has been shown — because the two [enjoyment and emanation bodies] produce one's own and others' purposes, and because the two are based upon that [<s>dharmakāya</s>], as stated previously.

children.translated_text: In basis, intention, and action, they are considered equal;
by nature, by non-decline, and by continuity — in these there is permanence. // AMsa_9.66 //

body.text: te ca trayaḥ kāyāḥ sarvabuddhānāṃ yathākramaṃ tribhir nirviśeṣā āśrayeṇa dharmadhātor abhinnatvāt āśayena pṛthak buddhāśayasyābhāvāt | karmaṇā ca sādhāraṇakarmakatvāt | teṣu ca triṣu kāyeṣu yathākramaṃ trividhā nityatā veditavyā yena nityakāyās tathāgatā ucyante | prakṛtyā nityatā svābhāvikasya svabhāvena nityatvāt | asraṃsanena sāṃbhogikasya dharmasaṃbhāgo vicchedāt | prabandhena nairmāṇikasyāntarvyaye punaḥ punar nirmāṇadarśanāt | buddhajñānavibhāge daśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: These three bodies are without distinction for all <s>Buddhas</s>, respectively, in three ways: in basis, because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is undifferentiated; in intention, because there is no separate Buddha-intention; and in action, because their activity is shared. In those three bodies, a threefold permanence should be understood, respectively, by which the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are called 'having a permanent body': permanence by nature — because the <s>svābhāvika</s> (natural body) is permanent by its own nature; permanence by non-decline — because the <s>sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment body) does not cease from the sharing of the <s>Dharma</s>; permanence by continuity — because when the <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation body) disappears, emanation-displays appear again and again. On the division of Buddha-knowledge, ten verses:

children.translated_text: Mirror-like knowledge is immovable; three knowledges depend upon it —
the knowledge of equality, discriminating knowledge, and the knowledge of duty-accomplishment. // AMsa_9.67 //

body.text: caturvidhaṃ buddhānāṃ jñānam ādarśajñānaṃ samatājñānaṃ pratyavekṣājñānaṃ kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñānaṃ ca | ādarśajñānam acalaṃ trīṇi jñānāni tadāśritāni calāni |
body.translated_text: The knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> is fourfold: mirror-like knowledge (<s>ādarśajñāna</s>), equality knowledge (<s>samatājñāna</s>), discriminating knowledge (<s>pratyavekṣājñāna</s>), and duty-accomplishing knowledge (<s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s>). Mirror-like knowledge is immovable; the three knowledges depend upon it and are movable.

children.translated_text: Mirror-like knowledge is without possessiveness, unlimited, always accompanying,

children.text: sarvajñeyeṣv asaṃmūḍhaṃ na ca teṣv āmukhaṃ sadā || AMsa_9.68 ||
children.translated_text: never confused regarding all knowable objects, yet never directly facing them. // AMsa_9.68 //

body.text: ādarśajñānam amamam aparicchinnaṃ deśataḥ sadānugaṃ kālataḥ | sarvajñeyeṣv asaṃmūḍhaṃ sadāvaraṇavigamāt na ca teṣv āmukham anākāratvāt |
body.translated_text: Mirror-like knowledge is without possessiveness (<s>amama</s>), unlimited (<s>aparicchinna</s>) in terms of location, always accompanying (<s>sadānuga</s>) in terms of time, never confused regarding all knowable objects because of the permanent removal of obscurations, yet never directly facing them because of being without aspect (<s>anākāra</s>).

children.translated_text: Because it is the cause of all knowledge, it is likened to a great mirror;
and because from it arises the reflection of the knowledge of the <s>saṃbhogabuddha</s> (enjoyment-body Buddha), that is it. // AMsa_9.69 //

body.text: teṣāṃ ca samatādijñānānāṃ sarvaprakārāṇāṃ hetutvāt sarvajñānānāmākaropamaṃ | saṃbhogabuddhatvatajjñānapratibimbodayācca tadādarśajñānam ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Because it is the cause of all varieties of knowledge — equality and the rest — it is likened to a great mirror of knowledge. And because from it arises the reflection of the knowledge of <s>saṃbhogabuddha</s>, it is called mirror-like knowledge (<s>ādarśajñāna</s>).

children.translated_text: Equality knowledge regarding beings, through the purity of cultivation, is considered stainless;
abiding in non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s>, it is accepted as equality knowledge. // AMsa_9.70 //

body.text: yadbodhisatvenābhisamayakāleṣu samatājñānaṃ pratilabdhaṃ tadbhāvanāśuddhito budhiprāptasyāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇe niviṣṭaṃ samatājñānamiṣyate |
body.translated_text: That equality knowledge which was attained by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> at the times of direct realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) — through the purity of cultivation, for one who has attained awakening abiding in non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), it is accepted as equality knowledge.

children.translated_text: Through great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), it is considered to accompany all times,
displaying Buddha-images to beings according to their dispositions. // AMsa_9.71 //

body.text: mahāmaitrīkaruṇābhyāṃ sarvakālānugaṃ yathādhimokṣaṃ ca satvānāṃ buddhabimbanidarśakaṃ | yataḥ kecit satvās tathāgataṃ nīlavarṇaṃ paśyanti kecit pītavarṇam ity evamādi |
body.translated_text: Through great loving-kindness and compassion, it accompanies all times and displays Buddha-images to beings according to their dispositions (<s>adhimokṣa</s>). For some beings see the <s>Tathāgata</s> as blue-colored, some as yellow-colored, and so forth.

children.translated_text: Discriminating knowledge, in respect to knowable objects, is always unobstructed;

children.text: dhāraṇīnāṃ samādhīnāṃ nidhānopamam eva ca || AMsa_9.72 ||
children.translated_text: and it is like a treasury of <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions) and <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). // AMsa_9.72 //
In the circle of the assembly, it displays all powers;
it cuts through all doubts and causes the great <s>Dharma</s> rain to fall. // AMsa_9.73 //
