body.translated_text: Discriminating knowledge is as stated in the verses.

children.translated_text: Duty-accomplishing knowledge, through emanations in all realms,
diverse, immeasurable, and inconceivable, accomplishes the welfare of all beings. // AMsa_9.74 //

body.text: kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñānaṃ sarvalokadhātuṣu nirmāṇair nānāprakārair aprameyair acintyaiś ca sarvasatvārthakaraṃ |
body.translated_text: Duty-accomplishing knowledge (<s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s>) accomplishes the welfare of all beings in all world-realms through emanations of various kinds, immeasurable and inconceivable.

children.translated_text: By the varieties of duty-accomplishment, by number, by realm, and always,

children.text: acintyaṃ buddhanirmāṇaṃ vijñeyaṃ tac ca sarvathā || AMsa_9.75 ||
children.translated_text: Buddha-emanation is to be understood as inconceivable in every way. // AMsa_9.75 //

body.text: tac ca buddhanirmāṇaṃ sadā sarvathā cācintyaṃ veditavyaṃ | kṛtyakriyābhedataḥ saṃkhyātakṣetrataś ca |
body.translated_text: That Buddha-emanation should be understood as always inconceivable in every way — in terms of the varieties of duty-accomplishment and in terms of number and realm.

children.translated_text: From retention, from equanimity, from right teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>,
and from duty-accomplishment — the arising of the four knowledges. // AMsa_9.76 //

body.text: tatra dhāraṇāt śrutānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ | samacittatā sarvasatveṣv ātmaparasamatayā | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | buddhānekatvāpṛthaktve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'from retention' — of the heard <s>dharmas</s>. 'Equanimity' — toward all beings, through the equality of self and other. The rest is self-evident. A verse on the non-plurality and non-separateness of <s>Buddhas</s>:

children.translated_text: Because of the diversity of lineages, because of non-futility, because of completeness, and because of beginninglessness,
there is not a single Buddhahood, and yet there is multiplicity in the stainless basis. // AMsa_9.77 //

body.text: eka eva buddha ity etann eṣyate | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | gotrabhedāt | anantā hi buddhagotrāḥ satvāḥ | tatraika evābhisaṃbuddho nānye 'bhisaṃbhotsyanta iti | kuta etat | puṇyajñānasaṃbhāravaiyarthyaṃ ca syād anyeṣāṃ bodhisatvānām anabhisaṃbodhān na ca yuktaṃ vaiyarthyaṃ | tasmād avaiyarthyād api naika eva buddhaḥ satvārthakriyāsākalyaṃ ca na syāt | buddhasya buddhatve kasyacit apratiṣṭhāpanād etac ca na yuktaṃ | na ca kaścid ādibuddho 'sti vinā saṃbhāreṇa buddhatvāyogād vinā cānyena buddhena saṃsthānāyogād ity anāditvād apy eko buddho na yuktaḥ | bahutvam api neṣyate buddhānāṃ dharmakāyasyābhedād anāsrave dhātau | buddhatvopāyapraveśe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'There is only one <s>Buddha</s>' — this is considered. What is the reason? Because of the diversity of lineages. For beings of Buddha-lineage are infinite. If only one had attained full awakening and the others would not attain it — how so? The accumulation of merit and knowledge of other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> would become futile through their non-awakening, and futility is not reasonable. Therefore, because of non-futility, there is not a single <s>Buddha</s>. And the completeness of accomplishing the welfare of beings would not exist — because in the Buddhahood of one <s>Buddha</s>, [if] someone were not established [in awakening], that too is not reasonable. Nor is there a first <s>Buddha</s>, because Buddhahood is impossible without accumulations, and because without another <s>Buddha</s>, establishment is impossible — thus, because of beginninglessness, a single <s>Buddha</s> is not reasonable. Multiplicity too is not accepted for the <s>Buddhas</s>, because of the non-differentiation of the <s>dharmakāya</s> in the undefiled realm. On the means of entry into Buddhahood, four verses:

children.translated_text: That which is non-existence is itself the supreme existence;

children.text: sarvathā 'nupalambhaś ca upalambhaḥ paro mataḥ || AMsa_9.78 ||
children.translated_text: and complete non-apprehension is considered the supreme apprehension. // AMsa_9.78 //

body.text: yā parikalpitena svabhāvenāvidyamānatā saiva paramā vidyamānatā pariniṣpannena svabhāvena | yaś ca sarvathā 'nupalambhaḥ parikalpitasya svabhāvasya sa eva parama upalambhaḥ pariniṣpannasvabhāvasya |
body.translated_text: That which is non-existence by the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>) is itself the supreme existence by the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>). And that which is the complete non-apprehension of the imagined nature is itself the supreme apprehension of the perfected nature.

children.translated_text: The supreme cultivation is the effort of those who do not see cultivation;

children.text: pratilambhaḥ paraś ceṣṭaḥ pratilambhaṃ ca paśyatām || AMsa_9.79 ||
children.translated_text: and the supreme attainment is the effort of those who see attainment. // AMsa_9.79 //

body.text: saiva paramā bhāvanā yo bhāvanāyā anupalambhaḥ | sa eva paramaḥ pratilambho yaḥ pratilambhānupalambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: That itself is the supreme cultivation which is the non-apprehension of cultivation. That itself is the supreme attainment which is the non-apprehension of attainment.

children.text: paśyatāṃ gurutvaṃ tāṃ dīrghaṃ nimittaṃ vīryam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: For those who see its magnitude, its duration, its sign, and their own effort,

children.text: mānināṃ bodhisatvānāṃ dūre bodhir nirūpyate || AMsa_9.80 ||
children.translated_text: for such conceited <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, awakening is declared to be far away. // AMsa_9.80 //

body.text: ye ca gurutvaṃ bahutvaṃ paśyanti adbhutadharmayuktaṃ | dīrghaṃ ca kālaṃ paśyanti tatsamudāgamāya | nimittaṃ na paśyanti cittālambanaṃ | ātmanaś ca vīryaṃ vayam ārabdhavīryā
body.translated_text: Those who see the magnitude — the abundance — as endowed with wondrous qualities; who see the time as long for its attainment; who do not see the sign — the mental object; and who [see] their own effort — 'we who have exerted effort

body.text: buddhatvaṃ prāpsyāma iti | teṣām evaṃ mānināṃ bodhisatvānām aupalambhikatvāt dūre bodhir nirūpyate |
body.translated_text: shall attain Buddhahood' — for such conceited <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, because of their apprehending nature, awakening is declared to be far away.

children.translated_text: For those who see all this as stated to be mere conceptualization,
for non-conceptualizing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, awakening is declared to have been attained. // AMsa_9.81 //

body.text: kalpanāmātraṃ tv etat sarvam iti paśyatāṃ tasyāpi kalpanāmātrasyāvikalpanād akalpabodhisatvānām anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāvasthāyām arthataḥ prāptaiva bodhir ity ucyate | buddhānām anyonya naikakāryatve catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: But for those who see all this as mere conceptualization, and who do not even conceptualize that mere conceptualization — for such non-conceptualizing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, at the stage of attaining the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>), awakening is in fact said to have been attained. On the non-separate activity of <s>Buddhas</s> among themselves, four verses:

children.text: bhinnāśrayā bhinnajalāś ca nadyaḥ alpodakāḥ kṛtyapṛthaktvakāryāḥ |
children.translated_text: Rivers with separate beds and separate waters, with little water, producing separate effects,
enjoyable only by creatures dwelling in the water, are those that have not yet entered the ocean. // AMsa_9.82 //

children.text: samudraviṣṭāś ca bhavanti sarvā ekāśrayā ekamahājalāś ca |
children.translated_text: But having entered the ocean, they all become of one bed and one great water,

children.text: miśraikakāryāś ca mahopabhogyā jalāśritaprāṇigaṇasya nityam || AMsa_9.83 ||
children.translated_text: mixed, producing a single effect, and always greatly enjoyable by the multitudes of creatures dwelling in the water. // AMsa_9.83 //

children.text: bhinnāśrayā bhinnamatāś ca dhīrāḥ svalpāvabodhāḥ pṛthagātmakṛtyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Wise ones with separate bases and separate views, with little understanding, each performing their own tasks,
enjoyable by only a few beings, are those who have not yet entered Buddhahood. // AMsa_9.84 //

children.text: buddhatvaviṣṭāś ca bhavanti sarve ekāśrayā ekamahāvabodhāḥ |
children.translated_text: But having entered Buddhahood, they all become of one basis, one great awakening,

children.text: miśrekakāryāś ca mahopabhogyāḥ sadā mahāsatvagaṇasya te hi || AMsa_9.85 ||
children.translated_text: mixed, producing a single effect, and always greatly enjoyable by the multitudes of great beings. // AMsa_9.85 //

body.text: tatra bhinnāśraya nadyaḥ svabhājanabhedāt | kṛtyapṛthaktvakāryāḥ pṛthaktvena kṛtyakaraṇāt | tanūpabhogyā ity alpānām upabhogyāḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | buddhatvaprotsahane ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'with separate beds' — rivers, because of the differentiation of their own receptacles. 'Producing separate effects' — because of producing effects separately. 'Enjoyable only by few' — enjoyable by only a few. The rest is self-evident. A verse on the encouragement toward Buddhahood:

children.translated_text: Thus, because of the connection with incomparable pure <s>dharmas</s>, because the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage) is the cause of benefit and happiness,

children.text: śubhaparamasukhākṣayākaratvāt śubhamatir arhati bodhicittam āptum || AMsa_9.86 ||
children.translated_text: and because it produces beautiful, supreme, inexhaustible happiness, one of virtuous mind is worthy of generating <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). // AMsa_9.86 //

body.text: nirupamaśulkadharmayogāt svārthasaṃpattitaḥ | hitasukhahetutvāc ca buddhatvasya parārthasaṃpattiḥ | anavadyotkṛṣṭākṣayasukhākaratvāc ca sukhavihāro viśeṣataḥ | buddhimān ahīnabodhicittam ādātuṃ tatpraṇidhānaparigrahāt |
body.translated_text: Because of the connection with incomparable pure <s>dharmas</s> — that is the attainment of one's own purpose. Because Buddhahood is the cause of benefit and happiness — that is the attainment of others' purpose. Because it produces blameless, supreme, inexhaustible happiness — that is the excellent abiding, in particular. The wise one should take up the unhesitant <s>bodhicitta</s> through the embrace of that aspiration.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, this is the ninth [chapter], the chapter on awakening (<s>bodhyadhikāra</s>).

CHAPTER X
The tenth chapter.

children.translated_text: <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse):

children.text: ādiḥ siddhiḥ śaraṇaṃ gotraṃ citte tathaiva cotpādaḥ |
children.translated_text: Beginning, accomplishment, refuge, lineage, and likewise in the mind, arising,
one's own and others' purpose, the meaning of reality, power, ripening, and awakening. // AMsa_10.1 //

body.text: eṣa ca bodhyadhikāra ādim ārabhya yāvat bodhipaṭalānusāreṇānugantavyaḥ | adhimuktiprabhedalakṣaṇavibhāge ślokau |
body.translated_text: This chapter on awakening should be followed from the beginning up to the chapter on <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), in accordance with the sequence of chapters. On the division of the characteristics of types of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), two verses:

children.text: jātājātā grāhikā grāhyabhūtā mitrādāttā svātmato bhrāntikā ca |
children.translated_text: Arisen, not arisen, apprehending, being the object of apprehension, received from a spiritual friend (<s>mitra</s>), from oneself, erroneous,

children.text: abhrāntānyā āmukhā naiva cānyā ghoṣācārā caiṣikā cekṣikā ca || AMsa_10.2 ||
children.translated_text: unerring, another kind, direct, and not direct, based on hearing, investigative, and contemplative. // AMsa_10.2 //

body.text: jātā atītapratyutpannā | ajātā anāgatā | grāhikā ādhyātmikī yayālambanam adhimucyate | grāhyabhūtā bāhyā yānālambanatvenādhimucyate | mitrādāttā audārikī | svātmataḥ sūkṣmā | bhrāntikā hīnā viparītādhimokṣāt | abhrāntikā praśāntā | āmukhā antike samavahitapratyayatvāt | anāmukhā dūre viparyayāt | ghoṣācārā śrutamayī | eṣikā cintāmayī | īkṣikā bhāvanāmayī pratyavekṣaṇāt |
body.translated_text: 'Arisen' — past and present. 'Not arisen' — future. 'Apprehending' — internal, by which one applies faith to an object. 'Being the object of apprehension' — external, that toward which one applies faith as the object of a vehicle. 'Received from a spiritual friend' — coarse. 'From oneself' — subtle. 'Erroneous' — inferior, because of perverted aspiration. 'Unerring' — peaceful. 'Direct' — nearby, because of the proximity of the cause of composure. 'Not direct' — distant, due to the opposite. 'Based on hearing' — born of learning (<s>śrutamayī</s>). 'Investigative' — born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī</s>). 'Contemplative' — born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī</s>), because of contemplation.

children.text: hāryā kīrṇā 'vyāvakīrṇā vipakṣair hīnodārā āvṛtā 'nāvṛtā ca |
children.translated_text: Shakeable, mixed, unmixed with opponents, inferior, superior, obscured, unobscured,

children.text: yuktā 'yuktā saṃbhṛtā 'saṃbhṛtā ca gāḍhaṃ viṣṭā dūragā cādhimuktiḥ || AMsa_10.3 ||
children.translated_text: engaged, disengaged, equipped, unequipped, deeply entered, and far-reaching — such is aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>). // AMsa_10.3 //

body.text: hāryā mṛdvī | vyavakīrṇā madhyā | avyavakīrṇā vipakṣair adhimātrā | hīnā'nyayāne | udārā mahāyāne | āvṛtā sāvaraṇā viśeṣagamanāya | anāvṛtā nirāvaraṇā | yuktā sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogāt | ayuktā tadvirahitā | saṃbhṛtādhigamayogyā |
body.translated_text: 'Shakeable' — weak. 'Mixed' — middling. 'Unmixed with opponents' — intense. 'Inferior' — in another vehicle. 'Superior' — in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. 'Obscured' — having obscurations, preventing progress to higher stages. 'Unobscured' — without obscurations. 'Engaged' — because of continuous and respectful application. 'Disengaged' — lacking that. 'Equipped' — suitable for realization.

body.text: asaṃbhṛtā viparyayāt | gāḍhaṃ viṣṭā bhūmipraviṣṭā | dūragā pariśiṣṭāsu bhūmiṣu | adhimuktiparipanthe trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Unequipped' — due to the opposite. 'Deeply entered' — entered into the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). 'Far-reaching' — in the remaining stages. On the obstacles to aspiration, three verses:

children.translated_text: Abundance of inattention, laziness, deviation from practice,
bad friends, weakness in the wholesome, and improper mental application. (AMsa 10.4)

body.text: jātāyā amanasikārabāhulyaṃ paripanthaḥ | ajātāyāḥ kauśīdyaṃ grāhyagrāhakabhūtāyā yogavibhramas tathaivābhiniveśāt | mitrādāttāyāḥ kumitraṃ viparītagrāhaṇāt | svātmato 'dhimukteḥ kuśalamūladaurbalyaṃ | abhrāntāyā ayoniśo amanasikāraḥ paripanthas tadvirodhitvāt |
body.translated_text: For conviction that has arisen, abundance of inattention (<s>amanasikāra</s>) is the obstacle. For conviction that has not arisen, laziness (<s>kauśīdya</s>). For that which pertains to the apprehended and the apprehender, deviation from practice (<s>yogavibhrama</s>), due to clinging to precisely that. For that obtained from friends, bad friends (<s>kumitra</s>), due to wrong apprehension. For conviction in oneself, weakness of wholesome roots. For that which is non-erroneous, improper mental application is the obstacle, since it is contrary to that.

children.translated_text: Heedlessness, being of little learning, contentment with mere hearing and thinking,
pride in mere tranquility, and likewise unfamiliarity — these are regarded as obstacles. (AMsa 10.5)

body.text: āmukhāyāḥ pramādas tasyā apramādakṛtatvāt | ghoṣācārāyā alpaśrutatvaṃ nītārthasūtrāntāśravaṇāt | eṣikāyāḥ śrutamātrasaṃtuṣṭatvam alpacintāsaṃtuṣṭatvaṃ ca | īkṣikāyāś cintāmātrasaṃtuṣṭatvaṃ śamathamātrābhimānaś ca | hāryāvyavakīrṇayor aparijayaḥ paripanthaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the introductory conviction, heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), since it is produced by non-heedlessness. For conviction based on hearing, being of little learning, due to not hearing sūtras of definitive meaning. For the probing conviction, contentment with mere hearing and contentment with little thinking. For the examining conviction, contentment with mere thinking and pride in mere <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility). For the conquerable and the undisturbed convictions, unfamiliarity is the obstacle.

children.translated_text: Non-dismay, and likewise dismay, obstruction, and also unsuitability,
and non-accumulation — these should be known as the obstacles to conviction. (AMsa 10.6)

body.text: hīnāyā anudvegaḥ saṃsārāt | udārāyā udvegaḥ | anāvṛtāyāś cāvṛttiḥ | yuktāyā ayuktatā | saṃbhṛtāyā asaṃbhṛtiḥ paripanthaḥ | adhimuktāv anuśaṃse pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: For the inferior conviction, non-dismay regarding <s>saṃsāra</s>. For the noble conviction, dismay. For the unobstructed conviction, obstruction. For the engaged conviction, unsuitability. For the well-equipped conviction, non-accumulation is the obstacle. Regarding the advantages of conviction, five verses:

children.translated_text: Great merit, freedom from remorse, happiness of mind, great bliss,

children.text: avipraṇāśaḥ sthairyaṃ ca viśeṣagamanaṃ tathā || AMsa_10.7 ||
children.translated_text: non-loss, stability, and likewise progression to distinction. (AMsa 10.7)
Realization of the <s>Dharma</s>, and then supreme attainment of one's own and others' welfare,
and swift attainment of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) — these are the advantages arising from conviction. (AMsa 10.8)

body.text: jātāyāṃ pratyutpannāyāṃ puṇyaṃ mahat | atītāyām akaukṛtyam avipratisārāt | grāhikāyāṃ grāhyabhūtāyāṃ ca mahatsaumanasyaṃ samādhiyogāt | kalyāṇamitrajanitāyām avipraṇāśaḥ | svayam adhimuktau sthairyaṃ | bhrāntikāyāmāmukhāyāṃ śrutamayādikāyāṃ ca yāvat madhyāyāṃ viśeṣagamanaṃ | adhimātrāyāṃ dharmābhisamayaḥ | hīnāyāṃ svārthaprāptiḥ | udārāyāṃ parārthaprāptiḥ paramā | anāvṛtayuktasaṃbhṛtādiṣu śulkapakṣāsu kṣiprābhijñatvam anuśaṃsaḥ |
body.translated_text: When conviction has arisen and is present, there is great merit. When it is past, freedom from remorse, due to absence of regret. When it pertains to the apprehender and the apprehended, great happiness of mind, through the practice of <s>samādhi</s>. When produced by good friends, non-loss. When conviction is in oneself, stability. When it is the erroneous, introductory, hearing-based, and so on up to the middling conviction, progression to distinction. When it is the highest degree, realization of the <s>Dharma</s>. When it is inferior, attainment of one's own welfare. When it is noble, supreme attainment of others' welfare. In the unobstructed, engaged, well-equipped, and other white-side convictions, swift attainment of <s>abhijñā</s> is the advantage.

children.translated_text: For the desirous, that conviction is like a dog; for those in <s>samādhi</s>, it is like a tortoise;

children.text: bhṛtyopamā svārthināṃ sā rājaprakhyā parārthinām || AMsa_10.9 ||
children.translated_text: for those seeking their own welfare, it is like a servant; for those seeking others' welfare, it is like a king. (AMsa 10.9)

body.text: yathā śvā duḥkhārtaḥ satatam avitṛptaḥ kṣudhitako yathā kūrmaś cāsau jalavivarake saṃkucitakaḥ | yathā bhṛtyo nityam upacakitamūrtir vicarati | yathā rājā rājñāṃ viṣaye vaśavartī viharati |
body.translated_text: Just as a dog, afflicted with suffering, always unsatisfied, is hungry; just as a tortoise contracts into a hole in the water; just as a servant always moves about with a frightened body; just as a king of kings dwells exercising mastery in his domain —

children.text: tathā kāmisthātṛsvaparajanakṛtyārtham udite viśeṣo vijñeyaḥ satatam adhimuktayā vividhayā |
children.translated_text: so too, when conviction of various kinds arises for the sake of the actions of the desirous, the stable, and those working for self and others, the distinction should be understood;

children.text: mahāyāne tasya vidhivad iha matvā paramatāṃ bhṛśaṃ tasmin dhīraḥ satatam iha tām eva vṛṇuyāt || AMsa_10.10 ||
children.translated_text: having understood the supremacy of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> here in the proper manner, the steadfast one should constantly choose that very conviction most intensely. (AMsa 10.10)

body.text: api khalu kāminām adhimuktiḥ śvasadṛśī laukikasamādhigatānāṃ kūrmaprakhyā svārthavatāṃ bhṛtyopamā | rājaprakhyā parārthavatāṃ | etam evārthaṃ pareṇopapādya mahāyānādhimuktau samādāpayati | adhimuktilayapratiṣedhe ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Indeed, the conviction of the desirous is like a dog; that of those who have attained worldly <s>samādhi</s> is like a tortoise; that of those concerned with their own welfare is like a servant; that of those concerned with others' welfare is like a king. Having demonstrated this very meaning by the following verse, he encourages conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Regarding the prevention of the decline of conviction, verses:

children.translated_text: Beings who are human attain <s>saṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening) at every moment;

children.text: aprameyā yataḥ satvā layaṃ nāto 'dhivāsayet || AMsa_10.11 ||
children.translated_text: since beings are immeasurable, one should therefore not tolerate decline. (AMsa 10.11)

body.text:
tribhiḥ kāraṇair layo na yuktaḥ | yato manuṣabhūtā bodhiṃ prāpnuvanti | nityaṃ prāpnuvanti | aprameyāś ca prāpnuvanti |
adhimuktipuṇyaviśeṣaṇe dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text:
Decline is not proper for three reasons: because those who are human attain awakening; because they always attain it; and because immeasurable numbers attain it.
Regarding the distinction of the merit of conviction, two verses:

children.text: yathā puṇyaṃ prasavate pareṣāṃ bhojanaṃ dadat |
children.translated_text: Just as one generates merit by giving food to others,

children.text: na tu svayaṃ sa bhuñjānas tathā puṇyamahodayaḥ || AMsa_10.12 ||
children.translated_text: but not by eating it oneself — so too there is a great arising of merit. (AMsa 10.12)
That which is stated in the sūtras is obtained from the <s>Dharma</s> taught as having others' welfare as its basis,

children.text: na tu svārthāśrayād dharmād deśitād upalabhyate || AMsa_10.13 ||
children.translated_text: but it is not obtained from the <s>Dharma</s> taught as having one's own welfare as its basis. (AMsa 10.13)

body.text: yathā bhojanaṃ dadataḥ puṇyam utpadyate parārthādhikārāt | na tu svayaṃ bhuñjānasya svārthādhikārāt | evaṃ parārthāśrayadeśitāt mahāyānadharmāt teṣu teṣu sūtreṣūktaḥ puṇyodayo mahāṃl labhyate | na tu svārthāśrayadeśitāt śrāvakayānadharmāt | adhimuktiphalaparigrahe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as merit arises for one who gives food, due to engagement in others' welfare, but not for one who eats it oneself, due to engagement in one's own welfare — so too, from the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s> taught as having others' welfare as its basis, the great arising of merit stated in those various sūtras is obtained; but not from the <s>Śrāvakayāna Dharma</s> taught as having one's own welfare as its basis. Regarding the comprehension of the fruit of conviction, a verse:

children.text: iti vipulagatau mahoghamahāryadharme janiya sadā matimān mahādhimuktim |
children.translated_text: Thus, having always generated great conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>, which is of vast scope and of noble, mighty flood,

children.text: vipulasatatapuṇyatadvivṛddhiṃ vrajati guṇair asamair mahātmatāṃ ca || AMsa_10.14 ||
children.translated_text: the wise one attains vast and constant growth of merit and its increase, and greatness of self through incomparable qualities. (AMsa 10.14)

body.text: yatra yādṛśyādhimuktyā yo yatphalaṃ parigṛhlāti | vistīrṇe mahāyānadharme 'pariṇīyayodārādhimuktyā matimān trividhaṃ phalaṃ parigṛhṇāti | vipulapuṇyavṛddhiṃ tasyā evādhimukter vṛddhiṃ taddhetukāṃ cātulyaguṇamahātmatāṃ buddhatvaṃ |
body.translated_text: Where, by what kind of conviction, one comprehends what fruit: in the extensive <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>, by noble conviction that is irrevocable, the wise one comprehends a threefold fruit — vast growth of merit, the growth of that very conviction, and, caused by that, greatness of self through incomparable qualities, which is <s>Buddhahood</s>.
The section on conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>) is the tenth in the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>.

CHAPTER XI
Eleventh Section
Regarding the section on seeking the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaparyeṣṭi</s>): in the seeking of the object of support, four verses:

children.text: piṭakatrayaṃ dvayaṃ vā saṃgrahataḥ kāraṇair navabhir iṣṭam |
children.translated_text: The three baskets — or two, in summary — are desired for nine reasons;
through habituation, awakening, pacification, and penetration, they liberate. (AMsa 11.1)

body.text: piṭakatrayaṃ sūtravinayābhidharmāḥ | tad eva trayaṃ hīnayānāgrayānabhedena dvayaṃ bhavati | śrāvakapiṭakaṃ bodhisatvapiṭakaṃ ca | tatpunas trayaṃ dvayaṃ vā kenārthena piṭakam ity āha | saṃgrahataḥ sarvajñeyārthasaṃgrahād veditavyaṃ | kena kāraṇena trayaṃ | navabhiḥ kāraṇair vicikitsāpratipakṣeṇa sūtraṃ yo yatrārthe saṃśayitas tasya tanniścayārthaṃ deśanāt | antadvayānuyogapratipakṣeṇa vinayaḥ sāvadyaparibhogapratiṣedhataḥ kāmasukhallikānuyogāntasyānavadyaparibhogānujñānata ātmaklamathānuyogāntasya | svayaṃdṛṣṭiparāmarṣapratipakṣeṇābhidharmo 'viparītadharmalakṣaṇābhidyotanāt |
body.translated_text: The three baskets are the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Abhidharma</s>. Those same three, divided into the <s>Hīnayāna</s> and the supreme vehicle, become two: the <s>Śrāvaka</s> basket and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> basket. For what purpose are those three or two called 'baskets'? He says: 'in summary' — because they gather all knowable meanings. For what reason are they three? For nine reasons: the <s>Sūtra</s> serves as the antidote to doubt — because for whoever is in doubt about any meaning, it teaches for the purpose of resolving that doubt. The <s>Vinaya</s> serves as the antidote to pursuit of the two extremes — through prohibition of blameworthy enjoyment, the extreme of pursuit of sensual pleasure, and through permission of blameless enjoyment, the extreme of self-mortification. The <s>Abhidharma</s> serves as the antidote to clinging to one's own views — because it illuminates the non-erroneous characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: punaḥ śikṣātrayadeśanā sūtreṇa adhiśīlādhicittasaṃpādanatā vinayena śīlavato 'vipratisārādavipratisāreṇa samādhilābhāt | adhiprajñāsaṃpādanābhidharmeṇāviparītārthapravicayāt | punar dharmārthadeśanā sūtreṇa | dharmārthaniṣpattirvinayena kleśavinayasaṃyuktasasya tayoḥ prativedhāt | dharmārthasāṃkathyaviniścayakauśalyam abhidharmeṇeti | ebhir nabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ piṭakatrayam iṣṭaṃ | tac ca saṃsārād vimocanārthaṃ | kathaṃ punas tad vimocayati | vāsanabodhaśamanaprativedhais tad vimocayati | śrutena cittavāsanataḥ | cintayā bodhanataḥ | bhāvanayā śamathena śamanataḥ | vipaśyanayā prativedhataḥ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Sūtra</s> teaches the threefold training; the <s>Vinaya</s> accomplishes higher morality and higher mind — because for one who is moral, from absence of regret comes the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>; the <s>Abhidharma</s> accomplishes higher wisdom — through non-erroneous analysis of meaning. Furthermore, the <s>Sūtra</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning; the <s>Vinaya</s> accomplishes the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning — through penetration of both, being connected with the discipline of afflictions; the <s>Abhidharma</s> provides skill in the discussion and determination of the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning. By these nine reasons, the three baskets are desired. And they are for the purpose of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>. How then do they liberate? Through habituation, awakening, pacification, and penetration, they liberate: through hearing, from habituating the mind; through thinking, from awakening; through meditation, by <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility), from pacification; through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), from penetration.

children.translated_text: The <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Abhidharma</s>, and <s>Vinaya</s> are regarded as having fourfold meaning in summary;

children.text: teṣāṃ jñānād dhīmān sarvākārajñatām eti || AMsa_11.2 ||
children.translated_text: through knowledge of them, the wise one attains omniscience in all its aspects. (AMsa 11.2)

body.text: te ca sūtravinayābhidharmāḥ pratyekaṃ caturvidhārthāḥ samāsatas teṣāṃ jñānād bodhisatvaḥ sarvajñatāṃ prāpnoti | śrāvakas tv ekasyā api gāthāyā artham ājñāyāsravakṣyaṃ prāpnoti |
body.translated_text: Those <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Abhidharma</s> each have fourfold meaning; through knowledge of them in summary, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains omniscience. A <s>Śrāvaka</s>, however, even by understanding the meaning of a single verse, attains the destruction of outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>).

children.text: āśrayato lakṣaṇato dharmād arthāc ca sūcanāt sūtram |
children.translated_text: From the standpoint of basis, characteristic, <s>dharma</s>, and meaning — from indicating these, it is <s>Sūtra</s>;
from confrontation, from frequency, from overcoming, and from approach — it is <s>Abhidharma</s>. (AMsa 11.3)

body.text: kathaṃ pratyekaṃ caturvidhārthaḥ | āśrayakṣaṇadharmārthasūcanāt sūtraṃ | tatrāśrayo yatra deśe deśitaṃ yena yasmai ca | lakṣaṇaṃ saṃvṛtisatyalakṣaṇaṃ paramārthasatyalakṣaṇaṃ ca | dharmāḥ skandhāyatanadhātvāhārapratītyasamutpādādayaḥ | artho 'nusaṃdhiḥ | abhimukhatvād abhīkṣṇatvād abhibhavanād abhigamanāc cābhidharmo veditavyaḥ | nirvāṇābhimukho dharmo 'bhidharmaḥ satyabodhipakṣavimokṣamukhādideśanāt | abhīkṣṇaṃ dharmo 'bhidharma ekaikasya dharmasya rūpyarūpisanidarśanādiprabhedena bahulanirdeśāt | abhibhavatīty abhidharmaḥ parapravādābhibhavanād vivādādhikaraṇādibhiḥ | abhigamyate sūtrārtha etenety abhidharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: How does each have fourfold meaning? The <s>Sūtra</s>, from indicating basis, characteristic, <s>dharma</s>, and meaning. There, 'basis' means the place where it was taught, by whom, and to whom. 'Characteristic' means the characteristic of conventional truth and the characteristic of ultimate truth. '<s>Dharmas</s>' are the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), nutriments (<s>āhāra</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), and so forth. 'Meaning' is the connected purport. The <s>Abhidharma</s> should be understood from confrontation, frequency, overcoming, and approach. A <s>dharma</s> that confronts <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is <s>Abhidharma</s> — through the teaching of truths, wings of awakening, doors of liberation, and so forth. A <s>dharma</s> treated repeatedly is <s>Abhidharma</s> — because each individual <s>dharma</s> is expounded extensively through distinctions such as material/immaterial, visible/invisible, and so forth. That which overcomes is <s>Abhidharma</s> — because it overcomes rival doctrines through debates, adjudications, and so forth. That by which the meaning of the <s>Sūtra</s> is approached is <s>Abhidharma</s>.

children.text: āpatter utthānād vyutthānān niḥsṛteś ca vinayatvam |
children.translated_text: From offense, from arising, from emergence, and from escape — this constitutes <s>Vinaya</s>;
and from the standpoint of the person, from establishment, from classification, and from determination. (AMsa 11.4)

body.text: āpattitaḥ samutthānato vyutthānato niḥsaraṇataś ca veditavyaḥ | tatrāpattiḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Vinaya</s> should be understood from offense, arising, emergence, and escape. There, 'offense' (<s>āpatti</s>)

body.text: pañcāpattinikāyāḥ | samutthānam āpattīnām ajñānāt pramādāt kleśaprācuryādanādarāc ca | vyutthānam āśayato na daṇḍakarmataḥ | niḥsaraṇaṃ saptavidhaṃ | pratideśanā | abhyupagamaḥ śikṣādattakādīnāṃ daṇḍakarmaṇaḥ | samavadyotaḥ prajñapte śikṣāpade punaḥ paryāyeṇa | ajñānāt prasrabdhiḥ samagreṇa saṃghena śikṣāpadastha pratiprasrambhaṇāt | āśrayaparivṛttir bhikṣubhikṣuṇyoḥ strīpuruṣavyañjanaparivartanād asādhāraṇā vedāpattiḥ | bhūtapratyavekṣā dharmoddānākaraiḥ pratyavekṣāviśeṣaḥ | dharmatāpratilambhaś ca satyadarśanena kṣudrānukṣudrāpannābhāve dharmapratilambhāt | punaś caturvidhenārthena vinayo veditavyaḥ | pudgalato yam āgamya śikṣā prajñapyate | prajñaptito yadā 'rocite pudgalāparādhe śāstā saṃnipātya saṃghaśikṣāṃ prajñāpayati | pravibhāgato yaḥ prajñapte śikṣāpade tad uddeśasya vibhāgaḥ | viniścayataś ca tatrāpattiḥ kathaṃ bhavaty anāpattir veti nirdhāraṇāt | ālambanalābhaparyeṣṭau trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: comprises the five classes of offenses. 'Arising' is the arising of offenses — from ignorance, from heedlessness, from preponderance of afflictions, and from disrespect. 'Emergence' is by intention, not by punitive action. 'Escape' is sevenfold: confession (<s>pratideśanā</s>); acceptance of punitive action for those who have taken the training rules and so forth; re-illumination — when in an established training rule, again through another occasion; relaxation due to ignorance — when the complete <s>Saṃgha</s> relaxes a training rule for one who has transgressed; transformation of the basis — the uncommon offense of monks and nuns through the interchange of female and male characteristics; examination of reality — the special examination through the patterns, summaries, and forms of the <s>Dharma</s>; and attainment of the nature of <s>dharmas</s> — through seeing the truths, when there is no transgression of minor rules, from the attainment of the <s>Dharma</s>. Furthermore, the <s>Vinaya</s> should be understood through fourfold meaning: from the person — in dependence upon whom the training rule is established; from establishment — when, upon a person's offense being reported, the Teacher, having assembled the <s>Saṃgha</s>, establishes the training rule; from classification — the analysis of the recitation of that established training rule; and from determination — through deciding how an offense occurs or does not occur in that case. Regarding the seeking of the attainment of the object, three verses:

children.text: ālambanaṃ mato dharmaḥ ādhyātmaṃ bāhyakaṃ dvayam |
children.translated_text: The object is regarded as the <s>dharma</s>: internal, external, and the dyad;

children.text: lābho dvayor dvayārthena dvayoś cānupalambhataḥ || AMsa_11.5 ||
children.translated_text: attainment of both is by the meaning of the dyad, and of both by non-apprehension. (AMsa 11.5)

body.text: ..... bāhyam ādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ ca | tatra grāhakabhūtaṃ kāyādikamādhyātmikaṃ grāhyabhūtaṃ bāhyaṃ tayor eva tathatādvayaṃ | tatra dvayor ādhyātmikabāhyayor ālambanayor dvayārthena lābho yathākramaṃ | yadi grāhyārthād grāhakārtham abhinnaṃ paśyati grāhakārthāc ca grāhyārthaṃ dvayasya punaḥ samastasyādhyātmikabāhyālambanasya tathatāyā lābhas tayor eva dvayor anupalambhād veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: ...the external, the internal, and the external — and the dyad of those very two as their <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). There, the attainment of both internal and external objects is by the meaning of the dyad, respectively: when one sees the apprehender-meaning as undifferentiated from the apprehended-meaning, and the apprehended-meaning from the apprehender-meaning. The attainment of the <s>tathatā</s> of those same two, the internal and external objects as a whole, should be understood from the non-apprehension of those very two.

children.translated_text: Through mental discourse, from the retention of the meaning as stated, with the mind clear,

children.text: arthakhyānasya jalpāc ca nāmni sthānāc ca cetasaḥ || AMsa_11.6 ||
children.translated_text: from the declaration of meaning, from discourse, and from the mind's establishment in the name; (AMsa 11.6)
the attainment of the <s>Dharma</s>-object should come about through the three knowledges beginning with hearing;

children.text: trividhālambanalābhaś ca pūrvoktas tat samāśritaḥ || AMsa_11.7 ||
children.translated_text: and the threefold attainment of the object previously stated depends on that. (AMsa 11.7)

body.text: dharmālambanalābhaḥ punas tribhir jñānair bhavati śrutacintābhāvanāmayaiḥ | tatra samāhitena cetasā manojalpair yathoktārthaprasannasya tatpradhāraṇāt | śrutamayena jñānena tallābhaḥ manojalpair iti saṃkalpaiḥ | prasannasyety adhimuktasya niścitasya | pradhāraṇād iti pravicayāt | jalpād arthakhyānasya pradhāraṇāc cintāmayena tallābhaḥ | yadi manojalpād evāyam arthaḥ khyātīti paśyati nānyan manojalpād yathoktaṃ dvayālambanalābhe | cittasya nāmni sthānāt bhāvanāmayena jñānena tallābho veditavyo dvayānupalambhād yathoktaṃ dvayālambanalābhe | ata eva ca sa pūrvoktas trividhālambanalābho dharmālambanalābhasaṃniśrito veditavyaḥ | manasikāraparyeṣṭau pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: The attainment of <s>dharma</s> as object comes about through three kinds of knowledge: those born of hearing, reflection, and meditation. Therein, through mental discourse in a concentrated mind, for one who has gained clarity regarding the meaning as taught, through the discernment of that — through knowledge born of hearing, that attainment comes about. 'Through mental discourse' means through conceptualization. 'Of one who has gained clarity' means of one who has conviction and certainty. 'Through discernment' means through analytical investigation. Through the presentation of meaning from discourse, through discernment — through knowledge born of reflection, that attainment comes about. If one sees that this meaning appears only from mental discourse and nothing other than mental discourse, as stated regarding the attainment of the twofold object — through the mind's abiding in name, through knowledge born of meditation, that attainment should be understood, due to the non-apprehension of duality, as stated regarding the attainment of the twofold object. Therefore, that previously stated threefold attainment of objects should be understood as dependent on the attainment of <s>dharma</s> as object. On the investigation of mental attention, five verses:

children.translated_text: Pertaining to the three realms, productive of function, with a basis that is restricted, and another
that instills conviction, and another that produces intense desire. || AMsa_11.8 ||
Having a deficient or complete basis, twofold — with discourse and without discourse,
conjoined with knowledge, and having the nature of the prerequisite of <s>yoga</s> (meditative practice). || AMsa_11.9 ||
It has a combined object and a differentiated object,

children.text: pañcadhā saptadhā caiva parijñā pañcadhā 'sya ca || AMsa_11.10 ||
children.translated_text: fivefold and sevenfold respectively; and its full comprehension is fivefold. || AMsa_11.10 ||
There are four and thirty-seven aspects that have entered into meditation,
it has the nature of the twofold path, with two benefits, and is receptive. || AMsa_11.11 ||
It is applied, it is under control, it is limited, and it is of vast nature —

children.text: yogināṃ hi manaskāra eṣa sarvātmako mataḥ || AMsa_11.12 ||
children.translated_text: this mental attention of <s>yogins</s> (meditators) is considered to be comprehensive. || AMsa_11.12 ||

body.text: aṣṭādaśavidho manaskāraḥ | dhātuniyataḥ kṛtyakara āśrayavibhakto 'dhimuktiniveśakaś cchandajanakaḥ samādhisaṃniśrito jñānasaṃprayuktaḥ saṃbhinnālambano vibhinnālambanaḥ parijñāniyato bhāvanākārapraviṣṭaḥ śamathavipaśyanāmārgasvabhāvo 'nuśaṃsamanaskāraḥ pratīcchakaḥ prāyogikamanaskāro vaśavartimanaskāraḥ parīttamanaskāro vipulamanaskāraś ca | tatra dhātuniyato yaḥ śrāvakādigotraniyataḥ | kṛtyakaro yaḥ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya | āśrayavibhakto yaḥ sasaṃbādhagṛhasthāśrayo 'saṃbādhapravrajitāśrayaś ca | adhimuktiniveśako yo buddhānusmṛtisahagataḥ | cchandajanako
body.translated_text: Mental attention is of eighteen kinds: determined by realm, productive of function, differentiated by basis, instilling conviction, generating desire, dependent on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), conjoined with knowledge, having a combined object, having a differentiated object, determined by full comprehension, having entered into aspects of meditation, having the nature of the <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) paths, the mental attention of benefits, receptive, the applied mental attention, the mental attention under control, the limited mental attention, and the vast mental attention. Therein, 'determined by realm' is that which is determined by the lineage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and so forth. 'Productive of function' is that of one who has accumulated the requisites. 'Differentiated by basis' is that which has the restricted basis of the householder and the unrestricted basis of the renunciant. 'Instilling conviction' is that accompanied by the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>. 'Generating desire'

body.text: yas tat saṃpratyayasahagataḥ | samādhisaṃniśrito yaḥ samantakamaulasamādhisahagataḥ savitarkasavicāramātrāvitarkāvicārasahagataś ca | jñānasaṃprayukto yo yogopaniṣad yogasahagataḥ sa punaryathākramaṃ śrutacintāmanyo bhāvanāmayaś ca | saṃbhinnālambanaḥ pañcavidhaḥ sūtroddānagāthānipātayāvadudgṛhītayāvaddeśitālambanaḥ | vibhinnālambanaḥ saptavidho nāmālambanaḥ padālambano vyañjanālambanaḥ pudgalanairātmyālambano dharmanairātmyālambano rūpidharmālambano 'rūpidharmālambanaś ca | tatra rūpidharmālambano yaḥ kāyālambanaḥ | arūpidharmālambano yo vedanācittadharmālambanaḥ | parijñāniyato yaḥ parijñeye vastuni parijñeye 'rthe parijñāyāṃ parijñāphale tatpravedanāyāṃ ca | tatra parijñeyaṃ vastu duḥkhaṃ parijñeyo 'rthas tasyaivānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmatā | parijñā mārgaḥ | parijñāphalaṃ vimuktiḥ | tatpravedanā vimuktijñānadarśanaṃ | bhāvanākārapraviṣṭaś caturākārabhāvanaḥ saptatriṃśadākārabhāvanaś ca | tatra caturākārabhāvanaḥ pudgalanairātmyākārabhāvano dharmanairātmyākārabhāvano darśanākārabhāvano jñānākārabhāvanaś ca | tatra saptatriṃśadākārabhāvanaḥ | aśubhākārabhāvano duḥkhākārabhāvano 'nityākārabhāvano 'nātmākārabhāvanaḥ smṛtyupasthāneṣu | pratilambhākārabhāvano nisevanākārabhāvano vinirdhāvanākārabhāvanaḥ pratipakṣākārabhāvanaḥ samyakprahāṇeṣu | saṃtuṣṭiprātipakṣikamanaskārabhāvano yadā cchandaṃ janayati | vikṣepasaṃśayaprātipakṣikamanaskārabhāvano yadā vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhate yathākramaṃ | auddhatyaprātipakṣikasamādhyākārabhāvano yadā cittaṃ pradadhāti | layaprātipakṣikasamādhyākārabhāvano yadā cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | ete yathākramaṃ caturṣu ṛddhipādeṣu veditavyāḥ | sthitacittasya lokottarasaṃpattisaṃpratyayākārabhāvano yathā saṃpratyayākārabhāvana evaṃ vyavasāyākārabhāvano dharmāsaṃpramoṣākārabhāvanaś cittasthityākārabhāvanaḥ pravicayākārabhāvana indriyeṣu | eta eva pañca nirlikhitavipakṣamanaskārā baleṣu | saṃbodhisaṃprakhyānākārabhāvanas tatraiva vicayotsāhasaumanasyakarmaṇyatā cittasthitisamatākārabhāvanāḥ saptasaṃbodhyaṅgeṣu | prāptiniścayākārabhāvanaḥ parikarmabhūmisaṃrakṣaṇākārabhāvanaḥ parasaṃprāptyākārabhāvana āryakāntaśīlapraviṣṭākārabhāvanaḥ saṃlikhitavṛttisamudācārakārabhāvanaḥ pūrvaparibhāvitapratilabdhamārgābhyāsākārabhāvano dharmasthitinimittāsaṃpramoṣākārabhāvano 'nimittasthityāśrayaparivṛttyākārabhāvanaś ca mārgāṅgeṣu | śamathavipaśyanābhāvanāmārgasvabhāvayor na kaścin nirdeśaḥ | anuśaṃsamanaskāro dvividho dauṣṭhulyāpakarṣaṇo
body.translated_text: is that accompanied by trust in that. 'Dependent on <s>samādhi</s>' is that accompanied by the preliminary and principal <s>samādhi</s>, and that accompanied by states with <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), with <s>vicāra</s> only, and without either. 'Conjoined with knowledge' is that which has the prerequisite of <s>yoga</s>, accompanied by <s>yoga</s>; and this in turn should be understood as, in order, born of hearing, reflection, and meditation. 'Having a combined object' is fivefold: having as object <s>sūtras</s>, summaries, verses, interpolated texts, and whatever has been received, whatever has been taught. 'Having a differentiated object' is sevenfold: having name as object, having a word as object, having a syllable as object, having the selflessness of persons as object, having the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> as object, having material <s>dharmas</s> as object, and having immaterial <s>dharmas</s> as object. Therein, 'having material <s>dharmas</s> as object' is that which has the body as object. 'Having immaterial <s>dharmas</s> as object' is that which has feeling, mind, and mental factors as object. 'Determined by full comprehension' is that regarding the thing to be fully comprehended, the meaning to be fully comprehended, the full comprehension itself, the fruit of full comprehension, and the experience of that. Therein, the thing to be fully comprehended is suffering; the meaning to be fully comprehended is its character of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self. Full comprehension is the path. The fruit of full comprehension is liberation. Its experience is the knowledge and vision of liberation. 'Having entered into aspects of meditation' is of four aspects and of thirty-seven aspects. Therein, the meditation of four aspects comprises: the meditation on the aspect of the selflessness of persons, the meditation on the aspect of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, the meditation on the aspect of seeing, and the meditation on the aspect of knowledge. Therein, the meditation of thirty-seven aspects comprises: in the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) — meditation on the aspect of impurity, on the aspect of suffering, on the aspect of impermanence, and on the aspect of non-self; in the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions) — meditation on the aspect of attainment, on the aspect of cultivation, on the aspect of purification, and on the aspect of the antidote; meditation on the aspect of the mental attention that counteracts discontent, when one generates desire; meditation on the aspect of the mental attention that counteracts distraction and doubt, when one exerts oneself and initiates vigor, respectively; meditation on the aspect of <s>samādhi</s> that counteracts excitement, when one settles the mind; meditation on the aspect of <s>samādhi</s> that counteracts torpor, when one uplifts the mind — these should be understood as belonging, in order, to the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of spiritual power); for one whose mind is settled, meditation on the aspect of trust in supramundane attainments, and likewise meditation on the aspect of determination, on the aspect of non-forgetfulness of <s>dharmas</s>, on the aspect of stability of mind, and on the aspect of analytical investigation — these belong to the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties); these same five, with mental attention whose adversaries have been eliminated, belong to the <s>balas</s> (powers); meditation on the aspect of the discernment of awakening — therein, the meditations on the aspects of investigation, vigor, joy, pliancy, stability of mind, and equanimity belong to the seven <s>saṃbodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening); meditation on the aspect of attaining certainty, on the aspect of guarding the preparatory stage, on the aspect of the attainment by others, on the aspect of entering the discipline beloved of the noble ones, on the aspect of conduct and behavior with eliminated faults, on the aspect of practicing the path attained through previous cultivation, on the aspect of non-forgetfulness of the sign of the stability of <s>dharmas</s>, and on the aspect of the transformation of the basis through abiding in signlessness — these belong to the <s>mārgāṅgas</s> (path factors). Regarding the nature of the paths of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) meditation, no instruction is given. The mental attention of benefits is twofold: the removal of rigidity

body.text: dṛṣṭinimittāpakarṣaṇaśca | pratīcchako yo dharmasrotasi buddhabodhisatvānām antikād avavādagrāhakaḥ | prāyogikamanaskāraḥ pañcavidhaḥ samādhigocare | saṃkhyopalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena sūtrādiṣu nāmapadavyañjanasaṃkhyām upalakṣayate | vṛttyupalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena dvividhāṃ vṛttim upalakṣayate parimāṇavṛttiṃ ca vyañjanānām aparimāṇavṛttiṃ ca nāmapadayoḥ | parikalpopalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena dvayam upādāya dvayaparikalpam upalakṣayate | nāmaparikalpam upādāyārthaparikalpam arthaparikalpamupādāya nāmaparikalpam aparikalpam akṣaraṃ | kramopalakṣaṇaprāyogiko yena nāmagrahaṇapūrvikām arthagrahaṇapravṛttim upalakṣayate | prativedhaprāyogikaś ca | sa punar ekādaśavidho veditavya āgantukatvaprativedhataḥ saṃprakhyānanimittaprativedhato 'rthānupalambhaprativedhata upalambhānupalambhaprativedhato dharmadhātuprativedhataḥ pudgalanairātmyaprativedhato dharmanairātmyaprativedhato hīnāśayaprativedhata udāramāhātmyāśayaprativedhato yathādhigamadharmavyavasthānaprativedhato vyavasthāpitadharmaprativedhataś ca | vaśavartimanaskārasrividhaḥ āvaraṇasuviśuddhaḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇasuviśuddho guṇābhinirhārasuviśuddhaś ca | dharmatatvaparyeṣṭau dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: and the removal of the sign of wrong views. 'Receptive' is that which, in the stream of <s>Dharma</s>, receives instruction from <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The applied mental attention is fivefold, in the domain of <s>samādhi</s>: the application of identifying enumeration, by which one identifies the enumeration of names, words, and syllables in <s>sūtras</s> and so forth; the application of identifying activity, by which one identifies the twofold activity — the measurable activity of syllables and the immeasurable activity of names and words; the application of identifying conceptualization, by which one identifies the conceptualization of duality based on the two — the conceptualization of names based on the conceptualization of objects, and the conceptualization of objects based on the conceptualization of names, while the syllable is unconceptualized; the application of identifying sequence, by which one identifies the operation of apprehending meaning preceded by the apprehension of names; and the application of penetration. This latter should be understood as elevenfold: penetration of the adventitious nature, penetration of the sign of discernment, penetration of the non-apprehension of objects, penetration of the non-apprehension of apprehension, penetration of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (reality realm), penetration of the selflessness of persons, penetration of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, penetration of the inferior disposition, penetration of the disposition of exalted greatness, penetration of the establishment of <s>dharmas</s> according to realization, and penetration of the established <s>dharmas</s>. The mental attention under control is threefold: thoroughly purified of obscurations, thoroughly purified of the obscurations of afflictions and of the knowable, and thoroughly purified of the accomplishment of qualities. On the investigation of the reality of <s>dharmas</s>, two verses:

children.text: tatvaṃ yat satataṃ dvayena rahitaṃ bhrānteś ca saṃniśrayaḥ śakyaṃ naiva ca sarvathābhilapituṃ yañ cāprapañcātmakam |
children.translated_text: Reality is that which is always devoid of duality and is the basis of error; it cannot be expressed in any way whatsoever, and is of the nature of non-elaboration;

children.text: jñeyaṃ heyam atho viśodhyamamalaṃ yac ca prakṛtyā matam yasyākāśasuvarṇavārisadṛśī kleśād viśuddhirmatā || AMsa_11.13 ||
children.translated_text: it is the knowable, the abandonable, and the purifiable, yet considered pure by nature; its purification from defilements is likened to space, gold, and water. || AMsa_11.13 ||

body.text: satataṃ dvayena rahitaṃ tatvaṃ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvo grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇenātyantamasatvāt | bhrānteḥ saṃniśrayaḥ paratantras tena tatparikalpanāt | anabhilāpyam aprapañcātmakaṃ ca pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ | tatra prathamaṃ tatvaṃ parijñeyaṃ dvitīyaṃ praheyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ viśodhyaṃ cāgantukamalādviśuddhaṃ ca prakṛtyā yasya prakṛtyā viśuddhasyākāśasuvarṇavārisadṛśī kleśād viśuddhiḥ | na hy ākāśādīni prakṛtyā aśuddhāni | na cāgantukamalāpagamād eṣāṃ viśuddhir neṣyata iti |
body.translated_text: 'Always devoid of duality' — reality is the imagined nature, which is characterized by apprehended and apprehender, because of its absolute non-existence. 'The basis of error' — the dependent nature, because it conceptualizes that therein. 'Inexpressible' and 'of the nature of non-elaboration' — this is the consummate nature. Therein, the first reality is to be fully comprehended; the second is to be abandoned; the third is to be purified — it is purified of adventitious defilement yet pure by nature. Its purification from defilements, which is by nature pure, is likened to space, gold, and water. For space and the rest are not impure by nature, and their purification through the removal of adventitious defilement is not denied.

children.text: na khalu jagati tasmād vidyate kiṃcid anyaj jagad api tad aśeṣaṃ tatra saṃmūḍhabuddhi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, indeed, nothing else whatsoever exists in the world; yet the entire world is confused in understanding regarding that.

children.text: katham ayam abhirūḍho lokamohaprakāro yadasadabhiniviṣṭaḥ satsamantād vihāya || AMsa_11.14 ||
children.translated_text: How has this mode of delusion of the world come about — attached to the unreal, abandoning the real on every side? || AMsa_11.14 ||

body.text: na khalu tasmād evaṃlakṣaṇād dharmadhātoḥ kiṃcit anyal loke vidyate dharmatāyā dharmasyābhinnatvāt | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | tatve māyopamaparyeṣṭau pañcadaśa ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Indeed, nothing other than this <s>dharmadhātu</s> (reality realm), characterized in this way, exists in the world, because <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is not different from <s>dharmas</s>. The rest is clear in meaning. On the investigation of reality as illusion-like, fifteen verses:

children.translated_text: Just as there is <s>māyā</s> (illusion), so is <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination) described;
just as there is the illusion-created, so is the delusion of duality described. || AMsa_11.15 ||

body.text: yathā māyā yantraparigṛhītaṃ bhrāntinimittaṃ kāṣṭhaloṣṭādikaṃ tathābhūtaparikalpaḥ paratantraḥ svabhāvo veditavyaḥ | yathā māyākṛtaṃ tasyāṃ māyāyāṃ hastyaśvasuvarṇādyākṛtis tadbhāvena pratibhāsitā tathā tasminn abhūtaparikalpe dvayabhrāntirgrāhyagrāhakatvena pratibhāsitā parikalpitasvabhāvākārā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: Just as <s>māyā</s> (illusion) is the basis of error — a piece of wood or clod and so forth, grasped by a mechanism — so the dependent nature should be understood as <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination). Just as the illusion-created — the appearance of elephants, horses, gold, and so forth created in that illusion, manifested as having that nature — so the delusion of duality manifested in that false imagination as apprehended and apprehender should be understood as having the form of the imagined nature.

children.text: yathā tasmin na tadbhāvaḥ paramārthas tatheṣyate |
children.translated_text: Just as in that there is no such nature — this is regarded as ultimate reality;

children.text: yathā tasyopalabdhis tu tathā saṃvṛtisatyatā || AMsa_11.16 ||
children.translated_text: just as there is the apprehension of that — so is conventional truth. || AMsa_11.16 ||

body.text: yathā tasmin na tadbhāvo māyākṛte hastitvādyabhāvas tathā tasmin paratantre paramārtha iṣyate parikalpitasya dvayalakṣaṇasyābhāvaḥ | yathā tasya māyākṛtasya hastyādibhāvenopalabdhis tathābhūtaparikalpasya saṃvṛtisatyatopalabdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as in the illusion-created there is no such nature — the absence of elephant-nature and so forth — so in the dependent nature, ultimate reality is regarded as the absence of the imagined, characterized by duality. Just as there is the apprehension of the illusion-created as having elephant-nature and so forth, so is the apprehension of false imagination as conventional truth.

children.translated_text: Just as, in the absence of that, the manifestation of its cause is obtained,
so too, in the transformation of the basis, the reality of false imagination is obtained. || AMsa_11.17 ||

body.text: yathā māyākṛtyasyābhāve tasya nimittasya kāṣṭhādikasya vyaktir bhūtārthopalabhyate tathāśrayaparāvṛttau dvayabhrāntyabhāvād abhūtaparikalpasya bhūto 'rtha upalabhyate |
body.translated_text: Just as, in the absence of the illusion-created, the true manifestation of its cause — the wood and so forth — is apprehended, so too in the transformation of the basis, through the absence of the delusion of duality, the true reality of false imagination is apprehended.

children.text: tannimitte yathā loko hy abhrāntaḥ kāmataś caret |
children.translated_text: Just as one who is undeluded regarding its cause moves freely in the world,

children.text: parāvṛttāv aparyas taḥ kāmacārī tathā patiḥ yatiḥ || AMsa_11.18 ||
children.translated_text: so too, in the transformation of the basis, the noble one who is unconfused becomes one who moves freely. || AMsa_11.18 ||

body.text: yathā tannimitte kāṣṭhādāv abhrānto lokaḥ kāmataś carati svatantras tathā 'śrayaparāvṛttvaparyasta āryaḥ kāmacārī bhavati svatantraḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as one undeluded regarding the cause — wood and so forth — moves freely in the world, being independent, so too in the transformation of the basis, the noble one who is unconfused becomes one who moves freely, being independent.

children.text: tadākṛtiś ca tatrāsti tadbhāvaś ca na vidyate |
children.translated_text: Its form exists therein, yet its reality does not exist;
therefore, existence and non-existence are established in illusion and so forth. || AMsa_11.19 ||

body.translated_text: This verse is clear in meaning.

children.text: na bhāvas tatra cābhāvo nābhāvo bhāva eva ca |
children.translated_text: There is no existence of non-existence therein, nor non-existence of existence;
the non-differentiation of existence and non-existence is established in illusion and so forth. || AMsa_11.20 ||

body.text: na bhāvas tatra cābhāvo yas tadākṛtibhāvo nāsau na bhāvaḥ | nābhāvo bhāva eva ca yo hastitvādyabhāvo nāsau na bhāvaḥ | tayoś ca bhāvābhāvayor aviśeṣo māyādiṣu vidhīyate | ya eva hi tatra tadākṛtibhāvaḥ | sa eva hastitvādyabhāvaḥ | ya eva hastitvādyabhāvaḥ sa eva tadākṛtibhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: There is no existence that is also non-existence — that which is the appearance of its form is not non-existence. And there is no non-existence that is also existence — that which is the absence of elephanthood and so forth is not non-existence [of appearance]. And the non-distinction of both existence and non-existence is established in illusions and the like. For that very appearance of its form there is the very absence of elephanthood and the like; and that very absence of elephanthood and the like is that very appearance of its form.

children.text: tathā dvayābhatātrāsti tadbhāvaś ca na vidyate |
children.translated_text: 'Similarly, there is the appearance of duality there, yet the reality of duality is not found;
therefore, existence and non-existence are established in forms and the like.' // AMsa_11.21 //

body.text: tathā 'trābhūtaparikalpe dvayābhāsatāsti dvayabhāvaś ca nāsti | tasmād astitvanāstitvaṃ rūpādiṣu vidhīyate 'bhūtaparikalpasvabhāveṣu |
body.translated_text: Similarly, in <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization), there is the appearance of duality, yet the reality of duality does not exist. Therefore, existence and non-existence are established in forms and the like, which have the nature of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>.

children.text: na bhāvas tatra cābhāvo nābhāvo bhāva eva ca |
children.translated_text: 'There is no existence that is also non-existence, and no non-existence that is also existence,
and the non-distinction of existence and non-existence is established in forms and the like.' // AMsa_11.22 //

body.text:
na bhāvas tatra cābhāvaḥ | yā dvayābhāsatā |
nābhāvo bhāva eva ca | yā dvayatā nāstitā | bhāvābhāvāviśeṣaś ca rūpādiṣu vidhīyate | ya eva hi ābhāsatāyā bhāvaḥ sa eva dvayasyābhāva iti |
body.translated_text: 'There is no existence that is also non-existence' — this refers to the appearance of duality. 'No non-existence that is also existence' — this refers to the non-existence of duality. 'And the non-distinction of existence and non-existence is established in forms and the like' — for the very existence of the appearance is the very non-existence of the duality.

children.translated_text: 'This is accepted for the purpose of rejecting superimposition and deprecation,

children.text: hīnayānena yānasya pratiṣedhārtham eva ca || AMsa_11.23 ||
children.translated_text: and also for the purpose of rejecting the vehicle by means of the <s>Hīnayāna</s>.' // AMsa_11.23 //

body.text: kim arthaṃ punar ayaṃ bhāvābhāvayor aikāntikatvam aviśeṣaś ceṣyate | yathākramaṃ | samāropāpavādābhapratiṣedhārtham iṣyate | hīnayānagamanapratiṣedhārthaṃ ca | abhāvasya hy abhāvatvaṃ viditvā samāropaṃ na karoti | bhāvasya bhāvatvaṃ viditvāpavādaṃ na karoti | tayoś cāviśeṣaṃ viditvā na bhāvād udvijayate tasmān na hīnayānena niryāti |
body.translated_text: For what purpose, then, is this absoluteness and non-distinction of existence and non-existence accepted? In due order: it is accepted for the purpose of rejecting superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and deprecation (<s>apavāda</s>), and also for the purpose of rejecting the going by the <s>Hīnayāna</s>. For, having understood the non-existence of what is non-existent, one does not superimpose. Having understood the existence of what exists, one does not deprecate. And having understood the non-distinction of the two, one does not shrink from existence — therefore one does not set out by the <s>Hīnayāna</s>.

children.text: bhrānter nimittaṃ bhrāntiś ca rūpavijñaptir iṣyate |
children.translated_text: 'The basis of delusion and the delusion [itself] — the cognition of form is accepted [as both];

children.text: arūpiṇī ca vijñaptir abhāvāt syān na cetarā || AMsa_11.24 ||
children.translated_text: and the formless cognition would exist through the non-existence [of form], but not the other.' // AMsa_11.24 //

body.text: rūpabhrānter yā nimittavijñaptiḥ sā rūpavijñaptir iṣyate rūpākhyā | sā tu
body.translated_text: The sign-cognition of the delusion of form — that is accepted as the form-cognition (<s>rūpavijñapti</s>), called 'form.' But that

body.text: rūpabhrāntir arūpiṇī vijñaptiḥ | abhāvād rūpāvijñapter itarāpi na syād arūpiṇī vijñaptiḥ | kāraṇābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: delusion of form is a formless cognition. Through the non-existence of form-cognition, the other — formless cognition — would also not exist, because of the absence of cause.

children.translated_text: 'From the delusion of grasping the appearance of a magical elephant, duality is illustrated;

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate || AMsa_11.25 ||
children.translated_text: just as duality does not exist there, yet duality is indeed apprehended.' // AMsa_11.25 //
'From the delusion of grasping a reflection and a chain, duality is illustrated;

children.text: dvayaṃ tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate || AMsa_11.26 ||
children.translated_text: just as duality does not exist there, yet duality is indeed apprehended.' // AMsa_11.26 //

body.text: māyāhastyākṛtigrāhyabhrāntito dvayam udāhṛtaṃ | grāhyaṃ grāhakaṃ ca tatra yathā nāsti dvayaṃ caivopalabhyate | pratibimbaṃ saṃkalikāṃ ca manasikurvataḥ tadgrāhabhrānter dvayam udāhṛtaṃ pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: From the delusion of grasping the appearance of a magical elephant, duality — the grasped and the grasper — is illustrated: just as duality does not exist there, yet duality is indeed apprehended. For one who mentally attends to a reflection and a chain, from the delusion of grasping those, duality is illustrated, as before.

children.translated_text: 'Through such existence, through such non-existence, and through the distinction of existence and non-existence,

children.text: sadasanto 'tha māyābhā ye dharmā bhrāntilakṣaṇāḥ || AMsa_11.27 ||
children.translated_text: those <s>dharmas</s> characterized by delusion are existent and non-existent, and resemble an illusion.' // AMsa_11.27 //

body.text: ye dharmā bhrāntilakṣaṇā vipakṣasvabhāvās te sadasanto māyopamāś ca | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | santas tathā bhāvād abhūtaparikalpatvena | asantas tathā 'bhāvāt grāhyagrāhakatvena | tayoś ca bhāvābhāvayor aviśiṣṭatvāt santo 'pya santo 'pi māyāpi caivaṃlakṣaṇās tasmān māyopamāḥ |
body.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> that are characterized by delusion and have the nature of the opponent [i.e., the defiled side] are existent and non-existent and resemble an illusion. For what reason? They are existent 'through such existence' — by being <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization). They are non-existent 'through such non-existence' — with respect to being the grasped and the grasper. And because of the non-distinction of those two — existence and non-existence — though existent, also non-existent, they have the very characteristic of illusion; therefore, they resemble an illusion.

children.translated_text: 'Through such non-existence, through such existence, through such non-existence — they are without characteristic;

children.text: māyopamāś ca nirdiṣṭā ye dharmāḥ prātipakṣikāḥ || AMsa_11.28 ||
children.translated_text: those <s>dharmas</s> that are antidotal are also declared to resemble an illusion.' // AMsa_11.28 //

body.text: ye 'pi prātipakṣikā dharmā buddhenopadiṣṭāḥ smṛtyupasthānādayas te 'pyalakṣaṇā māyāś ca nirdiṣṭāḥ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā 'bhāvād yathā bālair gṛhyante | tathā 'bhāvād yathā deśitāḥ | tathā 'bhāvād yathā saṃdarśitā buddhena garbhāvakramaṇajanmābhiniṣkramaṇābhisaṃbodhyādayaḥ | evam alakṣaṇā avidyamānāś ca khyānti tasmān māyopamāḥ |
body.translated_text: Those antidotal <s>dharmas</s> taught by the <s>Buddha</s> — the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) and so forth — are also without characteristic and declared to be illusions. For what reason? 'Through such non-existence' — not as they are apprehended by the foolish. 'Through such non-existence' — not as they are taught. 'Through such non-existence' — not as displayed by the <s>Buddha</s>, such as entry into the womb, birth, going forth, awakening, and so on. Thus, being without characteristic and appearing as non-existent, they therefore resemble an illusion.

children.translated_text: 'Just as one magic king is defeated by another magic king,

children.text: ye sarvadharmān paśyanti nirmārās te jinātmajāḥ || AMsa_11.29 ||
children.translated_text: those who see all <s>dharmas</s> as illusions — those sons of the <s>Jina</s> are without conceit.' // AMsa_11.29 //

body.text: ye prātipakṣikā dharmās te māyārājasthānīyāḥ saṃkleśaprahāṇe vyavadānādhipatyāt | ye 'pi sāṃkleśikā dharmās te 'pi rājasthānīyāḥ saṃkleśanirvṛttāv ādhipatyāt | atas taiḥ prātipakṣikaiḥ saṃkleśaparājayo māyārājñeva rājñaḥ parājayo draṣṭavyaḥ | tajjñānāc ca bodhisatvā nirmānāḥ] bhavanti ubhayapakṣe | aupamyārthe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Those antidotal <s>dharmas</s> stand in the position of a magic king with respect to the abandonment of defilement, through their sovereignty over it. Those defiling <s>dharmas</s> also stand in the position of a king, through their sovereignty over the production of defilement. Therefore, the defeat of defilement by those antidotal [<s>dharmas</s>] should be seen like the defeat of a king by a magic king. And through knowing this, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are without conceit regarding both sides. A verse on the meaning of analogy:

children.translated_text: 'Resembling illusion, dream, mirage, and reflection; like an apparition, an echo; resembling the moon's reflection in water; like an emanation again —

children.text: ṣaṭ ṣaṭ dvau ca punaś ca ṣaṭ dvayamatā ekaikaśaś ca trayaḥ saṃskārāḥ khalu tatra tatra kathitā buddhair vibuddhottamaiḥ || AMsa_11.30 ||
children.translated_text: six, six, then two, and again six, considered as pairs, and three one by one — <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned phenomena) have been declared there and there by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the best of the awakened.' // AMsa_11.30 //

body.text: yat tūktaṃ bhagavatā māyopamā dharmā yāvan nirmāṇopamā iti | tatra māyopamā dharmāḥ ṣaḍādhyātmikāny āyatanāni | asaty ātmajīvāditve tathā prakhyānāt | svapnopamāḥ ṣaṭ bāhyāny āyatanāni tadupabhogasyāvastukatvāt | marīcikopamau dvau dharmo cittaṃ caitasikāś ca bhrāntikaratvāt | pratibimbopamāḥ punaḥ ṣaḍ evādhyātmikāny āyatanāni pūrvakarmapratibimbatvāt | pratibhāsopamāḥ ṣaḍ eva bāhyāny āyatanāny ādhyātmikānām āyatanānāṃ chāyābhūtatvāt tadādhipatyotpattitaḥ | ṣaṭ dvayaṃ matāḥ ṣaṭ dvayamatāḥ | pratiśrutkopamā deśanādharmāḥ | udakacandrabimbopamāḥ samādhisaṃniśritā dharmāḥ samādher udakasthānīyatvād acchatayā | nirmāṇopamāḥ saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahe 'saṃkliṣṭasarvakriyāprayogatvāt | jñeyaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: What the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said — '<s>dharmas</s> resemble illusion' up to 'resemble an emanation' — therein: <s>dharmas</s> resembling illusion are the six internal sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), because of appearing as self, living being, and so forth, when there is no [such] entity. Dream-like are the six external sense-bases, because of the insubstantiality of their enjoyment. Mirage-like are two — <s>dharma</s>, meaning mind and mental factors — because of causing delusion. Reflection-like are again the six internal sense-bases, because of being reflections of past <s>karma</s>. Apparition-like are the six external sense-bases, because of being like shadows of the internal sense-bases, arising under their dominance. 'Six, considered as pairs, six' — echo-like are the <s>dharmas</s> of teaching. Water-moon-reflection-like are <s>dharmas</s> dependent on <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), because <s>samādhi</s> is like water in its clarity. Emanation-like is the embracing of existence through intentional rebirth, because of the application of all activities without defilement. A verse on the investigation of the knowable:

children.text: abhūtakalpo na bhūto nābhūto 'kalpa eva ca |
children.translated_text: 'Unreal conceptualization — not real, not unreal, and simply non-conceptualization;

children.text: na kalpo nāpi cākalpaḥ sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ nirucyate || AMsa_11.31 ||
children.translated_text: neither conceptualization nor non-conceptualization — all that is knowable is thus described.' // AMsa_11.31 //

body.text: abhūtakalpo yo na lokottarajñānānukūlaḥ kalpaḥ | na bhūto nābhūto yas tadanukūlo yāvan nirvedhabhāgīyaḥ | akalpas tathatā lokottaraṃ ca jñānaṃ | na kalpo
body.translated_text: Unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtakalpa</s>) is that which is conceptualization not conforming to supramundane knowledge. 'Not real and not unreal' is that which conforms to it, up to the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). 'Non-conceptualization' (<s>akalpa</s>) is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and supramundane knowledge. 'Neither conceptualization

body.text: nāpi cākalpo lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhaṃ laukikaṃ jñānaṃ | etāvac ca sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ | saṃkleśavyavadānaparyeṣṭau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: nor non-conceptualization' is the mundane knowledge subsequently obtained from the supramundane. And this is the entirety of the knowable. On the investigation of defilement and purification, two verses:

children.translated_text: 'From their own element, appearing as duality, having activities accompanied by ignorance and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
conceptualizations proceed, devoid of the substance of duality.' // AMsa_11.32 //

body.text: svadhātuta iti bhāvāṅgād ālayavijñānataḥ | dvayābhāsā iti grāhyagrāhakābhāsāḥ | sahāvidyayā kleśaiś ca vṛttir eṣāṃ ta ime sāvidyākleśavṛttayaḥ | dvayadravyavivarjitā iti grāhyadravyeṇa grāhakadravyeṇa ca | evaṃ kleśaḥ paryeṣitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'From their own element' means from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), which is the limb of existence (<s>bhavāṅga</s>). 'Appearing as duality' means appearing as the grasped and the grasper. 'Having activities accompanied by ignorance and <s>kleśas</s>' — their activity is accompanied by ignorance and <s>kleśas</s>; thus they are 'having activities accompanied by ignorance and <s>kleśas</s>.' 'Devoid of the substance of duality' means devoid of the substance of the grasped and the substance of the grasper. Thus defilement should be investigated.

children.translated_text: 'The attainment of a special object, through the connection of abiding in one's own element —

children.text: ta eva hy advayābhāsā vartante carmakāṇḍavat || AMsa_11.33 ||
children.translated_text: those same [conceptualizations] proceed without the appearance of duality, like hide and a shaft.' // AMsa_11.33 //

body.text: ālambanaviśeṣāptir iti yo dharmālambanalābhaḥ pūrvam uktaḥ | svadhātusthānayogata iti svadhātur vikalpānāṃ tathatā tatra sthānaṃ nāmni sthānāc cetasaḥ | yogata ity abhyāsāt | bhāvanāmārgeṇa ta eva vikalpā advayābhāsā vartante parāvṛttāśrayasya | carmavat kāṇḍavac ca | yathā hi kharatvāpagamāt tad eva carma mṛdu bhavati | agnisaṃtāpanayā tad eva kāṇḍaṃ ṛju bhavati | evaṃ śamathavipaśyanābhāvanābhyāṃ cetaḥprajñāvimuktilābhe parāvṛttāśrayasya ta eva vikalpā na punar dvayābhāsāḥ pravartante ity eva vyavadānaṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ | vijñaptimātratāparyeṣṭau dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: 'The attainment of a special object' refers to the previously mentioned attainment of the <s>Dharma</s> as object. 'Through the connection of abiding in one's own element' — one's own element of conceptualizations is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); abiding therein means from the abiding of the mind in the name [of suchness]; 'through connection' means through practice. By the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), those very conceptualizations proceed without the appearance of duality, for one whose basis has been transformed — like hide and like a shaft. For just as, through the removal of hardness, that very hide becomes soft, and through heating by fire, that very shaft becomes straight — so too, through the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), upon attaining liberation of mind and wisdom, for one whose basis has been transformed, those very conceptualizations no longer proceed with the appearance of duality. Thus purification should be investigated. On the investigation of mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>), two verses:

children.translated_text: 'Mind appearing as duality is accepted [as such]; similarly, [it is] appearing as desire and the like;

children.text: śraddhādyābhāsaṃ na tadanyo dharmaḥ kliṣṭakuśalo 'sti || AMsa_11.34 ||
children.translated_text: [it is also] appearing as faith and the like — there is no defiled or wholesome <s>dharma</s> other than that.' // AMsa_11.34 //

body.text: cittamātram eva dvayapratibhāsam iṣyate grāhyapratibhāsaṃ grāhakapratibhāsaṃ ca | tathā rāgādikleśābhāsaṃ tad eveṣyate | śraddhādikuśaladharmābhāsaṃ vā | na tu tadābhāsād anyaḥ kliṣṭo dharmo 'sti rāgādilakṣaṇaḥ kuśalo vā śraddhādilakṣaṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Mind alone, appearing as duality, is accepted — appearing as the grasped and appearing as the grasper. Similarly, appearing as the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) such as desire — that alone is accepted. Or appearing as wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as faith. But there is no defiled <s>dharma</s> other than that appearance, characterized by desire and so forth, nor any wholesome [<s>dharma</s>], characterized by faith and so forth.

children.translated_text: 'Just as there is no [entity] characterized by duality apart from the appearance of duality,

children.text: iti cittaṃ citrābhāsaṃ citrākāraṃ pravartate || AMsa_11.35 ||
children.translated_text: so mind, appearing as varied [images], operates with varied forms.' // AMsa_11.35 //

body.text: tathābhāsābhāvābhāvo na tu dharmāṇāṃ mataḥ | tatra cittam eva vastu tac citrābhāsaṃ
body.translated_text: The non-existence of those appearances is not the non-existence of the <s>dharmas</s> themselves, it is considered. Therein, mind alone is the reality; it

body.text: pravartate | paryāyeṇa rāgābhāsaṃ vā dveṣābhāsaṃ vā tadanyadharmābhāsaṃ vā | citrākāraṃ ca yugapat śraddhādyākāraṃ | bhāso bhāvābhāvaḥ kliṣṭakuśalāvasthe cetasi | na tu dharmāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ tatpratibhāsavyatirekeṇa tallakṣaṇābhāvāt | lakṣaṇaparyeṣṭau ślokā aṣṭau | ekenoddeśaḥ śeṣair nirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: operates appearing as varied [images] — appearing as desire, or appearing as hatred, or appearing as other <s>dharmas</s>; and with varied forms — simultaneously with forms such as faith and the like. The appearance is the existence and non-existence of the mind in its defiled and wholesome states. But there is no [wholesome <s>dharma</s>] apart from that appearance, because of the absence of their characteristic apart from that appearance. On the investigation of characteristics, eight verses. By one, the summary; by the rest, the explanation:

children.text: lakṣyaṃ ca lakṣaṇaṃ caiva lakṣaṇā ca prabhedataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The characterized, the characteristic, and the classification of characteristics,
have been illuminated by the perfectly awakened ones for the benefit of beings.' // AMsa_11.36 //

body.translated_text: This is the summary.

children.translated_text: 'Mind together with views, therein the states and the unchanging —

children.text: lakṣyam etat samāsena hy apramāṇaṃ prabhedataḥ || AMsa_11.37 ||
children.translated_text: this is the characterized in brief; in its divisions, however, it is immeasurable.' // AMsa_11.37 //

body.text: tatra cittaṃ vijñānaṃ rūpaṃ ca | dṛṣṭiś caitasikā dharmāḥ | tatrāvasthā cittaviprayuktā dharmāḥ | avikāritā asaṃskṛtam ākāśādikaṃ tadvijñapter nityaṃ tathāpravṛtteḥ | ity etat samāsena pañcavidhaṃ lakṣyaṃ prabhedenāpramāṇaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'mind' is consciousness and form. 'Views' are mental factors (<s>caitasika dharmas</s>). 'Therein the states' are <s>dharmas</s> dissociated from mind (<s>cittaviprayukta dharmas</s>). 'The unchanging' is the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) — space and the like — because the cognition thereof always proceeds in the same way. Thus, in brief, the characterized is fivefold; in its divisions, it is immeasurable.

children.translated_text: 'The sign of the conception of meaning according to verbal expression, its latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>),
and the manifestation of an object from that — this is the imagined characteristic (<s>parikalpitalakṣaṇa</s>).' // AMsa_11.38 //

body.text: lakṣaṇaṃ samāsena trividhaṃ parikalpitādilakṣaṇaṃ | tatra parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ yathājalpārthasaṃjñāyā nimittaṃ tasya jalpasya vāsanā tasmāc ca vāsanādyo 'rthaḥ khyāti avyavahārakuśalānāṃ vināpi yathājalpārthasaṃjñayā | tatra yathā 'bhilāpam arthasaṃjñā caitasikī yathājalpārthasaṃjñā | tasyā yad ālambanaṃ tannimittam evaṃ yac ca parikalpyate yataś ca kāraṇād vāsanatas tad ubhayaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇamatrābhipretaṃ |
body.translated_text: The characteristic, in brief, is threefold: the imagined characteristic (<s>parikalpita</s>) and so forth. Therein, the imagined characteristic is threefold: the sign of the conception of meaning according to verbal expression; the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of that verbal expression; and the object that manifests from that <s>vāsanā</s> — for those not skilled in conventions, even without the conception of meaning according to verbal expression. Therein, the mental conception of meaning according to speech is the 'conception of meaning according to verbal expression.' Its object — that is the sign. And that which is imagined and that cause from which — from <s>vāsanā</s> — both of these are intended here as the imagined characteristic.

children.text: yathā nāmārtham arthasya nāmnaḥ prakhyānatā ca yā |
children.translated_text: 'The manifestation of meaning as according to name, and of name as according to meaning —
the sign of non-conceptualization — this is the imagined characteristic.' // AMsa_11.39 //
