body.text: aparaparyāyo yathā nāma cārthaś ca yathānāmārtham arthasya nāmnaś ca prakhyānatā yathānāmārthaprakhyānatā | yadi yathānāmārthaḥ khyāti yathārthaṃ vā nāma ity etad abhūtaparikalpālambanaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ etāvad dhi parikalpyate yad uta nāma vā artho veti |

children.translated_text: 'Having the appearance of a threefold threefold [division], characterized by the grasped and the grasper,
<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization) is indeed the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>).' // AMsa_11.40 //

body.translated_text: An alternative formulation: name and meaning, and the manifestation of meaning as according to name and of name — the manifestation as according to the meaning of name — this is the manifestation of meaning according to name. If meaning manifests as according to name, or name as according to meaning — this is the object of <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization), [which is] the imagined characteristic. For only this much is imagined — namely, either name or meaning.

body.text: trividhas trividhaś cābhāso 'syeti trividhatrividhābhāsaḥ | tatra trividhābhāsaḥ padābhāso 'rthābhāso dehābhāsaś ca | punas trividhābhāso manaudgrahavikalpābhāsaḥ | mano yat kliṣṭaṃ sarvadā | udgrahaḥ pañca vijñānakāyāḥ | vikalpo manovijñānaṃ | tatra prathamatrividhābhāso grāhyalakṣaṇaḥ | dvitīyo grāhakalakṣaṇaḥ | ity ayam abhūtaparikalpaḥ paratantrasya lakṣaṇaṃ |
body.translated_text: It has a threefold threefold appearance — therein, the threefold appearance is: appearance of words (padābhāsa), appearance of meaning (arthābhāsa), and appearance of a body (dehābhāsa). Again, the [other] threefold appearance is: the appearance of mind (manas), apprehension (udgraha), and conceptualization (vikalpa). Mind is that which is always afflicted (kliṣṭa). Apprehension is the five consciousness-groups (vijñānakāyas). Conceptualization is the mental consciousness (manovijñāna). Therein, the first threefold appearance has the characteristic of the grasped (grāhya). The second has the characteristic of the grasper (grāhaka). Thus this <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptualization) is the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>).

children.translated_text: 'The non-existence of existence and the sameness of existence and non-existence,
unquiet yet quiescent, and non-conceptual — this is the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>).' // AMsa_11.41 //

body.text: pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ punas tathatā sā hy abhāvatā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ parikalpitā nābhāvatā ca tadabhāvatvena bhāvāt | bhāvābhāvasamānatā ca tayor bhāvābhāvayor abhinnatvāt | aśāntā cāgantukair upakleśaiḥ śāntā ca prakṛtipariśaddhatvāt | avikalpā ca vikalpāgocaratvāt niṣprapañcatayā | etena trividhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tathatāyāḥ paridīpitaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ kleśavyavadānalakṣaṇam avikalpalakṣaṇaṃ ca | uktaṃ trividhaṃ lakṣanāṃ |
body.translated_text: The characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) is again <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). For it is the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> as imagined, yet not non-existence, because of the existence of that very non-existence. It is the sameness of existence and non-existence, because of the non-difference between those two — existence and non-existence. It is unquiet due to adventitious defilements (<s>upakleśas</s>), yet quiescent due to being pure by nature. And it is non-conceptual because it is beyond the range of conceptualization, being free from elaboration (<s>niṣprapañca</s>). By this, a threefold characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> is illuminated: the own-characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of defilement and purification (<s>kleśavyavadānalakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of non-conceptuality (<s>avikalpalakṣaṇa</s>). Thus the threefold characteristic has been stated.

children.translated_text: 'Based upon a <s>dharma</s> free from disturbance, proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>),

children.text: cittasya dhātau sthānaṃ ca sadasattārthapaśyanā || AMsa_11.42 ||
children.translated_text: the abiding of the mind in the [<s>dharma</s>-]element, and seeing things as existent and non-existent.' // AMsa_11.42 //

body.text: lakṣaṇā punaḥ pañcavidhā yogabhūmiḥ | ādhāra ādhānam ādarśa āloka āśrayaś ca | tatrādhāro niṣpandadharmo yo buddhenādhigamo deśitaḥ sa tasyādhigamasya niṣpandaḥ | ādhānaṃ yoniśo manaskāraḥ | ādarśaḥ cittasya dhātau sthānaṃ samādhir yad etat pūrvaṃ nāmni sthānam uktaṃ | ālokaḥ sadasatvenārthadarśanaṃ lokottarā prajñā tathā sac ca sato yathābhūtaṃ paśyaty asaccāsataḥ | āśraya āśrayaparāvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: The characteristic is again a fivefold yoga-ground (<s>yogabhūmi</s>): support (<s>ādhāra</s>), placement (<s>ādhāna</s>), mirror (<s>ādarśa</s>), illumination (<s>āloka</s>), and basis (<s>āśraya</s>). Therein, the support is the '<s>dharma</s> free from disturbance' — the realization (<s>adhigama</s>) taught by the <s>Buddha</s>; that is the freedom from disturbance (<s>niṣpanda</s>) of that realization. The placement is proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>). The mirror is 'the abiding of the mind in the [<s>dharma</s>-]element' — <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), which was previously called 'abiding in the name.' The illumination is 'seeing things as existent and non-existent' — supramundane wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); thus it sees the existent as truly existent and the non-existent as non-existent. The basis is the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Attaining equality therein, the <s>Ārya</s>-lineage (<s>gotra</s>) is indeed pure,

children.text: samaṃ viśiṣṭam anyūnānadhikaṃ lakṣaṇā matā || AMsa_11.43 ||
children.translated_text: equal, superior, neither deficient nor excessive — such is the characteristic considered.' // AMsa_11.43 //

body.text: samatāgamanamanāsravadhātau āryagotre tadanyair āryaiḥ | tac ca nirmalam āryagotraṃ buddhānāṃ | samaṃ vimuktisamatayā śrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ | viśiṣṭaṃ pañcabhir viśeṣaiḥ | viśuddhiviśeṣeṇa savāsanakleśaviśuddhitaḥ | pariśuddhiviśeṣeṇa kṣetrapariśuddhitaḥ | kāyaviśeṣeṇa dharmakāyatayā | saṃbhogaviśeṣeṇa parṣanmaṇḍaleṣv avicchinnadharmasaṃbhogapravartanataḥ | karmaviśeṣeṇa ca tuṣitabhavanavāsādinirmāṇaiḥ satvārthakriyānuṣṭhānataḥ | na ca tasyonatvaṃ saṃkleśapakṣanirodhe nādhikatvaṃ vyavadānapakṣotpāda ity eṣā
body.translated_text: The attainment of equality in the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), in the <s>Ārya</s>-lineage, with other <s>Āryas</s>. And that pure <s>Ārya</s>-lineage belongs to the <s>Buddhas</s>. It is equal to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> in the equality of liberation. It is superior through five distinctions: through the distinction of purity — from the purification of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) together with their latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>); through the distinction of complete purity — from the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field; through the distinction of body — from being the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; through the distinction of enjoyment — from the uninterrupted turning of the enjoyment of <s>Dharma</s> in the assemblies; and through the distinction of activity — from accomplishing the welfare of beings through emanations such as dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and so forth. And there is no deficiency in the cessation of the side of defilement, nor excess in the arising of the side of purification — this is the

body.text: pañcavidhā yogabhūmir lakṣaṇā | tathā hi tallakṣyaṃ ca lakṣyate | vimuktiparyeṣṭau ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: fivefold yoga-ground characteristic. For that which is characterized is indeed characterized thereby. On the investigation of liberation (<s>vimukti</s>), six verses:

children.translated_text: 'The reversal of the appearance of words, meaning, and body — the undefiled

children.text: dhātur bījaparāvṛtteḥ sa ca sarvatragāśrayaḥ || AMsa_11.44 ||
children.translated_text: element (<s>dhātu</s>) — arises from the reversal of the seed; and that is the basis for all.' // AMsa_11.44 //

body.text: bījaparāvṛtter ity ālayavijñānaparāvṛttitaḥ | padārthadehanirbhāsānāṃ vijñānānāṃ parāvṛttir anāsravo dhātur vimuktiḥ | sa ca sarvatragāśrayaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhagataḥ |
body.translated_text: 'From the reversal of the seed' means from the reversal of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness). The reversal of the consciousnesses that appear as words, meaning, and body is the undefiled element — liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). And that is 'the basis for all' — pertaining to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>.

children.text: caturdhā vaśitā vṛtter manasaś codgrahaś ca ca |
children.translated_text: 'Fourfold mastery over the cessation of the mind, apprehension,

children.text: vikalpasyāvikalpe hi kṣetre jñāne 'tha karmaṇi || AMsa_11.45 ||
children.translated_text: and conceptualization — namely in non-conceptuality, in the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field, in knowledge, and in activity.' // AMsa_11.45 //

body.text: manasaś codgrahasya ca vikalpasya cāvṛtteḥ parāvṛtter ity arthaḥ | caturdhā vaśitā bhavati yathākramam avikalpe kṣetre jñānakarmaṇoś ca |
body.translated_text: The meaning is: from the reversal — the cessation — of mind, apprehension, and conceptualization, fourfold mastery arises, respectively in non-conceptuality, in the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field, and in knowledge and activity.

children.translated_text: 'In the three stages beginning with Immovable (<s>Acalā</s>), that mastery is fourfold;

children.text: dvidhaikasyāṃ tadanyasyām ekaikā vaśitā matā || AMsa_11.46 ||
children.translated_text: in one [stage] it is twofold, and in each of the others it is single — such is mastery considered.' // AMsa_11.46 //

body.text: sā ceyam acalādibhūmitraye caturdhā vaśitā veditavyā | ekasyām acalāyāṃ bhūmau dvividhā | avikalpe na cānabhisaṃskāranirvikalpatvāt | kṣetre ca buddhakṣetrapariśodhanāt | tadanyasyāṃ bhūmāv ekaikā vaśitā sādhumatyaṃ jñānavaśitā pratisaṃvidviśeṣalābhāt | dharmamedhāyāṃ karmaṇyabhijñākarmaṇām avyāghātāt |
body.translated_text: This fourfold mastery should be understood in the three stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) beginning with <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). In one — the <s>Acalā</s> stage — it is twofold: in non-conceptuality, because of being non-conceptual without effort (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>); and in the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field, because of the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field. In the other stages, mastery is single in each: in <s>Sādhumatī</s>, mastery in knowledge, because of attaining the distinction of the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges); and in <s>Dharmameghā</s>, mastery in activity, because of the unobstructed functioning of the activities of supernatural powers (<s>abhijñā</s>).

children.text: viditvā nairātmyaṃ dvividham iha dhīmān bhavagataṃ samaṃ tac ca jñātvā praviśati sa tatvaṃ grahaṇataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having known the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) here regarding the realms of existence, and having known that as equal, the wise one enters reality through apprehension alone;

children.text: tatas tatra sthānān manasa iha na khyāti tad api tadakhyānaṃ muktiḥ parama upalambhasya vigamaḥ || AMsa_11.47 ||
children.translated_text: then, from abiding therein, that too does not appear to the mind — that non-appearance is liberation, the supreme cessation of apprehension.' // AMsa_11.47 //

body.text: aparo vimuktiparyāyaḥ | dvividhaṃ nairātmyaṃ viditvā bhavatrayagataṃ bodhisatvaḥ samaṃ tac ca jñātvā dvividhinair ātmyaṃ parikalpitapudgalābhāvāt parikalpitadharmābhāvāt na tu sarvathaivābhāvataḥ | tatvaṃ praviśati vijñaptimātratāṃ grahaṇato grahaṇamātram etad iti | tatas tatra tatvavijñaptimātrasthānān manasas tad api tatvaṃ na khyāti
body.translated_text: Another formulation of liberation: having known the twofold selflessness extending to the three realms of existence, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having known that as equal — the twofold selflessness being due to the non-existence of the imagined person (<s>pudgala</s>) and due to the non-existence of imagined <s>dharmas</s>, but not from absolute non-existence in every respect — enters reality, mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>), 'through apprehension' — this is merely apprehension. Then, from abiding there in the reality of mere cognition, that too — reality — does not appear to the mind

body.text: vijñaptimātraṃ | tadakhyānaṃ muktiḥ parama upalambhasya yo vigamaḥ pudgaladharmayor anupalambhāt |
body.translated_text: — [that is,] mere cognition. That non-appearance is liberation, the supreme cessation of apprehension — due to the non-apprehension of person (<s>pudgala</s>) and <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: ādhāre saṃbhārād ādhāne sati hi nāmamātraṃ paśyan |
children.translated_text: 'On the support, from accumulation; when there is placement, seeing as mere name;

children.text: paśyati hi nāmamātraṃ tatpaśyaṃs tac ca naiva paśyati bhūyaḥ || AMsa_11.48 ||
children.translated_text: one sees indeed mere name — and seeing that, one no longer sees even that.' // AMsa_11.48 //

body.text: aparaparyāyaḥ | ādhāra iti śrutau saṃbhārād iti saṃbhṛtasaṃbhārasya pūrvasaṃbhāralābhāt | ādhāne satīti yoniśomanaskāre nāmamātraṃ paśyann ity abhilāpamātram artharahitaṃ | paśyati hi nāmamātram iti vijñaptimātraṃ nāma arūpiṇaś catvāraḥ skandhā iti kṛtvā tatpaśyaṃs tad api bhūyo naiva paśyaty arthabhāve tadvijñaptyadarśanād ity ayam anupalambho vimuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: An alternative formulation: 'on the support' means in scripture (<s>śruta</s>). 'From accumulation' means for one who has accumulated the accumulations, from the attainment of prior accumulation. 'When there is placement' means when there is proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>). 'Seeing mere name' means [seeing] mere verbal designation (<s>abhilāpamātra</s>), devoid of [real] object. 'One sees indeed mere name' means mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>) — for name is the four formless aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). 'Seeing that, one no longer sees even that' — because when the [real] object is absent, the cognition of it is also not seen. This non-apprehension is liberation.

children.translated_text: 'This mind, always having <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (unwholesomeness/heaviness), bound by the view of self,

children.text: pravartate nivṛttis tu tad adhyātmasthiter matā || AMsa_11.49 ||
children.translated_text: proceeds [in <s>saṃsāra</s>]; but cessation is considered to come from its abiding inwardly.' // AMsa_11.49 //

body.text: aparaprakāraś cittam etat sadauṣṭhulyaṃ pravartate janmasu | ātmadarśanapāśitam iti dauṣṭhulyakāraṇaṃ darśayati | dvividhenātmadarśanena pāśitamataḥ sadauṣṭhulyam iti | nivṛttis tu tad adhyātmasthiter iti tasya cittasya citta evāvasthānād ālambanānupalambhataḥ | niḥsvabhāvatāparyeṣṭau ślokadvayaṃ
body.translated_text: Another formulation: this mind, always having <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (unwholesomeness), proceeds in births. 'Bound by the view of self' indicates the cause of <s>dauṣṭhulya</s>: being bound by the twofold view of self, therefore it always has <s>dauṣṭhulya</s>. 'But cessation comes from its abiding inwardly' — from the mind abiding in mind itself, due to the non-apprehension of objects. On the investigation of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>), two verses:

children.translated_text: 'Because of non-existence by itself, through its own nature, and because of non-abiding in own-nature,
and because of the non-existence of that as [it is] grasped — essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>) is accepted.' // AMsa_11.50 //

body.text: svayam abhāvān niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratyayādhīnatvāt | svenātmanā 'bhāvān niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ niruddhānāṃ punas tenātmanānutpatteḥ | svabhāva 'navasthitatvān niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ kṣaṇikatvād ity etattrividhaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇatrayānugaṃ veditavyaṃ | grāhavat tadabhāvāc ca niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ tadabhāvād iti svābhāvāt | yathā bālānāṃ svabhāvagrāho nityasukhaśacyāt to vā 'nyena vā parikalpitalakṣaṇena tathāsau svabhāvo nāsti tasmād api niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ dharmāṇām iṣyate | ....
body.translated_text: Essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s> because of non-existence by itself — since they depend on conditions. Essencelessness because of non-existence through its own nature — since once ceased, they do not arise again with that same nature. Essencelessness because of non-abiding in own-nature — since they are momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>). This threefold essencelessness should be understood as following the three characteristics of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). 'Because of the non-existence of that as [it is] grasped' — essencelessness because of the non-existence of that [supposed] own-nature. Just as the ordinary beings' grasping of own-nature — whether as permanent, pleasant, self, or by some other imagined characteristic — that own-nature does not exist; therefore too, essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s> is accepted. ....

children.translated_text: 'Established through essencelessness, each successively dependent on the prior:
non-arising, non-cessation, primordial peace, and <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' // AMsa_11.51 //

body.text: ...... niḥsvabhāvatayā 'nutpādādayaḥ | yo hi niḥsvabhāvaḥ so 'nutpanno yo 'nutpannaḥ so 'niruddho yo 'niruddhaḥ sa ādiśānto ya ādiśāntaḥ sa prakṛtiparinirvṛta ity evam uttarottaraniśrayair ebhir niḥsvabhāvatābhir niḥsvabhāvatayā 'nutpādādayaḥ siddhā bhavanti | anutpattidharmakṣāntiparyeṣṭāvāryā |
body.translated_text: ...... Through essencelessness, non-arising and the rest [are established]. For that which is without essence is non-arisen; that which is non-arisen is non-ceased; that which is non-ceased is primordially peaceful; that which is primordially peaceful is naturally in <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Thus, through these essencelessnesses, each successively dependent on the prior, non-arising and the rest are established through essencelessness. On the investigation of the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattidharmakṣānti</s>):

children.translated_text: 'In the beginning, in sameness, in otherness, in own-characteristic, in [arising] by itself, then in [becoming] otherwise,
in defilement, and in distinction — acceptance regarding non-arising <s>dharmas</s> is declared.' // AMsa_11.52 //

body.text: aṣṭāsv anutpattidharmeṣu kṣāntir anutpattikadharmakṣāntiḥ | ādau saṃsārasya na hi tasyādyutpattir asti | tatve 'nyatve ca pūrvapaścimānāṃ na hi saṃsāre teṣām eva dharmāṇām utpattirye pūrvam utpannās tadbhāvenānutpatteḥ | na cānyeṣām apūrvaprakārānutpatteḥ | svalakṣaṇe parikalpitasya svabhāvasya na hi tasya kadācid utpattiḥ | svayamanutpattau paratantrasya | anyathābhāve pariniṣpannasya na hi tadanyathā bhāvasyotpattir asti | saṃkleśe prahīṇe na hi kṣayajñānalābhinaḥ sakleśasyotpattiṃ punaḥ paśyanti | viśeṣe buddhadharmakāyānāṃ na hi teṣāṃ viśeṣotpattir asti | ity eteṣv anutpattidharmeṣu kṣāntir anutpattidharmoktā | ekayānatāparyeṣṭau sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) regarding the eight non-arising <s>dharmas</s> is <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>). In the beginning of <s>saṃsāra</s> — for there is no initial arising of it. In sameness and otherness of the former and later [moments] — for in <s>saṃsāra</s>, those very <s>dharmas</s> that arose before do not arise again as the same, since they do not arise again as that very entity; nor do others arise, since they do not arise in an unprecedented manner. In own-characteristic — of the imagined own-nature, for it never arises at any time. In self-arising — of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). In [becoming] otherwise — of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>), for the arising of its becoming otherwise does not exist. In defilement that has been abandoned — for those who have attained the knowledge of destruction do not again see the arising of defilement. In distinction — of the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, for the arising of any distinction in them does not exist. Acceptance regarding these non-arising <s>dharmas</s> is called acceptance of non-arising <s>dharmas</s>. On the investigation of the one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>), seven verses:

children.translated_text: 'Because of the sameness of <s>Dharma</s>, selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), and liberation, because of the division of lineage (<s>gotra</s>),

children.text: dvyāśayāpteś ca nirmāṇāt paryantād ekayānatā || AMsa_11.53 ||
children.translated_text: because of the attainment of a twofold intention, because of emanation, and because of the endpoint — the one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>).' // AMsa_11.53 //

body.text: dharmatulyatvād ekayānatā śrāvakādīnāṃ dharmadhātor abhinnatvāt yātavyaṃ yānam iti kṛtvā nairātmyasya tulyatvād ekayānatā śrāvakādīnām ātmābhāvatāsāmānyād yātā yānam iti kṛtvā vimuktitulyatvād ekayānatā yāti yānam iti kṛtvā | gotrabhedād ekayānatā | aniyataśrāvakagotrāṇāṃ mahāyānena niryāṇād yānti tena yānam iti kṛtvā dvyāśayāpter ekayānatā buddhānāṃ ca sarvasatveṣv ātmāśayaprāpteḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca tadgotraniyatānāṃ pūrvaṃ bodhisaṃbhāracaritād anātmani baddhāśayaprāpter abhinnasaṃtānādhimokṣalābhato buddhānubhāvena tathāgatānugrahaviśeṣapradeśalābhāya ity ekatvāśayalābhenaikatvāt buddhatacchrāvakāṇām ekayānatā | nirmāṇād ekayānatā yathoktam anekaśatakṛtvo 'haṃ śrāvakayānena parinirvṛta iti vineyānām arthe tathā nirmāṇasaṃdarśanāt | paryantād apyekayānatā yataḥ pareṇa yātavyaṃ nāsti tadyānam iti kṛtvā | buddhatvam ekayānam evaṃ tatra tatra sūtre tena
body.translated_text: The one vehicle because of the sameness of <s>Dharma</s> — since the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is undifferentiated for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, as 'that which is traveled to is the vehicle.' The one vehicle because of the sameness of selflessness — since the absence of self is common to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others, as 'that which has been traveled is the vehicle.' The one vehicle because of the sameness of liberation, as 'that by which one travels is the vehicle.' The one vehicle because of the division of lineage (<s>gotra</s>) — since <s>Śrāvakas</s> of indeterminate lineage attain final departure through the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, as 'they travel by that vehicle.' The one vehicle because of the attainment of a twofold intention — since the <s>Buddhas</s> attain the intention of self regarding all beings, and since those <s>Śrāvakas</s> of determined lineage, through having previously practiced the accumulations of awakening, attain the intention of having been bound to non-self, through obtaining the conviction of an undivided continuum, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, in order to obtain the teaching of the special grace of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — thus through the attainment of the intention of oneness between the <s>Buddhas</s> and their <s>Śrāvakas</s>, the one vehicle. The one vehicle because of emanation — as it is said, 'Hundreds of times I have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> through the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle,' because of displaying such emanations for the sake of those to be trained. The one vehicle also because of the endpoint — since beyond that there is nothing further to be traveled, as 'that is the vehicle.' <s>Buddhahood</s> is indeed the one vehicle. Thus, in those various <s>sūtras</s>, with that

body.text: tanābhiprāyeṇaikayānatā veditavyā na tu yānatrayaṃ nāsti | kim arthaṃ punas tena tenābhiprāyeṇaikayānatā buddhair deśitā |
body.translated_text: various intention the one vehicle should be understood — but it is not that the three vehicles do not exist. For what purpose then is the one vehicle taught by the <s>Buddhas</s> with those various intentions?

children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of attracting some, and for holding others [back],
the one vehicle has been taught by the perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> for those of indeterminate [lineage].' // AMsa_11.54 //

body.text: ākarṣaṇārtham ekeṣām iti ye śrāvakagotrā aniyatāḥ | anyeṣāṃ ca saṃdhāraṇāya ye bodhisatvāgotrā aniyatāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'For the purpose of attracting some' refers to those of <s>Śrāvaka</s>-lineage who are indeterminate. 'And for holding others [back]' refers to those of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-lineage who are indeterminate.

children.translated_text: 'The indeterminate <s>Śrāvaka</s> is of two kinds, according to whether the goal has been seen or not seen;

children.text: dṛṣṭārtho vītarāgaś cāvītarāgo 'pya sau mṛduḥ || AMsa_11.55 ||
children.translated_text: the one who has seen the goal is free from desire, and the one not yet free is also gentle.' // AMsa_11.55 //

body.text: śrāvakaḥ punar aniyato dvividho veditavyaḥ | dṛṣṭārthayānaś ca yo dṛṣṭasatyo mahāyānena niryāti adṛṣṭārthayānaś ca yo na dṛṣṭasatyo mahāyānena niryāti | dṛṣṭārthaḥ punar vītarāgaś cāvītarāgaś ca kāmebhyaḥ | asau ca mṛdur dhandhagatiko veditavyaḥ | yo dṛṣṭārtho dvividha uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the indeterminate <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) should be understood as twofold: one who has seen the truth (<s>dṛṣṭasatya</s>) and goes forth by the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and one who has not seen the truth and goes forth by the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The one who has seen the truth is again either free from desire or not free from desire with respect to the sense-pleasures. And that one should be understood as gentle and slow-progressing. The one who has seen the truth has been stated to be twofold.

children.translated_text: And those two, through the transformation of the attained noble path in [future] existences,
are endowed with a rebirth of inconceivable transformation. // AMsa_11.56 //

body.text: tau ca dṛṣṭārtho labdhasyāryamārgasya bhaveṣu pariṇāmanāt | acintyapariṇāmikyā upapattyā samanvāgatau veditavyau | acintyo hi tasyāryamārgasya pariṇāma upapattau tasmād acintyapariṇāmikī |
body.translated_text: Those two who have seen the truth, through the transformation of the attained noble path in [future] existences, should be understood as endowed with a rebirth of inconceivable transformation. For the transformation of that noble path in rebirth is inconceivable; therefore it is 'of inconceivable transformation.'

children.translated_text: One, by the power of his vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), attains rebirth;
the other, by the force of the connection of non-returning (<s>anāgāmitā</s>), attains [rebirth] through emanations. // AMsa_11.57 //

body.text: tayoś caikaḥ praṇidhānavaśād upapattiṃ gṛhṇāti yatheṣṭaṃ yo na vītarāgaḥ | eko 'nāgāmitāyogabalena nirmāṇaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Of those two, one takes rebirth by the power of his vow as he wishes — the one who is not free from desire. The other, by the force of the connection of non-returning, [does so] through emanations.

children.translated_text: And because of their delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, those two are considered slow-progressing,
due to the repeated arising of their own minds. // AMsa_11.58 //

body.text: tau ca nirvāṇābhiratatvād ubhāv api dhandhagatikau matau ciratareṇābhisaṃbodhataḥ | svasya śrāvakacittasya nirvitsahagatasyābhīkṣṇaṃ samudācārāt |
body.translated_text: And because of their delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, both of those two are considered slow-progressing — taking a very long time to reach full awakening — due to the frequent arising of their own <s>śrāvaka</s>-minds accompanied by weariness.

children.text: so 'kṛtārtho hy abuddhe ca jāto dhyānārtham udyataḥ |
children.translated_text: That one, being unfulfilled, born when the <s>Buddha</s> is absent, strives for <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);

children.text: nirmāṇārthī tadāśritya parāṃ bodhim avāpnute || AMsa_11.59 ||
children.translated_text: desiring emanation, relying on that, he attains supreme awakening. // AMsa_11.59 //

body.text: yaḥ punar asāv avītarāgo dṛṣṭasatyaḥ so 'kṛtārthaḥ śaikṣo bhavan buddharahite kāle jāto dhyānārtham udyato bhavati nirmāṇārthī | tacca nirmāṇam āśritya krameṇa parāṃ bodhiṃ prāpnoti | tam avasthātrayasthaṃ saṃdhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā śrīmālāsūtre | śrāvako bhūtvā pratyekabuddho bhavati punaś ca buddha iti | agnidṛṣṭānte ca yadā ca pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭasatyāvasthā sadā buddharahite kāle svayaṃ dhyānam utpādya janmakāyaṃ tyaktvā nirmāṇakāyaṃ gṛhṇāti yadā ca parāṃ bodhiṃ prāpnotīti | vidyāsthānaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The one who has seen the truth but is not free from desire — being unfulfilled, a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), born in a time when the <s>Buddha</s> is absent — strives for <s>dhyāna</s> and desires emanation. Relying on that emanation, he gradually attains supreme awakening. Referring to that one as situated in three states, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said in the <s>Śrīmālā-sūtra</s>: 'Having been a <s>śrāvaka</s>, he becomes a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and then a <s>Buddha</s>.' And in the fire analogy: when first, in the state of having seen the truth, in a time always devoid of a <s>Buddha</s>, he generates <s>dhyāna</s> by himself, abandons the birth-body and takes up an emanation-body; and when he attains supreme awakening. A verse on the investigation of the fields of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>):

children.text: vidyāsthāne pañcavidhe yogamakṛtvā sarvajñatvaṃ naiti kathaṃcit paramāryaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without applying himself to the fivefold field of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>), the supreme noble one can in no way attain omniscience;

children.text: ity anyeṣāṃ nigrahaṇānugrahaṇāya svājñārthaṃ vā tatra karoty eva sa yogam || AMsa_11.60 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, for the subjugation and assistance of others, or for his own understanding, he indeed applies himself therein. // AMsa_11.60 //

body.text: pañcavidhaṃ vidyāsthānaṃ | adhyātmavidyā hetuvidyā śabdavidyā cikitsāvidyā śilpakarmasthānavidyā ca | tad yad arthaṃ bodhisatvena paryeṣitavyaṃ tad darśayati | sarvajñatvaprāptyartham abhedena sarvaṃ | bhedena punar hetuvidyāṃ śabdavidyāṃ ca paryeṣate nigrahārtham anyeṣāṃ tad anadhimuktānāṃ | cikitsāvidyāṃ śilpakarmasthānavidyāṃ cānyeṣām anugrahārthaṃ tadarthikānāṃ | adhyātmavidyāṃ svayam ājñārthaṃ | dhātupuṣṭiparyeṣṭau trayodaśa
body.translated_text: The fivefold field of knowledge is: <s>adhyātmavidyā</s> (inner science), <s>hetuvidyā</s> (science of reasoning), <s>śabdavidyā</s> (science of grammar), <s>cikitsāvidyā</s> (science of medicine), and <s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s> (science of arts and crafts). The purpose for which it should be investigated by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is shown: for the attainment of omniscience, [investigating] all without distinction. With distinction, however, he investigates <s>hetuvidyā</s> and <s>śabdavidyā</s> for the subjugation of others who have no faith in those. He investigates <s>cikitsāvidyā</s> and <s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s> for the benefit of others who seek those. [He investigates] <s>adhyātmavidyā</s> for his own understanding. On the investigation of nourishing the element (<s>dhātupuṣṭi</s>), thirteen

body.text: ślokāḥ | pāramitāparipūraṇārthaṃ ye pāramitāpratisaṃyuktā evaṃ manasikārā dhātupuṣṭaye bhavanti ta etābhir gāthābhir deśitāḥ |
body.translated_text: verses. The mental attitudes (<s>manasikāras</s>) that are connected with the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) and serve to nourish the element for the purpose of completing the <s>pāramitās</s> are taught by these verses:

children.translated_text: Satisfaction at finding the cause, reliance and its recollection,
desire for shared fruit, and conviction according to awakening. // AMsa_11.61 //

body.text: te punar hetopalabdhituṣṭimanasikārāt | yāvad agratvātmāvadhāraṇamanasikāraḥ | tatra hetūpalabdhituṣṭimanasikāra ādita eva tāvat | gotrastho bodhisatvaḥ svātmani pāramitānāṃ gotraṃ paśyan hetūpalabdhituṣṭyā pāramitādhātupuṣṭiṃ karoti | gotrastho 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayatīty ato 'nantaraṃ niśrayatadanusmṛtimanasikāraḥ | sa hi bodhisatvaḥ svātmani pāramitānāṃ saṃniśrayabhūtaṃ bodhicittaṃ samanupaśyann evaṃ manasikaroti niyatam etāḥ pāramitāḥ paripūriṃ gamiṣyanti | tathā hy asmākaṃ bodhicittaṃ saṃvidyate iti | utpāditabodhicittasya pāramitābhiḥ svaparārthaprayoge sādhāraṇaphalecchāmanasikāra āsāṃ pāramitānāṃ parasādhāraṇaṃ va phalāṃ bhavatv anyathā vā mā bhūd ity abhisaṃskaraṇāt | svaparārthaṃ prayujyamāno 'saṃkleśopāyaṃ tatvārthaṃ pratividhyatīty ato 'nantaraṃ yathābodhādhimucyanāmanasikāraḥ | evaṃ sarvatrānukramo veditavyaḥ | yathā buddhair bhagavadbhiḥ pāramitā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbhotsyante 'bhisaṃbudhyante ca tathā 'ham adhimucye ity abhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: These are, moreover, from the mental attitude of satisfaction at finding the cause up to the mental attitude of self-ascertainment of supremacy. Therein, first, the mental attitude of satisfaction at finding the cause: a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who possesses the lineage (<s>gotra</s>), seeing in himself the lineage of the <s>pāramitās</s>, nourishes the element of the <s>pāramitās</s> through satisfaction at finding the cause. 'One who possesses the lineage generates the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening' — immediately after this comes the mental attitude of reliance and its recollection. For that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing in himself <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind) as the support of the <s>pāramitās</s>, mentally attends thus: 'Surely these <s>pāramitās</s> will reach fulfillment, for <s>bodhicitta</s> is present in us.' For one who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, in the practice for one's own and others' benefit through the <s>pāramitās</s>, comes the mental attitude of desire for shared fruit — from the intention: 'May there be fruit shared with others from these <s>pāramitās</s>, or may it not be otherwise.' While engaged in practice for one's own and others' benefit, one penetrates the truth through a method free from defilement — therefore, immediately after, comes the mental attitude of conviction according to awakening — from the intention: 'Just as the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have fully awakened, will fully awaken, and do fully awaken to the <s>pāramitās</s>, so do I have conviction.' Thus the sequence should be understood throughout.

children.translated_text: Delight through fourfold power, determination in weariness,

children.text: vipakṣe pratipakṣe ca pratipattiś caturvidhā || AMsa_11.62 ||
children.translated_text: and fourfold practice regarding the opponent and the antidote. // AMsa_11.62 //

body.text: anubhāvaprīyaṇāmanasikāraś caturvidhānubhāvadarśanaprīyaṇā caturvidhānubhāvo vipakṣaprahāṇaṃ saṃbhāraparipākaḥ svaparānugraha āyatyāṃ vipākaphalaniḥṣyandaphaladānatā ca | satvasvabuddhadharmaparipākam ārabhyākhedaniścayamanasikāraḥ sarvasatvavipratipattibhiḥ sarvaduḥkhāpattipātaiś cākhedaniścayābhisaṃskaraṇāt paramabodhiprāptaye | vipakṣe pratipakṣe ca caturvidhapratipattimanasikāraḥ | dānādivipakṣāṇāṃ ca mātsaryādīnāṃ pratideśanā pratipakṣāṇāṃ ca dānādīnām anumodanā
body.translated_text: The mental attitude of delight through power is delight through seeing fourfold power. The fourfold power is: abandonment of the opponent, maturation of the accumulations, benefit of self and others, and the future giving of the fruits of ripening and of outflow. The mental attitude of determination against weariness, with regard to the maturation of beings and one's own <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, is from the intention of determination against weariness despite all the waywardness of all beings and all the calamities of suffering, for the attainment of supreme awakening. The mental attitude of fourfold practice regarding the opponent and the antidote: confession of the opponents of generosity and so forth — avarice and the like — and rejoicing in the antidotes — generosity and so forth

body.text: tadadhipateyadharmadeśanārthaṃ ca buddhādhyeṣaṇā | tāsāṃ ca bodhau pariṇāmanā |
body.translated_text: ; and supplication of the <s>Buddhas</s> for the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> under their sovereignty; and the dedication of those [merits] toward awakening.

children.text: prasādaḥ saṃpratīkṣā ca dānacchandaḥ paratra ca |
children.translated_text: Faith, acceptance,
desire for giving, armor [of resolve], aspiration, and the mental act of rejoicing. // AMsa_11.63 //

body.text: adhimuktibalādhānatām ārabhya pāramitādhipateyadharmārthe ca prasādamanasikāraḥ | dharmaparyeṣṭim ārabhya saṃpratīcchanamanasikāras tasyaiva dharmasyāprativahanayogena parigrahaṇatayā | daśanām ārabhya dānacchandamanasikāro dharmasyārthasya ca prakāśanārthaṃ pareṣāṃ | pratipattim ārabhya saṃnāhamanasikāro dānādiparipūraye saṃnahanāt | praṇidhānamanasikāras tatparipūriprāptaye samavadhānārthaṃ | abhinandamanasikāro 'ho bata dānādipratipattyā samyak saṃpādayeyam ity abhinandanāt | eta eva trayo manasikārā avavādānuśāsanyāṃ yojayitavyāḥ | upāyopasaṃhitakarmamanasikāraḥ saṃkalpaiḥ sarvaprakāradānādiprayogamanasikaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: With regard to the strength of conviction, the mental attitude of faith concerns the <s>Dharma</s> that is the object of the sovereignty of the <s>pāramitās</s>. With regard to the investigation of the <s>Dharma</s>, the mental attitude of acceptance is the embracing of that very <s>Dharma</s> through not turning away from it. With regard to teaching, the mental attitude of desire for giving is for the purpose of illuminating the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning to others. With regard to practice, the mental attitude of armor is from girding oneself for the completion of generosity and the rest. The mental attitude of aspiration is for the purpose of establishing the conditions for attaining their completion. The mental attitude of rejoicing is from the rejoicing: 'Oh, may I perfectly accomplish through the practice of generosity and the rest!' These same three mental attitudes should be applied to instruction and guidance. The mental attitude of action accompanied by skillful means is from mentally attending to the practice of generosity and the rest in every way through intentions.

children.translated_text: Eagerness regarding the acquisition of power, sixfold wealth in generosity and the rest,
and in maturation, in worship, in service — compassion. // AMsa_11.64 //

body.text: autsukyamanasikāraś caturvidhaḥ | śaktilābhe na dānādau ṣaḍvidhe dānadāne yāvat prajñādāne | evaṃ śīlādiṣu ṣaḍvidheṣu | pāramitābhir eva saṃgrahavastuprayogeṇa satvaparipāke | pūjāyāṃ ca dānena lābhasatkārapūjayā | śeṣābhiś ca pratipattipūjayā | aviparītapāramitopadeśāpañcakalyāṇamitrasevāyām autsukyamanasikāro veditavyaḥ | anukampāmanasikāraś caturbhir apramāṇair dānādyupasaṃhāreṇa maitrāyataḥ | mātsaryādisamavadhānena satveṣu karuṇāyataḥ | dānādisamanvāgateṣu muditāyataḥ | tadasaṃkleśādhimokṣataś ca upekṣāyataḥ |
body.translated_text: The mental attitude of eagerness is fourfold: regarding the acquisition of power; regarding the sixfold giving of gifts — up to the gift of wisdom (<s>prajñādāna</s>) — and likewise regarding the sixfold [practice] of moral discipline and so forth; regarding the maturation of beings through the practice of the means of gathering (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>) by means of the <s>pāramitās</s> themselves; regarding worship — through generosity, worship consisting of material gain, honor, and reverence, and through the remaining [<s>pāramitās</s>], worship consisting of practice; the mental attitude of eagerness should be understood regarding the service of the spiritual friend who gives non-erroneous instruction in the <s>pāramitās</s>. The mental attitude of compassion (<s>anukampā</s>) is through the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇas</s>) connected with generosity and the rest: from loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), through the application of generosity and so forth; from compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), through establishing [awareness of] avarice and the like in beings; from sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), toward those who are endowed with generosity and the rest; and from equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), through non-attachment to those [<s>pāramitās</s>].

children.text: akṛte kukṛte lajjā kaukṛtyaṃ viṣaye ratiḥ |
children.translated_text: Shame regarding what is undone and wrongly done, regret; delight in the object;
perception of an enemy regarding weariness, and the intention of composition and promotion. // AMsa_11.65 //

body.text: hrīdharmam ārabhya lajjāmanaskāro 'kṛteṣu vā dānādiṣv aparipūrṇamithyākṛteṣu vā lajjā lajjāyamānaś ca pravṛttinivṛttyartham anānuṣaṅgikaṃ kaukṛtyāyate | dhṛtim ārabhya ratimanaskāro dānādyālambane 'vikṣepataś cittasya dhāraṇāt | akhedamanaskāro
body.translated_text: With regard to moral shame (<s>hrī</s>), the mental attitude of shame is shame regarding generosity and the like that is either undone or incompletely and wrongly done; and being ashamed, one feels regret — not as a persistent state, but for the purpose of future engagement and cessation. With regard to steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), the mental attitude of delight is the holding of the mind without distraction upon the object of generosity and the like. The mental attitude of non-weariness

body.text: dānādiprayogaparikhede śatrusaṃjñākaraṇāt | racanāc chandamanaskāraḥ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktaśāstraracanābhisaṃskaraṇāt | lokajñatām ārabhya udbhāvanāmanaskāras tasyaiva śāstrasya loke yathābhājanam udbhāvanābhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: is from regarding weariness in the practice of generosity and the like as an enemy. The mental attitude of desire for composition is from the intention of composing treatises connected with the <s>pāramitās</s>. With regard to knowledge of the world (<s>lokajñatā</s>), the mental attitude of promotion is from the intention of promoting that very treatise in the world according to [people's] capacity.

children.translated_text: Generosity and the rest are the refuge for awakening, not <s>Īśvara</s> and the like,

children.text: doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca pratisaṃvedanād dvayoḥ || AMsa_11.66 ||
children.translated_text: from the experience of both the faults and the virtues. // AMsa_11.66 //

body.text: pratisaraṇamanaskāro bodhiprāptaye dānādīnāṃ pratisaraṇān neśvarādīnāṃ pratisaṃvinmanaskāro mātsaryadānādivipakṣapratipakṣayor doṣaguṇapratisaṃvedanāt |
body.translated_text: The mental attitude of refuge is from taking refuge in generosity and the rest for the attainment of awakening, not in <s>Īśvara</s> and the like. The mental attitude of experience is from experiencing the faults and virtues of the opponents and antidotes — avarice and generosity, and so forth.

children.translated_text: Joy in the recollection of accumulation, and the perception of great purpose,
desire for practice, [desire] for non-conceptualization, for its retention, and for the acquisition of conditions. // AMsa_11.67 //

body.text: cayānusmaraṇaprītimanaskāro dānādyupacaye puṇyajñānasaṃbhāropacayasaṃdarśanāt | māhārthyasaṃdarśanamanaskāro dānādīnāṃ bodhipakṣe bhāvārthena mahābodhiprāptyarthasaṃdarśanāt | abhilāṣamanaskāraḥ sa punaś caturvidhaḥ | yogābhilāṣamanaskāraḥ śamathavipaśyanāyogabhāvanābhilāṣāt | avikalpābhilāṣamanaskāraḥ pāramitāparipūraṇārtham upāyakauśalyābhilāṣāt | dhṛtyabhilāṣamanaskāraḥ pāramitādhipateyadharmārthadhāraṇābhilāṣāt | pratyayābhigamābhilāṣamanaskāraḥ samyakpraṇidhānābhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: The mental attitude of joy in the recollection of accumulation is from seeing, in the accumulation of generosity and the rest, the accumulation of the stores of merit and knowledge. The mental attitude of perceiving great purpose is from seeing that generosity and the rest have great purpose in the aids to awakening — seeing the purpose of attaining great awakening. The mental attitude of desire is, moreover, fourfold: the mental attitude of desire for practice is from the desire for the cultivation of the practice of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); the mental attitude of desire for non-conceptualization is from the desire for skillful means for the purpose of completing the <s>pāramitās</s>; the mental attitude of desire for retention is from the desire to retain the <s>Dharma</s> that is the object of the sovereignty of the <s>pāramitās</s>; the mental attitude of desire for the acquisition of conditions is from the intention of correct aspiration (<s>samyakpraṇidhāna</s>).

children.translated_text: Seeing the power to overcome sevenfold wrong grasping,

children.text: āścaryaṃ cāpyanāścaryaṃ saṃjñā caiva caturvidhā || AMsa_11.68 ||
children.translated_text: and wonder and non-wonder, and fourfold perception. // AMsa_11.68 //

body.text: saptaprakārāsadgrāhavyutthānaśaktidarśanamanaskāraḥ | saptavidho 'sadgrāhaḥ | asati sadgrāho doṣavati guṇavatvagrāho guṇavatyaguṇavatvagrāhaḥ | sarvasaṃskāreṣu ca nityasukhāsadgrāhau | sarvadharmeṣu cātmāsadgrāhaḥ nirvāṇe cāśāntāsadgrāhaḥ | yasya pratipakṣeṇa śūnyatāsamādhitrayaṃ dharmoddānacatuṣṭayaṃ ca deśyate | āścarye caturvidhasaṃjñāmanaskāraḥ | pāramitāsūdārasaṃjñā āyatatvasaṃjñā pratikāranirapekṣasaṃjñā vipākanirapekṣasaṃjñā ca | anāścarye 'pi caturvidhamanaskāraḥ | caturvidham anāścaryam audarya āyatatve ca sati pāramitānāṃ buddhatvaphalābhinivartanāt | asminn eva ca dvaye sati svaparasamacittāvasthāpanāt tadviśiṣṭebhyaś ca śarudibhyaḥ
body.translated_text: The mental attitude of seeing the power to overcome sevenfold wrong grasping: the sevenfold wrong grasping is — grasping as existent what does not exist; grasping as virtuous what is faulty; grasping as non-virtuous what is virtuous; in all conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāras</s>), the two wrong graspings of permanence and pleasure; in all <s>dharmas</s>, the wrong grasping of self; and in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the wrong grasping of non-peace. As the antidote to these, the three doors of liberation — emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) <s>samādhi</s> and the rest — and the fourfold <s>dharmôddāna</s> (summary of <s>Dharma</s>) are taught. The mental attitude of fourfold perception regarding wonder: noble perception regarding the <s>pāramitās</s>, perception of extensiveness, perception of disregard for recompense, and perception of disregard for the fruit of ripening. And the mental attitude of fourfold [perception] regarding non-wonder: the fourfold non-wonder — when there is nobility and extensiveness in the <s>pāramitās</s>, because of their leading to the fruit of Buddhahood; and in these same two, because of establishing an attitude of equality between self and others, and from those who are superior — <s>Śakra</s> and others
— upon obtaining worship and the like, disregard for recompense...

children.translated_text: Equality toward all beings, and also a vision of great-souled ones,
reciprocation of others' virtues — sixty-three [mental attitudes] in unbroken succession. // AMsa_11.69 //

body.text: ... pratyayakārāśaṃsanamanaskāro dānādiguṇapravṛttyā parebhyaḥ | āśāstimanaskāraḥ satveṣu tristhānāśaṃsanāt | pāramitānāṃ bodhisatvabhūminiṣṭhāyā buddhabhūminiṣṭhāyāḥ satvāvaraṇāśaṃsanā cca | nirantaramanaskāro dānādibhir avadhyakālakaraṇābhisaṃskaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: ... the mental attention of expressing expectations to others through engagement in qualities such as generosity and so forth is the mental attention of expectation; from aspiration toward beings in three domains, and aspiration toward the perfections for the completion of the Bodhisattva stages and the Buddha stage, and aspiration toward removing the obstructions of beings. The mental attention of continuity (nirantaramanaskāra) is from the conditioning of uninterrupted time through generosity and so forth.

children.translated_text: From practicing what was taught by the Buddha, from the intention of one not yet established [in the higher stages],
from the decrease and increase of that in beings — non-delight and delight. // AMsa_11.70 //

body.text: samyakprayogamanaskāro 'viparītānuṣṭhānād arvāgasthānamanasikāraṇāt | anāmodamanaskāro dānādibhir hīyamāneṣu | pramodamanaskāro dānādibhirvardhamāneṣu satveṣu |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of correct practice (samyakprayogamanaskāra) is from non-erroneous practice and from mentally attending as one not yet established [in the higher stages]. The mental attention of non-delight (anāmodamanaskāra) is toward beings who are declining in generosity and so forth. The mental attention of delight (pramodamanaskāra) is toward beings who are increasing in generosity and so forth.

children.translated_text: In the imitation, in the actual practice, and in cultivation — no distaste;
no mental attention of tolerance; for those determined to receive prediction — aspiration. // AMsa_11.71 //

body.text: arucimanaskāraḥ pāramitāprativarṇikā bhāvanāyāṃ | rucimanaskāro bhūtāyāṃ | anadhivāsanāmanaskāro mātsaryādivipakṣavinayanābhisaṃskāraṇāt | spṛhāmanaskāro dvividhiḥ pāramitāparipūrivyākaraṇalābhaspṛhāmanaskāraḥ pāramitāniyatabhūmyavasthālābhaspṛhāmanaskāraś ca |
body.translated_text: The mental attention of distaste (arucimanaskāra) is toward the imitation of the perfections in cultivation. The mental attention of relish (rucimanaskāra) is toward the actual [practice]. The mental attention of non-tolerance (anadhivāsanāmanaskāra) is from the conditioning of subjugating the opponents such as miserliness and so forth. The mental attention of aspiration (spṛhāmanaskāra) is twofold: the mental attention of aspiration for obtaining the prediction of the fulfillment of the perfections, and the mental attention of aspiration for obtaining the stage of being established on the determined ground of the perfections.

children.translated_text: From seeing in the future — the intention of conduct, equal regard,

children.text: agradharmeṣu vṛttyā ca agratvātmāvadhāraṇāt dhāraṇā || AMsa_11.72 ||
children.translated_text: and through conduct in the supreme dharmas — retention (dhāraṇā), from the determination of supremacy of oneself. // AMsa_11.72 //

body.text: āyatyāṃ darśanād vṛttimanaskāro yātvā gatiṃ gatvā bodhisatvena satā 'vaśyakaraṇīyatā 'bhisaṃskāraṇāt | dānādīnāṃ samatekṣaṇāmanaskāras tadanyair
body.translated_text: The mental attention of conduct from seeing in the future is from the conditioning of what must necessarily be done by a Bodhisattva having gone to [a particular] destiny. The mental attention of equal regard (samatekṣaṇāmanaskāra) toward generosity and so forth is for the purpose of the resolve toward continuous practice of the perfections with other

body.text: bodhisatvaiḥ sahātmanaḥ pāramitāsātatyakaraṇādhimokṣārthaṃ | agratvātmāvadhāraṇamanaskāraḥ pāramitāgradharmapravṛttyā svātmanaḥ pradhānabhāvasaṃdarśanāt |
body.translated_text: Bodhisattvas. The mental attention of determining one's own supremacy (agratvātmāvadhāraṇamanaskāra) is from demonstrating one's own preeminence through engaging in the supreme dharmas of the perfections.

children.translated_text: These wholesome mental attentions, following the ten perfections,

children.text: sarvadā bodhisatvānāṃ dhātupuṣṭau bhavanti hi || AMsa_11.73 ||
children.translated_text: always exist for Bodhisattvas in the nourishment of the element (dhātupuṣṭi). // AMsa_11.73 //

body.text: iti nigamanaśloko gatārthaḥ | dharmaparyeṣṭibhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the concluding verse, whose meaning has been explained. On the division of seeking the Dharma (dharmaparyeṣṭi), two verses:

children.text: puṣṭer adhyāśayato mahatī paryeṣṭir iṣyate dhīre |
children.translated_text: For the steadfast, a great seeking is accepted, from nourishment and from superior intention;

children.text: savivāsā hy avivāsā tathaiva vaibhutvikī teṣām || AMsa_11.74 ||
children.translated_text: with dwelling, without dwelling, and likewise pertaining to pervasiveness — these are theirs. // AMsa_11.74 //
Without body, with a light body, and with a full body — for Bodhisattvas;
with much pride, with subtle pride, and without pride — this is the desired seeking. // AMsa_11.75 //

body.text: trayodaśavidhā paryeṣṭiḥ | puṣṭitaḥ śrutādhimuktipuṣṭyā | adhyāśayato dharmamukhasrotasā | mahatī cittatvalābhināṃ | savipravāsā prathamā | avipravāsā dvitīyā vaibhutvikī tṛtīyā | akāyā śrutacintāmayī dharmakāyarahitatvāt | sakāyā bhāvanāmayī adhimukticaryābhūmau | laghukāyā saptasu bhūmiṣu | paripūrṇakāyā śeṣāsu | bahumānādhimukticaryābhūmau | sūkṣmamānā saptasu | nirmāṇā śeṣāsu | dharmahetutvaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The seeking is thirteenfold. 'From nourishment' means by the nourishment of learning and conviction (śrutādhimuktipuṣṭi). 'From superior intention' means by the stream of Dharma doors. 'Great' refers to those who have attained the reality of mind. The first is 'with dwelling.' The second is 'without dwelling.' The third is 'pertaining to pervasiveness.' 'Without body' is [seeking] born of learning and reflection, because of lacking the Dharmakāya. 'With body' is [seeking] born of meditation, on the stage of devotional practice (adhimukticaryābhūmi). 'With a light body' is on the seven stages. 'With a full body' is on the remaining [stages]. 'With much pride' is on the stage of devotional practice. 'With subtle pride' is on the seven [stages]. 'Without pride' is on the remaining [stages]. On seeking as the cause of Dharma, a verse:

children.translated_text: In form and formless [realms], Dharma is the cause of marks, and likewise of health;
in sovereignty, through superknowledges (abhijñā), and in the imperishability of that — for the steadfast. // AMsa_11.76 //

body.text: rūpe lakṣaṇahetur dharmaḥ | arūpe ārogyahetuḥ kleśavyādhipraśamanāt aiśvaryahetur abhijñābhis tadakṣayatvahetuś cānupadhiśeṣanirvāṇo 'pyanupacchedāt | ata evoktaṃ brahmaparipṛcchāsūtre | caturbhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisatvā dharmaṃ paryeṣante |
body.translated_text: In the form [realm], Dharma is the cause of marks. In the formless [realm], it is the cause of health, from the pacification of the disease of afflictions (kleśas). It is the cause of sovereignty through superknowledges. And it is the cause of imperishability of that, because even in nirvāṇa without remainder (anupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa) there is no cutting off. Hence it is said in the Brahmaparipṛcchā Sūtra: 'Bodhisattvas endowed with four dharmas seek the Dharma:

body.text: ratnasaṃjñayā durlabhārthena bhaiṣajyasaṃjñayā kleśavyādhipraśamanārthena arthasaṃjñayā avipraṇāśārthena nirvāṇasaṃjñayā sarvaduḥkhapraśamanārthena | ratnābhūtāni hi lakṣaṇāni śobhākaratvād atas taddhetutvād dharmaratnasaṃjñā | ārogyahetutvād bhaiṣajyasaṃjñā abhijñāiśvaryahetutvād arthasaṃjñā | tadakṣayahetutvān nirvāṇasaṃjñākṣayanirbhayatārthena | vikalpaparyeṣṭau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: with the perception of a jewel, for the purpose of what is rare; with the perception of medicine, for the purpose of pacifying the disease of afflictions; with the perception of wealth, for the purpose of non-loss; with the perception of nirvāṇa, for the purpose of pacifying all suffering.' For marks are like jewels because they produce beauty; hence the perception of Dharma as a jewel, since it is their cause. The perception of medicine is because of being the cause of health. The perception of wealth is because of being the cause of sovereignty through superknowledges. The perception of nirvāṇa is because of being the cause of imperishability — in the sense of freedom from fear through inexhaustibility. On the investigation of conceptual proliferation (vikalpa), a verse:

children.translated_text: Conceptualizations of non-existence, existence, superimposition, negation; of unity, diversity, intrinsic characteristic, and distinction;
conceptualizations of grasping names as according to meaning, and meaning as according to names — these are to be abandoned by the sons of the Jina. // AMsa_11.77 //

body.text: daśavidhavikalpo bodhisatvena parivarjanīyaḥ | abhāvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | prajñāpāramitāyām iha bodhisatvo bodhisatva eva sann iti | bhāvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | bodhisatvaṃ na samanupaśyatīty evam ādi | adhyāropavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | rūpaṃ śāriputra svabhāvena śūnyam iti | apavādavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | na śūnyatayeti | ekatvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | yā rūpasya śūnyatā na tadrūpam iti | nānātvavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | na cānyatra śūnyatāyā rūpaṃ rūpam eva śūnyatā śūnyataiva rūpam iti | svalakṣaṇavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | nāmamātram idaṃ yad idaṃ rūpam iti | viśeṣavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | rūpasya hi notpādo na nirodho na saṃkleśo na vyavadānam iti | yathānāmārthābhiniveśavikalpo yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | kṛtrimaṃ nāmety evam ādi | yathārthanāmābhiniveśavikalpaś ca yasya pratipakṣeṇāha | tāni bodhisatvaḥ sarvanāmāni na samanupaśyat yasamanupaśyan nābhiniviśate yathārthatayetya bhiprāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Tenfold conceptualization is to be abandoned by a Bodhisattva. The conceptualization of non-existence — as its antidote [the Prajñāpāramitā] says: 'Herein, a Bodhisattva being indeed a Bodhisattva...' The conceptualization of existence — as its antidote says: 'Does not perceive a Bodhisattva,' and so forth. The conceptualization of superimposition — as its antidote says: 'Form, Śāriputra, is empty by its own nature.' The conceptualization of negation — as its antidote says: 'Not by emptiness.' The conceptualization of unity — as its antidote says: 'That which is the emptiness of form is not that form.' The conceptualization of diversity — as its antidote says: 'Nor is form other than emptiness; form is precisely emptiness, emptiness is precisely form.' The conceptualization of intrinsic characteristic — as its antidote says: 'This which is called form is merely a name.' The conceptualization of distinction — as its antidote says: 'For form has no arising, no cessation, no defilement, no purification.' The conceptualization of grasping meaning according to name — as its antidote says: 'Name is constructed,' and so forth. And the conceptualization of grasping name according to meaning — as its antidote says: 'The Bodhisattva does not perceive all those names; not perceiving them, does not grasp them as according to their [supposed] meaning' — this is the intention.

children.text: iti śubhamatir etya yatnam ugraṃ dvayaparyeṣitadharmatāsatatvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, one of wholesome mind, having made intense effort, with the continuity of the dharmatā sought through both [truths],

children.text: pratiśaraṇamataḥ sadā prajānāṃ bhavati guṇaiḥ sa samudravat prapūrṇaḥ || AMsa_11.78 ||
children.translated_text: becomes a refuge for beings always, filled with qualities like the ocean. // AMsa_11.78 //

body.text:
anena nigamanaślokena paryeṣṭimāhātmyaṃ trividhaṃ darśayati | upāyamāhātmyam ugravīryatayā saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyadharmatāparyeṣaṇataś ca tatvaṃ satyam ity arthaḥ |
parārthamāhātmyaṃ pratiśaraṇībhāvāt prajānāṃ | sva-arthamāhātmyaṃ ca guṇaiḥ samudravat prapūrṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: By this concluding verse, the greatness of seeking the Dharma is shown in three ways: the greatness of method, through intense vigor and through seeking the dharmatā of both conventional and ultimate truths — 'continuity' means truth. The greatness of benefiting others, from becoming a refuge for beings. And the greatness of benefiting oneself, from being filled with qualities like the ocean.
In the Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra, the eleventh chapter on seeking the Dharma (dharmaparyeṣṭi).

CHAPTER XII
The twelfth chapter.
On the prohibition of miserliness regarding Dharma teaching, a verse:

children.text: prāṇān bhogāṃś ca dhīrāḥ pramuditamanasaḥ kṛcchralabdhān asārān satvebhyo duḥkhitebhyaḥ satatam avasṛjanty uccadānaprakāraiḥ |
children.translated_text: The steadfast, with delighted minds, constantly release with supreme forms of giving, to suffering beings, their lives and possessions — hard-won and insubstantial;

children.text: prāg evodāradharmaṃ hitakaram asakṛt sarvathaiva prajānāṃ kṛcchre naivopalabdhaṃ bhṛśamavasṛjatāṃ vṛddhigaṃ cāvyayaṃ ca || AMsa_12.1 ||
children.translated_text: how much more readily the noble Dharma, beneficial, repeatedly and in every way, to beings — not hard-won, and when released in abundance, only increasing and inexhaustible. // AMsa_12.1 //

body.text: kṛcchralabdhān apy asārān kṣayitvā prāṇān bhogāṃś ca bodhisatvā duḥkhitebhyaḥ kāruṇyāt satatam udārair visargair utsṛjanti prāg eva dharmaṃ yo naiva kṛcchreṇa vā bhṛśam api vāvasṛjatāṃ vṛddhiṃ gachati na kṣayaṃ | dharmanairarthakyasārthakye ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Bodhisattvas, out of compassion, constantly release through noble forms of generosity their lives and possessions — though hard-won, insubstantial, and perishable — to suffering beings; how much more readily the Dharma, which, even when released abundantly with great effort, increases and does not diminish. On the purposefulness and purposelessness of Dharma, two verses:

children.text: dharmo naiva ca deśito bhagavatā pratyātmavedyo yata ākṛṣṭā janatā ca yuktayuktivihitair dharmaiḥ svakīṃ dharmatāṃ |
children.translated_text: 'The Dharma was not taught by the Bhagavān, since it is to be known individually; yet beings are drawn by dharmas established through proper reasoning toward their own dharmatā;

children.text: svaśāntyāsyapuṭe viśuddhivipule sādhāraṇe 'thākṣaye lāleneva kṛpātmabhis tvajagaraprakhyaiḥ samāpāditā || AMsa_12.2 ||
children.translated_text: by those compassionate ones, resembling pythons, into the vast and pure mouth-cavity of their own peace — common [to all Buddhas] and inexhaustible — [beings] are brought as if being swallowed.' // AMsa_12.2 //

body.text: tatra buddhā ajagaropamās teṣāṃ svaśāntir āsyapuṭaṃ dharmakāyaḥ | viśuddhivipulaṃ savāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇaviśuddhitaḥ | sādhāraṇaṃ sarvabuddhaiḥ akṣayam ātyantikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, the Buddhas are like pythons; their 'mouth-cavity of their own peace' is the Dharmakāya. It is 'vast and pure' from purification of affliction-obstructions and knowledge-obstructions together with their latent impressions. It is 'common' to all Buddhas. It is 'inexhaustible' because of being ultimate.

children.text: tasmān naiva nirarthikā bhavati sā yā bhāvanā yogināṃ tasmān naiva nirarthikā bhavati sā yā deśanā saugatī |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, the meditation of yogins is not purposeless; therefore, the teaching of the Sugata is not purposeless.

children.text: dṛṣṭo 'rthaḥ śrutamātrakād yadi bhavet syād bhāvanāpārthikā aśrutvā yadi bhāvanām anuviśet syād deśanāpārthikā || AMsa_12.3 ||
children.translated_text: If the meaning were seen from mere hearing, then meditation would be purposeless; if one could enter [the meaning] without hearing through meditation, then teaching would be purposeless.' // AMsa_12.3 //

body.text: tasmān na nirarthikā yogināṃ bhāvanā bhavati pratyātmavedyasya dharmasya tadvaśenābhigamāt | na nirarthikā deśanā bhavati yuktivihitair dharmaiḥ svadharmatāyāṃ janatākarṣaṇāt | yathā punarbhāvanā sārthikā bhaved deśanā vā tat ślokārdhena darśayati | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | deśanāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the meditation of yogins is not purposeless, because the Dharma that is individually known is accessed through its power. Teaching is not purposeless, because beings are drawn toward their own dharmatā through dharmas established by reasoning. How meditation is purposeful and how teaching is [purposeful] — that is shown by the half-verse. The rest has been explained. On the division of teaching, a verse:

children.translated_text: From scripture (āgama), from realization (adhigama), from pervasiveness — the supreme teaching of beings:
from the mouth, from form, from all space, and also the utterance......... // AMsa_12.4 //

body.text: tatra vibhutvato yā mahābhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ | sarvato rūpādyā vṛkṣavāditrādibhyo 'pi niścarati | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | deśanāsaṃpattau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'from pervasiveness' is that of those established on the great stages (mahābhūmi). 'From all' means from form and so forth — it issues forth even from trees and musical instruments and so forth. The rest has been explained. On the accomplishment of teaching, two verses:

children.translated_text: Clear, doubt-removing, acceptable, truth-revealing, and twofold —
this accomplished teaching of Bodhisattvas should be known. // AMsa_12.5 //

body.text: ayaṃ catuṣkārthanirdeśena ślokaḥ | yad uktaṃ brahmaparipṛcchāyāṃ | caturbhir dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisatvā mahādharmadānaṃ vitaranti saddharmaparigrahaṇatayā ātmanaḥ prajñottāpanatayā satpuruṣakarmakaraṇatayā saṃkleśavyavadānasaṃdeśanatayā ca | ekena hi bāhuśrutyād viṣadā deśanā bhavati | dvitīyena mahāprājñatvāt saṃśayajahā pareṣāṃ saṃśayacchedāt | tṛtīyenānavadyakarmatvād ādeyā | caturthena tatvadarśikā dvividhā saṃkleśalakṣaṇasya ca tatvasya vyavadānalakṣaṇasya ca dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ satyābhyāṃ |
body.translated_text: This verse is an explanation of the fourfold meaning. As stated in the Brahmaparipṛcchā: 'Bodhisattvas endowed with four dharmas bestow the great gift of Dharma: through maintaining the true Dharma, through refining one's own wisdom, through performing the deeds of a true person, and through teaching defilement and purification.' For by the first, through great learning, teaching becomes clear. By the second, through great wisdom, it removes doubt — from cutting through others' doubts. By the third, through blameless conduct, it is acceptable. By the fourth, it reveals truth in two ways — the truth characterized by defilement and the truth characterized by purification — through the two truths respectively.

children.text: madhurā madavyapetā na ca khinnā deśanāgrasatvānāṃ |
children.translated_text: Sweet, free from intoxication, and unwearied — the teaching of supreme beings;
clear, varied, well-reasoned, flowing, without material [motive], and universal. // AMsa_12.6 //

body.text: asmin dvitīye śloke madhurā pareṇākṣiptasyāparuṣavacanāt | madavyapetā stutau siddhau vā madānanugamanāt | akhinnā akilāsikatvāt | sphuṭā nirācāryamuṣṭitvāt kṛtsnadeśanataḥ | citrā apunaruktatvāt | yuktā pramāṇāviruddhavāt | gamikā pratītapadavyañjanatvāt nirāmiṣā prasannādhikārānadhikatvāt | sarvatragā yānatrayagatatvāt | vāksaṃpattau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: In this second verse: 'sweet' — from speaking gently when challenged by others. 'Free from intoxication' — from not following pride when praised or successful. 'Unwearied' — from being indefatigable. 'Clear' — from teaching without a teacher's closed fist, teaching completely. 'Varied' — from non-repetition. 'Well-reasoned' — from not contradicting valid means of knowledge (pramāṇa). 'Flowing' — from using well-known words and expressions. 'Without material [motive]' — from not exceeding [what is appropriate] in occasions of faith and devotion. 'Universal' — from pertaining to the three vehicles. On the accomplishment of speech, a verse:

children.text: adīnā madhurā sūktā pratītā viṣadā tathā vāg jinātmaje |
children.translated_text: Undaunted, sweet, well-spoken, intelligible, clear — such is the speech of the sons of the Jina;

children.text: yathārhā nirāmiṣā ca parimitākṣayā tathā || AMsa_12.7 ||
children.translated_text: appropriate, without material [motive], and both measured and inexhaustible. // AMsa_12.7 //

body.text: adīnā paurī parṣanpūraṇāt | madhurā valguḥ | sūktā vispaṣṭā suniruktākṣaratvāt | pratītā vijñeyā pratītābhidhānatvāt | yathārhā śravaṇīyā vineyānurūpatvāt | anāmiṣā aniḥśritalābhasatkārā loke | pratatā apratikūlā | parimitā āyāmakhedāt | viṣadā aparyāttā | vyañjanasaṃpattau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Undaunted' — urbane, from filling the assembly. 'Sweet' — pleasant. 'Well-spoken' — distinct, from being clearly articulated. 'Intelligible' — knowable, from using intelligible expressions. 'Appropriate' — worth hearing, from being suited to those to be trained. 'Without material [motive]' — not dependent on gain and honor in the world. 'Extended' — not adverse. 'Measured' — from [avoiding] weariness of length. 'Clear' — unhesitating. On the accomplishment of phrasing, two verses:

children.translated_text: From synopsis, from detailed exposition, and likewise from conformity with the vehicles, from gentleness,
from intelligibility, from appropriateness, from leading to liberation, and from concordance — // AMsa_12.8 //

body.text: yuktaiḥ padavyañjanair uddeśāt pramāṇāvirodhena | sahitair nirdeśād uddeśāvirodhena | yānānulomanād ānulomikair yānatrayāvirodhena | ślākṣṇyād anucchavikair akaṣṭaśabdatayā | prātītyād aupayikaiḥ pratītārthatayā cārthopagamanāt | yāthārhāt pratirūpair vineyānurūpatayā | nairyāṇyāt pradakṣiṇair nirvāṇādhikāratayā | ānukūlyān nipakasyāṅgasaṃbhāraiḥ śaikṣasyāryāṣṭāṅgamārgānukūlyāt |
body.translated_text: With proper syllable-words, from indication (<s>uddeśa</s>), in non-contradiction with the means of valid knowledge; with consistent [words], from explanation (<s>nirdeśa</s>), in non-contradiction with the indication; with conforming [words], from conformity with the vehicles, in non-contradiction with the three vehicles; with smooth [words], from elegance, through freedom from harsh sounds; with reliable [words], from aptness, through having intelligible meaning and through the comprehension of meaning; with appropriate [words], from suitability, through conformity with those to be trained; with liberating [words], from leading to liberation, through having <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as their domain; with favorable limb-accumulations of a disciplined one, from being conducive — for a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>), from conformity with the Noble Eightfold Path.

children.translated_text: And this excellence of syllables (<s>vyañjanasaṃpad</s>) should be known as belonging to those who are foremost in every way.

children.text: ṣaṣṭyaṅgī sācintyā ghoṣo 'nantas tu sugatānāṃ || AMsa_12.9 ||
children.translated_text: It is sixty-fold and inconceivable; the voice of the <s>Sugatas</s> is infinite. // AMsa_12.9 //

body.text: ṣaṣṭyaṅgī sācintyā yā guhyakādhipatinirdeśe buddhasya ṣaṣṭyākārā vāg nirdiṣṭā | punar aparaṃ śāntamate tathāgatasya ṣaṣṭyākāropetā vāg niścarati snigdhā ca mṛdukā ca manojñā ca manoramā ca śuddhā ceti vistaraḥ | tatra
body.translated_text: 'Sixty-fold and inconceivable' — in the <s>Guhyakādhipati-nirdeśa</s>, the speech of the <s>Buddha</s> is described as having sixty aspects. Moreover, in the <s>Śāntamati</s> [sūtra], the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s speech goes forth endowed with sixty aspects: smooth, soft, pleasant, delightful, pure — and so forth in detail. Therein,

body.text:
snigdhā satvadhātukuśalamūlopastambhikatvāt | mṛdukā duṣṭa eva dharme sukhasaṃsparśatvāt | manojñā svarthatvāt | manoramā suvyañjanatvāt | śuddhā niruttaralokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhatvāt | vimalā sarvakleśānuśayavāsanāvisaṃyuktatvāt | prabhāsvarā pratītapadavyañjanatvāt | valguḥ sarvatīrthyakumatidṛṣṭivighātabalaguṇayuktatvāt | śravaṇīyā pratipattinairyāṇikatvāt | anantā sarvaparapravādibhir anāchedyatvāt | kalā rañjikatvāt | vinītā rāgādipratipakṣatvāt | akarkaśā śikṣāprajñaptisukhopāyatvāt | aparuṣā tadvyatikramasaṃpanniḥsaraṇopadeśakatvāt | suvinītā yānatrayanayopadeśikatvāt | karṇasukhā vikṣepapratipakṣatvāt | kāyaprahlādanakarī samādhyāvāhakatvāt | cittāudvilyakarī vipaśyanāprāmodyāvāhaphalakatvāt | hṛdayasaṃtuṣṭikarī saṃśayacchedikatvāt | prītisukhasaṃjananī mithyāniścayāpakarṣikatvāt | niḥparidāhā pratipattāvavipratisāratvāt | ājñeyā saṃpannaśrutamayajñānāśrayatvāt | vijñeyā saṃpannacintāmayajñānāśrayatvāt |
viṣpaṣṭā anācāryamuṣṭidharmavihitatvāt | premaṇīyā 'nuprāptasvaka-arthānāṃ premakaratvāt | abhinandanīyā 'nanuprāptasvakārthānāṃ spṛhaṇīyatvāt | ājñāpanīyā acintyadharmasamyagdarśikatvāt | vijñāpanīyā 'cintyadharmasamyagdeśikatvāt | yuktā pramāṇāviruddhatvāt | sahitā yathārhavineyadeśikatvāt | punaruktadoṣajahā avandhyatvāt | siṃhasvaravegā sarvatīrthyasaṃtrāsakatvāt | nāgasvaraśabdā udāratvāt | meghasvaraghoṣā gambhīratvāt | nāgendrarutā ādeyatvāt | kinnarasaṃgītighoṣā madhuratvāt | kalaviṅkasvararutaravitā 'bhīkṣṇabhaṅgaratvāt | brahmasvararutaravitā dūraṃgamatvāt | jīvaṃjīvakasvararutaravitā sarvasiddhipūrvaṃgamanaṅgalatvāt | devendramadhuranirghoṣā anatikramaṇīyatvāt | dundubhisvarā sarvamārapratyarthikavijayapūrvaṃgamatvāt | anunnatā stutyasaṃkliṣṭatvāt | anavanatā nindā'saṃkliṣṭatvāt | sarvaśabdānupraviṣṭā sarvavyākaraṇasarvākāralakṣaṇānupraviṣṭatvāt | apaśabdavigatā smṛtisaṃpramoṣe tadaniścaraṇatvāt | avikalā vineyakṛtyasarvakālapratyupasthitatvāt | alīnā lābhasatkārāniśritatvāt | adīnā sāvadyāpagatatvāt | pramuditā akheditvāt | prasṛtā sarvavidyāsthānakauśalyānugatatvāt | akhilā satvānāṃ tatsakalārthasaṃpādakatvāt | saritā prabandhānupacchinnatvāt | lalitā vicitrākārapratyupasthānatvāt | sarvasvarapūraṇī ekasvaranaikaśabdavijñaptipratyupasthāpanatvāt | sarvasatvendriyasaṃtoṣaṇī ekānekārthavijñaptipratyupasthānatvāt | aninditā yathāpratijñatvāt | acañcalā āgamitakālaprayuktatvāt | acapalā atvaramāṇavihitatvāt | sarvaparṣadanuravitā dūrāntikaparṣattulyaśravaṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Smooth' (<s>snigdhā</s>) because it supports the wholesome roots of the realm of beings. 'Soft' (<s>mṛdukā</s>) because it is pleasant to the touch even regarding corrupt <s>dharma</s>. 'Pleasant' (<s>manojñā</s>) because it conveys one's own meaning well. 'Delightful' (<s>manoramā</s>) because of excellent syllables. 'Pure' (<s>śuddhā</s>) because obtained subsequent to the unsurpassed supramundane. 'Stainless' (<s>vimalā</s>) because dissociated from the latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) of all afflictions. 'Luminous' (<s>prabhāsvarā</s>) because of intelligible words and syllables. 'Charming' (<s>valguḥ</s>) because endowed with the power and virtue to destroy the wrong views of all <s>tīrthikas</s>. 'Worth hearing' (<s>śravaṇīyā</s>) because leading to liberation through practice. 'Infinite' (<s>anantā</s>) because unbreakable by all opponents. 'Artful' (<s>kalā</s>) because it delights. 'Disciplined' (<s>vinītā</s>) because it is the antidote to desire and the like. 'Not harsh' (<s>akarkaśā</s>) because the means of prescribing training is gentle. 'Not rough' (<s>aparuṣā</s>) because of teaching the way of recovery from transgression thereof. 'Well-disciplined' (<s>suvinītā</s>) because of teaching the method of the three vehicles. 'Pleasing to the ear' (<s>karṇasukhā</s>) because it is the antidote to distraction. 'Causing bodily joy' (<s>kāyaprahlādanakarī</s>) because it brings about <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). 'Causing mental exhilaration' (<s>cittaudvilyakarī</s>) because it brings the fruit of joy through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). 'Causing satisfaction of the heart' (<s>hṛdayasaṃtuṣṭikarī</s>) because it cuts doubt. 'Generating joy and happiness' (<s>prītisukhasaṃjananī</s>) because it removes wrong certainty. 'Without remorse' (<s>niḥparidāhā</s>) because there is no regret in practice. 'To be known' (<s>ājñeyā</s>) because it is the basis of knowledge arising from learning. 'To be understood' (<s>vijñeyā</s>) because it is the basis of knowledge arising from reflection. 'Clear' (<s>viṣpaṣṭā</s>) because <s>dharma</s> is taught without a teacher's closed fist. 'Lovable' (<s>premaṇīyā</s>) because it inspires love in those who have attained their own aims. 'Delightful' (<s>abhinandanīyā</s>) because it is desirable for those who have not yet attained their own aims. 'Authoritative' (<s>ājñāpanīyā</s>) because it correctly shows inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>. 'Informative' (<s>vijñāpanīyā</s>) because it correctly teaches inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>. 'Reasonable' (<s>yuktā</s>) because not contradicting the means of valid knowledge. 'Consistent' (<s>sahitā</s>) because teaching to those worthy of being trained as befits them. 'Free from the fault of repetition' (<s>punaruktadoṣajahā</s>) because it is never fruitless. 'With the force of a lion's roar' (<s>siṃhasvaravegā</s>) because it causes terror to all <s>tīrthikas</s>. 'With the sound of an elephant' (<s>nāgasvaraśabdā</s>) because of its grandeur. 'With the resonance of thunder' (<s>meghasvaraghoṣā</s>) because of its profundity. 'With the cry of the lord of <s>nāgas</s>' (<s>nāgendrarutā</s>) because worthy of acceptance. 'With the melody of <s>kinnara</s> song' (<s>kinnarasaṃgītighoṣā</s>) because of its sweetness. 'With the sound of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird' (<s>kalaviṅkasvararutaravitā</s>) because of its continuous modulation. 'With the sound of <s>Brahmā</s>'s voice' (<s>brahmasvararutaravitā</s>) because it reaches far. 'With the sound of the <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> bird' (<s>jīvaṃjīvakasvararutaravitā</s>) because it is auspicious, preceding all accomplishments. 'With the sweet resonance of <s>Indra</s>' (<s>devendramadhuranirghoṣā</s>) because not to be transgressed. 'With the sound of a drum' (<s>dundubhisvarā</s>) because it precedes victory over all <s>Māra</s> opponents. 'Not elevated' (<s>anunnatā</s>) because unstained by praise. 'Not depressed' (<s>anavanatā</s>) because unstained by blame. 'Pervading all sounds' (<s>sarvaśabdānupraviṣṭā</s>) because pervading all grammars, all forms, and all characteristics. 'Free from incorrect speech' (<s>apaśabdavigatā</s>) because such does not arise when mindfulness is not lost. 'Complete' (<s>avikalā</s>) because always present for the duties of those to be trained at all times. 'Not withdrawn' (<s>alīnā</s>) because not dependent on gain and honor. 'Not dejected' (<s>adīnā</s>) because free from what is blameworthy. 'Joyful' (<s>pramuditā</s>) because indefatigable. 'Flowing forth' (<s>prasṛtā</s>) because following upon skill in all fields of knowledge. 'Entire' (<s>akhilā</s>) because accomplishing all the aims of beings completely. 'Streaming' (<s>saritā</s>) because the continuity is unbroken. 'Graceful' (<s>lalitā</s>) because presenting varied forms. 'Filling all tones' (<s>sarvasvarapūraṇī</s>) because presenting multiple word-communications in a single tone. 'Satisfying the faculties of all beings' (<s>sarvasatvendriyasaṃtoṣaṇī</s>) because presenting single and multiple meaning-communications. 'Blameless' (<s>aninditā</s>) because in accordance with what has been promised. 'Unwavering' (<s>acañcalā</s>) because applied at the appropriate time. 'Not hasty' (<s>acapalā</s>) because proceeding without haste. 'Resounding in all assemblies' (<s>sarvaparṣadanuravitā</s>) because heard equally by assemblies far and near.
Endowed with all excellent aspects, because it transforms all worldly meanings and illustrations into <s>Dharma</s>. On the greatness of teaching, four verses:

children.translated_text: With speech, with well-arranged words, with indication, division, and the cutting of doubt —
followed by elaboration, for those of quick understanding (<s>udghaṭitajña</s>) and detailed understanding (<s>vipañcitajña</s>). // AMsa_12.10 //

body.text: ākhyāti vācā | prajñāpayati padaiḥ suyuktaiḥ | prasthāpayati vibhājayati vivṛṇoti yathākramamuddeśavibhāgasaṃśayacchedaiḥ | uttānīkaroti uttānīkaraṇaṃ bahulīkārānugatā deśanā niścayabalādhānarthaṃ | deśayaty udghaṭitajñeṣu | saṃprakāśayati vipañcitajñeṣu |
body.translated_text: 'Declares' with speech. 'Makes known' with well-arranged words. 'Sets forth,' 'divides,' 'reveals' — respectively through indication (<s>uddeśa</s>), division (<s>vibhāga</s>), and the cutting of doubt (<s>saṃśayaccheda</s>). 'Makes clear' — making clear is teaching followed by elaboration, for the purpose of establishing certainty. 'Teaches' to those of quick understanding (<s>udghaṭitajña</s>). 'Illuminates' to those of detailed understanding (<s>vipañcitajña</s>).

children.text: śuddhā trimaṇḍalena hiteyaṃ deśanā hi buddhānāṃ |
children.translated_text: Pure through the three spheres, this teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> is beneficial —

children.text: doṣair vivarjitā punar aṣṭabhir eṣaiva vijñeyā || AMsa_12.11 ||
children.translated_text: free from eight faults — this very [teaching] should be known. // AMsa_12.11 //

body.text: śuddhā trimaṇḍaleneti | yena ca deśayati vācā padaiś ca | yathā coddeśādiprakāraiḥ | yeṣu codghaṭitavipañcitajñeṣu | eṣaiva ca deśanā punar aṣṭadoṣavivarjitā veditavyā yathākramaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Pure through the three spheres' means: by what one teaches — speech and words; how one teaches — through methods such as indication and so forth; and to whom — those of quick and detailed understanding.
