And this very teaching should be understood as free from eight faults, in due order:

children.text: kauśīdyam anavabodho hy avakāśasyākṛtir hy anītatvam |
children.translated_text: Laziness, lack of understanding, failure to provide opportunity, indeed failure to draw out [the meaning] —
failure to cut doubt, and failure to make firm the removal thereof. // AMsa_12.12 //

body.text: te punar aṣṭau doṣāḥ kauśīdyam anavasaṃbodhaḥ avakāśasyākaraṇaṃ anītārthatvaṃ saṃdehasyācchedanā tadvigamasyādṛḍhīkaraṇaṃ niścayasyety arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: These eight faults are: laziness, lack of understanding, failure to provide opportunity, failure to draw out the meaning, failure to cut doubt, and failure to make firm the removal thereof — that is, of certainty. This is the meaning.

children.text: khedo 'tha matsaritvaṃ doṣā hy ete matā kathāyāṃ hi |
children.translated_text: Weariness and then miserliness — these are considered faults in discourse;

children.text: tadabhāvād buddhānāṃ niruttarā deśanā bhavati || AMsa_12.13 ||
children.translated_text: through their absence, the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> becomes unsurpassed. // AMsa_12.13 //

body.text: khedo yenābhīkṣṇaṃ na deśayet | matsaritvaṃ cākṛtsnaprakāśantā | arthasaṃpattau ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: Weariness, by which one would not teach repeatedly; and miserliness, meaning incomplete revelation. On the excellence of meaning, two verses:

children.translated_text: This <s>Dharma</s> is excellent, being the cause of devotion, satisfaction, and wisdom —
twofold in meaning, easy to grasp, and expressing the fourfold holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). // AMsa_12.14 //
Solely through a practice unshared with others, fulfilling the destruction of the afflictions of the three realms,

children.text: svabhāvaśuddhaṃ malaśuddhitaś ca tac caturguṇabrahmavicaryam iṣyate || AMsa_12.15 ||
children.translated_text: pure by its own nature and through the purification of defilements — that fourfold holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is accepted. // AMsa_12.15 //

body.text: caturguṇabrahmacaryasaṃprakāśako dharmaḥ | ādimadhyaparyavasānakalyāṇo yathākramaṃ śrutacintābhāvanābhir bhaktituṣṭibuddhihetutvāt | tatra bhaktir adhimuktiḥ saṃpratyayaḥ tuṣṭiḥ prāmodyaṃ yuktinidhyānāc chakyaprāptitāṃ viditvā | buddhiḥ samāhitacittasya yathābhūtajñānaṃ | dvividhārtha ityataḥ svarthaḥ saṃvṛttiparamārthasatyayogāt | sugrāhya ityataḥ suvyañjanaḥ pratītapadavyañjanatvāt | caturguṇaṃ brahmacaryaṃ | kevalaṃ parair asādhāraṇatvāt paripūrṇaṃ tridhātukleśaprahāṇaparipūraṇāt | pariśuddhaṃ svabhāvaviśuddhito 'nāsravatvāt | paryavadātaṃ malaviśuddhitaḥ saṃtānaviśuddhyā kṣīṇāsravāṇāṃ | abhisaṃdhivibhāge ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> reveals the fourfold <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life). It is excellent at the beginning, middle, and end — respectively because of being the cause of devotion through learning, satisfaction through reflection, and wisdom through cultivation. Therein, 'devotion' (<s>bhakti</s>) is conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>), trust (<s>saṃpratyaya</s>). 'Satisfaction' (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is joy (<s>prāmodya</s>), through reasoning and meditation, having realized that it is achievable. 'Wisdom' (<s>buddhi</s>) is the knowledge of reality (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>) of one whose mind is concentrated. 'Twofold in meaning' — therefore it has its own meaning, through the conjunction of conventional and ultimate truths. 'Easy to grasp' — therefore well-expressed, through intelligible words and syllables. The fourfold <s>brahmacarya</s>: 'solely' (<s>kevala</s>) because unshared with others; 'complete' (<s>paripūrṇa</s>) because fulfilling the abandonment of the afflictions of the three realms; 'pure' (<s>pariśuddha</s>) by its own nature, because of being undefiled; 'purified' (<s>paryavadāta</s>) through purification of defilements, through the purification of the continuum of those whose outflows are destroyed. On the classification of intentions (<s>abhisaṃdhi</s>), two verses:

children.translated_text: The intention of entry (<s>avatāraṇasaṃdhi</s>), and the intention regarding characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇasaṃdhi</s>),

children.text: pratipakṣābhisaṃdhiś ca saṃdhiḥ pariṇatāv api || AMsa_12.16 ||
children.translated_text: the intention of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣābhisaṃdhi</s>), and the intention in transformation (<s>pariṇatasaṃdhi</s>). // AMsa_12.16 //
Regarding <s>śrāvakas</s>, regarding intrinsic natures, regarding the discipline of faults,

children.text: abhidhānasya gāmbhīrye saṃdhir eṣa caturvidhaḥ || AMsa_12.17 ||
children.translated_text: and regarding the profundity of expression — this intention is fourfold. // AMsa_12.17 //

body.text:
asāre sāramatayo viparyāse ca susthitāḥ |
kleśena ca susaṃkliṣṭā labhante bodhimuktamāṃ || AMsa_12.17* || || iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who consider the essenceless as having essence, who are well-established in error, and who are thoroughly afflicted by afflictions — they attain the supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>).' // AMsa_12.17* // // Thus //

body.text: caturvidho 'bhisaṃdhirdeśanāyāṃ buddhasya veditavyaḥ | avatāraṇābhisaṃdhir lakṣaṇābhisaṃdhiḥ pratipakṣābhisaṃdhiḥ pariṇāmana-abhisaṃdhiśca | tatrāvatāraṇābhisaṃdhiḥ śrāvakeṣu draṣṭavyaḥ | śāsanāvatāraṇārtham anuttrāsāya rūpādyastitvadeśanāt | lakṣaṇābhisaṃdhis triṣu parikalpitādisv abhāveṣu draṣṭavyo niḥsvabhāvānutpannādisarvadharmadeśanāt | pratipakṣābhisaṃdhir doṣāṇāṃ vinaye draṣṭavyo yathāṣṭāvaraṇapratipakṣāgrayānasaṃbhāṣānuśaṃse gāthādvayaṃ vakṣyati | pariṇāmanābhisaṃdhir abhidhānagāmbhīrye draṣṭavyo yathāha |
body.translated_text: The fourfold intention (<s>abhisaṃdhi</s>) in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching should be understood: the intention of entry (<s>avatāraṇābhisaṃdhi</s>), the intention regarding characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇābhisaṃdhi</s>), the intention of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣābhisaṃdhi</s>), and the intention of transformation (<s>pariṇāmanābhisaṃdhi</s>). Therein, the intention of entry should be seen regarding <s>śrāvakas</s> — because of teaching the existence of form and so forth, in order to facilitate entry into the teaching, so as not to terrify [them]. The intention regarding characteristics should be seen regarding the three — the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and so forth — [which are] non-existent, because of teaching that all <s>dharmas</s> are without self-nature, unborn, and so forth. The intention of the antidote should be seen regarding the discipline of faults — as in the two verses to be stated on the benefit of conversing with the foremost vehicle as an antidote to the eight obstructions. The intention of transformation should be seen regarding the profundity of expression, as it is said:

children.translated_text: 'Those who consider the essenceless as having essence, who are happy in error,

children.text: kleśena ca susaṃkliṣṭā labhante bodhim uttamāṃ || iti
children.translated_text: and who are thoroughly afflicted by afflictions — they attain the supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>).' // Thus //

body.text: ayam atrābhisaṃdhiḥ | asāre sāramataya ity avikṣepe yeṣāṃ sārabuddhiḥ pradhānabuddhirvikṣepo hi visāraś cetasaḥ | viparyāse ca susthitā iti nityasukhaśucyātmagrāhaviparyayeṇānityādike viparyāse susthitā aparihāṇitaḥ | kleśena ca sa saṃkliṣṭā iti dīrghaduṣkaravyāyām aśrameṇātyarthaṃ parikliṣṭāḥ | abhiprāyavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Herein, this is the intention: 'Those who consider the essenceless as having essence' — regarding non-distraction (<s>avikṣepa</s>), those for whom essence-perception is primary — for distraction is indeed the dissipation of the mind. 'Well-established in error' — well-established in the error of grasping permanence, happiness, purity, and self, [meaning] well-established regarding the error [of contemplating] impermanence and so forth, through non-regression. 'Thoroughly afflicted by affliction' — through the long, difficult, and arduous effort, they are thoroughly afflicted without weariness. On the classification of special purposes (<s>abhiprāya</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: Regarding sameness, regarding another meaning, and likewise regarding another time,
and regarding the disposition of a person — the special purpose (<s>abhiprāya</s>) is fourfold. // AMsa_12.18 //

body.text: caturvidho 'bhiprāyaḥ | satatābhiprāyo yad āha | aham eva sa tasmin samaye vipaśvī samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūvam ity aviśiṣṭadharmakāyatvāt | arthāntarābhiprāyo yad āha | niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā anutpannā ity evam ādi ayathārutārthatvāt kālāntarābhiprāyo yadāha | ye sukhāvatyāṃ prāṇidhānaṃ kariṣyanti te tatropapatsyanta iti kālāntareṇety abhiprāyaḥ | pudgalāśayābhiprāyo yat tad eva kuśalamūlaṃ kasyacit praśaṃsate kasyacid vigarhate 'lpamātrasaṃtuṣṭasya vaipulyasaṃgrahāt mahāyānasūtrāntasānuśaṃsaṃ gāthādvayam upādāyāha |
body.translated_text: The fourfold special purpose (<s>abhiprāya</s>): The purpose of sameness (<s>samatābhiprāya</s>) — as he said: 'I myself at that time was <s>Vipaśvin</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One,' because of the non-distinction of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. The purpose regarding another meaning (<s>arthāntarābhiprāya</s>) — as he said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self-nature, unborn,' and so forth, because the meaning is not as literally stated. The purpose regarding another time (<s>kālāntarābhiprāya</s>) — as he said: 'Those who make aspirations for <s>Sukhāvatī</s> will be reborn there,' meaning 'at another time' — this is the special purpose. The purpose regarding the disposition of a person (<s>pudgalāśayābhiprāya</s>) — when he praises one and the same wholesome root for one person and censures it for another, [such as] one who is content with a small measure, in order to gather [them] into the vast. Taking up two verses on the benefit of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtras, he said:

children.translated_text: Disrespect toward the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>, laziness, contentment with a small measure,

children.text: rāge māne caritaṃ kaukṛtaṃ cāniyatabhedaḥ || AMsa_12.19 ||
children.translated_text: conduct in desire, in pride, and regret — these are the divisions of the unfixed class (<s>aniyata</s>). // AMsa_12.19 //
This is the obstruction of beings; its antidote is conversation with the foremost vehicle (<s>agrayāna</s>);
the abandonment of all faults that are obstacles thereby comes about. // AMsa_12.20 //
One who applies oneself to retaining the two verses, whether by text or by meaning —

children.text: sa hi daśavidhamanuśaṃsaṃ labhate satvottamo dhīmān || AMsa_12.21 ||
children.translated_text: that supreme, wise being obtains a tenfold benefit. // AMsa_12.21 //

children.text: kṛtsnāṃ ca dhātupuṣṭiṃ prāmodyaṃ cottamaṃ maraṇakāle |
children.translated_text: Complete nourishment of the elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and supreme joy at the time of death,

children.text: janma ca yathābhikāmaṃ jātismaratāṃ ca sarvatra || AMsa_12.22 ||
children.translated_text: birth as one wishes, and the remembrance of past lives everywhere. // AMsa_12.22 //

children.text: buddhaiś ca samavadhānaṃ tebhyaḥ śravaṇaṃ tathāgrayān asya |
children.translated_text: Encounter with <s>Buddhas</s>, hearing from them the foremost vehicle (<s>agrayāna</s>),

children.text: adhimuktiṃ saha buddhyā dvayamukhatām āśubodhiṃ ca || AMsa_12.23 ||
children.translated_text: conviction together with wisdom, the twofold gateway, and swift awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). // AMsa_12.23 //

body.text: buddhe dharme 'vajñeti pañca gāthāḥ | tatrāniyatabhedo bodhisatvānām aniyatānāṃ mahāyānadbhedaḥ | agrayān asaṃbhāṣā yā mahāyānadeśanā | buddhe 'vajñāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | aham eva sa tena kālena vipaśvī samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūvam iti | dharme 'vajñāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | iyato gaṃgānadīvālikāsamānabuddhān paryupāsya mahāyāne 'vabodha utpadyata iti | kauśīdyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | ye sukhāvatyāṃ praṇidhānaṃ kariṣyanti te tatropapatsyanta iti | vimalacandraprabhasya ca tathāgatasya nāmadheyagrahaṇamātreṇa niyato bhavaty unattarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāv iti | alpamātrasaṃtuṣṭyāvarasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | yatra bhagavān kvacid dānādi vivarṇayati anyatra varṇitavān | rāgacaritasya cāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | yatra bhagavān buddhakṣetravibhūtiṃ varṇayati | mānacaritasyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | yatra bhagavān kasyacid buddhasyādhikāṃ saṃpattiṃ varṇayati | kaukṛtyāvaraṇasya
body.translated_text: On non-contempt toward the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>, five verses. Therein, the distinction of the indeterminate is the distinction of the indeterminate among <s>Bodhisattvas</s> regarding the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The supreme vehicle — the discourse that is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> teaching. The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of contempt for the <s>Buddha</s>: 'I myself was at that time <s>Vipaśvī</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One.' The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of contempt for the <s>Dharma</s>: 'Having attended upon <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, understanding arises in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.' The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of laziness: 'Those who will make the vow toward <s>Sukhāvatī</s> will be reborn there.' And: 'By merely holding the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vimalacandraprabha</s>, one becomes determined toward unsurpassed perfect awakening.' The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of contentment with the merely small: where the <s>Bhagavān</s> somewhere disparages giving and the like, having praised them elsewhere. The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of one of passionate temperament: where the <s>Bhagavān</s> describes the splendors of <s>Buddha</s>-fields. The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of one of proud temperament: where the <s>Bhagavān</s> describes the superior attainments of a certain <s>Buddha</s>. The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of remorse

body.text: pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | ye buddhabodhisatveṣv akāraṃ kariṣyanti te sarve svargopagā bhaviṣyantīti | aniyatabhedasyāvaraṇasya pratipakṣasaṃbhāṣā | mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ buddhatve vyākaraṇadeśanā ekayānadeśanā ca | kṛtsnadhātupuṣṭiḥ sarvamahāyānādhiṣṭhānāya dhātupuṣṭis tadāvaraṇavigamāt sarvatra mahāyāne 'dhimuktilābhataḥ | dvayamukhatā samādhimukhatā dhāraṇīmukhatā ca | dṛṣṭe dharme dvividho 'nuśaṃsaḥ sāṃparāyike 'ṣṭavidhaḥ krameṇottarāuttaraviśeṣalābhād veditavyaḥ | deśanānuśaṃse ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: : 'Those who will perform a deed toward <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — they will all become ones who go to heaven.' The discourse that is the antidote to the obstruction of the distinction of the indeterminate: the teaching of the prediction of <s>Buddhahood</s> for the great <s>śrāvakas</s>, and the teaching of the One Vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>). The complete nourishing of the element is the nourishing of the element for the establishment of the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through the removal of those obstructions — from obtaining faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> everywhere. The twofold gateway is the gateway of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and the gateway of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention). In the present life, the benefit is twofold; in the next life, it is eightfold, to be understood through the successive attainment of ever-higher distinctions. A verse on the benefit of teaching:

children.text: iti sugatirakhedavān kṛpāluḥ prathitayaśāḥ suvidhijñatām upetaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, possessing a good destiny, unwearied, compassionate, of renowned fame, endowed with knowledge of proper method,

children.text: bhavati sukathiko hi bodhisatvas tapati jane kathitair yathaiva sūryaḥ || AMsa_12.24 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> becomes a good speaker and shines among beings like the sun through his teachings. // AMsa_12.24 //

body.text: pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sukathikatvaṃ | sūryavat pratapanaṃ cānuśaṃsaḥ | lokāvarjanato bahumatatvāt | pañca kāraṇāni sukathikatvasya yenāviparītaṃ darśayati abhīkṣṇaṃ nirāmiṣacitta ādeyavākyavineyānurūpaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: Good speakership is due to five causes. And shining like the sun is the benefit — from winning over the world, due to being highly esteemed. The five causes of good speakership, by which one teaches correctly: frequently, with a mind free from material gain, with credible speech, and in accordance with those to be trained.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the twelfth chapter on teaching.

CHAPTER XIII
The thirteenth chapter.
On the classification of practice, six verses:

children.translated_text: Having understood the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) — of persons and of <s>dharmas</s> — the wise one
should abandon the wrong and the right regarding duality, by means of three [samādhis]. // AMsa_13.1 //

body.text: yathārtham ājñāya dharmamājñāya dharmānudharmapratipanno bhavati sāmīcīpratipanno 'nudharmacārī tatsaṃdarśayati | tatra dvidhā pudgaladharmanairātmyajñānaṃ grāhyagrāhakābhāvataḥ | dvayamithyātvasamyaktvaṃ vivarjyaṃ trayaṃ | abhāve ca śūnyatāsamādhiḥ parikalpitasya svabhāvasya | bhāve cāpraṇihitānimittau paratantraniṣpannayoḥ svabhāvayoḥ |
body.translated_text: Having understood [things] as they are, having understood the <s>Dharma</s>, one becomes one who practices in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>, one who practices correctly, one who conducts oneself in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> — this is shown. Therein, the twofold knowledge of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> is from the non-existence of the grasped and the grasper. The wrong and right of duality that should be abandoned is threefold: in non-existence, the <s>śūnyatā-samādhi</s> (emptiness concentration) — regarding the imagined self-nature; in existence, the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>) and wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>) [concentrations] — regarding the dependent and the consummate self-natures.

body.text: etat samādhitrayaṃ laukikaṃ na mithyātvaṃ lokottarajñānāvāhanāt | na samyaktvam alokottaratvāt |
body.translated_text: This threefold <s>samādhi</s> is mundane — it is not wrong, because it leads to supramundane knowledge; nor is it right, because it is not supramundane.

children.translated_text: One who knows the meaning, knowing the similarity of all <s>dharmas</s> to a sheath,
for the abandonment of contentment with mere learning — therefore he is called a knower of the <s>Dharma</s>. // AMsa_13.2 //

body.text: evam arthajñaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sūtrādīnāṃ kolopamatāṃ jānāti | śrutamātrasaṃtuṣṭiprahāṇāya tena dharmajño bhavati |
body.translated_text: Thus, one who knows the meaning knows the similarity of all <s>dharmas</s> — <s>sūtras</s> and the rest — to a sheath. He becomes a knower of the <s>Dharma</s> for the purpose of abandoning contentment with mere learning.

children.translated_text: Having penetrated duality through the knowledge of an ordinary being,
for the perfection of that knowledge, one practices in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>. // AMsa_13.3 //

body.text: etena dvividhena pārthagjanenārthadharmajñānena dvayaṃ nairātmyabhāvaṃ pratividhya yathākramaṃ tasya jñānasya pariniṣpattyarthaṃ pratipadyate | evam anudharmaṃ pratipadyate |
body.translated_text: Having penetrated duality — the state of selflessness — through this twofold knowledge of meaning and <s>Dharma</s> belonging to an ordinary being, one practices for the perfection of that knowledge, respectively. Thus one practices in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.translated_text: Then one obtains that supramundane, unsurpassed knowledge,

children.text: ādibhūmau samaṃ sarvair bodhisatvais tadātmabhiḥ || AMsa_13.4 ||
children.translated_text: on the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), equal with all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of that nature. // AMsa_13.4 //

body.text: tato jñānaṃ sa labhate lokottaramanuttaram iti | viśiṣṭatarayānābhāvāt | ādibhūmau pramuditāyāṃ bhūmau samaṃ sarvair bodhisatvais tadātmabhir iti tadbhūmikair evaṃ sāmīcīpratipanno bhavati tadbhūmikabodhisatvasamatayā |
body.translated_text: 'Then one obtains that supramundane, unsurpassed knowledge' — because there is no more distinguished vehicle. 'On the first stage' — on the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) stage, 'equal with all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of that nature' — that is, with those of that stage. Thus one practices correctly, through equality with the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of that stage.

children.translated_text: Having made a complete destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that are to be abandoned and that are the objects of the knowledge of seeing,
one applies oneself to the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) for the knowledge leading to the abandonment of the cognitive obscuration (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). // AMsa_13.5 //

body.translated_text: The verse is self-explanatory.

children.translated_text: With the knowledge of the establishment [of stages], non-conceptual, as a companion,

children.text: anudharmaṃ caraty evaṃ pariśiṣṭāsu bhūmiṣu || AMsa_13.6 ||
children.translated_text: one thus conducts oneself in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> on the remaining stages. // AMsa_13.6 //

body.translated_text: The remainder shows the conduct in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>. 'With the knowledge of the establishment [of stages], non-conceptual' — with the knowledge of the establishment of the stages, and non-conceptual

body.text: ca | sahacāriṇety anusaṃbaddhacāriṇā anyonyanairantaryeṇa | etena ślokadvayenānudharmacāritvaṃ darśitaṃ | pratipattāv apramādakriyāyāṃ catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: ; 'as a companion' — as a continuously accompanying companion, without interruption between the two. By these two verses, the conduct in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s> has been shown. On the act of diligence (<s>apramāda</s>) in practice, four verses:

children.translated_text: Easy to obtain [requisites], well-situated, good ground, good companions,

children.text: suyogo guṇavān deśo yatra dhīmān prapadyate || AMsa_13.7 ||
children.translated_text: well-suited for practice, a virtuous place — where the wise one takes up [residence]. // AMsa_13.7 //

body.text: caturbhiś cakrair apramādakriyāṃ darśayati pratirūpadeśavāsādibhiḥ | tatrānena ślokena pratirūpadeśavāsaṃ darśayati | sulābhaś cīvarapiṇḍapātādīnāṃ jīvitapariṣkārāṇām akṛcchena lābhāt | svadhiṣṭhāno durjanair dasyuprabhṛtibhir anadhiṣṭhitatvāt | subhūmir ārogyabhūmitvāt | susahāyakaḥ sabhāgaśīladṛṣṭisahāyakatvāt | suyogo divālpākīrṇābhilāpakatvāt rātrau cālpaśabdādikatvāt |
body.translated_text: The act of diligence is shown by means of four wheels, beginning with dwelling in a suitable place. Therein, by this verse, dwelling in a suitable place is shown. 'Easy to obtain' — because of obtaining the necessities of life such as robes, alms-food, and the like without difficulty. 'Well-situated' — because of not being occupied by wicked people such as bandits and the like. 'Good ground' — because of being a healthy region. 'Good companions' — because of having companions of like moral conduct and views. 'Well-suited for practice' — because of having few crowds and little chatter by day, and little noise and the like by night.

children.translated_text: Learned, one who has seen the truth, eloquent, sympathetic,

children.text: akhinno bodhisatvaś ca jñeyaḥ satpurūṣo mahān || AMsa_13.8 ||
children.translated_text: unwearied — such a <s>Bodhisattva</s> should be known as a great, noble person. // AMsa_13.8 //

body.translated_text: By this second [verse], the noble person is shown — through the qualities of scriptural learning, realization, skill in speech, selfless mind, and indefatigability.

children.translated_text: Well-grounded in its object, well-furnished with accumulations, well-stabilized, well-cultivated as taught,
with a good method of progress — such is one's own correct exertion. // AMsa_13.9 //

body.text: anena tṛtīyena yoniśomanaskārasaṃgṛhītāmātmanaḥ samyakpraṇidhānatāṃ darśayati | saddharmālambanatayā susaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāratayā śamathādinimittānāṃ kālena kālaṃ bhāvanātayā alpamātrāsaṃtuṣṭitayā satyuttarakaraṇīye sātatyasatkṛtyaprayogatayā ca |
body.translated_text: By this third [verse], one's own correct exertion, comprised in wise attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>), is shown: through having the true <s>Dharma</s> as object, through having well-gathered accumulations, through cultivating the signs of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and the like from time to time, through not being content with the merely small, and through the practice of continuity and earnestness regarding what truly still needs to be done.

children.translated_text: The cause of delight, of obtaining a [favorable] moment, of health,

children.text: samādher vicayasyāpi pūrve hi kṛtapuṇyatā || AMsa_13.10 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and of discernment — is indeed the merit made previously. // AMsa_13.10 //

body.text: anena caturthena pūrvakṛtapuṇyatāṃ pañcavidhena hetutvena darśayati | ratihetutvena yataḥ pratirūpadaśavāse 'bhiramate | kṣaṇaupapattihetutvena yataḥ satpuruṣāyāśrayaṃ
body.translated_text: By this fourth [verse], the merit previously made is shown through its fivefold causal function: as the cause of delight, since one delights in dwelling in a suitable place; as the cause of obtaining a [favorable] moment, since one obtains the support of a noble person

body.text: labhate | ārogyasamādhiprajñāhetutvena ca yata ātmanaḥ samyakpraṇidhānaṃ saṃpadyate | kleśata eva kleśaniḥsaraṇe ślokās trayaḥ |
body.translated_text: ; and as the cause of health, <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom, since one's own correct exertion succeeds. On escape from defilements through the defilements themselves, three verses:

children.translated_text: Since no <s>dharma</s> exists that is released from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>),

children.text: tasmād rāgādayas teṣāṃ buddhair niḥsaraṇaṃ matāḥ || AMsa_13.11 ||
children.translated_text: therefore desire and the like are themselves considered by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the escape from those [defilements]. // AMsa_13.11 //

body.text: yad uktaṃ bhagavatā | nāham anyatra rāgād rāgasya niḥsaraṇaṃ vadāmy evaṃ dveṣān mohād iti | tatrābhisaṃdhiṃ darśayati | yasmād dharmadhātuvinirmukto dharmo nāsti dharmatāvyatirekeṇa dharmābhāvāt | tasmād rāgādidharmatāpi rāgādyākhyāṃ labhate sa ca niḥsaraṇaṃ rāgādīnām ity evaṃ tatrābhisaṃdhir veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: As stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I do not speak of the escape from desire as being other than desire; likewise for hatred, for delusion.' Therein, the hidden intention is shown: since no <s>dharma</s> exists released from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — because of the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> apart from <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of <s>dharmas</s>) — therefore, the <s>dharmatā</s> of desire and the like also receives the name of desire and the like, and that [<s>dharmatā</s>] is the escape from desire and the like. Thus the hidden intention therein should be understood.

children.translated_text: Since no <s>dharma</s> exists that is released from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,

children.text: tasmāt saṃkleśanirdeśe sa saṃvid dhīmatāṃ mataḥ || AMsa_13.12 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, in the exposition of defilement, that [<s>dharmatā</s>] is considered by the wise as [true] knowledge. // AMsa_13.12 //

body.text: yad uktaṃ | avidyā ca bodhiś caikam iti | tatrāpi sakleśanirdeśe sa evābhisaṃdhiḥ | avidyā bodhidharmatā syāt tad upacārāt |
body.translated_text: As was said: 'Ignorance and awakening are one.' Therein too, in the exposition of defilement, the same hidden intention applies — ignorance would be the <s>dharmatā</s> of awakening, through metaphorical designation.

children.text: yatas tān eva rāgādīn yoniśaḥ pratipadyate |
children.translated_text: Since one wisely practices with regard to those very [defilements] — desire and the like —

children.text: tato vimucyate tebhyas tenaiṣāṃ niḥsṛtis tataḥ || AMsa_13.13 ||
children.translated_text: one is thereby freed from them; therefore, escape from them is through those [defilements] themselves. // AMsa_13.13 //

body.text: tān eva rāgādīn yoniśaḥ pratipadyamānas tebhyo vimucyate tasmāt parijñātās ta eva teṣāṃ niḥsaraṇaṃ bhavatīty ayam atrābhisaṃdhiḥ | śrāvakapratyekabuddhamanasikāraparivarjane ślokadvayaṃ |
body.translated_text: By wisely practicing with regard to those very [defilements] — desire and the like — one is freed from them; therefore, those [defilements], when fully understood, are themselves the escape from those [defilements]. This is the hidden intention herein. On the avoidance of the mental attitudes of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, two verses:

children.text: na khalu jinasutānāṃ bādhakaṃ duḥkhamugraṃ narakabhavanavāsaiḥ satvahetoḥ kathaṃcit |
children.translated_text: Indeed, fierce suffering that torments is not at all an obstacle for the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, even through dwelling in the hells, for the sake of beings;

children.text: śamabhavaguṇadoṣapreritā hīnayāne vividhaśubhavikalpā bādhakā dhīmatāṃ tu || AMsa_13.14 ||
children.translated_text: but for the wise, the various wholesome conceptualizations in the inferior vehicle, driven by [the perception of] the virtues and faults of peace and existence, are the [true] obstacle. // AMsa_13.14 //

children.text: na khalu narakavāso dhīmatāṃ sarvakālaṃ vimalavipulabodherantarāyaṃ karoti |
children.translated_text: Indeed, dwelling in the hells does not at all, at any time, create an obstacle to the stainless, vast awakening of the wise;

children.text: svahitaparamaśītas tvanyayāne vikalpaḥ paramasukhavihāre 'pyantarāyaṃ karoti || AMsa_13.15 ||
children.translated_text: but the conceptualization in the other [inferior] vehicle, intent upon supreme personal welfare, creates an obstacle even in the abode of supreme bliss. // AMsa_13.15 //

body.text:
anayoḥ ślokayor ekasya dvitīyaḥ sādhakaḥ | ubhau gatārtho |
niḥsvabhāvatāprakṛtipariśuddhitrāsapratiṣedhe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text:
Of these two verses, the second proves the first. Both are self-explanatory.
On the dispelling of fear regarding essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) and natural purity, four verses:

children.translated_text: The non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> and [their] apprehension, and purity through freedom from defilement —
should be understood as resembling an illusion and the like, and likewise as resembling space. // AMsa_13.16 //

children.text: yathaiva citre vidhivadvicitrite natonnataṃ nasti ca dṛśyate 'tha ca |
children.translated_text: Just as in a painting skillfully executed, there is no height and depth, yet it is seen;

children.text: abhūtakalpe 'pi tathaiva sarvathā dvayaṃ sadā nasti ca dṛśyate 'the ca || AMsa_13.17 ||
children.translated_text: so too in unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtakalpa</s>), in every way, duality never exists, yet it is always seen. // AMsa_13.17 //

children.text: yathaiva toye lutiṭite prasādite na jāyate sā punar acchatānyataḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as when turbid water is purified, its clarity does not arise from something other;

children.text: malāpakarṣas tu sa tatra kevalaḥ svacittaśuddhau vidhir eṣa eva hi || AMsa_13.18 ||
children.translated_text: it is merely the removal of impurities therein — this is indeed the method in the purification of one's own mind. // AMsa_13.18 //

children.text: mataṃ ca cittaṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaraṃ sadā tadāgantukadoṣadūṣitaṃ |
children.translated_text: And mind is considered to be luminous by nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>), always defiled by adventitious faults;

children.text: na dharmatācittamṛte 'nyacetasaḥ prabhāsvaratvaṃ prakṛtau vidhīyate || AMsa_13.19 ||
children.translated_text: apart from the <s>dharmatā</s>-mind, no luminosity in its [innate] nature is established for any other mind. // AMsa_13.19 //

body.text: dharmābhāvaś ca dharmopalabdhiś ceti trāsasthānaṃ niḥsaṃkleśatā ca dharmadhātoḥ prakṛtyā viśuddhatā ca paścād iti trāsasthānaṃ bālānāṃ | tadyathākramaṃ māyādisādṛśyenākāśasādṛśyena ca prasādhayaṃs tatas trāsaṃ pratiṣedhayati | tathā citre natonnatasādṛśyena lutitaprasāditatoyasādṛśyena ca yathākramaṃ | caturthena ślokena toyasādharmyaṃ citte pratipādayati | yathā toyaṃ prakṛtyā prasannam āgantukena tu kāluṣyeṇa lutitaṃ bhavaty evaṃ cittaṃ prakṛtyā prabhāsvaraṃ matam āgantukais tu doṣair dūṣitam iti | na ca dharmatācittād ṛte 'nyasya cetasaḥ paratantralakṣaṇasya prakṛtiprabhāsvaratvaṃ vidhīyate | tasmāc cittatathataivātra cittaṃ veditavyaṃ | rāgajāpattipratiṣedhe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: The non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> and the apprehension of <s>dharmas</s> — this is a cause of fear; and that the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is free from defilement and naturally pure — this too is a cause of fear for the foolish. Accordingly, he dispels that fear by establishing it through the analogy of illusion and the like, and the analogy of space, respectively. Likewise, through the analogy of height and depth in a painting, and through the analogy of turbid and clarified water, respectively. By the fourth verse, the analogy of water is applied to the mind: just as water is naturally clear but becomes turbid through adventitious impurities, so the mind is considered to be naturally luminous but defiled by adventitious faults. And apart from the <s>dharmatā</s>-mind, luminosity in its [innate] nature is not established for any other mind — that which has the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). Therefore, the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the mind alone should be understood here as 'the mind.' On the negation of offenses arising from desire, four verses:

children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s love for beings is great, reaching to the marrow,

children.text: yathaikaputrake tasmāt sadā hitakaraṃ matam || AMsa_13.20 ||
children.translated_text: like [that] for an only child; therefore it is considered to be always beneficial. // AMsa_13.20 //

children.text: satveṣu hitakāritvān naity āpattiṃ sa rāgajāṃ |
children.translated_text: Because of acting beneficially toward beings, he does not incur an offense born from desire;

children.text: dveṣo virudyate tvasya sarvasatveṣu satpathā || AMsa_13.21 ||
children.translated_text: hatred is indeed opposed to his right path regarding all beings. // AMsa_13.21 //

children.text: yathā kapotī svasutātivatsalā svabhāvakāṃs tān upaguhya tiṣṭhati |
children.translated_text: Just as a she-dove, exceedingly affectionate toward her own offspring, embraces and cherishes them by nature,

children.text: tathāvidhāyaṃ pratigho virudhyate suteṣu tadvat sakṛpe 'pi dehiṣu || AMsa_13.22 ||
children.translated_text: so too, for one of such character, hostility is opposed [to his nature]; toward beings, just as toward offspring, for one who has compassion. // AMsa_13.22 //

body.text: maitrī yataḥ pratighacittam ato viruddhaṃ śāntir yato vyasanacittam ato viruddhaṃ |
body.translated_text: Because of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), the mind of hostility is opposed; because of peace, the mind of misfortune is opposed;

body.text: artho yato nikṛticittam ato viruddhaṃ lhādo yataḥ pratibhayaṃ na ca tato viruddhaṃ || AMsa_13.23 ||
body.translated_text: because of benefit, the mind of dishonesty is opposed; because of delight, fear is not opposed therein. // AMsa_13.23 //

body.text: yat satveṣu bodhisatvasya prema so 'ca rāgo 'bhipretas tatkṛtām āpattiṃ teṣāṃ pratiṣedhayati | satvahitakriyāhetutvāt | kapotīm udāharati tadbahurāgatvāt apatyasnehādhimātratayā sakṛpe bodhisatve dehiṣu satveṣu pratigho virudhyate | bodhisatvānāṃ satveṣu maitrī bhavati vyasanaśāntiḥ arthadānaṃ hlādaś ca prītyutpādāt | yata ime maitryādayas tata eva pratighacittaṃ viruddhaṃ | tatpūrvakāṇi ca vyasanacittādīni | pratipattibhede pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: The affection that a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has toward beings is not intended as desire (<s>rāga</s>); he prevents the transgression that arises from it in them, because it is the cause of benefiting beings. He gives the example of a she-dove because of the abundance of that [affection] — because of the excess of affection for offspring. For one who has compassion, among beings as <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, hostility is opposed. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have loving-kindness toward beings, peace from misfortune, giving of benefit, and delight from generating joy. Because of these — loving-kindness and the rest — the mind of hostility and so forth, which are preceded by it, are opposed. On the divisions of practice, five verses:

children.translated_text: As a sick person toward good medicine, so he practices in <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: āture ca yathā vaidyaḥ satveṣu pratipadyate || AMsa_13.24 ||
children.translated_text: and as a physician toward the sick, so he practices toward beings. // AMsa_13.24 //
As toward an unfinished task of a servant, so he practices toward himself;

children.text: vaṇigyathā punaḥ puṇye kāmeṣu pratipadyate || AMsa_13.25 ||
children.translated_text: as a merchant toward merit, so he practices regarding sense-pleasures. // AMsa_13.25 //
Just as a washerman toward cloth, so he practices regarding action (<s>karma</s>);

children.text: pitā yathā sute bāle satvāheṭhe prapadyate || AMsa_13.26 ||
children.translated_text: as a father toward a young child, so he devotes himself to beings without harm. // AMsa_13.26 //
One seeking fire toward the lower fire-stick, so he devotes himself to continuity;
a trustworthy person toward an unfinished [task], so he devotes himself to higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>). // AMsa_13.27 //
Like a magician toward the knowable, so he practices with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>);

children.text: pratipattiryathā yasmin bodhisatvasya sā matā || AMsa_13.28 ||
children.translated_text: such is the practice of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> considered in each case. // AMsa_13.28 //

body.text: yathā yasmin pratipadyate tad abhidyotayati | yatheti subhaiṣajyādiṣv ivāturādayaḥ | yatreti saṃsārādiṣu pratisaṃkhyāya saṃsāraniṣevaṇāt | kāruṇyena kleśāturasatvāparityāgāt | svapraṇihitatvacittakaraṇāt | dānādipāramitābhiś ca yathākramaṃ bhogavṛddhinayanāt | kāyādikarmapariśodhanāt | satvāpakārākopāt | kuśalabhāvanānirantarābhiyogāt | samādhyanāsvādanāt | jñeyāviparyāsāc ca | pratipattitrimaṇḍalapariśuddhau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: He illustrates how one practices in each case. 'As' refers to good medicine and the like, while 'in' refers to <s>saṃsāra</s> and the like — after careful consideration, from attending to <s>saṃsāra</s>; from compassion, not abandoning beings afflicted by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); from making the mind subject to one's own vows; through the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of giving and so forth, in due order, from guiding the increase of wealth; from purifying actions of body and so forth; from not becoming angry at beings' offenses; from uninterrupted application to cultivating the wholesome; from not savoring <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); and from not being mistaken regarding the knowable. A verse on the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍala</s>) of practice:

children.translated_text: Thus, one who always has noble and proper vigor, well-engaged in ripening and purifying the two,

children.text: paramavimalanirvikalpabuddhyā vrajati sa siddhim anuttamāṃ krameṇa || AMsa_13.29 ||
children.translated_text: through the supremely pure wisdom of non-conceptualization, gradually proceeds to unsurpassed accomplishment. // AMsa_13.29 //

body.text: iti nirvikalpena dharmanairātmyajñānena pratipattuḥ pratipattavyasya pratipatteś cāvikalpanā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhir veditavyā | dvayaparipācanaśodhaneṣu yukta iti satvānām ātmanaś ca |
body.translated_text: Thus, through non-conceptual knowledge of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), the non-conceptualization regarding the practitioner, the object of practice, and the practice itself is to be understood as the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>). 'Engaged in ripening and purifying the two' means of beings and of oneself.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, this is the thirteenth [chapter], the chapter on practice (<s>pratipattyadhikāra</s>).

CHAPTER XIV
The fourteenth chapter.
On the division of instruction and guidance (<s>avavāda</s> and <s>anuśāsanī</s>), fifty-one verses.

children.translated_text: Having emerged from incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), increasing aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>),

children.text: saṃpūrṇaḥ kuśalair dharmaiḥ sāgaro vāribhiryathā || AMsa_14.1 ||
children.translated_text: filled with wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, like the ocean with waters. // AMsa_14.1 //

body.text: adhimuktiṃ vivardhayann ity adhimātrāvasthānayanāt | śeṣaṃ gatārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Increasing aspiration' means bringing it to the stage of the highest degree. The rest is self-evident.

children.translated_text: Having thus accumulated the stores [of merit and knowledge], the son of the <s>Jina</s>, pure from the beginning,

children.text: suvijñaḥ kalpacittaś ca bhāvanāyāṃ prayujyate || AMsa_14.2 ||
children.translated_text: well-learned and with a mind fit [for meditation], applies himself to cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). // AMsa_14.2 //

body.text: ādiśuddho bodhisatvasaṃvarapariśodhanān mahāyāne dṛṣṭiṛjjukaraṇāc cāviparītārthagrahaṇataḥ | suvijño bahuśrutatvāt | kalpacitto vinivaraṇatvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Pure from the beginning' — because of the purification of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> precepts and because of making views straight in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, through grasping the meaning without distortion. 'Well-learned' — because of being greatly learned. 'With a mind fit [for meditation]' — because of being free from the hindrances.

children.translated_text: He then obtains instruction from the <s>Buddhas</s> in the stream of the <s>Dharma</s>,
a vast [instruction], for the purpose of progressing in the vastness of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). // AMsa_14.3 //

body.translated_text: The verse is self-evident.

children.translated_text: Then, in the <s>Dharma</s> such as <s>sūtras</s> and the like, which illuminates the meaning of non-duality,

children.text: sūtrādināmni bandhīyāc cittaṃ prathamato yatiḥ || AMsa_14.4 ||
children.translated_text: the practitioner should first fix his mind upon the name of <s>sūtra</s> and so forth. // AMsa_14.4 //
Then he should examine the word-divisions in due order;

children.text: vicārayet tadarthāṃś ca pratyātmayoniśaś ca saḥ || AMsa_14.5 ||
children.translated_text: he should investigate their meanings, and also [do so] individually and methodically. // AMsa_14.5 //

children.text: avadhṛtya ca tān arthān dharme saṃkalayet punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having ascertained those meanings, he should again synthesize them in the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: tataḥ kuryāt samāśastiṃ tadarthādhigamāya saḥ || AMsa_14.6 ||
children.translated_text: then he should form the aspiration for the realization of those meanings. // AMsa_14.6 //

body.text: sūtrageyādike dharme yatsūtrādināma daśabhūmikam ity evamādi tatra cittaṃ prathamato badhnīyāt | ebhis tribhiḥ ślokaiḥ ṣaṭ cittāny upadiṣṭāni | mūlacittam anucaracittaṃ vicāraṇācittam avadhāraṇācittaṃ saṃkalanacittam āśāsticittaṃ ca | tatra mūlacittaṃ yatsūtrādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nāmālambanaṃ | avavādaṃ śrutvā svayaṃ vā kalpayitvā | tadyathā 'nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ śūnyam anātmyaṃ ca yoniśo na cety ādi | anucaracittaṃ yena sūtrādīnāṃ nāmata ālambitānāṃ padaprabhedam anugacchati | vicāraṇācittaṃ yenārthaṃ vyañjanaṃ ca vicārayati | tatrārthaṃ caturbhir ākārair vicārayati gaṇanayā tulanayā mīmāṃsayā pratyavekṣaṇayā ca | tatra gaṇanā saṃgrahaṇaṃ tadyathā rūpaṃ daśāyatanāny ekasya ca pradeśo vedanā ṣaḍ vedanākāyā ity evam ādi | tulanā saṃkhyāvato dharmasya śamalakṣagrahaṇam anādhyāropān apavādataḥ | mīmāṃsā pramāṇaparīkṣā | pratyavekṣaṇā | gaṇitatulitamīmāṃsitasyārthasyāvalokanaṃ | vyañjanaṃ dvābhyām ākārābhyāṃ vicārayati | sārthatathā ca samastānāṃ vyañjanānāṃ nirarthatayā ca vyastānāṃ | avadhāraṇācittaṃ yena yathānucaritaṃ vicāritaṃ vā tannimittam avadhārayati | saṃkalanacittaṃ tadyathā vicāritam arthaṃ mūlacitte saṃkṣipya paripiṇḍitākāraṃ vartate | āśāsticittaṃ yadarthaṃ prayukto bhavati samā tatparipūryarthaṃ vā śrāmaṇyaphalārthaṃ vā bhūmipraveśārthaṃ vā viśeṣagamanārthaṃ vā tacchandasahagataṃ vartate | cittam eva hy ālambanapratibhāsaṃ vartate na cittād anyad ālambanam astīti jānato vā cittamātram ajānato vā cittam evālambanaṃ nānyat | iti ṣaḍvidhaṃ cittam ālambanaṃ vyavasthāpyate |
body.translated_text: In the <s>Dharma</s> such as <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, and the like — whatever name of <s>sūtra</s> and the like, such as '<s>Daśabhūmika</s>' and so on — he should first fix the mind thereupon. By these three verses, six [types of] mind are taught: the root-mind (<s>mūlacitta</s>), the attendant mind (<s>anucaracitta</s>), the investigating mind (<s>vicāraṇācitta</s>), the ascertaining mind (<s>avadhāraṇācitta</s>), the synthesizing mind (<s>saṃkalanacitta</s>), and the aspiring mind (<s>āśāsticitta</s>). Therein, the root-mind is that which takes as its object the name of the <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sūtras</s> — having heard instruction or having conceived it by oneself — such as 'impermanent, suffering, empty, and non-self; and methodically, not...' and so forth. The attendant mind follows the word-divisions of the <s>sūtras</s> and the like that have been taken as objects by name. The investigating mind investigates the meaning and the expression. Therein, one investigates the meaning in four modes: by enumeration, by comparison, by examination, and by contemplation. Therein, enumeration is classification — such as 'form is the ten sense-bases and a portion of one; feeling is the six classes of feeling' — and so on. Comparison is the apprehension of the defilement-characteristic of a <s>dharma</s> that has been enumerated, without superimposition and without denial. Examination is the testing through valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Contemplation is the observation of the meaning that has been enumerated, compared, and examined. One investigates the expression in two modes: by the meaningfulness of the expressions taken together, and by the meaninglessness of the expressions taken separately. The ascertaining mind ascertains the sign of what has been followed and investigated. The synthesizing mind condenses the investigated meaning into the root-mind and proceeds in a summarized form. The aspiring mind proceeds accompanied by the wish for the purpose for which one has exerted oneself — whether for the fulfillment of <s>śamatha</s>, or for the fruit of the ascetic life, or for entry into the stages, or for progress to higher stages. For the mind itself proceeds as the appearance of the object — knowing that there is no object other than the mind, or not knowing it, the mind alone is the object, nothing else. Thus the sixfold mind is established as the object.

children.translated_text: One should seek and contemplate with mental discourse in continuous succession;
and one should also investigate with mental acts free from discourse, of a single savor. // AMsa_14.7 //
The path of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) should be known as the condensed <s>Dharma</s>-name;
the path of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) should be known as the investigation of those meanings. // AMsa_14.8 //

children.text: yuganaddhaś ca vijñeyo mārgas tatpiṇḍitaṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: The path of union (<s>yuganaddha</s>) should be known as the condensation of those again;

children.text: līnaṃ cittasya gṛhṇīyād uddhataṃ śamayet punaḥ || AMsa_14.9 ||
children.translated_text: one should grasp the sluggishness of the mind, and again calm the agitated. // AMsa_14.9 //
When the mind has attained calm, one should regard it with equanimity;

children.text: sātatyenātha satkṛtya sarvasmin yojayet punaḥ || AMsa_14.10 ||
children.translated_text: then again, with continuity and respect, one should engage in all of that. // AMsa_14.10 //

body.text: ebhiś caturbhiḥ ślokair ekādaśa manaskārā upadiṣṭāḥ | savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ | avitarko vicāramātraḥ | avitarko 'vicāraḥ | śamathamanaskāraḥ | vipaśyanāmanaskāraḥ |
body.translated_text: By these four verses, eleven mental acts (<s>manaskāras</s>) are taught: with applied thought (<s>savitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>savicāra</s>); without applied thought, with sustained thought only; without applied thought and without sustained thought; the mental act of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding); the mental act of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight);

body.text: yuganaddhamanaskāraḥ | śamathanimittamanaskāraḥ | upekṣānimittamanaskāraḥ | sātatyamanaskāraḥ | satkṛtyamanaskāraś ca |
body.translated_text: the mental act of union (<s>yuganaddha</s>); the mental act of the sign of calm; the mental act of the sign of equanimity; the mental act of continuity; and the mental act of respect.

children.translated_text: Having fixed the mind on the object, one should not let it be distracted from its penetration;

children.text: avagamyāśu vikṣepaṃ tasmin pratiharet punaḥ || AMsa_14.11 ||
children.translated_text: quickly recognizing distraction, one should bring it back to that [object] again. // AMsa_14.11 //

children.text: pratyātmaṃ saṃkṣipec cittam upary upari buddhimān |
children.translated_text: The wise one should inwardly collect the mind again and again to higher levels;

children.text: tataś ca ramayec cittaṃ samādhau guṇadarśanāt || AMsa_14.12 ||
children.translated_text: then he should delight the mind in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) from seeing its virtues. // AMsa_14.12 //
He should calm discontent therein from seeing the faults of distraction;

children.text: abhidhyā daurmanasyādīn vyutthitān śamayet tathā || AMsa_14.13 ||
children.translated_text: likewise, he should calm covetousness, ill-will, and the like when they arise. // AMsa_14.13 //
Then, having [first] an effortful [state] in the mind, and [then] one flowing spontaneously,
the practitioner attains the effortless [state] through repeated practice of that. // AMsa_14.14 //

body.text: ebhiś caturbhiḥ ślokair navākārayā cittasthityā sthityupāya upadiṣṭaḥ | cittaṃ sthāpayati saṃsthāpayati avasthāpayati upasthāpayati damayati śamayati vyupaśamayaty ekotīkaroti cittaṃ samādadhātīti navākārāḥ |
body.translated_text: By these four verses, the means of mental stability through nine modes of settling the mind is taught: one settles the mind, continuously settles it, firmly settles it, closely settles it, tames it, calms it, thoroughly calms it, unifies it, and places it in equipoise — these are the nine modes.

children.text: tataḥ sa tanukāṃ labdhvā praśrabdhiṃ kāyacetasoḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having attained a slight tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) of body and mind,

children.text: vijñeyaḥ samanaskāraḥ punas tāns tāṃ sa vivardhayan || AMsa_14.15 ||
children.translated_text: he should be understood as one with [proper] mental attention; then, increasing those [qualities] further — // AMsa_14.15 //
through increasing and far-reaching [practice], he attains the fundamental stability;

children.text: tāṃ śodhayann abhijñārtham eti karmaṇyatāṃ parāṃ || AMsa_14.16 ||
children.translated_text: purifying that for the purpose of higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), he reaches supreme workability (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>). // AMsa_14.16 //
Through the production of higher knowledges in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he goes to the world-realms,

children.text: pūjārtham aprameyāṇāṃ buddhāyāṃ śravaṇāya ca || AMsa_14.17 ||
children.translated_text: for the worship of immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> and for hearing [the <s>Dharma</s>]. // AMsa_14.17 //
Having attended upon immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> for incalculable <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: karmaṇyatāṃ parām eti cetasas tadupāsanāt || AMsa_14.18 ||
children.translated_text: he attains supreme workability of the mind from that attendance. // AMsa_14.18 //

body.text: eti karmaṇyatāṃ parāṃ dhyāne iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ | kalpair ameyagair ity aprameyasaṃkhyāgataiḥ | śeṣam eṣāṃ ślokānāṃ gatārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'He attains supreme workability in <s>dhyāna</s>' — this should be connected. 'For incalculable <s>kalpas</s>' means those gone through immeasurable numbers. The rest of these verses is self-evident.

children.text: tato 'nuśaṃsān labhate pañca śuddhaiḥ sa pūrvagān |
children.translated_text: Then he obtains five benefits, preceded by purities;

children.text: viśuddhibhājanatvaṃ ca tato yāti niruttaraṃ || AMsa_14.19 ||
children.translated_text: and then he attains the unsurpassed receptacle of purity. // AMsa_14.19 //

children.text: kṛtsnādau svalpadauṣṭhulya kāyo hi dravate 'sya pratikṣaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: In the totality [meditation] and so forth, his body, with its slight impurity, melts away at every moment;

children.text: āpūryate ca praśrabdhyā kāyacittaṃ samantataḥ || AMsa_14.20 ||
children.translated_text: and body and mind are filled everywhere with tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>). // AMsa_14.20 //
He perceives the unlimited radiance of <s>dharmas</s> everywhere;
and in purification, he beholds signs that are uncontrived. // AMsa_14.21 //

children.text: prapūrau ca viśuddhau ca dharmakāyasya sarvathā |
children.translated_text: For the fulfillment and purification of the <s>dharmakāya</s> in every way,

children.text: karoti satataṃ dhīmān evaṃ hetuparigrahaṃ || AMsa_14.22 ||
children.translated_text: the wise one constantly gathers the causes in this manner. // AMsa_14.22 //

body.text: tataḥ śuddheḥ pūrvaṃgamān pañcānuśaṃsān labhate | śuddher iti śuddhyāśayabhūmeḥ | teṣāṃ ca lābhādviśuddhibhājanatvaṃ prāpnoti | niruttaraṃ yānānantaryāt | prapūrau ca viśuddhau ca dharmakāyasyeti daśamyāṃ bhūmau paripūri rbuddhabhūmau viśuddhiḥ | eteṣāṃ pañcānām anuśaṃsānāṃ trayaḥ śamathapakṣā dvau vipaśyanāpakṣau veditavyau | ato yāval laukikaḥ samudāgamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then he obtains the five benefits that are precursors of purity. 'Of purity' means of the stage of pure intention (<s>śuddhyāśayabhūmi</s>). And from obtaining these, he reaches the receptacle of purity — unsurpassed, because of the certainty of the vehicle. 'For the fulfillment and purification of the <s>dharmakāya</s>' — on the tenth stage there is fulfillment; on the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage) there is purification. Of these five benefits, three should be understood as belonging to the side of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and two to the side of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). From this point on, the attainment is mundane.

children.translated_text: Then, that <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being in such a state, in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration),

children.text: manojalpād vinirmuktān sarvārthān na prapaśyati || AMsa_14.23 ||
children.translated_text: does not perceive any objects that are free from mental discourse (<s>manojalpa</s>). // AMsa_14.23 //
He initiates firm effort for the increase of the light of the <s>Dharma</s>;
and through the increase of the <s>Dharma</s>-light, he abides in mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). // AMsa_14.24 //
Then he perceives in the mind the appearance of all objects;

children.text: prahīno grāhyanivikṣepas tadā tasya bhavaty asau || AMsa_14.25 ||
children.translated_text: at that time, his distraction toward the grasped has been abandoned. // AMsa_14.25 //
Then only the distraction toward the grasper remains for him;

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiṃ ca spṛśaty āśu tadā punaḥ || AMsa_14.26 ||
children.translated_text: and then he quickly touches the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s> (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>). // AMsa_14.26 //

body.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ nirvedhabhāgīyāni | tathābhūto bodhisatvaḥ samāhitacitto manojalpād vinirmuktān sarvadharmān na paśyati svalakṣaṇasāmānyalakṣaṇākhyān manojalpamātram eva khyāti | sāsyoṣmagatāvasthā | ayaṃ sa āloko yam adhikṛtyoktaṃ kṣāranadyām | āloka iti dharmanidhyānakṣānter etad adhivacanam iti | sa tasyaiva dharmālokasya vivṛddhyartham āsthitakriyayā dṛḍhaṃ vīryam ārabhate | sāsya mūrdhāvasthā dharmālokavivṛddhyā ca cittamātre 'vatiṣṭhate | cittam etad iti prativedhāt | tataś citta eva sarvārthapratibhāsatvaṃ paśyati | na cittād anyam arthaṃ | tadā cāsya grāhyavikṣepaḥ prahīno bhavati | grāhakavikṣepaḥ kevalo 'vaśiṣyate | sāsya kṣāntyavasthā | tadā ca kṣipram ānantaryasamādhiṃ spṛśati | sāsya laukikāgradharmāvasthā | kena kāraṇena sa ānantarya ucyate |
body.translated_text: From here onward are the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). A <s>Bodhisattva</s> in such a state, with concentrated mind, does not perceive any <s>dharmas</s> — those called 'own-characteristic' and 'common-characteristic' — as freed from mental discourse (<s>manojalpa</s>); only mental discourse itself appears. This is his stage of heat (<s>uṣmagata</s>). This is the 'light' (<s>āloka</s>) regarding which it is said in the <s>Kṣāranadī</s>: 'Light — this is a designation for the patient acceptance of Dharma-contemplation (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>).' He undertakes vigorous effort with established practice for the purpose of increasing that very light of Dharma. This is his stage of summit (<s>mūrdha</s>). And through the increase of the light of Dharma, he abides in mere mind (<s>cittamātra</s>) — from the penetration that 'this is mind.' Then he sees that all objects are merely appearances in mind alone, and no object other than mind. At that time, his distraction toward the grasped (<s>grāhyavikṣepa</s>) is abandoned; only distraction toward the grasper (<s>grāhakavikṣepa</s>) remains. This is his stage of acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>). Then he quickly touches the immediate concentration (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>). This is his stage of supreme mundane dharma (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>). For what reason is it called 'immediate' (<s>ānantarya</s>)?

children.translated_text: Because the distraction toward the grasper is removed immediately thereafter.

children.text: jñeyāny uṣmagatādīni etāni hi yathākramaṃ || AMsa_14.27 ||
children.translated_text: These — heat and so forth — should be known as the aids to penetration, in sequence. // AMsa_14.27 //

body.translated_text: Thus these — heat and so forth — are the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>).

children.translated_text: Disconnected from the duality of grasping, supramundane, unsurpassed,

children.text: nirvikalpaṃ malāpetaṃ jñānaṃ sa labhate punaḥ || AMsa_14.28 ||
children.translated_text: non-conceptual, free from defilement — such knowledge he then obtains. // AMsa_14.28 //

body.text: ataḥ pareṇa darśanamārgāvasthā | dvayagrāhavisaṃyuktaṃ grāhyagrāhagrāhakagrāhavisaṃyogāt | anuttaraṃ yānānantaryeṇa | nirvikalpaṃ grāhyagrāhakavikalpavisaṃyogāt | malāpetaṃ darśanajñeyakleśaprahāṇāt | etena virajo vigatamalam ity uktaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Beyond this is the stage of the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). 'Disconnected from the duality of grasping' — from the disconnection from grasping the grasped and grasping the grasper. 'Unsurpassed' — through the supremacy of the vehicle. 'Non-conceptual' — from the disconnection from conceptualization of grasped and grasper. 'Free from defilement' — from the abandonment of afflictions and knowable [obstructions] to be abandoned by seeing. By this, the statement 'dustless, free from stain' is made.

children.translated_text: His first transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) is accepted as the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>);

children.text: ameyaiś cāsya sā kalpaiḥ suviśuddhiṃ nigacchati || AMsa_14.29 ||
children.translated_text: and that [stage] reaches complete purification for him through immeasurable eons. // AMsa_14.29 //

body.translated_text: The verse's meaning has been explained.

children.text: dharmadhātoś ca samatāṃ pratividhya punas tadā |
children.translated_text: And having penetrated the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, then
he obtains constant equal-mindedness toward all beings, as toward himself. // AMsa_14.30 //
In selflessness, in the meaning of suffering, in what is to be done, in the absence of recompense —
he is equal-minded toward beings, just as other sons of the <s>Jina</s>. // AMsa_14.31 //

body.text: dharmanairātmyena ca dharmasamatāṃ pratividhya sarvasatveṣu sadā ātmasamacittatāṃ pratilabhate | pañcavidhayā samatayā | nairātmyasamatayā duḥkhasamatayā svaparasaṃtāneṣu nairātmyaduḥkhatayor aviśeṣāt | kṛtyasamatayā svaparaduḥkhaprahāṇakāmatāsāmānyāt | niṣpratikārasamatayā | ātmana iva parataḥ pratikārānabhinandanāt | tadanyabodhisatvasamatayā ca yathā tair abhisamitaṃ tathābhisamayāt |
body.translated_text: Having penetrated the equality of <s>dharmas</s> through the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, he always obtains equal-mindedness toward all beings as toward himself — through fivefold equality: equality of selflessness, and equality of suffering — because of the non-distinction of selflessness and suffering in one's own and others' continuums. Equality of what is to be done — from the commonality of the wish to abandon one's own and others' suffering. Equality of the absence of recompense — from not delighting in recompense from others, as toward oneself. And equality with other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — from realizing just as they have realized.

children.translated_text: The formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of self in the three realms — as mere unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) —
he sees with thoroughly purified knowledge, in the meaning of non-duality. // AMsa_14.32 //

body.text: sa traidhātukātmasaṃskārān abhūtaparikalpanāmātrān paśyati | suviśuddhena jñānena lokottaratvāt |
body.translated_text: He sees the formations of self in the three realms as mere unreal conceptualization — with thoroughly purified knowledge, because it is supramundane.

children.translated_text: And the existence of its non-existence — liberated from what is abandoned by seeing —

children.text: labdhvā darśanamārgo hi tadā tena nirūcyate || AMsa_14.33 ||
children.translated_text: having obtained [this], the path of seeing is thus proclaimed by him. // AMsa_14.33 //

body.text: tasya grāhyagrāhakābhāvasya bhāvaṃ dharmadhātūn darśanaprahātavyaiḥ kleśair vimuktaṃ paśyati |
body.translated_text: He sees the existence of the non-existence of grasped and grasper — the <s>dharmadhātu</s> — liberated from the afflictions to be abandoned by seeing.

children.translated_text: Having known the emptiness of non-existence, and likewise the emptiness of existence,

children.text: prakṛtyā śūnyatāṃ jñātvā śūnyajña iti kathyate || AMsa_14.34 ||
children.translated_text: having known the emptiness of nature — he is called a 'knower of emptiness.' // AMsa_14.34 //

body.text: sa ca bodhisatvaḥ śūnyajña ity ucyate | trividhiśūnyatājñānāt | abhāvaśūnyatā parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ svena lakṣaṇenābhāvāt | tathā bhāvasya śūnyatā paratantrasya sa hi na tathābhāvo yathā kalpyate svena lakṣaṇena bhāvaḥ | prakṛtiśūnyatā pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ śūnyatāsvabhāvatvāt |
body.translated_text: And that <s>Bodhisattva</s> is called a 'knower of emptiness,' from knowing threefold emptiness. The emptiness of non-existence is the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>), because of the non-existence of its own characteristic. Likewise, the emptiness of existence is of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) — for it does not exist as it is imagined, [yet] it exists by its own characteristic. The emptiness of nature is the consummate nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>), because its nature is emptiness itself.

children.translated_text: The signless (<s>animitta</s>) state should be known, and the exhaustion of conceptualizations,
and unreal conceptualization — these indeed pertain to the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>). // AMsa_14.35 //

body.text: animittapadaṃ jñeyaṃ vikalpānāṃ ca saṃkṣayaḥ | abhūtaparikalpas tadapraṇidhānasya padam ālambanam ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: The signless state should be known, and the exhaustion of conceptualizations. Unreal conceptualization is the object (<s>ālambana</s>) — meaning the basis — of that wishlessness.

children.text: tena darśanamārgeṇa saha lābhaḥ sadā mataḥ |
children.translated_text: Together with that path of seeing, the attainment is always accepted
for the son of the <s>Jina</s> of all the varied wings of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>). // AMsa_14.36 //

body.text: tena darśanamārgeṇa saha bodhisatvasya sarveṣāṃ bodhipakṣāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lābho veditavyaḥ smṛtyupasthānādīnāṃ |
body.translated_text: Together with that path of seeing, the attainment by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> that are wings of awakening — the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and so forth — should be understood.

children.text: saṃskāramātraṃ jagad etya buddhyā nirātmakaṃ duḥkhivirūḍhimātraṃ |
children.translated_text: Having realized through wisdom that the world is mere formations, selfless, merely an outgrowth of suffering,

children.text: vihāya yānarthamayātmadṛṣṭiḥ mahātmadṛṣṭiṃ śrayate mahārthāṃ || AMsa_14.37 ||
children.translated_text: abandoning the self-view that has the purpose of harm, he resorts to the great self-view that has great purpose. // AMsa_14.37 //

children.text: vinātmadṛṣṭyā ya ihātmadṛṣṭir vināpi duḥkhena suduḥkhitaś ca |
children.translated_text: He who, without the [afflicted] self-view, has a [noble] self-view, and though without suffering [of his own], is greatly suffering [for others],

children.text: sarvārthakartā na ca kārakāṅkṣī yathātmanaḥ svātmahitāni kṛtvā || AMsa_14.38 ||
children.translated_text: the doer of all purposes yet not desiring an agent — having accomplished benefits for himself as if for his own self. // AMsa_14.38 //

children.text: yo muktacittaḥ parayā vimuktyā baddhaś ca gāḍhāyatabandhanena |
children.translated_text: He whose mind is liberated with the supreme liberation, yet bound with a tight and extensive bond,

children.text: duḥkhasya paryantam apaśyamānaḥ prayujyate caiva karoti caiva || AMsa_14.39 ||
children.translated_text: seeing no end to suffering — yet he engages and he acts. // AMsa_14.39 //

children.text: svaṃ duḥkham udvoḍhum ihāsamartho lokaḥ kutaḥ piṇḍitam anyaduḥkhaṃ |
children.translated_text: The world is unable to bear even its own suffering here — how much less the accumulated suffering of others?

children.text: janmaikam ālokayate gataṃ tvacinto viparyayāt tasya tu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_14.40 ||
children.translated_text: It looks upon even a single past birth as inconceivable — but the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on the contrary, [looks upon all]. // AMsa_14.40 //

children.text: yatprema yā vatsalatā prayogaḥ satveṣv akhedaś ca jinātmajānāṃ |
children.translated_text: The love, the tenderness, the engagement toward beings, and the unwearied [effort] of the sons of the <s>Jina</s> —

children.text: āścaryam etat paramaṃ bhaveṣu na caiva satvātmasamān abhāvāt || AMsa_14.41 ||
children.translated_text: this is the supreme wonder in all existences, and yet not [a wonder], because of the non-existence of beings different from himself. // AMsa_14.41 //

body.text: ebhiḥ pañcabhiḥ ślokair darśanamārgalābhino bodhisatvasya māhātmyodbhāvanaṃ | anarthamayātmadṛṣṭir yā kliṣṭā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ | mahātmadṛṣṭir iti mahārthā yā sarvasatveṣv ātmasamacittalābhātmadṛṣṭiḥ | sā hi sarvasatvārthakriyāhetutvāt mahārthā | vinātmadṛṣṭyā anarthamayyātmadṛṣṭir mahārthā yā vināpi duḥkhena svasaṃtānajena suduḥkhitā sarvasatvasaṃtānajena | yo vimuktacitto darśanaprahātavyebhyaḥ parayā vimuktyānuttareṇa yānena | baddhaś ca gāḍhāyatabandhanena sarvasatvasāṃntāniṃkena
body.translated_text: By these five verses, the greatness of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained the path of seeing is displayed. 'The self-view that has the purpose of harm' is the afflicted view of the transitory collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). 'The great self-view' is that which has great purpose — the self-view of equal-mindedness toward all beings gained [through realization]; for it has great purpose because it is the cause of accomplishing the welfare of all beings. 'Without the [afflicted] self-view' — the self-view that has the purpose of harm has great purpose [when transformed]: though without suffering born from one's own continuum, [one is] greatly suffering from the continuums of all beings. 'Whose mind is liberated' — from what is to be abandoned by seeing, 'with the supreme liberation' — by the unsurpassed vehicle. 'Yet bound with a tight and extensive bond' — belonging to the continuums of all beings.

body.text: duḥkhasya paryantaṃ na paśyati svadhātor anantatvād ākāśavat prayujyate ca duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai satvānāṃ karoti caiva tām aprameyāṇāṃ satvānāṃ | viparyayāt tasya tu bodhisatvaḥ sa hi saṃpiṇḍitasarvasatvaduḥkhaṃ yāval lokagatam udvoḍhuṃ samarthaḥ | yā satveṣu bodhisatvasya priyatā yā ca hitasukhaiṣitā yaś ca tadarthaṃ prayogo yaś cittaprayuktasyākheda etat sarvam āścaryaṃ paramaṃ lokeṣu | na caivāścaryaṃ satvānām ātmasamānatvāt |
body.translated_text: He sees no end to suffering because of the infinity of his own element, like space. He engages in making an end of suffering for beings, and he does so for immeasurable beings. 'But the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on the contrary' — for he is able to bear the accumulated suffering of all beings, as much as exists in the world. The love of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> toward beings, the desire for their benefit and happiness, the engagement for that purpose, and the unwearied [effort] of one whose mind is engaged — all this is the supreme wonder in the worlds. And yet it is not a wonder, because of the sameness of beings with himself.

children.translated_text: Thereafter, on the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), on the remaining stages,
he applies himself here to the cultivation of twofold knowledge. // AMsa_14.42 //
One is the non-conceptual knowledge that purifies the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities;
the other, the knowledge as [things] are established, ripens beings. // AMsa_14.43 //
And the culmination of cultivation is from the completion of two incalculable [eons];
reaching the final cultivation, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is consecrated (<s>abhiṣikta</s>). // AMsa_14.44 //
And reaching the diamond-like concentration (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>), unbreakable by conceptualizations,
the final transformation of the basis, free from all obstructions, // AMsa_14.45 //
and the omniscience of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) — he obtains the unsurpassed state,

children.text: yatra sthaḥ sarvasatvānāṃ hitāya pratipadyate || AMsa_14.46 ||
children.translated_text: wherein abiding, he proceeds for the benefit of all beings. // AMsa_14.46 //

body.text: ebhir bhāvanāmārgaḥ paridīpitaḥ | dvividhaṃ jñānaṃ | nirvikalpaṃ ca yenātmano buddhadharmāṇ viśodhayati | yathāvyavasthānaṃ ca lokottarapṛṣṭhalabdhaṃ laukikaṃ yena satvān paripācayati | asaṃkhyeyadvayasya samāptau paścimāṃ bhāvanām āgamyāvasānagatām abhiṣikto vajropamaṃ samādhiṃ labhate | vikalpānuśayābhedyārthena vajropamaḥ | tato niṣṭhāgatām āśrayaparāvṛttiṃ labhate sarvakleśajñeyāvaraṇanirmalāṃ | sarvākārajñatāṃ cānuttarapadaṃ yatrastho yāvat saṃsāram abhisaṃbodhinirvāṇasaṃdarśanādibhiḥ satvānāṃ hitāya pratipadyate |
body.translated_text: By these [verses], the path of cultivation is illuminated. The twofold knowledge is: the non-conceptual, by which he purifies the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities for himself; and that which is 'as [things] are established' — the mundane [knowledge] obtained subsequent to the supramundane — by which he ripens beings. Upon the completion of two incalculable [eons], reaching the final cultivation — the end-point — the consecrated one (<s>abhiṣikta</s>) obtains the diamond-like concentration. It is 'diamond-like' in the sense of being unbreakable by the latent tendencies of conceptualization. Then he obtains the final transformation of the basis, free from all defilements of affliction-obstruction and knowledge-obstruction. And the omniscience of all aspects, the unsurpassed state — wherein abiding, he proceeds for the benefit of beings throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>, through displaying awakening, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and so forth.

children.text: kathaṃ tathā durlabhadarśane munau bhaven mahārthaṃ na hi nityadarśanaṃ |
children.translated_text: How could the seeing of the <s>Muni</s>, so hard to obtain, not be of great purpose? For it is not constant seeing;

children.text: bhṛśaṃ samāpyāyitacetasaḥ sadā prasādavegair asamaśravodbhavaiḥ || AMsa_14.47 ||
children.translated_text: his mind is always greatly nourished by surges of faith arising from incomparable hearing. // AMsa_14.47 //

children.text: apracodyamānaḥ satataṃ ca saṃmukhaṃ tathāgatair dharmasumukhe vyavasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Without being urged, constantly face-to-face, established at the excellent opening of the <s>Dharma</s> by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: nigṛhya keśeṣv iva doṣagahvarāt nikṛṣya bodhau sa balān niveśyate || AMsa_14.48 ||
children.translated_text: as if seized by the hair, he is dragged from the abyss of faults and forcibly placed in awakening. // AMsa_14.48 //

children.text: sa sarvalokaṃ suviśuddhadarśanair akalpabodhair abhibhūya sarvathā |
children.translated_text: He, with thoroughly pure vision, with non-conceptual awakenings, having overcome the entire world in every way,

children.text: mahāndhakāraṃ vidhamayya bhāsate jaganmahāditya ivātyudārataḥ || AMsa_14.49 ||
children.translated_text: dispelling the great darkness, shines forth like the great sun of the world, most noble. // AMsa_14.49 //

body.text: ebhis tribhiḥ ślokair avavādamāhātmyaṃ darśayati | yo hi dharmamukhaśrotasy avavādaṃ labhate tasya nityaṃ buddhadarśanaṃ bhavati | tataś cāsamaṃ dharmaśravaṇaṃ | yato 'syātyarthaṃ prasādaḥ prasādavegair āpyāyitacetasas tannityadarśanaṃ buddhānāṃ mahārthaṃ bhavati | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: By these three verses, the greatness of admonition is shown. For one who receives admonition at the excellent opening of the <s>Dharma</s>-stream, there is constant seeing of the <s>Buddha</s>. And from that, incomparable hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. Since his faith is exceedingly great, for one whose mind is nourished by surges of faith, that constant seeing of the <s>Buddhas</s> is of great purpose. The rest has been explained.

children.text: buddhāḥ samyakpraśaṃsāṃ vidadhati satataṃ svārthasamyakprayukte nindām īrṣyāprayukte sthitivicayapare cāntarāyānukūlān |
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> constantly bestow proper praise on the supreme being rightly engaged in his own purpose; [they bestow] censure on one engaged in jealousy; and to one devoted to abiding and investigation, [they show] all <s>dharmas</s> of every kind that are conducive to and adverse to obstacles, according to rule — those to be avoided and those to be practiced, through which there is vastness in this <s>Sugata's</s> teaching regarding yoga. // AMsa_14.50 //

children.text: dharmān sarvaprakārān vidhivad iha jinā darśayanty agrasatve yān varjyāsevya yoge bhavati vipulatā saugate śāsane 'smim || AMsa_14.50 ||

body.text: caturvidhām anuśāsanīm etena ślokena darśayati | adhiśīlam adhikṛtya samyaksvārthaprayukte bodhisatve praśaṃsāvidhānataḥ | adhicittam adhiprajñaṃ cādhikṛtya sthitivicayapare tadantarāyāṇāṃ tadanukūlānāṃ ca sarvaprakārāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ deśanataḥ | yān varjyāsevyety antarāyān anukūlāṃś ca yathākramaṃ | yoga iti śamathavipaśyanābhāvanāyāṃ |
body.translated_text: By this verse, the fourfold instruction (<s>anuśāsanī</s>) is shown: with respect to higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), from bestowing praise on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> rightly engaged in his own purpose. With respect to higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) and higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>), from teaching <s>dharmas</s> of every kind — those that are obstacles to them and those that are conducive — to one devoted to abiding and investigation. 'Those to be avoided and those to be practiced' refers to obstacles and conducive [factors] respectively. 'Yoga' refers to the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).

children.text: iti satataśubhācayaprapūrṇaḥ suvipulam etya sa cetasaḥ samādhiṃ |
children.translated_text: Thus, filled with the constant accumulation of virtue, having reached the vast concentration of mind,
having obtained the constant great admonition of the <s>Muni</s>, the supreme being reaches the far shore of the ocean of qualities. // AMsa_14.51 //

body.translated_text: The concluding verse's meaning has been explained.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fourteenth chapter on admonition and instruction (<s>avavādānuśāsani</s>).

CHAPTER XV
The fifteenth chapter.

children.translated_text: Summary: conviction, abundance, seeking the <s>Dharma</s>, and teaching;
likewise practice, and proper admonition and instruction. // AMsa_15.1 //

body.translated_text: On the division of action accompanied by skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), four verses:

children.translated_text: Just as the earth is the foundation everywhere for forests, bodies, mountains, and rivers,

children.text: tathaiva dānādiśubhasya sarvato budheṣu karma trividhaṃ nirucyate || AMsa_15.2 ||
children.translated_text: so for the wise, the threefold action is proclaimed as [the foundation] of all virtue such as generosity and so forth. // AMsa_15.2 //

body.text: anena ślokena samutthānopāyaṃ darśayati | sarvaprakārasya dānādiśubhasya pāramitābodhipakṣādikasya karmatrayasamutthitatvāt | budheṣv iti bodhisatveṣu | vanādigrahaṇam upabhojyāsthirasthiravastunidarśanārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: By this verse, the means of arising (<s>samutthānopāya</s>) is shown — because all kinds of virtue such as generosity and so forth — the perfections, wings of awakening, and so on — arise from the three [types of] action. 'For the wise' means 'for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' The mention of forests and so forth is for the purpose of illustrating things that are enjoyable, unstable, and stable.

children.translated_text: 'For the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, exerting themselves in deeds most difficult to accomplish, of varied forms, extending over many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons),

children.text: na kāyavākcittamayasya karmaṇo jinātmajānāṃ bhavatīha saṃnatiḥ || AMsa_15.3 ||
children.translated_text: there is no weariness regarding action of body, speech, and mind.' // AMsa_15.3 //

children.text: yathā viṣāc chastramahāśanād ripor nivārayed ātmahitaḥ svam āśrayaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as one concerned with self-benefit would protect one's own body from poison, weapons, and a great fire, and from an enemy,

children.text: nihīnayānād vividhāj jinātmajo nivārayet karma tathā trayātmakaṃ || AMsa_15.4 ||
children.translated_text: so too the son of the <s>Jina</s> would ward off the threefold action [pertaining to] the inferior vehicle (<s>hīnayāna</s>).' // AMsa_15.4 //

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ vyutthānopāyaṃ darśayati | mahāyānakhedānyayānapātavyutthānād yathākramaṃ | saṃnatiḥ kheda ity arthaḥ | viṣādisādharmyaṃ hīnayānapratisaṃyuktasya karmaṇo hīnayānacittapariṇāmanāt mahāyāne kuśalamūlasamucchedanāt anutpannakuśalamūlānutpādāya | utpannakuśalamūlasya dhvaṃsanāt | buddhatvasaṃpatprāptivibandhanāc ca |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, the means of recovery is shown — recovery from weariness with the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and from falling into other vehicles, respectively. 'Weariness' (<s>saṃnati</s>) means dejection. The analogy with poison and so forth [applies to] action connected with the inferior vehicle, because through the mental transformation toward the inferior vehicle: it cuts off the roots of wholesome [action] in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; it prevents the arising of unarisen roots of wholesome [action]; it destroys already arisen roots of wholesome [action]; and it obstructs the attainment of the perfection of <s>Buddhahood</s>.

children.text: na karmiṇaḥ karma na karmaṇaḥ kriyāṃ sadāvikalpaḥ samudīkṣate tridhā |
children.translated_text: 'One who is always non-conceptual does not regard the three — the agent, the action, or the activity of action;
