children.text: tato 'sya tatkarma viśuddhipāragaṃ bhavaty anantaṃ tadupāyasaṃgrahāt || AMsa_15.5 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, that action of his reaches the far shore of purity and becomes infinite, through the inclusion of means (<s>upāya</s>).' // AMsa_15.5 //

body.text: anena ślokena caturthena viśuddhyupāyaṃ karmaṇo darśayati | maṇḍalapariśuddhitaḥ kartṛkarmakriyāṇām anupalambhāt | anantam ity akṣayaṃ |
body.translated_text: By this fourth verse, the means of purification of action is shown — from the non-apprehension of the agent, action, and activity, through the purity of the maṇḍala. 'Infinite' means inexhaustible.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the fifteenth chapter on action accompanied by means (<s>upāyasahitakarmādhikāra</s>).

CHAPTER XVI
The sixteenth chapter.
On the division and classification of the perfections (<s>pāramitās</s>), the summary verse:

children.text: sāṃkhyātha tallakṣaṇam ānupūrvī niruktir abhyāsaguṇaś ca tāsāṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Their number, then their characteristic, their sequence, their etymology, their practice and quality,

children.text: prabhedanaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ vipakṣo jñeyo guṇo 'nyonyaviniścayaś ca || AMsa_16.1 ||
children.translated_text: their division, their inclusion, their opponent, the knowable quality, and the mutual determination.' // AMsa_16.1 //

body.translated_text: On the division of the number, six verses:

children.translated_text: 'Prosperity of possessions, personal existence, attendants, and undertakings;

children.text: kleśāvaśagatvam api ca kṛtyeṣu sadāviparyāsaḥ || AMsa_16.2 ||
children.translated_text: freedom from the power of afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), and perpetual non-error in duties.' // AMsa_16.2 //

body.text: iti prathamaḥ | tatra catasṛbhiḥ pāramitābhiś caturvidho 'bhyudayaḥ | dānena bhogasaṃpat | śīlenātmabhāvasaṃpat | kṣāntyā paricārasaṃpat | tathā hi tadāsevanād āyatyād bahujanasupriyo bhavati | vīryeṇārambhasaṃpat sarvakarmāntasaṃpattitaḥ | pañcamyā kleśāvaśagatvaṃ dhyānena kleśaviṣkambhanāt | ṣaṣṭyā kṛtyeṣv aviparyāsaḥ sarvakāryayathābhūtaparijñānāt | ity abhyudayaḥ tatra cāsaṃkleśamaviparītakṛtyārambhaṃ cādhikṛtya ṣaṭ pāramitā vyavasthitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the first. Therein, by four <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), there is fourfold prosperity. By generosity (<s>dāna</s>), prosperity of possessions. By morality (<s>śīla</s>), prosperity of personal existence. By patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), prosperity of attendants — for through devotion to it, one becomes well-beloved by many people in the future. By vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), prosperity of undertakings, through the perfection of all enterprises. By the fifth [<s>dhyāna</s>], freedom from the power of afflictions, since through meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) afflictions are suppressed. By the sixth [<s>prajñā</s>], non-error in duties, through the knowledge of all affairs as they truly are. Thus there is prosperity; and with respect to freedom from defilement, non-erroneous engagement in duties, six <s>pāramitās</s> are established.

children.translated_text: 'Well-engaged in the welfare of beings, one accomplishes [their aims] through relinquishment, non-harm, and forbearance;
and through [having] a cause, stability, and liberation, one pursues one's own welfare in every way.' // AMsa_16.3 //

body.text: iti dvitīyaḥ | satvārtheṣu samyakprayukto bodhisatvas tisṛbhir dānaśīlakṣāntipāramitābhir yathākramaṃ tyāgenānupaghātenāupaghātamarṣaṇena ca satvārthaṃ kurute | tisṛbhiḥ sanidānatayā cittasthityā vimuktyā ca sarvaprakāram ātmārthaṃ carati | vīryaṃ niśritya yathākramaṃ dhyānaprajñābhyāsamāhitasya cittasya samavadhānāt samāhitasya mocanāt | iti parārtham ātmārthaṃ cārabhya ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the second. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> properly engaged in the welfare of beings accomplishes the welfare of beings through the three [perfections] — generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), and patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) — respectively through relinquishment, non-harm, and forbearance of harm. Through the [other] three, one pursues one's own welfare in every way — through having a cause (<s>sanidāna</s>), through stability of mind, and through liberation. Based on vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), respectively: through the concentration (<s>dhyāna</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) practice — through the composure of the concentrated mind, and through the liberation of the composed [mind]. Thus, with respect to the welfare of others and one's own welfare, six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: 'Through non-obstruction, non-harassment, forbearance of harassment, unwearied activity,

children.text: āvarjanaiḥ sulapitaiḥ parārtha ātmārtha etasmāt || AMsa_16.4 ||
children.translated_text: attraction, and good speech — the welfare of others [is achieved], and from that, one's own welfare.' // AMsa_16.4 //

body.text: iti tṛtīyaḥ | dānādibhirbodhisatvasya sakalaḥ parārtho bhavati | yathākrama pareṣām upakaraṇāvighātai | aviheṭhaiḥ viheṭhanāmarṣaṇaiḥ | sāhāyyakriyāsvakhedaiḥ ṛddhyādiprabhāvāvarjanaiḥ subhāṣitasulapitaiś ca saṃśayacchedanāt | etasmāt parārthāt bodhisatvasyātmārtho bhavati | parakāryasvakāryatvān mahābodhiprāptitaś ca | iti sakalaparārthādhikārāt ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the third. Through generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s complete welfare of others is achieved. In order, respectively: through non-obstruction of others' resources; through non-harassment and forbearance of harassment; through unwearied activity in helping; through attraction by the power of miraculous abilities (<s>ṛddhi</s>) and the like; and through well-spoken words, from cutting through doubts. From this welfare of others, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s own welfare arises — because others' tasks become one's own tasks, and because of attaining great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). Thus, from the scope of complete welfare of others, six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.text: bhogeṣu cānabhiratis tīvrā gurutādvaye akhedaś ca |
children.translated_text: 'Non-attachment to enjoyments, intense reverence for the twofold [training], unwearied [effort],

children.text: yogaś ca nirvikalpaḥ samas tam idam uttamaṃ yānaṃ || AMsa_16.5 ||
children.translated_text: non-conceptual yoga, and equanimity — this is the supreme vehicle.' // AMsa_16.5 //

body.text: iti caturthaḥ | dānena bodhisatvasya bhogeṣv abhiratir nirapekṣatvāt | śīlasamādānena bodhisatvaśikṣāsu tīvrā gurutā | kṣāntyā vīryeṇa cākhedo dvaye yathākramaṃ duḥkhe ca satvāsatvakṛte kuśalaprayoge ca | dhyānaprajñāyāṃ nirvikalpo
body.translated_text: This is the fourth. Through generosity (<s>dāna</s>), a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has non-attachment to enjoyments, from being free of expectation. Through undertaking morality (<s>śīla</s>), there is intense reverence for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> trainings. Through patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) and vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), there is unwearied [effort] regarding the twofold [challenge], respectively: regarding suffering caused by sentient beings and non-sentient [forces], and regarding wholesome practice. Through meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), there is non-conceptual

body.text: yogaḥ śamathavipaśyanāsaṃgṛhītaḥ | etāvac ca samastamahāyānasaṃgrahādhikārāt ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: yoga, comprised of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). And this much constitutes the entire scope of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; hence six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.translated_text: 'A path of non-attachment to objects; another in restraint regarding their attainment and distraction;
another in not abandoning beings and increasing [wholesome qualities], and in purifying obstructions.' // AMsa_16.6 //

body.text: iti pañcamaḥ | tatra dānaṃ viṣayeṣv asaktimārgas tyāgābhyāsena tatsaktivigamāt | śīlaṃ tadāptivikṣepasaṃyameṣu bhikṣusaṃvarasthasya viṣayāprāptaye sarvakarmāntavikṣepāṇām apravṛtteḥ | kṣāntiḥ satvānutsarge sarvopakāraduḥkhānudvegāt | vīryaṃ kuśalavivardhana ārabdhavīryasya tadvaddhigamanāt | dhyānaṃ prajñā cāvaraṇaviśodhaneṣu mārgas tābhyāṃ kleśajñeyāvaraṇaviśodhanāt | mārga ity upāyaḥ | evaṃ sarvakāramārgādhikārāt ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the fifth. Therein, generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is the path of non-attachment to objects, since through the practice of relinquishment, attachment to them departs. Morality (<s>śīla</s>) is for restraint regarding the attainment of objects and distractions — for one established in the <s>bhikṣu</s>-discipline, through non-attainment of objects and non-engagement in all distracting activities. Patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is for not abandoning beings, from being undisturbed by all the suffering of service. Vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is for increasing wholesome [qualities], since for one who has aroused vigor, those [qualities] increase. Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) are the path for purifying obstructions, since through those two, the affliction-obstruction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the knowledge-obstruction (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) are purified. 'Path' means method. Thus, from the scope of the complete path, six <s>pāramitās</s>.

children.text: śikṣātrayam adhikṛtya ca ṣaḍ pāramitā jinaiḥ samākhyātāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'With reference to the threefold training (<s>śikṣā</s>), six <s>pāramitās</s> have been declared by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors);

children.text: ādyā tisro dvedhā antyadvayatas tisṛṣv ekā || AMsa_16.7 ||
children.translated_text: the first three in one way, and one [perfection] in each of the last two, and one in [all] three.' // AMsa_16.7 //

body.text: iti ṣaṣṭhaḥ | tatrādyā adhiśīlaṃ śikṣā tisraḥ pāramitāḥ sasaṃbhārasaparivāragrahaṇāt | dānena hi bhoganirapekṣaḥ śīlaṃ samādatte samāttaṃ ca kṣāntyā rakṣaty ākruṣṭāpratyākrośanādibhiḥ | dvidhety adhicittam adhiprajñaṃ ca śikṣā sā antena dvayena saṃgṛhītā yathākramaṃ dhyānena prajñayā ca | tisṛṣv api śikṣāsv ekā vīryapāramitā veditavyā | sarvāsāṃ vīryasahāyatvāt | lakṣaṇavibhāge ślokāḥ ṣaṭ |
body.translated_text: This is the sixth. Therein, the first — the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>) — comprises three <s>pāramitās</s>, since it includes the provisions and accompaniments. For through generosity (<s>dāna</s>), being free from attachment to possessions, one undertakes morality (<s>śīla</s>); and through patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), one guards what has been undertaken, through not retaliating when reviled, and so forth. 'Twofold' means the training in higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) and the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>) — those are comprised by the last two, respectively by meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). In all three trainings, the one [perfection] of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) should be understood, since vigor accompanies all of them. On the division of characteristics, six verses:

children.text: dānaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: 'Generosity (<s>dāna</s>) — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfilling all wishes, and maturing beings in three ways.' // AMsa_16.8 //

body.text: bodhisatvānāṃ dānaṃ caturvidhalakṣaṇaṃ | vipakṣahīnaṃ tātparyasya prahīṇatvāt | nirvikalpajñānasahagataṃ dharmanairātmyaprativedhayogāt sarvecchāparipūrakaṃ yo yad icchati tasmai tasya dānāt | satvaparipācakaṃ tredhā dānena satvān saṃgṛhya triṣu yāneṣu yathābhavyaniyojanāt |
body.translated_text: The generosity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> has a fourfold characteristic: free from the opponent, since the inclination [toward the opponent] has been abandoned; accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge, through the penetration of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>; fulfilling all wishes, from giving to each what they desire; and maturing beings in three ways — by gathering beings through generosity and engaging them in the three vehicles according to their capacity.

children.text: śīlaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: 'Morality (<s>śīla</s>) — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfilling all wishes, and maturing beings in three ways.' // AMsa_16.9 //
'Patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfilling all wishes, and maturing beings in three ways.' // AMsa_16.10 //

children.text: vīryaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nivikalpena |
children.translated_text: 'Vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfilling all wishes, and maturing beings in three ways.' // AMsa_16.11 //

children.text: dhyānaṃ vipakṣahīnaṃ jñānena gataṃ ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: 'Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfilling all wishes, and maturing beings in three ways.' // AMsa_16.12 //

children.text: prajñā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatā ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: 'Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
fulfilling all wishes, and maturing beings in three ways.' // AMsa_16.13 //

body.text: yathā dānalakṣaṇaṃ caturvidham evaṃ śīlādīnāṃ veditavyaṃ | eṣāṃ tu vipakṣā dauḥśīlyaṃ krodhaḥ kauśīdyaṃ vikṣepo dauṣprajñyaṃ yathākramaṃ | sarvecchāparipūrakatvaṃ śīlādibhiḥ pareṣāṃ sarvakāyavāksaṃyamāparādhamarṣaṇasāhāyyamanorathasaṃśayacchedanecchāparipūraṇāt | satvaparipācakatvaṃ śīlādibhir āvarjya triṣu yāneṣu paripācanāt | anukramavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as the characteristic of generosity is fourfold, so too should it be understood for morality and the rest. Their opponents are, respectively: immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), laziness (<s>kauśīdya</s>), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), and wrong understanding (<s>dauṣprajñya</s>). The fulfillment of all wishes through morality and the rest is from fulfilling others' wishes for complete bodily and verbal restraint, forbearance of offenses, assistance, fulfillment of aspirations, and cutting through doubts, respectively. The maturation of beings through morality and the rest is from attracting [beings] and maturing them in the three vehicles.

children.translated_text: 'From the dependence of the later upon the former, and from the production [of each from the prior],
the teaching is in that order — from the standpoints of inferior and superior, and from coarse to subtle.' // AMsa_16.14 //

body.text: tribhiḥ kāraṇais teṣāṃ dānādīnāṃ krameṇa nirdeśaḥ | pūrvasaṃniśrayeṇottarasyotpatteḥ | bhoganirapekṣo hi śīlaṃ samātte śīlavān kṣamo bhavati kṣamāvān vīryam ārabhate ārabdhavīryaḥ samādhim utpādayati samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | pūrvasya ca hīnatvāt uttarasyotkarṣasthānatvāt | hīnaṃ hi dānam utkṛṣṭaṃ śīlam evaṃ yāvad dhīnaṃ dhyānam utkṛṣṭā prajñeti | pūrvasya cāudārikatvād uttarasya sūkṣmatvāt | audārikaṃ hi dānaṃ supraveśatvāt sukaratvāc ca | sūkṣmaṃ śīlaṃ tato duṣpraveśatvād duṣkaratvāc ca | evaṃ yāvad audārikaṃ dhyānaṃ sūkṣmā prajñeti | nirvacanavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The teaching of generosity and the rest in sequence is for three reasons: because the later arises from the dependence upon the former — for one free from attachment to possessions undertakes morality; one possessing morality becomes patient; the patient one arouses vigor; one who has aroused vigor produces <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); one whose mind is concentrated knows things as they truly are. Also because the former is inferior and the later is the standpoint of superiority — for generosity is inferior and morality is superior, thus up to meditation being inferior and wisdom being superior. And because the former is coarser and the later subtler — for generosity is coarse, being easy to enter and easy to practice; morality is subtler, being harder to enter and harder to practice; thus up to meditation being coarse and wisdom being subtle. On the division of etymology, a verse:

children.text: dāridyasyāpanayāc chaityasya ca lambhanāt kṣayāt kruddheḥ |
children.translated_text: 'From removing poverty, from imparting coolness, from the destruction of anger,
from yoke to the excellent, from holding the mind inwardly, and from knowledge of ultimate truth — the designations.' // AMsa_16.15 //

body.text: dāridryam apanayatīti dānaṃ | śaityaṃ lambhayatīti śīlaṃ tadvato viṣayanimittakleśaparidāhābhāvāt kṣayaḥ kruddher iti kṣāntis tayā krodhakṣayāt | vareṇa yojayatīti
body.translated_text: It removes poverty (<s>dāridrya</s>), hence 'generosity' (<s>dāna</s>). It imparts coolness (<s>śaitya</s>), hence 'morality' (<s>śīla</s>), because one possessing it lacks the burning of afflictions caused by sense-objects. Destruction of anger — hence 'patience' (<s>kṣānti</s>), because through it anger is destroyed. It yokes to the excellent — hence

body.text: vīryaṃ kuśaladharmayojanāt | dhārayaty adhyātmaṃ mana iti dhyānaṃ | paramārtha jānāty anayeti prajñā | bhāvanāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'vigor' (<s>vīrya</s>), from yoking to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. It holds the mind inwardly — hence 'meditation' (<s>dhyāna</s>). It knows ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) through this — hence 'wisdom' (<s>prajñā</s>). On the division of practice (<s>bhāvanā</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: 'Depending on the basis of practice (<s>bhāvanā</s>), the mental attention, the intention,

children.text: upāyaṃ ca vibhutvaṃ ca sarvāsām eva kathyate || AMsa_16.16 ||
children.translated_text: the means, and the mastery — [the practice] of all [perfections] is declared.' // AMsa_16.16 //

body.text: pañcavidhā pāramitābhāvanā | upadhisaṃniśritā | tatropadhisaṃniśritā caturākārā hetusaṃniśritā yo gotrabalena pāramitāsu pratipattyabhyāsaḥ | vipākasaṃniśritā ya ātmabhāvasaṃpattibalena | praṇidhānasaṃniśritā yaḥ pūrvapraṇidhānabalena | pratisaṃkhyānasaṃniśritā yaḥ prajñābalena pāramitāsu pratipattyabhyāsaḥ | manasikārasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā caturākārā | adhimuktimanaskāreṇa sarvapāramitāpratisaṃyuktaṃ sūtrāntam adhimucyamānasya | āsvādanāmanaskāreṇa labdhāḥ pāramitā āsvādayato guṇasaṃdarśayogena | anumodanāmanaskāreṇa sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasatvānāṃ dānādikam anumodamānasya | abhinandanāmanaskāreṇātmanaḥ satvānāṃ cānāgataṃ pāramitāviśeṣam abhinandamānasya | āśayasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā ṣaḍākārā | atṛptāśayena vipulāśayena muditā--āśayena upakārāśayena nirlepāśayena kalyāṇāśayena ca | tatra bodhisatvasya dāne 'tṛptāśayo yad bodhisatva ekasatvasyaikakṣaṇe gaṃgānadīvālukāsamān lokadhātūn saptaratnaparipūrṇān kṛtvā pratipādayet | gaṃgānadīvālikāsamāṃś cātmabhāvān | evaṃ ca pratikṣaṇaṃ gaṃgānadīvālikāsamān kalpān pratipādayet | yathā caikasya satvasyaivaṃ yāvān satvadhātur anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācayitavyas tam anena paryāyeṇa pratipādayet | atṛpta eva bodhisatvasya dānāśaya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya dāne 'tṛptāśayaḥ | na ca bodhisatva evaṃrūpāṃ dānaparaṃparāṃ kṣaṇamātram api hāpayati | na vicchinattyā bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanād iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya dāne vipulāśaya iti | muditataraś ca bodhisatvo bhavati tān satvān dānena tathānugṛhṇan | na tv eva te satvās tena dānenānugṛhyamāṇā iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya dāne muditāśayaḥ | upakārakatarāṃś ca sa bodhisatvas tān satvān ātmanaḥ samanupaśyati | yeṣāṃ tathā dānenopakaroti nātmānaṃ | teṣām anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyupastambhatām upādāya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ āśayaḥ | na ca bodhisatvaḥ satveṣu tathā vipulam api dānamayaṃ puṇyam abhisaṃskṛtya pratikāreṇa vā artho bhavati vipākena vā iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya dānapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ nirlepāśayaḥ | yadbodhisatvas tathā vipulasyāpi
body.translated_text: The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) is fivefold, based on a support (<s>upadhi</s>). Therein, the support-based [cultivation] is fourfold: based on cause — the repeated practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the power of one's lineage (<s>gotra</s>); based on fruition — through the power of the excellence of one's bodily existence; based on aspiration — through the power of former aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>); and based on discernment — the repeated practice of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the power of wisdom. The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>) is fourfold: through the mental attention of conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>), by having conviction in all the <s>sūtras</s> connected with the <s>pāramitās</s>; through the mental attention of savoring (<s>āsvādana</s>), by savoring the attained <s>pāramitās</s> through the experience of their virtues; through the mental attention of rejoicing (<s>anumodanā</s>), by rejoicing in the generosity and the like of all beings in all world-realms; and through the mental attention of delight (<s>abhinandana</s>), by delighting in one's own and beings' future distinction in the <s>pāramitās</s>. The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on intention (<s>āśaya</s>) is sixfold: with an insatiable intention, a vast intention, a joyful intention, a beneficial intention, an unattached intention, and a wholesome intention. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable intention regarding generosity (<s>dāna</s>): a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having filled world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with the seven precious things, would give them to a single being in a single moment; and [he would give] as many bodily existences as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; and thus at every moment he would give for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; and just as for one being, so for as many beings as the entire realm of beings that must be matured toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — he would give to them in this manner — yet the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s intention regarding generosity remains insatiable. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable intention regarding generosity. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not let this succession of generosity lapse even for a moment, does not interrupt it until sitting at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vast intention regarding generosity. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is exceedingly joyful in thus benefiting those beings through generosity — yet it is not those beings who are [truly] benefited by that generosity. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s joyful intention regarding generosity. And that <s>Bodhisattva</s> regards those beings as more beneficial to himself — those whom he thus benefits through generosity, not himself — because of their being the support for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such is that intention. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having generated even such vast merit consisting of generosity toward beings, has no concern with recompense or with fruition. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s unattached intention in the cultivation of the perfection of generosity. That a <s>Bodhisattva</s> rejoices in the ripening of even such vast

body.text: dānaskandhasya vipākam satveṣv abhinandati nātmanaḥ | sarvasatvasādhāraṇaṃ ca kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayati iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya dānapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ kalyāṇāśayaḥ | tatra bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyām atṛptāśayaḥ | yad bodhisatvo gaṃgānadīvālikāsameṣv ātmabhāveṣu gaṃgānadīvālikāsamakalpāyuṣpramāṇeṣu sarvāupakaraṇanirantaravighātī trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātāv agnipratipūrṇe caturvidham īryāpathaṃ kalpayann ekaṃ śīlapāramitākṣaṇaṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitākṣaṇaṃ bhāvayed etena paryāyeṇa yāvāṃś chīlaskandho yāvān ca prajñāsakandho yenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate śīlaskandhaṃ yāvat prajñāskandhaṃ bhāvayed atṛpta eva bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyām āśayo yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyām āśaya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyām atṛptāśayo yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyām āśayaḥ | yadbodhisatvāstāṃ śīlapāramitābhāvanāparaṃparāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanā paraṃparāmā bodhimaṇḍaniṣadanān na sraṃsayati na vicchinatti iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ vipulāśayaḥ | muditataraś ca bodhisatvo bhavati tayā śīlapāramitābhāvanayā yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanayā satvānanugṛhlan | na tv eva te satvā anugṛhyamāṇā iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśyo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ muditāśayaḥ | upakārakatarāṃś ca bodhisatvastān satvānātmanaḥ samanupaśyati | yeṣāṃ tathā śīlapāramitābhāvanayā yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanayā upakaroti nātmānaṃ | teṣām anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhyupastambhatām upādāya iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyām upakārāśayaḥ | na ca bodhisatvastathā vipulam api śīlapāramitābhāvanāmayaṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyam abhisaṃskṛtya pratikāreṇa vārtho bhavati vipākena vā iti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ nirlepāśayaḥ | tatra yad bodhisatva evaṃ śīlapāramitābhāvanāmayasya yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāmayapuṇyaskandhasya vipākaṃ satveṣv evābhinandati nātmanaḥ | sarvasatvasādhāraṇaṃ ca kṛtvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau pariṇāmayatīti | ya evaṃrūpa āśayo 'yaṃ bodhisatvasya śīlapāramitābhāvanāyāṃ yāvat prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāṃ kalyāṇāśayaḥ | upāyasaṃniśritā bhāvanā tryākārā | nirvikalpena jñānena trimaṇḍalapariśuddhipratyavekṣaṇatām upādāya | tathā hi sa upāyaḥ sarvamanasikārāṇām abhiniṣpattaye | vibhutvasaṃniśritā pāramitābhāvanā tryākārā | kāyavibhutvataḥ | caryāvibhutvataḥ | deśanāvibhutvataś ca | tatra kāyavibhutvaṃ
body.translated_text: accumulations of generosity among beings, not for himself, and making it common to all beings, dedicates it toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome intention in the cultivation of the perfection of generosity. Therein, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>) up to the cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>): a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in as many bodily existences as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, of lifespans measuring as many <s>kalpas</s> as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, destroying all hindrances uninterruptedly, maintaining the four postures in a great trichiliocosm filled with fire, would cultivate one moment of the perfection of moral discipline up to one moment of the perfection of wisdom — in this manner, he would cultivate the entire aggregate of moral discipline up to the entire aggregate of wisdom by which one awakens to unsurpassed perfect awakening — yet the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom remains insatiable. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s insatiable intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. That the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not let that succession of cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom lapse or be interrupted until sitting at the seat of awakening — such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s vast intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is exceedingly joyful in thus benefiting beings through the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom — yet those beings are not [truly] being benefited. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s joyful intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s> regards those beings as more beneficial to himself — those whom he thus benefits through the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, not himself — because of their being the support for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s beneficial intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. And the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having generated even such vast merit consisting of the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom, has no concern with recompense or with fruition. Such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s unattached intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. Therein, that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> rejoices in the ripening of the accumulation of merit consisting of the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom among beings alone, not for himself, and making it common to all beings, dedicates it toward unsurpassed perfect awakening — such an intention is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s wholesome intention in the cultivation of the perfection of moral discipline up to the perfection of wisdom. The cultivation based on skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) is threefold: based on the observation of the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>) through non-conceptual knowledge. For that skillful means is for the completion of all mental attitudes. The cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s> based on sovereign power (<s>vibhutva</s>) is threefold: through sovereignty of body, through sovereignty of conduct, and through sovereignty of teaching. Therein, with respect to sovereignty of body

body.text:
tathāgate dvau kāyau draṣṭavyau svābhāvikaḥ sāṃbhogikaś ca | tatra caryāvibhutvaṃ nairmāṇikaḥ kāyo draṣṭavyaḥ | yena sarvākārāṃ sarvasatvānāṃ sahadhārmikacaryāṃ darśayati | deśanāvibhutvaṃ
ṣaṭpāramitāsarvākāradeśanāyām avyāghātaḥ | prabhedasaṃgrahe dvādaśa ślokāḥ | dānādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ ṣaḍarthaprabhedataḥ | ṣaḍarthāḥ svabhāvahetuphalakarmayogavṛttyarthāḥ | tatra dānaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: , in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, two bodies should be seen: the essential body (<s>svābhāvikakāya</s>) and the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s>). Therein, with respect to sovereignty of conduct, the emanation body (<s>nairmāṇikakāya</s>) should be seen — by which he displays the conduct of <s>Dharma</s>-companionship in all its aspects to all beings. Sovereignty of teaching is unobstructed teaching of all aspects of the six <s>pāramitās</s>. On the summary of divisions, twelve verses. For each of generosity and the rest, there is a sixfold division of meaning. The six meanings are: self-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), cause (<s>hetu</s>), fruit (<s>phala</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), application (<s>yoga</s>), and mode (<s>vṛtti</s>). Therein, on the division of generosity, two verses:

children.translated_text: The giving of goods, with volition (<s>cetanā</s>) as the established root,
excellence of possessions and of bodily existence — fulfilling the benefit of both [self and others]. // AMsa_16.17 //
Accompanied by freedom from avarice, and with regard to what is seen, to the present, to material things, and to fearlessness —

children.text: dānam eva parijñāya paṇḍitaḥ samudānayet || AMsa_16.18 ||
children.translated_text: having fully understood generosity in this way, the wise one should undertake it. // AMsa_16.18 //

body.text: arthapratipādanaṃ pratigrāhakeṣu dānasya svabhāvaḥ | alobhādisahajā cetanā hatuḥ | bhogasaṃpattir ātmabhāvasaṃpattiś cāyurādisaṃgṛhītā phalaṃ pañcasthānasūtravat | svaparānugraho mahābodhisaṃbhāraparipūriś ca karma | amātsaryayogo amatsariṣu vartate | dṛṣṭadharmāmiṣābhayapradānaprabhedena ceti vṛttiḥ | śīlaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: The giving of goods to recipients is the self-nature of generosity. Volition, conjoined with non-greed and the like, is the cause. Excellence of possessions and excellence of bodily existence, including longevity and the like, is the fruit — as in the <s>Pañcasthāna-sūtra</s>. The benefit of self and others and the completion of the accumulations for great awakening is the action. The application of freedom from avarice operates among those who are free from avarice. And the mode is through the division of giving what is seen, what pertains to the present life, material things, and fearlessness. On the division of moral discipline, two verses:

children.translated_text: Having six limbs, culminating in the state of calm, bestowing stability in good destinies,
a foundation, peaceful, fearless, and conjoined with the accumulation of merit. // AMsa_16.19 //
Obtained through convention and through <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things), it exists among those established in restraint;

children.text: śīlam evaṃ parijñāya paṇḍitaḥ samudānayet || AMsa_16.20 ||
children.translated_text: having fully understood moral discipline in this way, the wise one should undertake it. // AMsa_16.20 //

body.text: ṣaḍaṅgam iti svabhāvaḥ | ṣaḍaṅgīti śīlavān viharati yāvat samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣv iti | śamabhāvāntam iti hetuḥ | nirvāṇābhiprāyeṇa samādānāt | sugatisthitidāyakam iti phalaṃ | śīlena sugatigamanāt | avipratisārādikrameṇa cittasthitilābhāc ca | pratiṣṭhāśāntanirbhītam iti karma | śīlaṃ hi sarvaguṇānāṃ pratiṣṭhā bhavati | kleśaparidāhaśāntyā ca śāntaṃ | prāṇātipātādipratyayānāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Having six limbs' is the self-nature: 'one endowed with moral discipline dwells... up to... one trains in the training rules having undertaken them.' 'Culminating in the state of calm' is the cause — from undertaking [discipline] with the intention of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Bestowing stability in good destinies' is the fruit — because moral discipline leads to good destinies, and because one obtains stability of mind through the sequence beginning with freedom from remorse (<s>avipratisāra</s>). 'A foundation, peaceful, fearless' is the action: moral discipline becomes the foundation of all virtues; it is 'peaceful' through the pacification of the burning of defilements; and it is 'fearless' through the non-arising

body.text: ca bhayāvadyavairāṇām aprasavān nirbhotaṃ | puṇyasaṃbhārasaṃyutam iti yogaḥ sarvakālaṃ kāyavāṅmanaskarmasamāvaraṇāt | saṃketadharmatālabdhaṃ saṃvarastheṣu vidyata iti vṛttis tatra saṃketalabdhaṃ prātimokṣasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ | dharmatāpratilabdhaṃ dhyānānāsravasaṃvarasaṃgṛhītam eṣāsya prabhedavṛttiḥ trividhena prabhedena vartanāt | saṃvarastheṣu vidyata ity ācāravṛttiḥ | kṣāntiprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: of fear, blame, and enmity, which are the conditions for killing and the like. 'Conjoined with the accumulation of merit' is the application — from constantly restraining bodily, verbal, and mental action. 'Obtained through convention and through <s>dharmatā</s>, existing among those established in restraint' is the mode: therein, 'obtained through convention' is included within the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation) restraint; 'obtained through <s>dharmatā</s>' is included within the restraints of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and the undefiled — this is its mode of division, operating through the threefold division. 'Existing among those established in restraint' is the mode of conduct. On the division of patience, two verses:

children.translated_text: Forbearance, endurance, and knowledge — arising from compassion and reliance on the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: pañcānuśaṃsam ākhyātaṃ dvayor arthakaraṃ ca tat || AMsa_16.21 ||
children.translated_text: declared to have five benefits, and serving the purpose of both [self and others]. // AMsa_16.21 //
Conjoined with austerity and strength, it is considered threefold among those [practitioners];

children.text: kṣāntim evaṃ parijñāya paṇḍitaḥ samudānayet || AMsa_16.22 ||
children.translated_text: having fully understood patience in this way, the wise one should undertake it. // AMsa_16.22 //

body.text:
marṣādhivāsajñānam iti trividhiyāḥ kṣānteḥ svabhāvaḥ | apakāramarṣaṇakṣānter marṣaṇāṃ marṣa iti kṛtvā | duḥkhādhivāsakṣānter dharmanidhyānakṣānteś ca yathākramaṃ |
kāruṇyād dharmasaṃśrayād iti hetuḥ | dharmasaṃśrayaḥ punaḥ | śīlasamādānaṃ śrutaparyavāptiś ca | pañcānuśaṃsam ākhyātam iti phalaṃ | yathoktaṃ sūtre | pañcānuśaṃsāḥ kṣāntau | na vairabahulo bhavati | na bhedabahulo bhavati | sukhasaumanasya bahulo bhavati | avipratisārī kālaṃ karoti | kāyasya na bhedāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyate iti | dvayor arthakaraṃ ca tad iti marṣādhivāsanam ity adhikṛtaṃ idaṃ karma | yathoktaṃ |
body.translated_text:
'Forbearance, endurance, and knowledge' is the self-nature of the threefold patience: the patience of forbearing harm (<s>apakāramarṣaṇakṣānti</s>) — using the term 'forbearance' (<s>marṣa</s>); the patience of enduring suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsakṣānti</s>); and the patience of reflecting on the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>), respectively.
'Arising from compassion and reliance on the <s>Dharma</s>' is the cause. 'Reliance on the <s>Dharma</s>' furthermore refers to undertaking moral discipline and acquiring learning. 'Declared to have five benefits' is the fruit, as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'There are five benefits of patience: one is not full of enmity; one is not full of discord; one is full of happiness and mental ease; one dies without remorse; and upon the breaking up of the body, one is reborn among the gods in the heavenly world.' 'Serving the purpose of both' — this refers to forbearance and endurance; this action has been stated [elsewhere]:

children.text: dvayor arthaṃ sa kurūte ātmanaś ca parasya ca |
children.translated_text: One serves the purpose of both — of oneself and of the other —

children.text: yaḥ paraṃ kupitaṃ jñātvā svayaṃ tatropaśāmyati || iti ||
children.translated_text: who, knowing the other to be angry, himself becomes calm therein.

body.text: tapaḥprābalyasaṃyuktam iti yogaḥ | yathoktaṃ | kṣāntiḥ paramaṃ tapa iti | teṣu tad ity ādhāravṛttiḥ kṣamiṣu tadvṛtteḥ | trividhaṃ matam iti prabhedavṛttis trividhakṣāntiprabhedena yathoktaṃ prāk | vīryaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: 'Conjoined with austerity and strength' is the application, as stated: 'Patience is the supreme austerity.' 'Among those, that' is the mode of support — because it operates among those who are patient. 'Considered threefold' is the mode of division, through the threefold division of patience as previously stated. On the division of vigor, two verses:

children.translated_text: Enthusiasm for wholesome [action], properly established in faith and zeal,
and for the increase of virtues such as mindfulness and the like — counteracting defilement. // AMsa_16.23 //
Endowed with virtues such as non-greed and the like, and sevenfold among those [practitioners] —

children.text: vīryam eva parijñāya paṇḍitaḥ samudānayeta || AMsa_16.24 ||
children.translated_text: having fully understood vigor in this way, the wise one should undertake it. // AMsa_16.24 //

body.text: utsāhaḥ kuśale samyag iti svabhāvaḥ | kuśala iti tadanyakṛtyotsāhavyudāsātha samyag ity anyatīrthikamokṣārthotsāhavyudāsārthaṃ | śraddhāc chandapratiṣṭhita iti hetuḥ śraddadhāno hy atīva vīryam ārabhati | smṛtyādiguṇavṛddhāv iti phalaṃ | ārabdhavīryasya
body.translated_text: Enthusiasm for the wholesome in the right way — this is its essential nature. 'Wholesome' is for the exclusion of enthusiasm for tasks other than that; and 'right' is for the exclusion of enthusiasm for liberation according to other <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). 'Established upon faith and desire' — this is the cause, for one who has faith initiates effort exceedingly. 'For the increase of qualities such as mindfulness and so forth' — this is the result,

body.text: smṛtisamādhyādiguṇodbhavāt | saṃkleśaprātipakṣika iti karma | yathoktaṃ ārabdhavīryas tu sukhaṃ viharaty avyavakīrṇaḥ pāpakair akuśalair dharmair iti | alobhādiguṇopeta iti yogaḥ | teṣv ity ārabdhavīryeṣu iyam ādhāravṛttiḥ | saptavidha iti prabhedavṛttiḥ | sa punar adhiśīlādiśikṣātraye kāyikaṃ cetasikaṃ ca sātatyena satkṛtya ca yad vīryaṃ | dhyānaprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: because of the arising of qualities such as mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s>, and so forth for one who has initiated effort. 'Antidotal to defilement' — this is the function. As stated: 'One who has initiated effort abides happily, unmixed with evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.' 'Endowed with qualities of non-attachment and so forth' — this is the connection. 'In those' — in those who have initiated effort — this is the basis-occurrence. 'Sevenfold' — this is the division-occurrence. That effort, moreover, is of body and mind, with continuity and respect, in the three trainings of higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>) and so forth. On the division of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), two verses:

children.translated_text: Stability of the mind internally, established upon mindfulness and effort,
governing higher knowledges and sublime abodes for attaining a happy rebirth. // AMsa_16.25 //

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ pramukhaṃ teṣu vidyate trividhaś ca saḥ |
children.translated_text: It is foremost among <s>dharmas</s>, and it is found in them; it is threefold;

children.text: dhyānam evaṃ parijñāya paṇḍitaḥ samudānayet || AMsa_16.26 ||
children.translated_text: having thus understood <s>dhyāna</s>, the wise one should cultivate it. // AMsa_16.26 //

body.text: sthitiś cetasa adhyātmam iti svabhāvaḥ | smṛtivīryapratiṣṭhitam iti hetuḥ | ālambanāsaṃpramoṣe sati vīryaṃ niśritya samāpattyabhinirhārāt | sukhopapattaye iti phalaṃ dhyānasyāvyābādhopapattiphalatvāt | abhijñāvihāravaśavartakam iti karma | dhyānenābhijñāvaśavartanāt | āryadivyabrāhmavihāravaśavartanāc ca | dharmāṇāṃ pramukham iti prāmukhyena yogaḥ | yathoktaṃ | samādhipramukhāḥ sarvadharmā iti | teṣu vidyata iti dhyāyiṣv iyam ādhāravṛttiḥ | trividhaś ca sa iti savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ avitarko vicāramātraḥ | avitarko avicāraḥ | punaḥ prītisahagataḥ | sātasahagataḥ | upekṣāsahagataś ca | iyaṃ prabhedavṛttiḥ | prajñāprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: 'Stability of the mind internally' — this is its essential nature. 'Established upon mindfulness and effort' — this is the cause, for when there is non-forgetfulness of the object, through reliance on effort, the attainments are produced. 'For attaining a happy rebirth' — this is the result, because the fruit of rebirth in <s>dhyāna</s> is without affliction. 'Governing higher knowledges and sublime abodes' — this is the function, because through <s>dhyāna</s> one governs the higher knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and the noble, divine, and <s>Brahma</s>-abodes (<s>vihāras</s>). 'Foremost among <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the connection by way of pre-eminence. As stated: 'All <s>dharmas</s> have <s>samādhi</s> as their foremost.' 'Found in them' — in meditators — this is the basis-occurrence. 'It is threefold' — with applied thought and sustained thought; without applied thought but with sustained thought only; and without applied thought and without sustained thought. Again: accompanied by joy (<s>prīti</s>); accompanied by pleasure (<s>sāta</s>); and accompanied by equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). This is the division-occurrence. On the division of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), two verses:

children.translated_text: Right discrimination of the knowable, established upon calm and concentration,
for complete liberation from defilement — the living of wisdom and good teaching. // AMsa_16.27 //

children.text: dharmāṇām uttaras teṣu vidyate trividhaś ca saḥ |
children.translated_text: It is supreme among <s>dharmas</s>, and it is found in them; it is threefold;

children.text: prajñām evaṃ parijñāya paṇḍitaḥ samudānayet || AMsa_16.28 ||
children.translated_text: having thus understood <s>prajñā</s>, the wise one should cultivate it. // AMsa_16.28 //

body.text: samyak pravicayo jñeya iti svabhāvaḥ | samyag iti na mithyā jñeya iti laukikakṛtyasamyakpravicayavyudāsārthaṃ | samādhānapratiṣṭhita iti hetuḥ | samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | yasmāt suvimokṣāya saṃkleśād iti phalaṃ | tena hi saṃkleśāt suvimokṣo bhavati | laukikahīnalokottaramahālokottareṇa pravicayena | prajñājīvasudeśana iti prajñājīvaḥ sudeśanā cāsya karma | tena hy anuttaraprajñā jīvakānāṃ jīvati | samyag dharma deśayatīti | dharmāṇām uttara ity uttaratvena yogaḥ | yathoktaṃ | prajñottarāḥ sarvadharmā iti | teṣu vidyate trividhaś ca sa iti vṛttiḥ | prājñeṣu vartanāt trividhena ca prabhedena | laukiko hīnalokottaro
body.translated_text: 'Right discrimination of the knowable' — this is its essential nature. 'Right' means not erroneous; 'of the knowable' is for the exclusion of right discrimination regarding mundane tasks. 'Established upon concentration' — this is the cause, for one whose mind is concentrated knows things as they truly are. 'Because for complete liberation from defilement' — this is the result, for through it there is complete liberation from defilement — through mundane, inferior supramundane, and great supramundane discrimination. 'The living of wisdom and good teaching' — the living of wisdom (<s>prajñājīva</s>) and good teaching — this is its function. For through it, the unsurpassed wisdom lives for living beings, and one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> rightly. 'Supreme among <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the connection by way of supremacy. As stated: 'All <s>dharmas</s> have wisdom as their supreme.' 'Found in them, and it is threefold' — this is the occurrence, because it operates in the wise, and through the threefold division: mundane, inferior supramundane,

body.text: mahālokottaraś ca | uktaḥ pratyekaṃ dānādīnāṃ ṣaḍarthaprabhedena prabhedaḥ | saṃgrahavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: and great supramundane. The division of each of the <s>pāramitās</s> — generosity and the rest — has been stated through the sixfold division of meaning. A verse on the division of classification:

children.translated_text: All wholesome <s>dharmas</s> should be known as scattered, concentrated, or both,

children.text: dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ pāramitābhyāṃ parigṛhītāḥ || AMsa_16.29 ||
children.translated_text: each embraced by two <s>pāramitās</s>. // AMsa_16.29 //

body.text: sarve śuklā dharmā dānādidharmāḥ | tatra vikṣiptā dvābhyāṃ pāramitābhyāṃ saṃgṛhītāḥ prathamābhyāṃ dānasamādānaśīlayor asamāhitatvāt | samāhitā dvābhyāṃ paścimābhyāṃ dhyānayathābhūtaprajñayoḥ samāhitatvāt | ubhaye dvābhyāṃ kṣāntivīryābhyāṃ | tayoḥ samāhitāsamāhitatvāt | vipakṣavibhāge ślokāḥ ṣaṭ |
body.translated_text: All wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are the <s>dharmas</s> of generosity and so forth. Among them, the scattered [<s>dharmas</s>] are embraced by two <s>pāramitās</s> — the first two, generosity and the undertaking of moral discipline, because they are not concentrated. The concentrated [<s>dharmas</s>] are embraced by the last two — <s>dhyāna</s> and wisdom of things as they truly are — because they are concentrated. Both [scattered and concentrated] are embraced by two — patience and effort — because they are both concentrated and non-concentrated. On the division of opponents, six verses:

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktam eva na ca dānaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the giving

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.30 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached, not attached, not attached. // AMsa_16.30 //

body.text: saptavidhā saktir dānasya vipakṣaḥ | bhogasaktiḥ vilambanaśaktiḥ tanmātrasaṃtuṣṭisaktiḥ pakṣapātasaktiḥ pratikārasaktiḥ vipākasaktiḥ | vipakṣasaktistu tadvipakṣalābhānuśayāsamudghātāt | vikṣepasaktiś ca | sa punar vikṣepo dvividhaḥ | manasikāravikṣepaś ca hīnayānaspṛhaṇāt | vikalpavikṣepaś ca dāyakapratigrāhakadānavikalpanāt | ataḥ saptavidhasaktimuktatvāt saptakṛtvo dānasyāsaktatvam uktaṃ |
body.translated_text: The sevenfold attachment is the opponent of giving: attachment to possessions, attachment to delay, attachment to mere contentment with that, attachment to partiality, attachment to reciprocation, attachment to ripening [of merit], and attachment to the opponent — because the latent tendency toward the opponent of giving has not been eradicated; and attachment to distraction. That distraction, moreover, is twofold: distraction of mental attention, from aspiring to the <s>Hīnayāna</s>; and distraction of conceptualization, from conceptualizing the giver, the recipient, and the gift. Therefore, because of being free from sevenfold attachment, the non-attachment of giving has been stated seven times.

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktam eva na ca śīlaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the moral discipline

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.31 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached, not attached, not attached. // AMsa_16.31 //

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā saktikā na kṣāntiḥ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached — the patience

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.32 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached, not attached, not attached. // AMsa_16.32 //

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktam eva ca na vīryaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the effort

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.33 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached, not attached, not attached. // AMsa_16.33 //

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ saktam eva na ca dhyānaṃ |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached, and not attached — the meditation

children.text: na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ na ca saktaṃ bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.34 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached, not attached, not attached. // AMsa_16.34 //

children.text: na ca saktā na ca saktā na ca saktā saktikā na ca prajñā |
children.translated_text: Not attached, not attached, not attached, not attached — the wisdom

children.text: na ca saktā na ca sakta na ca saktā bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.35 ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is not attached, not attached, not attached. // AMsa_16.35 //

body.text: yathā dānāsaktir uktā evaṃ śīle yāvat prajñāyāṃ veditavyā | atra tu viśeṣabhogasaktiparivartena dauḥśīlyādyāsaktir veditavyā vipakṣasaktis tadvipakṣānuśayāsamudghātanāt | vikalpavikṣepaś ca yathāyogaṃ trimaṇḍalaparikalpanāt | guṇavibhāge trayoviṃśatiḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as the non-attachment of giving has been stated, so it should be understood for moral discipline up to wisdom. Here, however, as a special case, by substituting attachment to possessions, one should understand attachment to misconduct and the like as the opponent; and attachment to the opponent — because the latent tendency toward the opponent [of each <s>pāramitā</s>] has not been eradicated; and the distraction of conceptualization — because of the conceptualization of the three spheres, as appropriate. On the division of virtues, twenty-three verses:

children.text: tyaktaṃ buddhasutaiḥ svajīvitam api prāpyārthinaṃ sarvadā kāruṇyāt parato na ca pratikṛtir neṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prārthitaṃ |
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have always given up even their own lives upon finding a supplicant, out of compassion; reciprocation is not desired, nor is any fruit sought;

children.text: dānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā dānaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punar loke 'jñayaṃ sthāpitam || AMsa_16.36 ||
children.translated_text: and through that very giving, all people have been established in the three types of awakening; and through the embrace of giving with knowledge, [giving] has been established as imperishable in the world. // AMsa_16.36 //

body.translated_text: The meaning of the words is easily understood.

children.text: āttaṃ buddhasutair yamodyamamayaṃ śīlatrayaṃ sarvadā svargo nābhimataḥ sametya ca punaḥ saktirna tatrāhitā |
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have always undertaken the threefold moral discipline, consisting of restraint and exertion; heavenly rebirth is not desired, and having attained it, attachment is not placed therein;

children.text: śīlenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā śīlaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punar loke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || AMsa_16.37 ||
children.translated_text: and through that very moral discipline, all people have been established in the three types of awakening; and through the embrace of moral discipline with knowledge, [moral discipline] has been established as imperishable in the world. // AMsa_16.37 //

body.text: trividhaṃ śīlaṃ | saṃvaraśīlaṃ | kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlaṃ | satvārthakriyāśīlaṃ ca | ekātmakaṃ yamasvabhāvaṃ | dve udyamasvabhāve |
body.translated_text: The threefold moral discipline is: the moral discipline of restraint (<s>saṃvaraśīla</s>); the moral discipline that gathers wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīla</s>); and the moral discipline of acting for the welfare of beings (<s>satvārthakriyāśīla</s>). One has the nature of restraint; the [other] two have the nature of exertion.

children.text: kṣāntaṃ buddhasutaiḥ suduṣkaramatho sarvāpakāraṃ nṛṇāṃ na svargārtham asaśaktimato na ca bhayān naivopakārekṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have endured the most difficult [to bear] — all the offenses of people — not for the sake of heavenly rebirth, not from powerlessness, not from fear, and not from expectation of benefit;

children.text: kṣāntyānuttarayā ca sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā kṣāntir jñānaparigraheṇa ca punar loke 'kṣayā sthāpitā || AMsa_16.38 ||
children.translated_text: and through that unsurpassed patience, all people have been established in the three types of awakening; and through the embrace of patience with knowledge, [patience] has been established as imperishable in the world. // AMsa_16.38 //

body.text: iti | kṣāntyānuttarayā caiti duḥkhādhivāsanakṣāntyā ca parāpakāramarṣaṇakṣāntyā ca yathākramaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Through unsurpassed patience' refers to the patience of enduring suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsanakṣānti</s>) and the patience of tolerating the offenses of others (<s>parāpakāramarṣaṇakṣānti</s>), in due order.

children.text: vīryaṃ buddhasutaiḥ kṛtaṃ nirūpamaṃ saṃnāhayogātmakaṃ hantuṃ kleśagaṇaṃ svato 'pi parataḥ prāptuṃ ca bodhiṃ parāṃ |
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have exerted incomparable effort, consisting of armor and application, to destroy the host of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) both in themselves and in others, and to attain supreme awakening;

children.text: vīryeṇaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā vīryaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punar loke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || AMsa_16.39 ||
children.translated_text: and through that very effort, all people have been established in the three types of awakening; and through the embrace of effort with knowledge, [effort] has been established as imperishable in the world. // AMsa_16.39 //

body.translated_text: The armor-effort (<s>saṃnāhavīrya</s>) and the application-effort (<s>prayogavīrya</s>).

children.text: dhyānaṃ buddhasutaiḥ samādhibahulaṃ saṃpāditaṃ sarvathā śreṣṭhair dhyānasukhair vihṛtya kṛpayā hīnāpapattiḥ śritā |
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have accomplished meditation abundant in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) in every way; having dwelt in the most excellent meditative joys, out of compassion they have resorted to a lower rebirth;

children.text: dhyānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā dhyānaṃ jñānaparigraheṇa ca punar loke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || AMsa_16.40 ||
children.translated_text: and through that very meditation, all people have been established in the three types of awakening; and through the embrace of meditation with knowledge, [meditation] has been established as imperishable in the world. // AMsa_16.40 //

body.translated_text: 'Abundant in <s>samādhi</s>' means comprised of the infinite <s>Bodhisattva samādhis</s>.

children.text: jñātaṃ buddhasutaiḥ satatvam akhilaṃ jñeyaṃ ca yat sarvathā saktir naiva ca nirvṛtau prajanitā buddhaiḥ kutaḥ saṃvṛtau |
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> have known the reality of all beings and whatever is knowable in every way; no attachment whatsoever is produced toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> — how much less toward the conditioned;

children.text: jñānenaiva ca tena sarvajanatā bodhitraye ropitā jñānaṃ satvaparigraheṇa punar loke 'kṣayaṃ sthāpitam || AMsa_16.41 ||
children.translated_text: and through that very knowledge, all people have been established in the three types of awakening; and through the embrace of knowledge with beings, [knowledge] has been established as imperishable in the world. // AMsa_16.41 //

body.text: iti | satatvaṃ paramārthasaṃgṛhītaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ pudgaladharmanairātmyaṃ | jñeyaṃ ca yat sarvathety anantasvasaṃketādilakṣaṇabhedabhinnaṃ yad ajñeyaṃ | dānādīnāṃ nirvikalpajñānaparigraheṇākṣayatvaṃ nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe 'pi tadakṣayāt | jñānasya punaḥ satvaparigraheṇa karuṇayā satvānām aparityāgāt | eṣāṃ punaḥ ṣaṇāṃ ślokānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ saptamena ślokena nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Reality' (<s>satattva</s>) — the general characteristic comprised of ultimate truth, the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> (<s>pudgaladharmanairātmya</s>). 'Whatever is knowable in every way' — that which is unknowable, differentiated by the infinite divisions of characteristics such as self-designation and so forth. The imperishability of generosity and the rest through the embrace of non-conceptual knowledge — even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>), because they do not perish. And the imperishability of knowledge through the embrace of beings — because of not abandoning beings out of compassion. The summary meaning of these six verses is indicated by the seventh verse:

children.translated_text: Nobility, disinterestedness, great purpose, and imperishability —

children.text: dānādīnāṃ samas taṃ hi jñeyaṃ guṇacatuṣṭayam || AMsa_16.42 ||
children.translated_text: this fourfold virtue of giving and the rest should be known as equal. // AMsa_16.42 //

body.text: iti | tatra dānādīnāṃ prathamena pādenodāratā paridīpitā | dvitīyena nirāmiṣatā | tṛtīyena mahārthatāḥ mahataḥ satvārthasya saṃpādanāt | caturthenākṣayatā ity eṣāṃ guṇacatuṣṭayam ebhiḥ ślokair veditavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the nobility of giving and the rest is illuminated by the first quarter-verse; disinterestedness by the second; great purpose by the third — because of accomplishing great benefit for beings; and imperishability by the fourth — this fourfold virtue should be understood through these verses.

children.translated_text: The satisfaction of seeing the giver, the fulfillment [of wishes], and even the dissatisfaction of the supplicant, and the aspiration —

children.text: abhibhavati sa tāṃ dātā kṛpālurādhikyayogena || AMsa_16.43 ||
children.translated_text: a compassionate giver surpasses all that through his superior connection. // AMsa_16.43 //

body.text: yācanake hi jane dāyakadarśanāt tataś ca yathā-īpsitaṃ labdhvā manorathaparipūraṇādyā tuṣṭir utpadyate | atuṣṭiś cādarśanād aparipūraṇāc ca | āśāstiś ca yā taddarśane manorathaparipūraṇe ca | sā bodhisatvasyādhikotpadyate
body.translated_text: For in a supplicant, upon seeing the giver and then obtaining what is desired, satisfaction arises from the fulfillment of wishes. Dissatisfaction arises from not seeing [the giver] and from non-fulfillment. And the aspiration — that aspiration to see [the giver] and for the fulfillment of wishes — that arises even more in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

body.text: sarvakālaṃ yācanakadarśanāt tanmanorathaparipūraṇāc ca | adarśanād aparipūraṇāc cātuṣṭiḥ | ato dātā kṛpālus tāṃ sarvam abhibhavaty ādhikyayogāt |
body.translated_text: because of seeing supplicants at all times and fulfilling their wishes; and dissatisfaction arises from not seeing [them] and from non-fulfillment. Therefore, the compassionate giver surpasses all that through his superior connection.

children.translated_text: Because of always giving up lives, possessions, and spouses to beings, and being compassionate in their abandonment,

children.text: āmodate nikāmaṃ tadviratiṃ pālayātra katham || AMsa_16.44 ||
children.translated_text: he rejoices exceedingly — how then could he practice abstinence from that? // AMsa_16.44 //

body.text: tebhyo viratiṃ tadviratiṃ parakīyebhyaḥ prāṇabhogadārebhyaḥ | etena trividhāt kāyaduścaritād viratiśīlaguṇaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: 'Abstinence from that' means abstinence from others' lives, possessions, and spouses. By this, he shows the virtue of the moral discipline of abstinence from the threefold bodily misconduct.

children.translated_text: Without self-regard, equanimous, fearless, giving everything, out of compassion —

children.text: mithyāvādaṃ brūyāt paropaghātāya katham āryaḥ || AMsa_16.45 ||
children.translated_text: how could the noble one speak a false word for the injury of others? // AMsa_16.45 //

body.text: etena mṛṣāvādād viratiguṇaṃ darśayati | ātmahetor mṛṣāvāda ucyeta kāyajīvitāpekṣayā | parahetor vā priyajanapremnā | bhayena vā rājādibhayāt | āmiṣakiṃcitkahetor vā lābhārthaṃ | bodhisatvaś ca svakāyajīvitanirapekṣaḥ | samacittaś ca sarvasatveṣv ātmasamacittatayā | nirbhayaś ca pañcabhayasamatikrāntatvāt | sarvapradaś cārthibhyaḥ sarvasvaparityāgāt | sa kena hetunā mṛṣāvādaṃ brūyāt |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the virtue of abstinence from false speech. False speech might be uttered for one's own sake — from concern for one's body and life; or for others' sake — from affection for dear ones; or from fear — from fear of kings and the like; or for the sake of some small material gain — for the purpose of profit. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is without concern for his own body and life; equanimous toward all beings through the equality of self and other; fearless, having transcended the five fears; giving everything — from the relinquishment of all he has to supplicants. For what reason would he speak a falsehood?

children.translated_text: Equally desiring the welfare [of all], compassionate, extremely fearful of producing suffering in others,
and well-engaged in disciplining beings — he is far removed from the threefold fault of speech. // AMsa_16.46 //

body.text: bodhisatvaḥ sarvasatveṣu samaṃ hitakāmaḥ sa kathaṃ pareṣāṃ mitrabhedārthaṃ paiśunyaṃ kariṣyatīti | sakṛpaś ca paraduḥkhāpanayābhiprāyāt | paraduḥkhotpādane cātyarthaṃ bhīruḥ sa kathaṃ pareṣāṃ duḥkhotpādanārthaṃ paruṣaṃ vakṣyati | satvānāṃ vinaye samyakprayuktaḥ sa kathaṃ saṃbhinnapralāpaṃ kariṣyati tasmād asau suvidūre trividhavāgdoṣāt paiśunyāt pāruṣyāt saṃbhinnapralāpāc ca |
body.translated_text: A <s>Bodhisattva</s> equally desiring the welfare of all beings — how would he engage in slander for the purpose of dividing friends? And being compassionate, with the intention of removing others' suffering, and extremely fearful of producing suffering in others — how would he speak harshly for the purpose of producing suffering in others? Being rightly engaged in the discipline of beings — how would he engage in senseless chatter? Therefore he is far removed from the threefold fault of speech: slander, harsh speech, and senseless chatter.

children.translated_text: Giving everything, compassionate, and well-skilled in dependent arising of <s>dharmas</s> —

children.text: adhivāsayet katham asau sarvākāraṃ manaḥ kleśam || AMsa_16.47 ||
children.translated_text: how would he tolerate any mental affliction (<s>kleśa</s>) in any form? // AMsa_16.47 //

body.text: abhidhyā vyāpādo mithyādṛṣṭir vā yathākramaṃ | eṣa dauḥśīlyapratipakṣadharmaviśeṣayogāc chīlaviśuddhigūṇo bodhisatvānāṃ veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Covetousness, malice, or wrong view, respectively. This quality of moral purity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as arising from the connection with specific <s>dharmas</s> that are antidotes to immorality.

children.text: upakarasaṃjñāmodaṃ hy apakāriṇiparahita saṃjñāṃparahite sadā duḥkhe |
children.translated_text: The perception of benefit and delight [arises] toward the harmful; the perception of the welfare of others [arises] toward the welfare of others; always [there is perception of] suffering [toward beings] in suffering.

children.text: labhate yadā kṛpāluḥ kṣamitavyaṃ tasya kiṃ na syāt || AMsa_16.48 ||
children.translated_text: When the compassionate one obtains [these perceptions], what would there be that is not to be endured for him? // AMsa_16.48 //

body.translated_text: For him, no perception of a harmful agent operates, nor a perception of suffering.

children.translated_text: From the disappearance of the perception of self and other, from love toward others always greater than toward oneself,

children.text: duṣkaracaraṇāt sakṛpe hy aduṣkaraṃ vīryaṃ || AMsa_16.49 ||
children.translated_text: from performing difficult deeds — for the compassionate one, vigor is not difficult. // AMsa_16.49 //

body.text:
sakṛpo bodhisatvaḥ | tatra sakṛpe yat parārthaṃ duṣkaracaraṇād vīrthaṃ tadaduṣkaraṃ ca suduṣkaraṃ ca |
katham aduṣkaraṃ | paratra parasaṃjñāpagamāt | svato'dhikatarāc ca sarvadā pareṣu snehāt | kathaṃ suduṣkaraṃ | yad evaṃ parasaṃjñāpagataṃ ca svatodhikatarasnehaṃ ca tadvīryaṃ |
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is compassionate. Therein, for the compassionate one, the vigor that comes from performing difficult deeds for the sake of others is both not difficult and extremely difficult. How is it not difficult? From the disappearance elsewhere of the perception of other. And from love toward others always greater than toward oneself. How is it extremely difficult? Because that vigor is both free from the perception of other and has love greater than toward oneself.

children.text: alpasukhaṃ hy ātmasukhaṃ līnaṃ parihāṇikaṃ kṣayi samohaṃ |
children.translated_text: Of little happiness, self-focused happiness, contracted, subject to decline, perishable, and accompanied by delusion —

children.text: dhyānaṃ mataṃ trayāṇāṃ viparyayād bodhisatvānām || AMsa_16.50 ||
children.translated_text: such is the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) considered to belong to the [other] three; for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, it is the opposite. // AMsa_16.50 //

body.text: alpasukhaṃ dhyānaṃ laukikānām ātmasukhaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ | līnaṃ laukikānāṃ satkāye śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ ca nirvāṇe | parihāṇikaṃ laukikānāṃ kṣayi śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe tatkṣayāt | samohaṃ sarveṣāṃ yathāyogakliṣṭākliṣṭena mohena | bodhisatvānāṃ punar dhyānaṃ bahusukham ātmaparasukham alīnamaparihāṇikam akṣayyasamohaṃ ca |
body.translated_text: 'Of little happiness' is the meditation of worldly beings. 'Self-focused happiness' is that of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. 'Contracted' refers to worldly beings [who are contracted] in the transitory self, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> [who are contracted] in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Subject to decline' refers to worldly beings. 'Perishable' refers to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder, from the cessation of that [meditation]. 'Accompanied by delusion' refers to all, with afflicted or non-afflicted delusion respectively. But the meditation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is of great happiness, directed to the happiness of self and others, uncontracted, not subject to decline, imperishable, and free from delusion.

children.text: āmoṣais tamasi yathā dīpair nunnaṃ tathā trayajñānaṃ |
children.translated_text: Like [groping] in darkness, like lamps — such is the knowledge of the three;
but like the rays of the sun — the knowledge of the compassionate ones is incomparable. // AMsa_16.51 //

body.text: yathā hastāmoṣais tamasi jñānaṃ parīttaviṣayamapratyakṣam avyaktaṃ ca tathā pṛthagjanānāṃ | yathāvacarake dīpairjñānaṃ prādeśikaṃ pratyakṣaṃ nātinirmalaṃ tathā śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ ca | yathā dinakarakiraṇair jñānaṃ samantāt pratyakṣaṃ sunirmalaṃ ca tathā bodhisatvānāṃ | ata eva tad atulyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Just as [groping] by hand in darkness produces knowledge of limited scope, not directly perceived, and indistinct — such is the [knowledge] of ordinary beings. Just as by lamps in a room, knowledge is local, directly perceived, but not exceedingly clear — such is [the knowledge] of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Just as by the rays of the sun, knowledge is all-pervading, directly perceived, and perfectly clear — such is [the knowledge] of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Therefore it is incomparable.

children.translated_text: From the basis, from the substance, generosity; from the motive, from the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca paraṃ matam || AMsa_16.52 ||
children.translated_text: from the cause, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support — it is considered supreme. // AMsa_16.52 //

body.text: tatrāśrayo bodhisatvaḥ | vastu āmiṣadānasyādhyātmikaṃ vastu paramaṃ | abhyadānasyāpāyasaṃsārabhītebhyas tu
body.translated_text: Therein, the basis is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The substance — the supreme substance of material giving is internal [objects, i.e., the body]. Of the gift of fearlessness, it is [giving] freedom from fear to those afraid of the lower realms and <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text:
tadabhayaṃ |
dharmadānasya mahāyānaṃ | nimittaṃ karuṇā | pariṇāmanā tena mahābodhiphalaprārthanā | hetuḥ pūrvadānapāramitābhyāsavāsanā | jñānaṃ nirvikalpaṃ yena trimaṇḍalapariśuddhaṃ dānaṃ dadāti dātṛdeyapratigrāhakāvikalpanāt | kṣetraṃ pañcavidhaṃ | arthī duḥkhito niḥpratisaraṇo duścaritacārī guṇavāṃś ca | caturṇām uttaraṃ kṣetraṃ paraṃ | tadabhāve pañcamaṃ | niśrayas trividho yaṃ niśritya dadāti | adhimuktir manasikāraḥ samādhiś ca | adhimuktir yathā bhāvanāvibhāge 'dhimuktimanaskāra uktaḥ | manaskāro yathā tatraivāsvādanābhinandanamanaskāra uktaḥ | samādhir ādir yathā tatraiva vibhutvam uktaṃ | evam āśrayādiparasamayo dānaṃ paramaṃ | so'yaṃ cāpadeśo veditavyaḥ | yaś ca dadāti yac ca yena ca yasmai ca yataś ca yasya ca parigraheṇa yatra ca yāvat prakāraṃ tad dānaṃ |
body.translated_text: Of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, it is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The motive is compassion. The dedication is the aspiration for the fruit of great awakening through that. The cause is the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) from previous practice of the perfection of generosity. Knowledge is the non-conceptual [knowledge], by which he gives with the purity of the three spheres — from not conceptualizing the giver, the gift, and the recipient. The field is fivefold: one who is in need, one who is suffering, one who is without refuge, one who is engaged in misconduct, and one who is endowed with qualities. Among the first four, the last field is supreme; in their absence, the fifth. The support is threefold — that upon which he relies when giving: conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>), mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), and concentration (<s>samādhi</s>). Conviction is as stated in the division of cultivation, where the 'mental attention of conviction' is mentioned. Mental attention is as stated there, where the 'mental attention of savoring and delighting' is mentioned. Concentration is the beginning, as 'pervasiveness' is mentioned there. Thus, generosity that is supreme through the basis and so forth should be known. And this designation should be understood: who gives, what, by what [motive], to whom, from what [cause], with what [knowledge], in what [field], and to what extent — that is generosity.

children.translated_text: From the basis, from the substance, morality (<s>śīla</s>); from the motive, from the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca paraṃ matam || AMsa_16.53 ||
children.translated_text: from the cause, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support — it is considered supreme. // AMsa_16.53 //
From the basis, from the substance, vigor (<s>vīrya</s>); from the motive, from the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca paraṃ matam || AMsa_16.54 ||
children.translated_text: from the cause, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support — it is considered supreme. // AMsa_16.54 //
From the basis, from the substance, meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>); from the motive, from the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca paraṃ matam || AMsa_16.55 ||
children.translated_text: from the cause, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support — it is considered supreme. // AMsa_16.55 //
From the basis, from the substance, wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); from the motive, from the dedication,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca parā matā || AMsa_16.56 ||
children.translated_text: from the cause, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support — it is considered supreme. // AMsa_16.56 //

body.text: śīlasya paramaṃ vastu bodhisatvasaṃvaraḥ | kṣānteḥ prāṇāpahāriṇau hīnadurbalau | vīryasya pāramitābhāvanā tadvipakṣaprahāṇaṃ ca | dhānasya bodhisatvasamādhayaḥ | prajñāyās tathatā | sarveṣāṃ śīlādīnāṃ kṣetraṃ mahāyānaṃ | śeṣaṃ pūrvavad veditavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: The supreme substance of morality is the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vow (<s>saṃvara</s>). Of patience, [the supreme field is] one who takes life, [being] inferior and weak. Of vigor, the substance is the cultivation of the perfections and the abandonment of their opponents. Of meditation, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> concentrations. Of wisdom, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). The field of all — morality and the rest — is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The remainder should be understood as before.

children.translated_text: Even a gift that brings happiness to a single being and causes obstruction for many eons

children.text: priyaṃ syād bodhisatvānāṃ prāg eva tadviparyayāt || AMsa_16.57 ||
children.translated_text: would be dear to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — how much more so when it is the opposite! // AMsa_16.57 //

body.text: yadi bodhisatvānāṃ dānam ekasyaiva satvasya sukhadaṃ syād ātmanaś ca bahukalpavighātakṛt | tathāpi tat teṣāṃ priyaṃ syāt karuṇāviśeṣāt kiṃ punar yad anekasatvasukhaṃ ca bhavatyā tmanaś ca bahukalpānugrahakṛt |
body.translated_text: If generosity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were to bring happiness to only a single being and cause obstruction to oneself for many eons, even so it would be dear to them, because of their extraordinary compassion. How much more so when it brings happiness to many beings and provides benefit for many eons!

children.text: yad artham icchanti dhanāni dehinas tadeva dhīrā visṛjanti dehiṣu |
children.translated_text: That very purpose for which embodied beings desire wealth — that the steadfast release to embodied beings;

children.text: śarīrahetor dhanam iṣyate janais tad eva dhīraiḥ śataśo visṛjyate || AMsa_16.58 ||
children.translated_text: that very wealth which people desire for the sake of the body — that the steadfast release a hundredfold. // AMsa_16.58 //

body.translated_text: Herein, the first half is explained by the second half.

children.text: śarīram evotsṛjato na duḥkhyate yadā manaḥ kā draviṇe 'vare kathā |
children.translated_text: When the mind does not suffer even when releasing the body itself, what need is there to speak of inferior possessions?

children.text: tadasya lokottaram iti yan mudaṃ sa tena tat tasya tad uttaraṃ punaḥ || AMsa_16.59 ||
children.translated_text: That [experience] of his is supramundane — this is what [brings] him joy; that for him is superior indeed. // AMsa_16.59 //

body.text: atra śarīram evāutsṛjato yadā mano na duḥkhyate tadasya lokottaram iti saṃdarśitaṃ | eti yan mudaṃ sa tena duḥkhena tat tasya taduttaram iti tasmāl lokottarād uttaraṃ |
body.translated_text: Herein, when the mind does not suffer even when releasing the body itself — this is shown to be supramundane for him. 'That [brings] him joy' — by that suffering, 'that for him is superior' — superior to that which is supramundane.

children.translated_text: Even having obtained desired and wished-for gifts, the one in need does not attain satisfaction;

children.text: sarvastidānena yatheha dhīmān tuṣṭiṃ vrajaty arthijanasya tuṣṭyā || AMsa_16.60 ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one attains satisfaction through giving everything here, by the satisfaction of the one in need. // AMsa_16.60 //

body.text: iṣṭanikām alabdhair ity abhipretaparyāptalabdhaiḥ | sarvāstidāneneti yāvat svajīvitadānena |
body.translated_text: 'Not having obtained the desired and wished-for' means not having obtained what is desired in full measure. 'Through giving everything' means up to and including the gift of one's own life.

children.text: saṃpūrṇabhogo na tathāstimantam ātmānam anvīkṣati yācako 'pi |
children.translated_text: Even one whose enjoyments are complete does not see himself as one who possesses, even [when receiving] as a supplicant;

children.text: sarvastidānād adhano 'pi dhīmān ātmānam anveti yathāstimantaṃ || AMsa_16.61 ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one, though destitute, from giving everything, sees himself as one who possesses. // AMsa_16.61 //

children.text: suvipulam api vittaṃ prāpya naivopakāraṃ vigaṇayati tathārthī dāyakāl lābhahetoḥ |
children.translated_text: Even having obtained exceedingly abundant wealth, the one in need does not consider the benefit thus [received] from the donor for the sake of gain;

children.text: vidhivad iha sudānair arthinas tarpayitvā mahadupakarasaṃjñāṃ teṣu dhīmān yathaiti || AMsa_16.62 ||
children.translated_text: but the wise one here, having satisfied those in need with proper and excellent gifts, develops the perception of great benefit toward them. // AMsa_16.62 //

body.translated_text: Because of extraordinary compassion. The meaning of the [following] verses has been explained:

children.text: svayam apagataśokā dehinaḥ svastharūpā vipulam api gṛhītvā bhuñjate yasya vittaṃ |
children.translated_text: Embodied beings, free from grief, healthy in form, enjoy the abundant wealth of one who

children.text: pathi paramaphalāḍhyād bhogavṛkṣād yathaiva pravisṛtir atibhogī bodhisatvān na so 'nyaḥ || AMsa_16.63 ||
children.translated_text: is like a fruit-laden tree on the path, supremely fruitful — that overflowing giver is none other than a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // AMsa_16.63 //

body.text: pravisṛtir atibhogaś cāsyeti pravisṛtir atibhogī sa ca nānyo bodhisatvād veditavyaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Overflowing and one who gives abundantly' — that overflowing giver should be known as none other than a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The rest has been explained.

children.translated_text: From the distinction of preeminence, its cause, and action; from the distinction of types, of basis,

children.text: caturvibandhapratipakṣabhedāt vīryaṃ parijñeyam iti pradiṣṭam || AMsa_16.64 ||
children.translated_text: and from the distinction of the antidote to the fourfold bondage — vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) has been taught as what should be fully known. // AMsa_16.64 //

body.text: ṣaḍvidhena prabhedena vīryaṃ parijñeyaṃ | prādhānyabhedena | tatkāraṇabhedena | prakārabhedena | āśrayabhedena | caturvibandhapratipakṣabhedena ca | asyād deśasyottaraiḥ ślokair nirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: Vigor should be fully known through sixfold distinction: distinction of preeminence, distinction of its cause, distinction of action, distinction of types, distinction of basis, and distinction of the antidote to the fourfold bondage. The exposition of this subject [follows] in the subsequent verses.

children.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ śuklagaṇasya madhye tanniśritas tasya yato 'nulābhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Vigor is supreme among the class of wholesome [qualities], for dependent on it, their attainment follows.

children.text: vīryeṇa sadyaḥ susukho vihāro lokottarā lokagatāṃ ca siddhiḥ || AMsa_16.65 ||
