children.translated_text: Through vigor, there is immediately a perfectly happy abiding; and both supramundane and mundane accomplishment. // AMsa_16.65 //

body.text: vīryaṃ paraṃ śuklagaṇasya madhye iti sarvaśuklagaṇasya madhye iti sarvakuśaladharmaprādhānyaṃ vīryasya nirdiṣṭaṃ | tanniśritastasya yato 'nulābha iti prādhānyakāraṇaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ | yasmād vīryāśritaḥ sarvakuśaladharmalābhaḥ | vīryeṇa sadyaḥ susukho vihāro lokottarā lokagatā ca siddhir iti karma nirdiṣṭaṃ | vīryeṇa hi dṛṣṭadharme paramaḥ sukhavihāraḥ | sarvā ca lokottarā siddhir laukikī ca kriyate |
body.translated_text: 'Vigor is supreme among the class of wholesome [qualities]' — the preeminence of vigor among all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is stated. 'Dependent on it, their attainment follows' — the cause of preeminence is stated, since the attainment of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> depends on vigor. 'Through vigor, there is immediately a perfectly happy abiding, and both supramundane and mundane accomplishment' — the action [of vigor] is stated. For through vigor, in the present life there is supreme happy abiding, and all supramundane as well as mundane accomplishment is achieved.

children.text: vīryāvad avāptaṃ bhavabhogam iṣṭaṃ vīryeṇa śuddhiṃ prabalām upetāḥ |
children.translated_text: Through vigor, desired enjoyments of existence are obtained; through vigor, they attain powerful purification;

children.text: vīryeṇa satkāyam atītya muktā vīryeṇa bodhiṃ paramāṃ vibuddhāḥ || AMsa_16.66 ||
children.translated_text: through vigor, having transcended the [compounded] body, they are liberated; through vigor, they are awakened to supreme <s>bodhi</s>. // AMsa_16.66 //

body.text: iti | paryāyadvāreṇa vīryasya karma nirdiṣṭaṃ | laukikalokottarasiddhibhedāt | tatra prabalā laukikī siddhir anātyantikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus, by way of synonymous expression, the action of vigor is stated — from the distinction of mundane and supramundane accomplishment. Therein, the 'powerful' is the mundane accomplishment, because it is not ultimate.

children.text: punar mataṃ hānivivṛddhivīryaṃ mokṣādhipaṃ pakṣavipakṣam anyat |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, vigor of decrease and increase; another that is sovereign over liberation;

children.text: tattve praviṣṭaṃ parivartakaṃ ca vīryaṃ mahārthaṃ ca niruktam anyat || AMsa_16.67 ||
children.translated_text: that of the favorable and unfavorable factor; that entered into reality; that which transforms; and another proclaimed as of great purpose. // AMsa_16.67 //

children.text: saṃnāhavīryaṃ prathamaṃ tataś ca prayogavīryaṃ vidhivatprahitaṃ |
children.translated_text: First is the armor-vigor (<s>saṃnāhavīrya</s>); then the vigor of application (<s>prayogavīrya</s>), properly directed;

children.text: alīnam akṣobhyam atuṣṭivīryaṃ sarvaprakāraṃ pravadanti buddhāḥ || AMsa_16.68 ||
children.translated_text: uncontracted, unshakeable, and vigor of non-complacency — the <s>Buddhas</s> declare all types. // AMsa_16.68 //

body.text: ity eṣa prakārabhedaḥ | tatra hānivivṛddhivīryaṃ samyakprahāṇeṣu ca dvayoḥ kuśaladharmābhivṛddhaye | mokṣādhipaṃ vīryam indriyeṣu | mokṣādhipatyārthena yasmād indriyāṇi | pakṣavipakṣaṃ baleṣu vipakṣānavamṛdyārthena yasmād balāni | tatve praviṣṭaṃ bodhyaṅgeṣu darśanamārge tadvyavasthāpanāt | parivartakaṃ mārgāṅgeṣu bhāvanāmārge 'ntasyāśrayaparivṛttihetutvāt | mahārthaṃ vīryaṃ pāramitāsvabhāvaṃ svaparārthādhikārāt | saṃnāhavīryaṃ prayogāya saṃnahyataḥ | prayogavīryaṃ tathā prayogataḥ | alīnavīryam udāre 'pyadhigantavye layābhāvataḥ | akṣobhyavīryaṃ śītaloṣṇādibhir duḥkhair avikopanataḥ | asaṃtuṣṭivīryam alpenādhigamenāsaṃtuṣṭitaḥ | ebhir eva
body.translated_text: This is the distinction of types. Therein, 'vigor of decrease and increase' is in the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), for the increase of both wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. 'Sovereign over liberation' is vigor in the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), because the faculties have sovereignty for the purpose of liberation. 'Of the favorable and unfavorable factor' is in the powers (<s>bala</s>), because the powers serve the purpose of not being overcome by the unfavorable factor. 'Entered into reality' is in the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), on the path of seeing, because of being established therein. 'That which transforms' is in the limbs of the path (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), on the path of cultivation, because it is the cause of the final transformation of the basis. 'Of great purpose' is vigor in the nature of the perfections, because of the scope of one's own and others' purposes. Armor-vigor is that of one who girds [himself] for the undertaking. Application-vigor is that of the actual undertaking. Uncontracted vigor is from the absence of laxity even when what is to be attained is lofty. Unshakeable vigor is from not being disturbed by sufferings such as cold, heat, and so forth. Vigor of non-complacency is from not being satisfied with small attainments. By these very [types] — armor-vigor and so forth — in the <s>sūtra</s> it is said:

body.text: saṃnāhavīryādibhiḥ sūtre | sthāmavān vīryavānutsāhī dṛḍhaparākramo anikṣiptadhuraḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣv ity ucyate yathākramaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Endowed with strength, endowed with vigor, enthusiastic, of firm exertion, not casting aside the burden with respect to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — [these terms] correspond to them in sequence.

children.translated_text: Another [distinction of vigor is] inferior, middling, and superior — according to the basis of persons engaged in the three vehicles;

children.text: līnātyudārāśayabuddhiyogāt vīryaṃ tad alpārthamahārtham iṣṭam || AMsa_16.69 ||
children.translated_text: from the connection of contracted, overly lofty, and [balanced] intention and wisdom — that vigor is considered of small purpose and great purpose. // AMsa_16.69 //

body.text: atrāśrayaprabhedena vīryabhedo nirdiṣṭaḥ | yānatraye prayukto yo janas tadāśrayeṇa yathākramaṃ nikṛṣṭamadhyottamaṃ vīryaṃ veditavyaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | līnātyudārāśayabuddhiyogāt | līno hi buddhyāśayo yānadvaye prayuktānāṃ kevalātmārthādhikārāt | atyudāro mahāyāne prayuktānāṃ parārthādhikārāt | ata eva yathākramaṃ vīryaṃ ta dalpārthaṃ mahārtham iva svārthādhikārāc ca |
body.translated_text: Here, the division of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is indicated according to the difference of basis. The person engaged in the three vehicles — according to their basis, inferior, middling, and superior vigor should be understood, respectively. For what reason? Because of withdrawn, excessively great aspiration and intelligence. For the aspiration and intelligence of those engaged in the two [lower] vehicles is withdrawn, because of being devoted solely to one's own welfare. It is excessively great for those engaged in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, because of being devoted to the welfare of others. Therefore, respectively, that vigor is of small purpose and of great purpose, as it were, and because of devotion to one's own welfare.

children.text: na vīryavān bhogaparājito 'sti no vīryavān kleśaparājito 'sti |
children.translated_text: 'One who has vigor is never defeated by enjoyments; one who has vigor is never defeated by afflictions;

children.text: na vīryavān khedaparājito 'sti no vīryavān prāptiparājito 'sti || AMsa_16.70 ||
children.translated_text: one who has vigor is never defeated by weariness; one who has vigor is never defeated by [premature] attainment.' // AMsa_16.70 //

body.text: ity ayaṃ caturvibandhapratipakṣabhedaḥ | caturvidho dānādīnāṃ vibandho yena dānādiṣu na pravartate | bhogasaktis tadāgrahataḥ | kleśasaktis tatparibhogādhyavasānataḥ | khedo dānādiṣu prayogābhiyogaparikhedataḥ | prāptir alpamātradānādisaṃtuṣṭitaḥ | tatpratipakṣabhedenaitac caturvidhaṃ vīryam uktaṃ | anyonyaviniścayavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: This is the division of the antidote to the fourfold obstruction. There is a fourfold obstruction to generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest, by which one does not engage in generosity and so forth: attachment to enjoyments, from grasping at them; attachment to afflictions, from the resolve to indulge in them; weariness, from exhaustion through the exertion and effort in generosity and the rest; and [premature] attainment, from contentment with a mere small amount of generosity and so forth. Through the division of their antidotes, this fourfold vigor is stated. On the division of mutual determination, a verse:

children.text: anyonyaṃ saṃgrahataḥ prabhedato dharmato nimittāc ca |
children.translated_text: 'Through mutual inclusion, through division, through <s>dharma</s>, and through cause —

children.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ viniścayaḥ sarvathā jñeyaḥ || AMsa_16.71 ||
children.translated_text: the determination of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) should be known in every way.' // AMsa_16.71 //

body.text: anyonyasaṃgrahato viniścayaḥ | abhayapradānena śīlakṣāntisaṃgraho yasmāt tābhyām abhayaṃ dadāti | dharmadānena dhyānaprajñayor yasmāt tābhyāṃ dharmaṃ dadāti | ubhābhyāṃ vīryasya yasmāt tenābhayaṃ dadāti | kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakeṇa śīlena sarveṣāṃ dānādīnāṃ saṃgrahaḥ | evaṃ kṣāntyādibhir anyonyasaṃgraho yathāyogaṃ yojyaḥ | prabhedato viniścayaḥ | dānaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ dānadānaṃ śīladānaṃ yāvat prajñādānaṃ | parasaṃtāneṣu śīlādiniveśanāt | dharmato viniścayaḥ | ye sūtrādayo yeṣu dānādiṣv artheṣu saṃdṛśyante | ye ca dānādayo yeṣu sūtrādiṣu dharmeṣu saṃdṛśyante | teṣāṃ parasparaṃ saṃgraho veditavyaḥ | nimittato viniścayaḥ | dānaṃ śīlādīnāṃ nimittaṃ bhavati | bhoganirapekṣasya śīlādiṣu pravṛtteḥ | śīlam api dānādīnāṃ bhikṣusaṃvarasamādānaṃ sarvasvaparigrahatyāgāc chīlapratiṣṭhitasya ca kṣāntyādiyogāt | kuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakaśīlasamādānaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ dānādīnāṃ nimittaṃ | evaṃ
body.translated_text: Determination through mutual inclusion: through the gift of fearlessness, morality (<s>śīla</s>) and patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) are included, since through those two one gives fearlessness. Through the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) [are included], since through those two one gives <s>Dharma</s>. Through both [gifts], vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) [is included], since through it one gives fearlessness. Through morality that gathers wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, all [perfections] — generosity and the rest — are included. Likewise, mutual inclusion through patience and the rest should be applied as appropriate. Determination through division: generosity is sixfold — the generosity of generosity, the generosity of morality, up to the generosity of wisdom — because of establishing morality and the rest in the continua of others. Determination through <s>dharma</s>: those sūtras and other [scriptures] that are seen pertaining to those topics of generosity and so forth, and those [practices of] generosity and so forth that are seen in those <s>dharmas</s> — sūtras and the rest — their mutual inclusion should be understood. Determination through cause: generosity becomes the cause of morality and the rest, since one who is indifferent to enjoyments engages in morality and so forth. Morality too is the cause of generosity and the rest — through the undertaking of the <s>bhikṣu</s> discipline, from the relinquishment of all possessions, and from the engagement in patience and the rest by one established in morality. And the undertaking of morality that gathers wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is the cause of all [perfections] — generosity and the rest. Likewise,

body.text: kṣāntyādīnām anyonyanimittabhāvo yathā yojyaḥ | saṃgrahavastuvibhāge sapta ślokāḥ | catvāri saṃgrahavastūni | dānaṃ priyavāditā arthacaryā samānārthatā | tatra |
body.translated_text: the mutual causal relation of patience and the rest should be applied as appropriate. On the division of the means of gathering (<s>saṃgrahavastu</s>), seven verses. There are four means of gathering: generosity (<s>dāna</s>), kind speech (<s>priyavāditā</s>), beneficial conduct (<s>arthacaryā</s>), and equality of purpose (<s>samānārthatā</s>). Therein:

children.translated_text: 'Generosity, equal [to that of the perfections]; kind speech as teaching thereof; beneficial conduct as equality of purpose —
that is accepted as [established] through undertaking and following one's own practice.' // AMsa_16.72 //

body.text: dānaṃ samam iṣyate yathā pāramitāsu priyākhyānaṃ taddeśanā | arthacaryā tatsamādāpanā | tac chabdena pāramitānāṃ grahaṇāt pāramitādeśanā pāramitāsamādāpanety arthaḥ | samānārthatā yatra paraṃ samādāpayati tatra svayam anuvṛttiḥ | kim arthaṃ punar etāni catvāri saṃgrahavastūnīṣyante | eṣa hi pareṣāṃ |
body.translated_text: Generosity is accepted as equal to [the generosity] among the <s>pāramitās</s>. Kind speech is the teaching thereof. Beneficial conduct is the inducement thereof. Since the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>) refers to the <s>pāramitās</s>, the meaning is: the teaching of the <s>pāramitās</s> and the inducement to the <s>pāramitās</s>. Equality of purpose is the following of one's own practice where one induces others. For what purpose are these four means of gathering accepted? For this is toward others:

children.translated_text: 'The means that bestows benefit, that attracts, that sets in motion,
and that follows along — these should be known as the four means of gathering.' // AMsa_16.73 //

body.text: dānam anugrāhaka upāyaḥ | āmiṣadānena kāyikānugrahotpādanāt | priyavāditā grāhakaḥ | avyutpannasaṃdigdhārthagrāhaṇāt | arthacaryā pravartakaḥ | kuśale pravartanāt | samānārthatā 'nuvartakaḥ | yathāvāditathākāriṇaṃ hi samādāpakaṃ viditvā yatra kuśale tena pravartitāḥ pare bhavanti tad anuvartante |
body.translated_text: Generosity is the means that bestows benefit, because it produces bodily welfare through material gifts. Kind speech is that which attracts, because it causes the unlearned and the doubtful to grasp the meaning. Beneficial conduct is that which sets in motion, because it engages [beings] in wholesome [actions]. Equality of purpose is that which follows along, because having recognized the one who induces as one who practices what they preach, others follow along in that wholesome [practice] in which they have been set in motion by that person.

children.translated_text: 'Through the first, one becomes a vessel; through the second, conviction;
through the third, practice; and through the fourth, purification.' // AMsa_16.74 //

body.text: āmiṣadānena bhājanībhavati dharmasya vidheyatāpatteḥ | priyavāditayā taṃ dharmam adhimucyate tadarthavyutpādanasaṃśayacchedanataḥ | arthacaryayā pratipadyate yathādharma | samānārthatayā tāṃ pratipattiṃ viśodhayati dīrghakālānuṣṭhānād | idaṃ saṃgrahavastūnāṃ karma |
body.translated_text: Through material gifts, one becomes a vessel for the <s>Dharma</s>, because of attaining receptivity. Through kind speech, one develops conviction in that <s>Dharma</s>, because of elucidating the meaning and cutting through doubts. Through beneficial conduct, one practices in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Through equality of purpose, one purifies that practice, through long-term cultivation. This is the function of the means of gathering.

children.translated_text: 'The fourfold means of gathering is considered to be based on a twofold gathering —
through material [gifts] and through <s>Dharma</s>, and through <s>Dharma</s> as object.' // AMsa_16.75 //

body.text: yad apy anyat saṃgrahavastudvayam uktaṃ bhagavatā āmiṣasaṃgraho dharmasaṃgrahaś ca | tābhyām etāny eva
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has also spoken of another twofold means of gathering — material gathering and <s>Dharma</s> gathering. Through those two, these very

body.text: catvāri saṃgrahavastūni saṃgṛhītāni | āmiṣasaṃgraheṇa prathame | dharmasaṃgraheṇāvaśiṣṭāni | tāni punas trividhena dharmeṇa | ālambanadharmeṇa pratipattidharmeṇa tadviśuddhidharmeṇa ca yathākramaṃ |
body.translated_text: four means of gathering are included. The first through the material gathering. The remaining [three] through the <s>Dharma</s> gathering. And those [three] are through threefold <s>Dharma</s>: through <s>Dharma</s> as object, through <s>Dharma</s> as practice, and through <s>Dharma</s> as the purification thereof, respectively.

children.translated_text: 'Inferior, middling, and superior; mostly barren and mostly fruitful;

children.text: abandhyaḥ sarvathā caiva jñeyo hy ākārabhedataḥ || AMsa_16.76 ||
children.translated_text: and fruitful in every way — this should be known through the division of aspects.' // AMsa_16.76 //

body.text: eṣa saṃgrahasya prakārabhedaḥ | tatra hīnamadhyottamaḥ saṃgraho bodhisatvānāṃ yānatrayaprayukteṣu veditavyo yathākramaṃ | prāyeṇa vandhyo 'dhimukticaryābhūmau | prāyeṇābandhyo bhūmipraviṣṭānāṃ | avandhyaḥ sarvathā aṣṭamyādiṣu bhūbhiṣu satvārthasyāvaśyaṃ saṃpādanāt |
body.translated_text: This is the division of types of gathering. Therein, the inferior, middling, and superior gathering of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood with respect to those engaged in the three vehicles, respectively. Mostly barren on the stage of practice through aspiration (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>). Mostly fruitful for those who have entered the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>). Fruitful in every way on the eighth and subsequent stages, because of the certain accomplishment of the welfare of beings.

children.translated_text: 'This method is relied upon by those engaged in attracting assemblies;

children.text: sarvārthasiddhau sarveṣāṃ sukhopāyaś ca śasyate || AMsa_16.77 ||
children.translated_text: and it is praised as the easy means for the accomplishment of all aims of all [beings].' // AMsa_16.77 //

body.text: ye kecit parṣatkarṣaṇe prayuktāḥ sarvais tair ayam evopāyaḥ samāśrito yaduta catvāri saṃgrahavastūni | tathā hi sarvārthasiddhaye sarveṣāṃ sukhaś caiṣa upāyaḥ praśasyate buddhaiḥ |
body.translated_text: Whoever is engaged in attracting assemblies — by all of them this very means is relied upon, namely the four means of gathering. For indeed, it is praised by the <s>Buddhas</s> as the easy means for the accomplishment of all aims of all [beings].

children.translated_text: 'Those who have been gathered, those who will be gathered, and those who are being gathered now —

children.text: sarve ta evaṃ tasmāc ca vartma tat satvapācane || AMsa_16.78 ||
children.translated_text: all of them [are gathered] in this way; therefore this is the path for the maturation of beings.' // AMsa_16.78 //

body.text: etena lokatraye 'pi sarvasatvānāṃ paripācane caturṇāṃ saṃgrahavastūnām ekāyanamārgatvaṃ darśayati | anyamārgābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows that the four means of gathering are the sole path (<s>ekāyanamārga</s>) for the maturation of all beings even across the three worlds, because there is no other path.

children.translated_text: 'Thus, with intelligence always unattached to enjoyments, having reached the far shore of calm, self-control, and effort, standing firm,

children.text: bhavaviṣayanimittanirvikalpo bhavati sa satvagaṇasya saṃgṛhītā || AMsa_16.79 ||
children.translated_text: free from conceptualization regarding the signs of existence and sense-objects — one becomes the gatherer of the multitude of beings.' // AMsa_16.79 //

body.text: etena yathoktāsu ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu sthitasya bodhisatvasya saṃgrahavastuprayoga darśayati svaparārthasaṃpādanāt pāramitābhiḥ saṃgrahavastubhiś ca yathākramaṃ |
body.translated_text: By this, he shows the practice of the means of gathering for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> established in the six <s>pāramitās</s> as described, because of accomplishing one's own and others' welfare through the <s>pāramitās</s> and the means of gathering, respectively.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the sixteenth chapter on the perfections (<s>pāramitādhikāra</s>) is completed.

CHAPTER XVII
The seventeenth chapter.
On the division of <s>Buddha</s>-worship (<s>buddhapūjā</s>), seven verses:

children.translated_text: 'Worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> face-to-face and in their absence, with robes and so forth,
by one whose mind is deeply devoted, for the fulfillment of the twofold accumulation.' // AMsa_17.1 //
'For one who makes aspirations, so that <s>Buddha</s>-births may not be fruitless —
the non-apprehension of the three [spheres] is the perfected <s>Buddha</s>-worship.' // AMsa_17.2 //
'For the maturation of immeasurable beings, another [form of worship];

children.text: upadheś cittataś cānyā adhimukter nidhānataḥ || AMsa_17.3 ||
children.translated_text: and another from material offerings and from the mind, from aspiration and from dedication.' // AMsa_17.3 //
'And another from compassion and forbearance, from [wholesome] conduct,

children.text: vastvābhogāvabodhāc ca vimukteś ca tathātvataḥ || AMsa_17.4 ||
children.translated_text: from the understanding of the engagement with reality (<s>vastu</s>), from liberation, and from suchness (<s>tathatā</s>).' // AMsa_17.4 //

body.translated_text: By these four verses:

children.translated_text: 'Worship is demonstrated from the basis, from the substance, from the cause, from the transformation,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca pradarśitā || AMsa_17.5 ||
children.translated_text: from the ground, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support.' // AMsa_17.5 //

body.text: veditavyā | tatrāśrayaḥ samakṣaparokṣā buddhāḥ | vastu cīvarādayaḥ | nimittaṃ pragāḍhaprasādasahagataṃ cittaṃ | pariṇāmanā utpādaḥ syād iti pūrvapraṇidhānaṃ | jñānaṃ nirvikalpaṃ pūjakapūjyapūjānupalambhataḥ | kṣetram aprameyāḥ satvāḥ | tatparipācanāya tais tatprayojatāt teṣu tadropaṇataḥ | niśraya upadhiśritaṃ ca | tatropadhiṃ niśritya pūjā cīvarādibhiś cittaṃ niśrityāsvādanānumodanābhinandanamanaskāraiḥ | tathoktaiś cādhimuktyādibhir yad uta mahāyānadharmādhimuktaḥ bodhicittotpādataḥ | praṇidhānam eva hi nidhānam atroktaṃ ślokavattvānurodhāt | satvānukampanataḥ | duṣkaracaryā duḥkhakṣamaṇataḥ | pāramitāsamudācārataḥ | yoniśo dharmamanasikārataḥ | sa hy aviparyayastatvād vastvābhogaḥ | samyagdṛṣṭito darśanamārge | sa hi yathābhūtāvabodhād vastvavabodhaḥ | vimuktitaḥ kleśavimokṣāc chrāvakāṇāṃ | tathā tv ato mahābodhiprāpter ity ayaṃ pūjāyāḥ prakārabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: It should be understood. Therein, the basis is <s>Buddhas</s> present and absent. The substance is robes and so forth. The cause is a mind accompanied by deep devotion. The transformation is the prior aspiration — 'may it arise.' Knowledge is non-conceptual, through the non-apprehension of worshipper, worshipped, and worship. The field is immeasurable beings — for their maturation, because of engaging them for that purpose and establishing that [wholesome quality] in them. The support is that which depends on material offerings; therein, worship supported by material offerings is through robes and so forth; worship supported by the mind is through mental acts of relishing, rejoicing, and delight. And through the aforementioned aspiration and the rest — namely, aspiration for the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s>, from the generation of the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). For aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) is indeed called 'dedication' (<s>nidhāna</s>) here, in accordance with the meter. From compassion toward beings. From forbearing hardship in difficult practices. From the conduct of the <s>pāramitās</s>. From proper mental attention to the <s>Dharma</s> — for that, being non-erroneous, is the engagement with reality as object. From right view on the path of seeing — for that, being realization as it truly is, is the comprehension of reality. From liberation, through the liberation from afflictions of <s>śrāvakas</s>. 'From suchness' means from the attainment of great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). This is the division of types of worship.

children.text: hetutaḥ phalataś caiva ātmanā ca parair api |
children.translated_text: 'From the standpoint of cause and fruit, by oneself and by others,

children.text: lābhasatkārataś caiva pratipatter dvidhā ca sā || AMsa_17.6 ||
children.translated_text: from the standpoint of gain and honor, and from practice — it is twofold.' // AMsa_17.6 //

children.text: parīttā mahatī pūjā samānāmānikā ca sā |
children.translated_text: 'Small and great worship, and also that which has equal designation;

children.text: prayogād gatitaś caiva praṇidhānāc ca sā matā || AMsa_17.7 ||
children.translated_text: from the standpoint of practice, course, and aspiration — that [worship] is thus considered.' // AMsa_17.7 //

body.text:
ity ayam arthādibhedenāparaḥ prakārabhedaḥ |
tatrātītā hetuḥ pratyutpannā phalaṃ pratyutpannā hetur anāgatā phalam ity evaṃ hetuphalato 'tītānāgatapratyutpannā veditavyā | ātmanety ādhyātmikī parair iti bāhyā | lābhasatkārato audārikī | pratipattitaḥ sūkṣmā | parīttā hīnā mahatī praṇītā | punaḥ samānā hīnā nirmānā praṇītā trimaṇḍalāvikalpanāt | kālāntaraprayojyā dūre | tatkālaprayojyāntike | punar vicchinnāyāṃ gatau dūre | samanantarāyām antike | punar yāṃ pūjām āyatyāṃ prayojayituṃ praṇidadhāti sā dūre yāṃ praṇihitaḥ kartuṃ sāntike | katamā punar buddhapūjā paramā veditavyety āha |

children.text: buddheṣu pūjā paramā svacittāt dharmādhimuktyāśayato vibhutvāt |
children.translated_text: 'The supreme worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> is from one's own mind, from aspiration for the <s>Dharma</s>, from [noble] intent, from sovereignty,
through the embrace of non-conceptual means, and from the establishment in the single purpose of all.' // AMsa_17.8 //

body.translated_text: This is another division of types, by the difference of meaning and so forth. Therein, the past is the cause, the present is the fruit; the present is the cause, the future is the fruit — thus it should be understood as past, present, and future through cause and fruit. 'By oneself' means internal; 'by others' means external. From gain and honor, it is gross. From practice, it is subtle. Small means inferior; great means excellent. Again, 'equal' means inferior; 'emanated' (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) means excellent, because of non-conceptualization of the three spheres. To be practiced at another time means distant. To be practiced at the present time means near. Again, when the course is interrupted, it is distant; when immediately continuous, it is near. Again, the worship one aspires to practice in the future is distant; that which one undertakes as already aspired to is near. What, then, should be known as the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-worship? He says:

body.text: ity ebhiḥ pañcabhir ākāraiḥ svacittapūjā buddheṣu paramā veditavyā | yad uta pūjopasaṃhitamahāyānadharmādhimuktitaḥ | āśayato navabhir āśayaiḥ | āsvādanānumodanābhinandanāśayaiḥ | atṛptavipulam uditopakaranirlepakalyāṇāśayaiś ca ye pāramitābhāvanāyāṃ nirdiṣṭāḥ | vibhutvato gaganagañjādisamādhibhiḥ | nirvikalpajñānopāyaparigrahataḥ | sarvamahābodhisatvaikakāryatvapraveśataś ca miśropamiśrakāryatvāt | kalyāṇamitrasevāvibhāge sapta ślokāḥ | tatrārdhapañcamaiḥ ślokaiḥ |
body.translated_text: By these five aspects, worship from one's own mind should be known as supreme worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>: namely, from aspiration for the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s> accompanied by worship; from [noble] intent, through the nine intents — the intents of relishing, rejoicing, and delighting, and the intents of being insatiable, vast, arisen, preparative, unstained, and excellent — which are taught in the cultivation of the <s>pāramitās</s>; from sovereignty, through <s>samādhis</s> such as the <s>Gaganagañja</s> and others; through the embrace of non-conceptual knowledge and means; and from the entry into the single purpose of all great <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, because of having mixed and combined purposes. On the division of attending upon a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), seven verses. Therein, with four and a half verses:

children.translated_text: 'Attendance [upon a spiritual friend] is demonstrated from the basis, from the substance,

children.text: hetuto jñānataḥ kṣetrān niśrayāc ca pradarśitā || AMsa_17.9 ||
children.translated_text: from the cause, from the transformation, from the ground, from knowledge, from the field, and from the support.' // AMsa_17.9 //

children.text: mitraṃ śrayed dāntaśamopaśāntaṃ guṇādhikaṃ sodyamam āgamāḍhyaṃ |
children.translated_text: 'One should attend a friend who is disciplined, calm, and serene, who has superior qualities, who is diligent, who is rich in scripture,

children.text: prabuddhatatvaṃ vacas ābhyupetaṃ kṛpātmakaṃ khedavivarjitaṃ ca || AMsa_17.10 ||
children.translated_text: who has realized the truth, who possesses [excellent] speech, who is compassionate by nature, and who is free from weariness.' // AMsa_17.10 //

body.text: ity evaṃ guṇamitraṃ sevāyā āśrayaḥ | dāntaṃ śīlayogād indriyadamena | śāntaṃ samādhiyogād adhyātmaṃ cetaḥśamathena | upaśāntaṃ prayogād upasthitakleśopaśamanataḥ | guṇair adhikaṃ na samaṃ vā nyūnaṃ vā | sodyamaṃ nodāsīnaṃ parārthe | āgamāḍhyaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus a virtuous friend (<s>guṇamitra</s>) is the basis of attendance. 'Tamed' (<s>dānta</s>) — through the practice of morality (<s>śīla</s>), by the restraint of the senses. 'Peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>) — through the practice of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), by inner tranquility of mind. 'Thoroughly pacified' (<s>upaśānta</s>) — through practice, from the pacification of present afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>). 'Superior in qualities' — not equal or inferior. 'Energetic' (<s>sodyama</s>) — not indifferent toward the welfare of others. 'Rich in scripture' (<s>āgamāḍhya</s>)

body.text: nālpaśrutaṃ | prabuddhatatvaṃ tatvādhigamāt | vacasābhyupetaṃ vākkaraṇenopetaṃ | kṛpātmakaṃ nirāmiṣacittatvāt | khedavivarjitaṃ sātatyasatkṛtyadharmadeśanāt |
body.translated_text: — not of little learning. 'Awakened to reality' (<s>prabuddhatatva</s>) — from realization of reality (<s>tatva</s>). 'Endowed with speech' — endowed with verbal skill. 'Compassionate by nature' (<s>kṛpātmaka</s>) — from having a mind free of material [motives]. 'Free from weariness' — from teaching the <s>Dharma</s> continuously and respectfully.

body.text: satkāralābhaiḥ paricaryayā ca seveta mitraṃ pratipattitaś ca |
body.translated_text: 'One should attend the [spiritual] friend through honor, gifts, service, and practice.'
Thus regarding attendance:

children.text: dharme tathājñāśaya eva dhīmān mitraṃ pragacchet samaye nataś ca || AMsa_17.11 ||
children.translated_text: 'The wise one, with intention toward the <s>Dharma</s>, should approach the friend at the proper time, and with humility.' // AMsa_17.11 //

body.text: iti trividhaṃ nimittaṃ | ājñātukāmatā | kālajñatā | nirmānatā ca |
body.translated_text: Thus there is a threefold condition: the desire to understand; knowledge of the [proper] time; and humility.

body.text: satkāralābheṣu gataspṛho 'sau prapattaye taṃ pariṇāmayec ca |
body.translated_text: 'One who is free from desire for honor and gains should dedicate [them] for the purpose of practice.'

body.text: iti pariṇāmanā pratipattyarthaṃ sevanān na lābhasatkārārthaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thus, the dedication is for the purpose of practice — attending [the friend] not for the sake of gains and honor.

body.text: yathānuśiṣṭapratipattitaś ca saṃrādhayec cittam ato 'sya dhīraḥ || AMsa_17.12 ||
body.translated_text: 'And the steadfast one should please the [friend's] mind through practice in accordance with instructions.' // AMsa_17.12 //
Thus, practice in accordance with instructions is the cause of attendance — because through it, the [friend's] mind is pleased.

body.text: yānatraye kauśalam etya buddhyā svasyaiva yānasya yateta siddhau |
body.translated_text: 'Having gained skill in the three vehicles through wisdom, one should strive for the accomplishment of one's own vehicle.'
Thus, from skill in the three vehicles, knowledge [arises].

body.text: satvān ameyān paripācanāya kṣetrasya śuddhasya ca sādhanāya || AMsa_17.13 ||
body.translated_text: 'For the maturation of immeasurable beings, and for the accomplishment of a pure [Buddha-]field.' // AMsa_17.13 //

body.text: iti dvividhaṃ kṣetraṃ tatsevāyāḥ | aprameyāś ca satvāḥ pariśuddhaṃ ca buddhakṣetraṃ | dharmaṃ śrutvā yeṣu pratiṣṭhāpanāt | yatra ca sthitena |
body.translated_text: Thus there is a twofold domain of that attendance: immeasurable beings and the purified <s>Buddha</s>-field — beings in whom one establishes [them] upon hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and [the field] in which one abides.

body.text: dharmeṣu dāyād aguṇena yukto naivāmiṣeṇa pravesat sa mitram |
body.translated_text: 'As an heir to the <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with [spiritual] qualities, one should approach the friend — not through material [motives].'

body.text:
iti niśrayaḥ sevāyāḥ | dharmadāyādatāṃ niśritya kalyāṇamitraṃ seveta | nāmiṣadāyādatāṃ |
ata ūrdhvamadhyardhena ślokena prakārabhedaḥ sevāyā veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text:
Thus there is the basis of attendance: one should attend the spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) depending on <s>Dharma</s>-inheritance — not on material inheritance.
From here onward, the division of types of attendance should be understood through one and a half verses:

body.text: hetoḥ phalād dharmamukhānuyānāt seveta mitraṃ bahitaś ca dhīmān || AMsa_17.14 ||
body.translated_text: 'From the cause, from the fruit, from following the gateway of <s>Dharma</s>, the wise one should attend the friend both externally [and internally].' // AMsa_17.14 //
'From hearing and learning, from yoga in the mind, and from the pursuit with a mind free from pride and equal [to others].'

body.text: hetoḥ phalād ity atītādibhedataḥ pūrvavat dharmamukhānuyānāt seveta mitraṃ
body.translated_text: 'From the cause, from the fruit' is the division into past and so forth, as before. 'From following the gateway of <s>Dharma</s>, the wise one should attend the friend

body.text: bahitaś ca dhīmān ity ādhyātmikabāhyabhedaḥ | dharmamukhasroto hi dharmamukhānuyānaṃ bahirdhā bahitaḥ śrutaśravāc cetasi yogataś cety audārikasūkṣmabhedaḥ | śravaṇaṃ hy audārikaṃ cintanabhāvanaṃ sūkṣmaṃ | tad eva cetasi yogaḥ | samānanirmānamano'nuyogād iti hīnapraṇītabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: externally' is the division into internal and external. Following the stream of the <s>Dharma</s> gateway externally is 'externally.' 'From hearing and learning, from yoga in the mind' is the division into coarse and subtle — for hearing is coarse, while reflection and meditation are subtle; that itself is 'yoga in the mind.' 'From the pursuit with a mind free from pride and equal [to others]' is the division into inferior and excellent.

body.text: gatiprayogapraṇidhānataś ca kalyāṇamitraṃ hi bhajet dhīmān || AMsa_17.15 ||
body.translated_text: 'From the course of practice, from aspiration — the wise one should devote oneself to the spiritual friend.' // AMsa_17.15 //

body.text:
iti dūrāntikabhedaḥ purvavad yojayitavyaḥ |
katamā punaḥ paramā seveti saptamaḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text:
This is the division into distant and near, to be connected as before.
What then is the supreme attendance? The seventh verse:

children.translated_text: 'The supreme attendance of a good friend is from one's own mind, from the intention of devotion to the <s>Dharma</s>, through masteries,
through the embrace of non-conceptual means, and from being established in the single task of all.' // AMsa_17.16 //

body.translated_text: This is as before. On the division of the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇas</s>), twelve verses:

children.text: brāhmā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatāś ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Brahma</s>-[abodes] — free from the opponent, accompanied by non-conceptual knowledge,
operating with threefold objects, and maturing beings — for the steadfast.' // AMsa_17.17 //

body.text: brāhmyā vihārāś catvāry apramāṇāni | maitrī karuṇā muditopekṣā ca | te punar bodhisatve caturlakṣaṇā veditavyāḥ | vipakṣahānitaḥ | pratipakṣaviśeṣayogataḥ | vṛttiviśeṣatas trividhālambanavṛttitvāt | tathā hi te satvālambanā dharmālambanāśca | karmaviśeṣataś ca | satvaparipācakatvāt | satvadharmālambanāt | punaḥ katamasmin satvanikāye dharme vā pravartante | anālambanāś ca katamasminn ālambane |
body.translated_text: The <s>Brahma</s>-abodes (<s>brahmavihāras</s>) are the four immeasurables: loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). They should be understood as having a fourfold characteristic in a <s>Bodhisattva</s>: from the removal of the opponent; from the special connection with the antidote; from the special mode of operation, since they operate with threefold objects; and from the special activity, since they mature beings. [They operate with] objects of beings and objects of <s>dharmas</s>. Furthermore, in which class of beings or <s>dharma</s> do they operate? And in which object are they without object (<s>anālambana</s>)?

children.text: saukhyārthini duḥkhārte sukhite kliṣṭe ca te pravartante |
children.translated_text: 'They operate toward those who desire happiness, those afflicted by suffering, those who are happy, and those who are defiled;

children.text: taddeśite ca dharme tat tathatāyāṃ ca dhīrāṇām || AMsa_17.18 ||
children.translated_text: and toward the <s>Dharma</s> taught regarding them, and toward <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — for the steadfast.' // AMsa_17.18 //

body.text: satvālambanāḥ sukhārthini yāvat kliṣṭe satvanikāye pravartante | tathā hi maitrī satveṣu sukhasaṃyogākārā | karuṇā duḥkhaviyogākārā | muditā sukhāviyogākārā | upekṣāsu vedanāsu teṣāṃ satvānāṃ niḥkleśatopasaṃhārākārā | dharmālambanās taddeśite dharme | yatra te vihārā deśitāḥ | anālambanās tattathatāyāṃ | te hy avikalpatvād anālambanā ivety anālambanāḥ | api khalu |
body.translated_text: With objects of beings, they operate toward the class of beings who desire happiness, up to those who are defiled. For loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) operates toward beings in the mode of union with happiness. Compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) in the mode of separation from suffering. Sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) in the mode of non-separation from happiness. Equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) in the mode of drawing those beings toward freedom from afflictions in their feelings. With objects of <s>dharmas</s>, [they operate] toward the <s>Dharma</s> taught regarding them — where those abodes have been taught. Without object (<s>anālambana</s>), [they operate] toward the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of those — for being non-conceptual, they are as if without object, hence 'without object.' Moreover:

children.translated_text: 'From its having the meaning of <s>tathatā</s>, from the attainment of acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>), from purification,

children.text: karmadvayād anālambā maitrī kleśakṣayād api || AMsa_17.19 ||
children.translated_text: from the twofold activity, loving-kindness is without object — and also from the destruction of afflictions.' // AMsa_17.19 //

body.text: ebhiś caturbhiḥ kāraṇair anālambanā maitrī veditavyā | tathatālambanatvāt | anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhenāṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau | dhātupuṣṭyā tadviśuddhitaḥ | karmadvayataś ca | yā maitrī niṣpandena kāyakarmaṇā saṃgṛhītā | kleśakṣayataś ca | tathā hi kleśa ālambanam uktaṃ | manomayānāṃ granthānāṃ prahāṇād ucchidyate ālambanam iti vacanāt |
body.translated_text: By these four reasons, loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) should be understood as without object (<s>anālambana</s>): from having <s>tathatā</s> as its object; from the attainment of <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>) on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage); from the purification through the nourishment of the element (<s>dhātupuṣṭi</s>); from the twofold activity — that loving-kindness which is accompanied by effortless bodily action; and from the destruction of afflictions — for affliction is called an object, since it is said 'from the abandonment of mental fetters, the object is cut off.'

body.text: te niścalāś ca calāś ca kṛpaṇair āsvāditā na ca jñeyāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'They are both unmoved and moved, savored by the wretched, and not to be known [by them].'

body.text: te ca brāhmyā vihārāś caturvidhā veditavyāḥ | tatra calā hānabhāgīyāḥ parihāṇīyatvāt | acalāḥ sthitiviśeṣabhāgīyā aparihāṇīyatvāt | āsvāditāḥ kliṣṭāḥ anāsvāditā akliṣṭāḥ | kṛpaṇair iti sukhalolair anudāracittaiḥ | eṣa brāhmyavihārāṇāṃ hānabhāgīyādiprakāramedaḥ | teṣu punaḥ |
body.translated_text: And those <s>Brahma</s>-abodes should be understood as fourfold. Therein, the 'moved' are those pertaining to decline, since they are subject to deterioration. The 'unmoved' are those pertaining to stability and distinction, since they are not subject to deterioration. The 'savored' (<s>āsvādita</s>) are the defiled ones; the 'unsavored' are the undefiled. 'By the wretched' means by those who are pleasure-seeking and of ignoble mind. This is the division of the <s>Brahma</s>-abodes into types such as those pertaining to decline. Among those, furthermore:
'<s>Bodhisattvas</s> are established in the unmoved ones, free from attachment.' // AMsa_17.20 //
Not in the moved ones, nor in the savored ones.

children.translated_text: 'Those that are unconcentrated in nature, mild and middling, of the lower stages,

children.text: hīnāśayāḥ samānā hīnās te hy anyathā tv adhikāḥ || AMsa_17.21 ||
children.translated_text: of inferior intention, equal [to others'] — they are inferior; otherwise, they are superior.' // AMsa_17.21 //

body.text: eṣa mṛdvadhimātratābhedaḥ | tatra ṣaḍvidhā mṛdukā asamāhitasvabhāvāḥ | sarve samāhitā api | ye mṛdumadhyāḥ | hīnabhūmikā ye 'pi uttarāṃ bodhisatvabhūmim apekṣya | hīnāśayā api | śrāvakādīnāṃ samānā api | ye 'nutpattikadharmakṣāntirahitā hīnās te mṛdukā ity arthaḥ | anyathā tv adhikā iti yathoktaviparyayeṇādhimātratā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: This is the division into mild and intense. Therein, the sixfold mild are: unconcentrated in nature — even when all are concentrated; those that are mild and middling; those of the lower stages — relative to the higher <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages; those of inferior intention; those equal to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others; those lacking <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>) — they are mild, meaning inferior. 'Otherwise they are superior' — intensity should be understood as the opposite of what has been stated.

children.text: brāhmyair vihṛtavihāraḥ kāmiṣu saṃjāyate yadā dhīmān |
children.translated_text: 'When the wise one, having dwelt in the <s>Brahma</s>-abodes, is born among those in the desire [realm],

children.text: saṃbhārān pūrayate satvāṃś ca vipācayati tena || AMsa_17.22 ||
children.translated_text: that one fulfills the accumulations and matures beings thereby.' // AMsa_17.22 //

children.text: sarvatra cāvirahito brāhmyai rahitaś ca tadvipakṣeṇa |
children.translated_text: 'And everywhere one is never separated from the <s>Brahma</s>-[abodes] and free from their opponent;

children.text: tatpratyayair api bhṛśair na yāti vikṛtiṃ pramatto 'pi || AMsa_17.23 ||
children.translated_text: even with strong conditions for them [i.e., opponents], one does not undergo alteration, even when heedless.' // AMsa_17.23 //

body.text: hetuphalaliṅgabhedaḥ | tatra brāhmyair vihṛto vihārair iti hetuḥ | kāmiṣu satveṣu
body.translated_text: This is the division into cause, fruit, and sign. Therein, 'having dwelt in the <s>Brahma</s>-abodes' is the cause. 'Being born among beings in the desire [realm]'

body.text: saṃjāyata iti vipākaphalaṃ | saṃbhārān pūrayaty adhipatiphalaṃ | satvān paripācayatīti puruṣakāraphalaṃ | sarvatra cāvirahito brāhmyair vihārair jāyata iti niṣpandaphalaṃ | rahitaś ca tadvipakṣeṇeti visaṃyogaphalaṃ bhṛśair api tatpratyayair avikṛtigamanaṃ liṅgaṃ | pramatto 'pīty asaṃmukhībhūte 'pi pratipakṣe | anyaiś caturbhiḥ ślokair guṇadoṣabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: is the fruit of ripening (<s>vipāka</s>). 'Fulfilling the accumulations' is the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>). 'Maturing beings' is the fruit of human effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>). 'Everywhere being never separated from the <s>Brahma</s>-abodes when born' is the natural outflow fruit (<s>niṣpandaphala</s>). 'Being free from their opponent' is the fruit of disconnection (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>). Not undergoing alteration even with strong conditions for those [opponents] is the sign. 'Even when heedless' means even when the antidote is not present. By four more verses, the division of faults and qualities:

children.translated_text: 'Through ill-will and harmfulness, through discontent, ill-will, and sensual desire,

children.text: yukto hi bodhisatvo bahuvidham ādīnavaṃ spṛśati || AMsa_17.24 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is [thus] engaged touches manifold danger.' // AMsa_17.24 //

body.text: iti doṣaḥ | brāhmyavihārabhāve tadvipakṣayogāt | tatra vyāpādādayo maitryādīnāṃ yathākramaṃ vipakṣāḥ | vyāpādakāmarāgāv upekṣāyāḥ | kathaṃ bahuvidhādīnavaṃ spṛśatīty āha |
body.translated_text: This is the fault — from being engaged with the opponents in the absence of the <s>Brahma</s>-abodes. Therein, ill-will and the rest are the opponents of loving-kindness and the rest, respectively. Ill-will and sensual desire are the opponents of equanimity. How does one touch manifold danger? It says:

children.text: kleśair hantyātmānaṃ satvān upahanti śīlam upahanti |
children.translated_text: 'Through afflictions one destroys oneself, harms beings, and harms morality;
one loses gains with remorse, and is unguarded — and so also by the teacher.' // AMsa_17.25 //
'Subject to reproach, self-willed, one is born in the next life in unfavorable states;

children.text: prāptāprāptavihīno manasi mahad duḥkham āpnoti || AMsa_17.26 ||
children.translated_text: one loses what has been attained and what has not been attained, and in the mind one incurs great suffering.' // AMsa_17.26 //

body.text: tatra prathamais tribhiḥ padair ātmavyābādhāya cetayate paravyābādhāyobhayavyābādhāyety etam ādīnavaṃ darśayati | savilekhādibhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ padair dṛṣṭadhārmikam avadyaṃ prasavatīti darśayati | kathaṃ ca prasavati | ātmāsyāpavadate | pare 'pi devatā api | śāstāpyanye 'pi vijñāḥ sabrahmacāriṇo dharmatayā vigarhante | digvidikṣu cāsya pāpako 'varṇaśabdaśloko niścaratīty evaṃ savilekho yāvad ayaśas vīty anena yathākramaṃ darśayati | śeṣais tribhiḥ padair yathākramaṃ sāṃparāyikaṃ dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikam avadyaṃ prasavati | tajjaṃ caitasikaṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ pratisaṃvedayata ity etad ādīnavaṃ darśayati |
body.translated_text: Therein, by the first three phrases, this danger is shown: one acts with intent to harm oneself, to harm others, and to harm both. By the six phrases beginning with 'with remorse,' this is shown: one produces wrongdoing in this very life. And how does one produce it? One's own [conscience] reproaches oneself. Others also, and deities also. The teacher and other wise fellow practitioners rightfully censure [one]. And in all directions, an evil report of ill repute and notoriety spreads forth — thus, 'with remorse' up to 'ill repute' is shown in order respectively. By the remaining three phrases, one produces wrongdoing pertaining to the next life, to this life and the next, respectively; and one experiences mental suffering and displeasure born from that — this danger is shown.

children.text: ete sarve doṣā maitryādiṣu susthitasya na bhavanti |
children.translated_text: 'All these faults do not arise for one well-established in loving-kindness and the rest;

children.text: akliṣṭaḥ saṃsāraṃ satvārthaṃ no ca saṃtyajati || AMsa_17.27 ||
children.translated_text: undefiled, one does not abandon <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of beings.' // AMsa_17.27 //

body.text: iti | brāhmavihārayoge trividhaṃ guṇaṃ darśayati | yathoktadoṣābhāvaṃ akliṣṭasya satvahetoḥ saṃsārāparityāgaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thus, a threefold quality is shown through engagement with the <s>Brahma</s>-abodes: the absence of the stated faults; the non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of beings while remaining undefiled.

children.text: na tathaikaputrakeṣv api guṇavatsv api bhavati sarvasatvānāṃ |
children.translated_text: 'Not even toward only-children, nor toward those endowed with qualities, among all beings,
does there arise such a mental intention of loving-kindness and the rest toward beings as [arises in] the sons of the <s>Jina</s>.' // AMsa_17.28 //

body.text: ity ete ca bodhisatvamaitrādīnāṃ tīvratāṃ darśayati | karuṇāvibhāge tadālambanaprabhedam ārabhya dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: And these [verses] show the intensity of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s loving-kindness and the rest. On the division of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), beginning with its objects, two verses:

children.translated_text: 'Those blazing [with desire], under the power of enemies, overwhelmed by suffering, enveloped in darkness,
embarked on an impassable path, bound by great fetters; // AMsa_17.29 //
seized by great poison of food, agitated, lost from the path,
set forth on a wrong road, and weak — [toward these] beings one has compassion.' // AMsa_17.30 //

body.text: tatra pradīptāḥ kāmarāgeṇa kāmasukhabhaktāḥ | śatruvaśagā mārakṛtāntarāyāḥ kuśale 'prayuktāḥ duḥkhākrāntāḥ duḥkhābhūtā narakādiṣu | tamovṛtā aurabhrikādayo duścaritaikāntikāḥ | karmavipākasaṃmūḍhatvāt | durgamārgasamārūḍhā aparinirvāṇadharmāṇaḥ saṃsāravartmātyantānupacchedāt | mahābandhanasaṃyutā anyatīrthyāḥ | mokṣasaṃprasthitā nānākudṛṣṭigāḍhabandhanabaddhatvāt | mahāśanaviṣākrāntalolāḥ samāpattisukhasaktāḥ | teṣāṃ hi tat kliṣṭaṃ samāpattisukhaṃ | yathā mṛṣṭam aśanaṃ viṣākrāntaṃ | tataḥ pracyāvanāt | mārgapraṇaṣṭakā abhimānikā mokṣamārgabhrāntatvāt | utpathaprasthitā hīnayānaprayuktā aniyatāḥ | durbalā aparipūrṇasaṃbhārā bodhisatvāḥ | ity ete daśavidhāḥ satvā bodhisatvakaruṇāyā ālambanaṃ | pañcaphalasaṃdarśane karuṇāyāḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein: 'blazing' — with sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>), devoted to sensual pleasures. 'Under the power of enemies' — those who face obstacles created by <s>Māra</s>, not engaged in wholesome [action]. 'Overwhelmed by suffering' — those experiencing suffering in the hells and other [lower realms]. 'Enveloped in darkness' — those like butchers who are exclusively devoted to misconduct, from being confused about the ripening of <s>karma</s>. 'Embarked on an impassable path' — those whose nature is not to attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>, from the utter uninterruptedness of the path of <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'Bound by great fetters' — non-Buddhist sectarians (<s>anyatīrthyas</s>), who, though having set out toward liberation, are bound by the tight bonds of various wrong views. 'Seized by great poison of food, agitated' — those attached to the pleasure of meditative attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>), for their defiled pleasure of attainment is like delicious food that is poisoned, because of falling from it. 'Lost from the path' — the conceited (<s>abhimānika</s>), from being confused about the path to liberation. 'Set forth on a wrong road' — those engaged in the inferior vehicle (<s>hīnayāna</s>) who are of indeterminate [lineage]. 'Weak' — <s>Bodhisattvas</s> whose accumulations are incomplete. Thus these tenfold beings are the object of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s compassion. On showing the five fruits of compassion, a verse:

children.text: heṭhāpahaṃ hy uttamabodhibījaṃ sukhāvahaṃ tāyapakam iṣṭahetuṃ |
children.translated_text: 'The seed of supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), which removes harm, brings happiness, protects, is the cause of what is desired,

children.text: svabhāvadaṃ dharmam upāśritasya bodhir na dūre jinātmajasya || AMsa_17.31 ||
children.translated_text: and bestows [its] own nature — for one who has resorted to this <s>dharma</s>, awakening is not far away for the son of the <s>Jina</s>.' // AMsa_17.31 //

body.text: tataḥ heṭhāpahatvena tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇād visaṃyogaphalaṃ darśayati | uttamabodhibījatvenādhipatiphalaṃ | parātmanor yathākramaṃ sukhāvahatāyakatvena puruṣakāraphalaṃ | iṣṭahetutvena vipākaphalaṃ | svabhāvadatvena niṣpandaphalam āyatyāṃ viśiṣṭakaruṇāphaladānāt | evaṃ pañcavidhāṃ karuṇām āśritya buddhatvam adūre veditavyaṃ | apratiṣṭhitasaṃsāranirvāṇatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then, through its quality of being a secondary cause, from the non-abandonment of the destruction of its opponent, the fruit of separation (<s>visaṃyogaphala</s>) is shown. Through being the seed of supreme awakening, the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>) [is shown]. Through being the bearer of happiness to both others and oneself, respectively, the fruit of personal effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>) [is shown]. Through being the cause of what is desired, the fruit of ripening (<s>vipākaphala</s>) [is shown]. Through giving what is of its own nature, the outflow fruit (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) — from the future giving of the fruit of distinguished compassion. Thus, relying on fivefold compassion, <s>Buddhahood</s> should be understood as not far off. A verse on non-establishment in <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>:

children.text: vijñāya saṃsāragataṃ samagraṃ duḥkhātmakaṃ caiva nirātmakaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Having fully known <s>saṃsāra</s> in its entirety as being of the nature of suffering and as selfless,

children.text: nodvegam āyāti na cāpi doṣaiḥ prabādhyate kāruṇiko 'grabuddhiḥ || AMsa_17.32 ||
children.translated_text: the compassionate one of supreme wisdom neither becomes disgusted nor is afflicted by faults. // AMsa_17.32 //

body.text: sarvaṃ saṃsāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ parijñāya bodhisatvo nodvegam āyāti kāruṇikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Having fully known all of <s>saṃsāra</s> as it truly is, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not become disgusted, because of being compassionate.

body.text: na doṣair bādhyate 'grabuddhitvāt | evaṃ nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhito bhavati na saṃsāre yathākramaṃ | saṃsāraparijñāne ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: He is not afflicted by faults, because of being of supreme wisdom. Thus he is not established in <s>nirvāṇa</s> or in <s>saṃsāra</s>, respectively. A verse on the full knowledge of <s>saṃsāra</s>:

children.text: duḥkhātmakaṃ lokam avekṣamāṇo duḥkhāyate vetti ca tadyathāvat |
children.translated_text: Observing the world as being of the nature of suffering, the compassionate one feels sorrow and yet knows it as it truly is,

children.text: tasyābhyupāyaṃ parivarjane ca na khedam āyaty api vā kṛpāluḥ || AMsa_17.33 ||
children.translated_text: and knowing the method for its avoidance, he does not become weary. // AMsa_17.33 //

body.text: duḥkhāyata iti karuṇāyate | vetti ca tad yathāvad iti duḥkhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ tasya ca duḥkhasya parivarjane 'bhyupāyaṃ | vetti yenāsya duḥkhaṃ nirudhyate | etena jānann api saṃsāraduḥkhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ tatparityāgopāyaṃ ca na khedam āpadyate bodhisatvaḥ karuṇāviśeṣād iti pradarśayati | karuṇāprabhede dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: 'Feels sorrow' means he feels compassion. 'And knows it as it truly is' — he knows suffering as it truly is and the method for the avoidance of that suffering — by which his suffering ceases. By this, it is shown that even though the <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> as it truly is and the means for its abandonment, he does not become weary, due to the excellence of his compassion. On the division of compassion, two verses:

children.text: kṛpā prakṛtyā pratisaṃkhyayā ca pūrvaṃ tadabhyāsavidhānayogāt |
children.translated_text: Compassion by nature, by discernment, previously through the practice of its cultivation,

children.text: vipakṣahīnā ca viśuddhilābhāt caturvidheyaṃ karūṇātmakānāṃ || AMsa_17.34 ||
children.translated_text: and free from its opponent through the attainment of purity — this fourfold [compassion belongs to] those whose nature is compassion. // AMsa_17.34 //

body.text: seyaṃ yathākramaṃ gotraviśeṣataḥ | guṇadoṣaparīkṣaṇataḥ | janmāntaraparibhāvanataḥ | vairāgyalābhataś ca veditavyā | tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇe sati viśuddhilābhata iti vairāgyalābhataḥ |
body.translated_text: This should be understood, respectively, as from the distinction of one's lineage (<s>gotra</s>); from the examination of virtues and faults; from cultivation in previous lives; and from the attainment of detachment — through the non-abandonment of the destruction of the opponent, 'through the attainment of purity' means 'from the attainment of detachment.'

children.text: na sā kṛpā yā na samā sadā vā nādhyāśayād vā pratipattito vā |
children.translated_text: That compassion which is not equal, not constant, not from superior intention, not from practice,

children.text: vairāgyato nānupalambhato vā na bodhisatvo hy akṛpas tathā yaḥ || AMsa_17.35 ||
children.translated_text: not from detachment, not from non-apprehension — a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is such is not [truly] without compassion. // AMsa_17.35 //

body.text: tatra samā sukhitādiṣu yatkiṃcid veditam idam atra duḥkhasyeti viditvā | sadā nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe tadakṣayāt | adhyāśayād bhūmipraviṣṭānām ātmaparasamatāśayalābhāt | pratipattito duḥkhaparitrāṇakriyayā | vairāgyatas tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇāt | anupalambhato 'nutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāt | karuṇāvṛkṣapratibimbake pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'equal' means toward the happy and the like — knowing 'this too belongs to suffering.' 'Constant' — because of its inexhaustibility even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder. 'From superior intention' — because those who have entered the stages have attained the intention of equality between self and others. 'From practice' — through the act of rescuing from suffering. 'From detachment' — from the non-abandonment of the destruction of its opponent. 'From non-apprehension' — from the attainment of the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). On the simile of the compassion-tree, five verses:

children.translated_text: Compassion, patience, contemplation, aspiration, birth, and the maturation of beings —

children.text: karuṇā tarur eṣa mahān mūlādiḥ puṣpapatraphalaḥ || AMsa_17.36 ||
children.translated_text: this is the great tree of compassion, beginning with the root [and having] flowers, leaves, and fruits. // AMsa_17.36 //

body.text: ity eṣa mūlaskandhaśākhāpatrapuṣpaphalāvasthaḥ karuṇāvṛkṣo veditavyaḥ | etasya karuṇā mūlaṃ | kṣāntiḥ skandhaḥ | satvārthacintā śākhā | praṇidhānaṃ śobhaneṣu janmasu patrāṇi | śobhanaṃ janma puṣpaṃ | satvaparipākaḥ phalaṃ |
body.translated_text: This tree of compassion should be understood as having the stages of root, trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits. Therein, compassion is the root; patience is the trunk; contemplation of the welfare of beings is the branches; aspiration is — in favorable births — the leaves; favorable birth is the flower; and the maturation of beings is the fruit.

children.text: mūlaṃ karuṇā na bhaved duṣkaracaryāsahiṣṇutā na bhavet |
children.translated_text: If compassion were not the root, there would be no endurance of difficult practices;

children.text: duḥkhākṣamaś ca dhīmān satvārthaṃ cintayen naiva || AMsa_17.37 ||
children.translated_text: and the wise one, unable to bear suffering, would never contemplate the welfare of beings. // AMsa_17.37 //
One whose intelligence is devoid of contemplation would not make aspirations in favorable births;

children.text: śubhajanmān anugacchan satvān paripācayen naiva || AMsa_17.38 ||
children.translated_text: and pursuing favorable births, one would never mature beings. // AMsa_17.38 //

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ pūrvottaraprasavasādharmyāt karuṇādīnāṃ mūlādibhāvaṃ sādhayati |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, the root-status and so forth of compassion and the rest is established through the analogy of the earlier producing the later.

children.translated_text: The watering of compassion is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>); through [seeing another's] suffering from [their own] happiness, there is vast nourishment;
the growth of the branches is clear — it should be known as arising from wise attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>). // AMsa_17.39 //
The shedding and taking on of leaves [corresponds to] the unbroken continuity of aspirations;
through the accomplishment of twofold conditions, the flower is not barren, and the fruit [comes] from this. // AMsa_17.40 //

body.text: etābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ vṛkṣamūlasekādisādharmyaṃ karuṇāvṛkṣasya darśayati | karuṇā hi mūlavṛkṣā | tasyāḥ seko maitrī tayā tadāpy āyanāt | maitricitto hi paraduḥkhena duḥkhāyate | tataś ca karuṇodbhavaduḥkham utpadyate bodhisatvasya svārthaprayuktasya tatra saukhyotpādād vipulapuṣṭiḥ kṣāntipuṣṭir ity arthaḥ | sā hi skandha ity uktā | skandhaś ca vipulaḥ | yoniśomanaskārād bahuvidhā mahāyāne śākhāvṛddhiḥ | cintā hi śākhety uktā | pūrvāparanirodhotpādakrameṇa praṇidhānasaṃtānasyānucchedāt | parṇatyāgādānasādharmyaṃ praṇidhānānāṃ veditavyaṃ | ādhyātmikapratyayasiddhitaḥ svasaṃtānaparipākāt puṣpam iva janmābandhyaṃ veditavyaṃ | bāhyapratyayasiddhitaḥ parasaṃtānaparipākāt phalabhūtaḥ satvaparipāko veditavyaḥ | karuṇānuśaṃse ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: By these two verses, the analogy of watering the root of a tree and so forth is shown for the compassion-tree. Compassion is indeed the tree from the root. Its watering is loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), because through it there is sustenance. For one with a mind of loving-kindness feels sorrow at another's suffering. And from that, the suffering born of compassion arises in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — for one engaged in one's own welfare, from the arising of happiness therein, there is vast nourishment — meaning the nourishment of patience. For patience has been called the trunk, and the trunk becomes vast. From wise attention, the manifold growth of branches in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [occurs]. For contemplation has been called the branches. Through the unbroken continuity of the succession of aspirations in the sequence of cessation and arising of earlier and later [aspirations], the analogy of the shedding and taking on of leaves should be understood for the aspirations. Through the accomplishment of internal conditions — from the maturation of one's own continuum — birth should be understood as not barren, like a flower. Through the accomplishment of external conditions — from the maturation of others' continua — the maturation of beings, which is the fruit, should be understood. A verse on the benefit of compassion:

children.text: kaḥ kurvīta na karuṇāṃ satveṣu mahākṛpāguṇakareṣu |
children.translated_text: Who would not practice compassion toward beings, who produce the virtue of great compassion,

children.text: duḥkhe 'pi saukhyam atulaṃ bhavati yad eṣāṃ kṛpājanitaṃ || AMsa_17.41 ||
children.translated_text: since for them, even in suffering, there arises incomparable happiness born from compassion? // AMsa_17.41 //

body.text: atra mahākaruṇāguṇa uttarārdhena saṃdarśitaḥ | śeṣo gatārthaḥ | karuṇāniḥsaṅgatāyāṃ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the virtue of great compassion is shown by the second half-verse. The rest is self-explanatory. Verses on the non-attachment of compassion:

children.text: aviṣṭānāṃ kṛpayā na tiṣṭhati manaḥ śame kṛpālūnāṃ |
children.translated_text: The mind of the compassionate does not remain in peace because it is pervaded by compassion;

children.text: kuta eva lokasaukhye svajīvite vā bhavet snehaḥ || AMsa_17.42 ||
children.translated_text: how then could there be attachment to worldly happiness or even to one's own life? // AMsa_17.42 //

body.text: sarvasya hi lokasya laukike saukhye svajīvite ca snehaḥ | tatrāpi ca niḥsnehānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ sarvaduḥkhopaśame nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhitaṃ manaḥ | bodhisatvānāṃ
body.translated_text: For the whole world has attachment to worldly happiness and to one's own life. And even among those free from such attachment — the <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — the mind is established in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the cessation of all suffering. But for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

body.text: tu karuṇāviṣṭatvān nirvāṇe 'pi mano na pratiṣṭhitaṃ | kuta eva tayoḥ sneho bhaviṣyati | karuṇāsnehavaiśeṣye trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: because they are pervaded by compassion, the mind is not established even in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. How then could there be attachment to those two [worldly happiness and life]? On the superiority of the love of compassion, three verses:

children.text: sneho na vidyate 'sau yo 'niravadyo na laukiko yaś ca |
children.translated_text: That love does not exist which is blameless and not worldly;
among the wise, the love of compassion is blameless and transcends the world. // AMsa_17.43 //

body.text: mātāpitṛprabhṛtīnāṃ hi tṛṣṇāmayaḥ snehaḥ sāvadyaḥ | laukikakaruṇāvihāriṇāṃ niravadyo 'pi laukikaḥ | bodhisatvānāṃ tu karuṇāmayaḥ sneho niravadyaś ca laukikātikrāntaś ca | kathaṃ ca punar niravadya ity āha |
body.translated_text: For the love of parents and the like, being of the nature of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), is blameworthy. The [love] of those who dwell in worldly compassion, though blameless, is worldly. But the love of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, consisting of compassion, is both blameless and transcends the world. And how is it blameless? He says:

children.translated_text: The world is beset by the great flood of suffering and ignorance, and by great darkness —

children.text: uddhartuṃ ya upāyaḥ katham iva na syāt sa niravadyaḥ || AMsa_17.44 ||
children.translated_text: how could the means to rescue them not be blameless? // AMsa_17.44 //

body.text: duḥkhamahāugha ajñānamahāndhakāre ceti yojyaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | kathaṃ lokātikrānta ityāha |
body.translated_text: 'The great flood of suffering and the great darkness of ignorance' — this should be construed. The rest is self-explanatory. How does it transcend the world? He says:

children.text: sneho na so 'sty arihatāṃ loke pratyekabodhibuddhānāṃ |
children.translated_text: That love does not exist among the <s>Arhats</s> in the world, nor among <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>;

children.text: prāg eva tad anyeṣāṃ katham iva lokottaro na syāt || AMsa_17.45 ||
children.translated_text: still less among others — how could it not be supramundane? // AMsa_17.45 //

body.text: pratyekāṃ bodhiṃ buddhāḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | trāsābhinandananimittatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: '<s>Pratyeka</s>-<s>buddhas</s>' — those awakened individually. The rest is self-explanatory. A verse on [compassion's] being the cause of both fear and delight:

children.translated_text: The suffering that arises from compassion for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the absence of suffering —

children.text: saṃtrāsayati tad ādau spṛṣṭaṃ tv abhinandayati gāḍhaṃ || AMsa_17.46 ||
children.translated_text: that terrifies at first, but when touched deeply, it delights. // AMsa_17.46 //

body.text: duḥkhābhāve iti duḥkhābhāvo nimittaṃ | satveṣu karuṇayā bodhisatvānāṃ yad duḥkham utpadyate tadādau saṃtrāsayati adhimukticaryābhūmau | ātmaparasamatayā duḥkhasya yathābhūtam aspṛṣṭatvāt | spṛṣṭaṃ tu śuddhādhyāśayabhūmāv abhinandayaty evety arthaḥ | karuṇāduḥkhena sukhābhibhave ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'In the absence of suffering' — the absence of suffering is the occasion. The suffering that arises from compassion toward beings for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> terrifies at first — on the stage of conduct through conviction (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>) — because, through the equality of self and others, suffering has not yet been truly touched. But when touched, on the stage of pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayabhūmi</s>), it indeed delights — this is the meaning. A verse on the overcoming of [worldly] happiness by the suffering of compassion:

children.text: kim ataḥ paramāścaryaṃ yad duḥkhaṃ saukhyam abhibhavati sarva |
children.translated_text: What is more wondrous than this — that suffering overcomes all happiness;

children.text: kṛpayā janitaṃ laukyaṃ yena vimukto api kṛtārthaḥ || AMsa_17.47 ||
children.translated_text: that born from compassion, that worldly [suffering], by which even the liberated are fulfilled? // AMsa_17.47 //

body.text: nāsty ata āścaryataraṃ yad duḥkham eva karuṇājanitaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ tathā sukhaṃ
body.translated_text: There is nothing more wondrous than this — that the very suffering born from compassion in <s>Bodhisattvas</s> becomes such happiness

body.text: bhavati | yat sarvaṃ laukikaṃ sukham abhibhavati | yena sukhena vimuktā arhanto 'pi kṛtārthāḥ prāg evānye | kṛpākṛtadānānuśaṃse ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: that it overcomes all worldly happiness — the happiness by which even liberated <s>Arhats</s> are fulfilled, let alone others. A verse on the benefit of giving made through compassion:

children.text: kṛpayā sahitaṃ dānaṃ yad dānasukhaṃ karoti dhīrāṇāṃ |
children.translated_text: The giving accompanied by compassion that produces the joy of giving for the steadfast —

children.text: traidhātukam upabhogair na tatsukhaṃ tatkalāṃ spṛśati || AMsa_17.48 ||
children.translated_text: all the enjoyments of the three realms cannot touch even a fraction of that joy. // AMsa_17.48 //

body.text: yacca traidhātukaṃ sukham upabhogaiḥ kṛtaṃ na tatsukhaṃ tasya sukhasya kalāṃ spṛśatīty ayam uttarārdhasyārthaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | kṛpayā duḥkhābhyupagame ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: And the happiness produced by enjoyments in the three realms cannot touch even a fraction of that happiness — this is the meaning of the second half-verse. The rest is self-explanatory. A verse on the acceptance of suffering through compassion:

children.text: duḥkhamayaṃ saṃsāraṃ yatkṛpayā na tyajati satvārthaṃ |
children.translated_text: Because one does not, out of compassion, abandon <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is of the nature of suffering, for the sake of beings —

children.text: parahitahetor duḥkhaṃ kiṃ kārūṇikair na samupetam || AMsa_17.49 ||
children.translated_text: what suffering is not undertaken by the compassionate for the benefit of others? // AMsa_17.49 //

body.text: sarvaṃ hi duḥkhaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhe 'ntarbhūtaṃ | tasyābhyupagamāt sarvaṃ duḥkham abhyupagataṃ bhavati | tatra tatphalavṛddhau ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: For all suffering is included within the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>. From the acceptance of that, all suffering is accepted. A verse on the increase of its fruit therein:

children.text: karūṇā dānaṃ bhogāḥ sadā kṛpālor vivṛddhim upayānti |
children.translated_text: Compassion, giving, and enjoyments — for the compassionate, these always increase;

children.text: snehānugrahajanitaṃ tac chaktikṛtaṃ sukhaṃ cāsmāt || AMsa_17.50 ||
children.translated_text: and the happiness born from loving concern and benefiting [others], and made possible by that capacity, comes from this. // AMsa_17.50 //

body.text: trayaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ sarvajanmasu vardhate karuṇāyogāt | karuṇā tadabhyāsāt | dānaṃ karuṇāvaśāt | bhogāś ca dānavaśāt | tasmāc ca trayāt phalaṃ trividhaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati | snehajanitaṃ karuṇātaḥ | satvānugrahajanitaṃ dānāt | tadanugrahakriyāśaktikṛtaṃ bhogebhyaḥ | dānaprotsāhanāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: These three increase for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in all their births through the practice of compassion: compassion, through its cultivation; giving, through the power of compassion; and enjoyments, through the power of giving. And from that threefold [increase], a threefold happiness arises as fruit: born from loving concern — from compassion; born from benefiting beings — from giving; and made possible by the capacity for that benefiting activity — from enjoyments. A verse on the encouragement to give:

children.text: vardhe ca vardhayāmi ca dāne paripācayāmi sukhayāmi |
children.translated_text: 'I increase and I cause increase in giving; I mature [beings] and I make them happy;

children.text: ākarṣāmi nayāmi ca karuṇāsannān pravadatīva || AMsa_17.51 ||
children.translated_text: I attract and I lead' — [compassion] speaks thus, as it were, to those devoted to giving. // AMsa_17.51 //

body.text: dāne sannān iti saṃbandhanīyaṃ | ṣaḍbhir guṇair dāne 'vasannān bodhisatvānkaruṇā protsahayatīva | svabhāvavṛddhyā | bhogais tadvardhanayā | dānena satvaparipācanayā | dātuś ca sukhotpādanāt | mahābodhisaṃbhārasyānyasyākarṣaṇāt | mahābodhisamīpanayanāc ca | parasaukhyena sukhābhave ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'To those devoted to giving' — this should be connected. Compassion, as it were, encourages <s>Bodhisattvas</s> devoted to giving through six virtues: through the increase of its own nature; through the increase of enjoyments; through the maturation of beings through giving; through producing happiness in the giver; through attracting the other accumulations for great awakening; and through leading near to great awakening. A verse on happiness through others' happiness:

children.text: duḥkhe duḥkhī kṛpayā sukhāny anādhāya kena sukhitaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: Suffering in suffering through compassion, and not establishing happiness — by whom could one be made happy?

children.text: sukhayaty ātmānam ataḥ kṛpālur ādhāya parasaukhyam || AMsa_17.52 ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the compassionate one makes himself happy by establishing happiness in others. // AMsa_17.52 //

body.text: karuṇayā bodhisatvaḥ paraduḥkhair duḥkhitaḥ satveṣv anādhāya sukhaṃ kathaṃ sukhitaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, suffering through compassion from the sufferings of others — without establishing happiness among beings, how could he be happy?

body.text: syāt | tasmāt pareṣu sukham ādhāya bodhisatva ātmānam eva sukhayatīti veditavyaṃ | kṛpayā dānasamanuśāstau ṣaṭ ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, it should be understood that by establishing happiness in others, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> makes himself happy. On the instruction regarding giving through compassion, six verses:

children.text: svaṃ dānaṃ kāruṇikaḥ śāstīva sadaiva niḥsvasukhakāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: The compassionate one, desiring happiness free from selfishness, always instructs his own giving, as it were:

children.text: bhogaiḥ sukhaya paraṃ vā māma py ayutasaukhyam || AMsa_17.53 ||
children.translated_text: 'Make the other happy with enjoyments, or [make] me [happy with] conjoined happiness.' // AMsa_17.53 //

body.text: na hi kāruṇikasya vinā parasukhenāsti sukhaṃ | tasyāyutasaukhyatvād bodhisatvas tena vinā no dānasya phalaṃ sukhaṃ necchati |
body.translated_text: For the compassionate one has no happiness without the happiness of others — because his happiness is conjoined [with theirs]. Therefore, without that [happiness of others], the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not desire the happiness that is the fruit of giving.

children.text: saphalaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ tan me satveṣu tat sukhasukhena |
children.translated_text: 'My giving, given to beings, has borne fruit through the happiness of their happiness;

children.text: phala teṣv eva nikāmaṃ yadi me kartavyatā te 'sti || AMsa_17.54 ||
children.translated_text: let it bear fruit abundantly in them alone, if I have any obligation toward them.' // AMsa_17.54 //

body.text: dānaṃ dadatā dānaṃ ca dānaphalaṃ ca tanmayā satveṣu dattaṃ | tatsukham eva me sukhaṃ yasmāt | atas teṣv eva yāvat phalitavyaṃ tāvat phaleti loṭ | bodhisatvaḥ karuṇayā dānam anuśāsti |
body.translated_text: In giving, the giver has given both the giving and the fruit of giving to beings. 'Their happiness alone is my happiness' — because of that. Therefore, 'let it bear fruit in them alone' — as far as it must bear fruit — so it bears fruit: this is an optative. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> instructs giving through compassion.

children.translated_text: To the giver who is averse to enjoyment, possessions come in greater abundance and beauty;

children.text: na hi tatsukhaṃ mataṃ me dāne pāraṃparo 'smi yataḥ || AMsa_17.55 ||
children.translated_text: 'That is not considered happiness by me, for I am devoted to the continuation of giving.' // AMsa_17.55 //

body.text: bhogavimukhasya dātur bhogā bahutarāś copatiṣṭhante | śobhanatarāś ca | dharmataiveyaṃ cittasyodārataratvāt | na hi tatsukhaṃ mataṃ me yad bhogās tathopatiṣṭhate | yasmād ahaṃ dāne pāraṃparas tatprabandhakāmatvān na sukhe |
body.translated_text: To a giver who is averse to enjoyment, possessions arise in greater abundance and greater beauty. This is simply the natural order, because of the mind's greater nobility. 'That is not considered happiness by me' — that possessions arise in such a way. 'For I am devoted to the continuation of giving' — because of desiring the continuation of that [giving], not happiness.

children.translated_text: 'When out of compassion you constantly look upon me who have renounced all possessions,

children.text: nanu te tena jñeyaṃ na matphalenārthitā 'syeti || AMsa_17.56 ||
children.translated_text: surely you should know by that that I have no desire for the fruit of my [giving].' // AMsa_17.56 //

body.text: yo 'haṃ dānaphalaṃ sarvam eva karuṇayā nityaṃ parityajāmi nanv ata eva veditavyaṃ nāsti me dānaphalenārthitvam iti bodhisatvo dānaṃ samanuśāsti |
body.translated_text: 'I who out of compassion always renounce all the fruit of giving — surely from that itself it should be known: I have no desire for the fruit of giving' — thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> instructs in giving.

body.text: dānābhirato na syāṃ prāptaṃ cet tatphalaṃ na visṛjeyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'I would not be delighted in giving if, having obtained that fruit, I did not give it away;
for indeed,

body.text: kṣaṇam api dānena vinā dānābhirato bhavati naiva || AMsa_17.57 ||
body.translated_text: one who is delighted in giving is never without giving, even for a moment.' // AMsa_17.57 //
The verse is self-evident.

body.text: akṛtaṃ na phalasi yasmāt pratikārāpekṣayā na me tulyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'You do not bear fruit for what has not been done, and with regard to reciprocation you are not equal to me;

body.text: yas tvā karoti tasya tvaṃ phalasi | tasmāt tvaṃ pratikārāpekṣayā na mattulyaṃ | tathā hy ahaṃ |
body.translated_text: you bear fruit for the one who acts [toward you]. Therefore, with regard to reciprocation, you are not equal to me. For indeed, I am

body.text: pratikāranirvyapekṣaḥ paratra phalado 'sya kāmaṃ te || AMsa_17.58 ||
body.translated_text: without regard for reciprocation, giving fruit in the other world — so be it for you!' // AMsa_17.58 //
This is self-evident. On compassionate giving, two verses:

children.text: niravadyaṃ śuddhapadaṃ hitāv ahaṃ caiva sānurakṣaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Blameless, of pure foundation, beneficent, and with safeguarding,
unsolicited, unstained — such is the compassionate giving of the sons of the <s>Jina</s>. // AMsa_17.59 //

body.text: tatra niravadyaṃ param anupahṛtya dānāt | śuddhapadaṃ kalpikavasudānāt | viṣaśastramadyādivivarjanataḥ | hitāvahaṃ dānena saṃgṛhya kuśale niyojanāt | sānurakṣaṃ parijanasyāvighātaṃ kṛtvā anyasmai dānāt | nirmṛgyam ayācamāne 'py arthitvaṃ vighātaṃ vāvagamya svayam eva dānāt dakṣiṇīyāparimārgaṇāc ca | nirlepaṃ pratikāravipākaniḥspṛhatvāt | aparaḥ prakāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'blameless' — because of giving without harming others. 'Of pure foundation' — because of giving things that are appropriate, avoiding poison, weapons, intoxicants, and the like. 'Beneficent' — because of employing [the recipient] in the wholesome after gathering them through giving. 'With safeguarding' — because of giving to another after ensuring no injury to one's dependents. 'Unsolicited' — because of giving spontaneously upon discerning [another's] need or distress even when not asked, and because of not seeking out a worthy recipient. 'Unstained' — because of being free from desire for reciprocation and [karmic] ripening. Another way [of characterizing]:

children.text: sakalaṃ vipulaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ satataṃ muditaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ śuddhaṃ |
children.translated_text: Complete, extensive, excellent, constant, joyful, disinterested, pure,
devoted to awakening, devoted to the wholesome — such is the compassionate giving of the sons of the <s>Jina</s>. // AMsa_17.60 //
