body.text: tatra sakalam ādhyātmikabāhyavastudānāt | vipulaṃ prabhūtavastudānāt | śreṣṭhaṃ praṇītavastudānāt | satatam abhīkṣṇadānāt | muditapratisaṃkhyāya prahṛṣṭadānāt | nirāmiṣaṃ yathā nirlepaṃ | śuddhaṃ yathā śuddhapadaṃ | bodhinataṃ mahābodhipariṇāmanāt | kuśalanataṃ yathā hitāvahaṃ | upabhogaviśeṣe ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'complete' — because of giving both internal and external things. 'Extensive' — because of giving abundant things. 'Excellent' — because of giving exquisite things. 'Constant' — because of giving repeatedly. 'Joyful' — because of giving joyfully after deliberation. 'Disinterested' — as [explained for] 'unstained.' 'Pure' — as [explained for] 'of pure foundation.' 'Devoted to awakening' — because of dedicating [the merit] toward great awakening. 'Devoted to the wholesome' — as [explained for] 'beneficent.' A verse on the distinction of enjoyment:

children.text: na tathopabhogatuṣṭiṃ labhate bhogī yathā parityāgāt |
children.translated_text: The one who indulges does not obtain from enjoyment such satisfaction as
the compassionate one attains from renunciation, with a mind nourished by the threefold happiness. // AMsa_17.61 //

body.text: tatra sukhatrayaṃ dānaprītiḥ parānugrahaprītiḥ bodhisaṃbhārasaṃbharaṇaprītiś ca | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | pāramitābhinirhārakaruṇāyāṃ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the threefold happiness is: the joy of giving, the joy of benefiting others, and the joy of accumulating the stores for awakening (<s>bodhisaṃbhāra</s>). The rest is self-evident. A verse on the compassion that produces the <s>pāramitās</s>:

children.translated_text: Compassion toward the wretched, compassion toward the cruel, compassion toward the agitated, compassion toward the heedless,
compassion toward those enslaved by sense-objects, and compassion toward those holding wrong views. // AMsa_17.62 //

body.text: tatra kṛpaṇā matsariṇaḥ | raudrā duḥśīlāḥ paropatāniḥ | saṃkṣubdhāḥ
body.translated_text: Therein, 'the wretched' are the miserly. 'The cruel' are the immoral who injure others. 'The agitated'

body.text: krodhanāḥ | pramattāḥ kuśīdāḥ | viṣayaparatantrāḥ kāmeṣu vikṣiptacittāḥ | mithyābhiniviṣṭāḥ duḥprajñāḥ tīrthikādayaḥ | eṣu pāramitāvipakṣadharmāvasthiteṣu yā karuṇā sā kṛpaṇādikaruṇā | sā ca tadvipakṣavidūṣaṇāt pāramitābhinirhārāya saṃpadyate | tasmāt pāramitābhinirhārakaruṇety ucyate | karuṇāpratyayasaṃdarśane ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: are the wrathful. 'The heedless' are the lazy. 'Those enslaved by sense-objects' are those with minds scattered in sensual pleasures. 'Those holding wrong views' are those of poor wisdom, such as <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) and the like. The compassion toward those established in <s>dharmas</s> that are opponents of the <s>pāramitās</s> is the compassion toward the wretched and so forth. That [compassion] becomes effectual for the production of the <s>pāramitās</s> through the criticism of their respective opponents. Therefore it is called 'the compassion that produces the <s>pāramitās</s>.' A verse on demonstrating the conditions of compassion:

children.translated_text: The compassion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [arises] from happiness, from suffering, and from what follows upon them;

children.text: karuṇā bodhisatvānāṃ hetor mitrāt svabhāvataḥ || AMsa_17.63 ||
children.translated_text: the compassion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [arises] from a cause, from a spiritual friend, and from its own nature. // AMsa_17.63 //

body.text: tatra pūrvārdhenālambanapratyayaṃ karuṇāyāḥ saṃdarśayati | trividhāṃ vedanām ālambya tisṛbhir duḥkhatābhiḥ karuṇāyanāt | aduḥkhāsukhā hi vedanā sukhaduḥkhayor anvayaḥ punas tadāvāhanāt | uttarārdhena yathākramaṃ hetumitrasvabhāvaiḥ karuṇāyā hetvadhipatisamanantarapratyayān saṃdarśayati | mahākaruṇatve ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, by the first half, he demonstrates the object-condition of compassion: it operates compassionately by taking as its object the three types of feeling through the three types of suffering (<s>duḥkhatā</s>). For the feeling that is neither-suffering-nor-pleasure is a sequel to pleasure and suffering, because it again brings them about. By the second half, he demonstrates, in due order, the causal condition (<s>hetu</s>), the dominant condition (<s>adhipati</s>), and the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) of compassion through cause, spiritual friend, and own nature. A verse on great compassion:

children.translated_text: The compassion of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be known as equal, from its intention,

children.text: pratipatter virāgāc ca nopalambhād viśuddhitaḥ || AMsa_17.64 ||
children.translated_text: from its practice, from dispassion, from non-apprehension, and from purity. // AMsa_17.64 //

body.text: tatra samā trividhavedanāvastheṣu yat kiṃcid veditam idam atra duḥkhasyeti viditvā | sā punar āśayato 'pi cittena karuṇāyanāt | pratipattito 'pi tatparitrāṇāt | virāgato 'pi tadvipakṣavihiṃsāprahāṇāt | anupalambhato 'py ātmaparakaruṇānupalambhāt | viśuddhito 'py aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmāv anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'equal' — toward those in the three states of feeling, knowing 'whatever is felt, this is suffering.' And that [compassion], moreover, [is great] from its intention — because of being compassionate through the mind; from its practice — because of rescuing them; from dispassion — because of not abandoning the harm-removal of their opponents; from non-apprehension — because of the non-apprehension of self, other, and compassion; and from purity — because of attaining the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>) on the eighth stage.

children.translated_text: The highest cultivation of loving-kindness and the rest [arises] from one's own mind, from the <s>Dharma</s>, from aspiration,

children.text: āśayato 'pi vibhutvād avikalpād aikyataś cāpi || AMsa_17.65 ||
children.translated_text: from intention, from sovereignty, from non-conceptualization, and from oneness. // AMsa_17.65 //

body.translated_text: The meaning should be followed in accordance with the previous exposition.

children.translated_text: Thus, with deep faith born toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, one who greatly honors [him] through constant worship with great offerings,
who constantly serves a spiritual friend endowed with many virtues and benefit, who has compassion for the world — he attains all accomplishments. // AMsa_17.66 //

body.text: etena yathoktānāṃ pūjāsevā'pramāṇānām anukramaṃ guṇaṃ ca samāsena saṃdarśayati | mahopadhibhir dhruvaṃ satkriyā cātyarthaṃ pūjanān mahadupadhidhruvasatkriyābhipūjī veditavyaḥ | satkriyā punaḥ samyakpratipattirveditavyā | evaṃ satkārapratipattipūjī
body.translated_text: By this, he shows in summary the virtues and sequence of the worship, service, and immeasurables that have been described. 'One who greatly honors through constant worship with great offerings' means one who worships with great material offerings and constant reverent honor, and should be understood as 'one who greatly honors through constant worship with great offerings.' The reverent honor, moreover, should be understood as right practice. Thus he becomes one who worships through veneration, practice, and worship.

body.text: bhavati | bahuguṇaṃ mitraṃ tadanyair guṇaiḥ | hitam anukampakatvena veditavyaṃ | eti sarvasiddhim iti svaparārthasiddhiṃ prāpnotīti |
body.translated_text: 'A spiritual friend endowed with many virtues' — endowed with virtues other [than benefit]. 'Beneficial' should be understood through being compassionate. 'Attains all accomplishments' — he obtains the accomplishment of one's own and others' purposes.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, this is the seventeenth [chapter], the chapter on worship, service, and the immeasurables, completed.

CHAPTER XVIII
The eighteenth chapter.
On the division of moral shame (<s>lajjā</s>), sixteen verses.

children.text: lajjā vipakṣahīnā jñānena gatā ca nirvikalpena |
children.translated_text: Moral shame (<s>lajjā</s>), devoid of opponents, gone [beyond] through non-conceptual knowledge,
having the domain of the inferior and the blameless, ripening beings — [found] in the courageous. // AMsa_18.1 //

body.text: etena svabhāvasahāyālambhanakarmapadā caturvidhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bodhisatvalajjāyāḥ saṃdarśayati |

in the <s>pāramitās</s>,

and in <s>dharmas</s> favorable to the <s>kleśas</s> —

body.translated_text: This is the shame of non-application —

children.translated_text: Of non-concentrated nature, weak, middling, on inferior stages — moral shame

the weak

body.translated_text: This is

body.text: ity atra ātmavyābādhāya cetayate paravyābadhāyobhayavyābhādhāya cety saṃdarśitaṃ | ayoniśata ity ayoniśo manaskāreṇa | katham

Through heedlessness regarding all purposes.

body.translated_text: Here, it is shown that he intends harm to himself, harm to others, and harm to both. 'Through improper attention' means through improper mental attention (<s>ayoniśo manaskāra</s>). How does

children.text: kaukṛtyāt savilekho bhavati sa saṃmānahānim āpnoti |
children.translated_text: From remorse, he becomes distressed; he suffers the loss of respect;

children.text: śrāddhāt mānuṣasaṃghāc chāstrā copekṣyate tasmāt || AMsa_18.5 ||
children.translated_text: and he is disregarded by the faithful, by the human community, and by the teacher. // AMsa_18.5 //

body.text:
sahadhārmikair jinasutair vinindyate lokato 'yaśo labhate |
dṛṣṭe dharme
body.translated_text:
He is reproached by fellow practitioners, the sons of the <s>Jina</s>; and from the world he receives ill repute.
In the present life —

body.text: ity etena dṛṣṭadhārmikam avadyaṃ prasavatīti darśanaṃ | yathākramam ātmaparadevatāśāstṛbhir apavadanāt | vijñaiḥ sabrahmacāribhir dharmatayā vigarhanāt | digvidkṣu ca pāpakāvarṇaniścaraṇāt |
body.translated_text: by this, it is shown that he produces fault in the present life — being censured, in due order, by himself, others, deities, and the teacher; being blamed by the wise, fellow celibates, on account of the nature [of his actions]; and because of the spreading of evil report in all directions.
In another [life], he is born deprived of [favorable] conditions. // AMsa_18.6 //
He suffers the decline of both attained and unattained wholesome <s>dharmas</s> because of that;

body.text: ity anena dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikam avadyaṃ prasavatīty saṃdarśitam

body.text: duḥkhaṃ viharati tasmān manaso 'py asvasthatām eti || AMsa_18.7 ||

body.translated_text: By this, it is shown that the mental (<s>caitasika</s>) [quality] of moral shame

body.text: ete sarve doṣā hrīmatsu bhavanti no jinasuteṣu |

body.text: deveṣu ca manujeṣu ca nityaṃ saṃjāyate ca budhaḥ || AMsa_18.8 ||
body.translated_text: And among gods and humans, the wise one is constantly reborn. // AMsa_18.8 //
This is its fruit of ripening (<s>vipākaphala</s>).

body.text: saṃbhārāṃś ca sa bodheḥ kṣipraṃ pūrayati lajjayā dhīmān |
body.translated_text: And the wise one who possesses moral shame quickly fulfills the accumulations for awakening;
this is the dominant fruit (<s>adhipatiphala</s>).

body.text: satvānāṃ pācanayā na khidyate caiva jinaputraḥ || AMsa_18.9 ||

This is the fruit of human effort (<s>puruṣakāraphala</s>).

body.text: sa vipakṣapratipakṣai rahito 'rahitaś ca jāyate satataṃ |
body.translated_text: He is constantly reborn free from opponents and not free from antidotes;

children.translated_text: freedom from opponents and non-freedom from antidotes.

body.translated_text: these are the fruit of separation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) and the fruit of outflow (<s>niṣpanda</s>) — namely,

body.translated_text: This benefit is obtained by the son of the <s>Jina</s> who possesses moral shame. // AMsa_18.10 //

body.text: iti yathoktadoṣābhāvaṃ guṇayogaṃ ca prāpnotīti saṃdarśitaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thus, it is shown that he obtains the absence of the stated faults and the endowment with virtues.

children.text: doṣamalino hi bālo hrīvirahāt suvasanaiḥ sugupto 'pi |
children.translated_text: For the fool devoid of moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) is stained with the impurity of faults, even though well-dressed and well-protected;
but the son of the <s>Jina</s>, even though unclothed, clothed in moral shame, is free from the stain of faults. // AMsa_18.11 //
stained with the impurity of faults;

body.translated_text: By this, moral shame is likened to a garment. For one who is covered with other garments but devoid of moral shame is

body.text: ākāśam iva na lipto hrīyuktaḥ jinasuto bhavati dharmaiḥ |
body.translated_text: The son of the <s>Jina</s> endowed with moral shame is unstained by [worldly] <s>dharmas</s>, like space;

children.translated_text: by '<s>dharmas</s>'

body.text: hrībhūṣitaś ca śobhati saṃparkagato jinasutānām || AMsa_18.12 ||

children.translated_text: to space

body.translated_text: By this verse, the likeness of moral shame

body.text: mātur iva vatsalatvaṃ hriyo vineyeṣu bodhisatvānāṃ |
body.translated_text: Like a mother's tenderness — such is the moral shame of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> toward those to be trained;
because of feeling shame at the neglect of beings who are to be rescued.

body.text: ārakṣā cāpi hrīḥ saṃsaratāṃ sarvadoṣebhyaḥ || AMsa_18.13 ||

body.translated_text: Because it is [present] in beings [taking the form of] elephants, horses, bodies, and so forth. By these similes of garment and the like, he shows that moral shame serves as an antidote to <s>kleśas</s> in one's way of life, as an antidote to worldly <s>dharmas</s> in one's conduct, as favorable to the companionship of fellow practitioners, as favorable to the ripening of beings, and as favorable to undefiled [participation in] <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: ity asya nirdeśo yathāpūrvaṃ | dhṛtivibhāge sapta ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: The exposition of this is as before. On the division of fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>), seven verses:

children.translated_text: The fortitude of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is distinguished from all others

children.text: dṛḍhatvena ca sarvebhyas tadanyebhyo viśiṣyate || AMsa_18.16 ||
children.translated_text: by its characteristic, by its divisions, and by its firmness. // AMsa_18.16 //

children.text: vīryaṃ samādhiḥ prajñā ca satvaṃ dhairyaṃ dhṛtirmatā |
children.translated_text: Vigor, concentration, and wisdom are the essence; courage and fortitude are considered [synonyms];

children.text: nirbhīto bodhisatvo hi trayād yasmāt pravartate || AMsa_18.17 ||
children.translated_text: for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is fearless because he proceeds from [these] three. // AMsa_18.17 //
the
characteristic of fortitude, together with its synonyms and its undertaking, is stated.
Vigor

children.translated_text: and the rest is the characteristic. Essence and the rest are the synonyms. The remainder is the means. From which three is he fearless in proceeding? It states:

from contraction of

body.translated_text: For in the tasks [of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>],

ebhis tribhiḥ ślokair dhṛtiprabhedaṃ darśayati | yathākramaṃ gotrataḥ | cittotpādaḥ | svārthataḥ | satvārthataḥ | prabhāvataḥ |
satvaparipācanataḥ | paramabodhitaś ca | tatra
body.translated_text: By these three verses, the divisions of fortitude are shown. In sequence: from the lineage (<s>gotra</s>); the generation of the mind [of awakening]; from one's own purpose; from the purpose of beings; from power; from the ripening of beings; and from supreme awakening. Therein,
'indifference'
should be understood as the indifference to body and life of one engaged in one's own purpose. Furthermore,
from practicing the difficult;
from intentional birth in [various] existences; and from the absence of defilement therein — these are also divisions.

children.translated_text: The hero is not shaken by evil friends, by suffering, or by hearing of the profound —

children.text: śalabhaiḥ pakṣavātaiś ca samudraiś ca sumeruvat || AMsa_18.22 ||
children.translated_text: like <s>Sumeru</s> by moths, by gusts of wind, and by oceans. // AMsa_18.22 //

body.text: etena bodhisatvadhṛter dṛḍhatvaṃ darśayati | upamātrayaṃ trayeṇākampane yathākramaṃ veditavyaṃ | akhedavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: By this, the firmness of <s>Bodhisattva</s> fortitude is shown. The threefold analogy should be understood with the three [causes of] non-shaking, in sequence. On the division of non-weariness (<s>akheda</s>), two verses:

children.translated_text: The non-weariness of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is incomparable in three objects,
based on moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>), [arising from] insatiability for learning, great vigor, and suffering. // AMsa_18.23 //
Intense aspiration toward great awakening is considered the non-weariness of the wise;

children.text: aniṣpannaś ca niṣpannaḥ suniṣpannaś ca bhūmiṣu || AMsa_18.24 ||
children.translated_text: it is unaccomplished, accomplished, and well-accomplished on the [respective] stages. // AMsa_18.24 //

body.text: ābhyāṃ vastuno niśrayataḥ svabhāvataḥ | prabhedataś cā

children.translated_text: and the divisions.
'In three objects':
in insatiability for learning;
in long-duration
vigor
-undertaking; and in <s>saṃsāric</s>
suffering.
Based on moral shame and fortitude
— for through these,

children.text: | tābhyāṃ hi khedotpattito lajjayate na cotpādayati |
children.translated_text: he is ashamed of the arising of weariness and does not produce it.
'Intense aspiration toward great awakening'

children.text: iti svabhāvvaḥ | chando hi vyāvṛtte khinno bhavati |
children.translated_text: — this is its nature. For one whose aspiration has ceased becomes weary.
'Unaccomplished'
is on the stage of devotional practice (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>).
'Accomplished'
is on the seven stages.
'Well-accomplished'

children.text: pareṇa ity eṣa prabhādaḥ | śāstrajñatāyāyāṃ dvau ślokau |
children.translated_text: is beyond [those] — this is the division. On the knowledge of treatises (<s>śāstrajñatā</s>), two verses:

body.translated_text: By these two [verses], non-weariness is stated in terms of the object, the support, the nature,

children.translated_text: It is distinguished by object, scope, function,
characteristic, inexhaustibility, and the arising of fruit. // AMsa_18.25 //
For the knowledge of treatises of the steadfast is the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of the gateway of concentration (<s>samādhimukha</s>);

children.text: gṛhītā satvapākāya saddharmasya ca dhāraṇe || AMsa_18.26 ||
children.translated_text: it is held for the ripening of beings and for maintaining the true <s>Dharma</s>. // AMsa_18.26 //

body.translated_text: Therein,
the objects of the knowledge of treatises
are the five places of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthāna</s>):

body.text: | adhyātmavidyā hetuvidyā śabdavidyā cikitsāvidyā śilpakarmasthānavidyā ca | svaparārthakriyā
body.translated_text: the inner science (<s>adhyātmavidyā</s>), the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>), the science of grammar (<s>śabdavidyā</s>), the science of medicine (<s>cikitsāvidyā</s>), and the science of arts and crafts (<s>śilpakarmasthānavidyā</s>). The activity for one's own and others' purposes is
the scope.
The function:

body.text: prathamavastuni svayaṃ pratipattiḥ parebhyaś ca tatsamākhyānaṃ | dvitīye taddoṣaparijñānaṃ paravādinigrahaś ca | trtīye svayaṃ suniruktābhidhānaṃ parasaṃpratyayaś ca | caturthe pareṣāṃ vyādhiśamanaṃ | pañcame parebhyas tat saṃvibhāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: in the first object — one's own practice and the explanation thereof to others; in the second — the full knowledge of its faults and the defeat of opposing doctrines; in the third — one's own clearly articulated expression and convincing others; in the fourth — curing others' diseases; in the fifth — sharing that with others.
The characteristic

body.text: śāstrajñatāyā etāny evas pañca vastuni śrutāni bhavanti | dhṛtāni | vacasā parijitāni | manasā anvīkṣitāni | dṛṣṭyā supratividdhāni | śrutvā yathākramaṃ | tad udgrahaṇataḥ | svādhyāyataḥ | prasannena manasārthacittanato yathāyogaṃ taddoṣaguṇāvagamāt | svākhyātadurākhyātāvadhāraṇataś ca |
body.translated_text: of the knowledge of treatises: these same five objects are heard, retained, mastered by speech, investigated by the mind, and well-penetrated by insight. Through hearing, in sequence: from memorization; from recitation; from reflecting on the meaning with a clear mind, according to context, from understanding their faults and qualities; and from ascertaining what is well-explained and poorly explained.
Inexhaustibility:
because it is inexhaustible even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder.
The arising of the fruit:
omniscience regarding all <s>dharmas</s> in all their aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). This
knowledge of treatises
of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>
is held through the gateways of concentration (<s>samādhimukha</s>) and through the gateways of
<s>dhāraṇī</s>.
It serves the ripening of beings
— through the gateways of concentration, from carrying out the activities for that purpose.
And for maintaining the true <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: pāraṇāya ca dhāraṇībhis taddhāraṇāt | lokajñatāyāṃ catvāraḥ ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: — through <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, from retaining it. On the knowledge of the world (<s>lokajñatā</s>), four verses:

children.translated_text: By body, by speech, and by the knowledge of truth — incomparable

children.text: lokajñatā hi dhīrāṇāṃ tadanyebhyo viśiṣyate || AMsa_18.27 ||
children.translated_text: is the knowledge of the world of the steadfast, distinguished from all others. // AMsa_18.27 //

body.translated_text: How by body? It states:
'With ever-smiling faces, the steadfast
How by speech? It states:
are always the first to speak.'

body.text: sā punaḥ kim artham ity āha |
body.translated_text: For what purpose? It states:
'For making beings receptive
To what end, receptive?
to the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s>.' // AMsa_18.28 //
How by the knowledge of truth? It states:

children.translated_text: From the two truths, since the arising of worlds is repeated,

children.text: dvayād astaṃgamas tasmāt tajjño lokajña ucyate || AMsa_18.29 ||
children.translated_text: and from the two, their cessation — therefore, one who knows that is called a 'knower of the world.' // AMsa_18.29 //
From the two truths, the arising of the world —

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ saṃsāro yaś codayo yena ceti kṛtvā |
children.translated_text: meaning repeated <s>saṃsāra</s>: both what arises and by what it arises.
From the two, the cessation —

children.text: nirodhamārgasatyābhāṃ | yaś cāstaṃgamo yena cetu kṛtvā |
children.translated_text: from the truths of cessation and path: both what ceases and by what it ceases.
'Therefore, one who knows that is called a knower of the world'
— because of being endowed with the wisdom that [understands] the arising and cessation of the world.

children.text: śamāya prāptaye teṣāṃ dhīmān satyeṣu yujyate |
children.translated_text: For the peace and attainment of those [beings], the wise one applies himself to the truths;

children.text: satyajñānād yato dhīmān lokajño hi nirucyate || AMsa_18.30 ||
children.translated_text: since from the knowledge of truth the wise one is proclaimed as a knower of the world. // AMsa_18.30 //
'for peace'
refers to the truths of suffering and origination.
'For attainment'
refers to the truths of cessation and path. On the division of reliance (<s>pratisaraṇa</s>), three verses:

body.translated_text: By this, the function of the knowledge of the world is stated. Therein,

children.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> of teaching is that which comes from the <s>ṛṣis</s>; and its meaning is intentional;

children.text: prāmāṇikaś ca nītārtho nirjalpā prāptir asya ca || AMsa_18.31 ||
children.translated_text: it is authoritative and of definitive meaning; and its attainment is free from verbal elaboration. // AMsa_18.31 //
the 'authoritative'
meaning is that which has been conveyed by one who is authoritative —
conveyed [means]
analyzed — by the Teacher or by one who has been authorized by him.
'Attainment free from verbal elaboration'
is the supramundane knowledge of realization — because of its inexpressibility. The rest has been explained.

body.translated_text: This is the characteristic of the reliances. Therein,

children.translated_text: Of one who rejects what has been stated, of what has been wrongly transmitted,

children.text: sābhilāṣasya ca prāpteḥ pratiṣedho 'tra deśitaḥ || AMsa_18.32 ||
children.translated_text: and of one with attachment to attainment — the prohibition is taught here. // AMsa_18.32 //
of the <s>ṛṣis</s>,

children.text: pudgalasya pratiṣedgo deśitaḥ | dvitīye yathārutasya vyañjanasya nābhiprāyikārthena | tṛtīyena
children.translated_text: the prohibition is taught. In the second — of the literal [meaning], not of the intentional meaning. In the third —
of the wrongly
inferred meaning, being led to what is distorted. In the fourth —
of [knowledge] with attachment
— [i.e.,] of knowledge [that is not] individually experienced.

body.translated_text: In the first reliance — of the person who rejects the <s>Dharma</s>

children.text: adhimukter vicārāc ca yathāvat parataḥ śravāt |
children.translated_text: From conviction, from investigation, from hearing properly from others,

children.text: nirjalpād api ca jñānād apraṇāśo hi dhīmatāṃ || AMsa_18.33 ||
children.translated_text: and from knowledge free from verbal elaboration — there is no loss for the wise. // AMsa_18.33 //
through conviction.
By the second, through one's own investigation of the intentional
meaning.
By the third,
from others,
through hearing the method of the meaning that is contrary to that [distorted interpretation].
By the fourth — through supramundane knowledge. On the division of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), four verses:

body.translated_text: Now, the benefit of the reliances. By the first reliance, the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>ṛṣis</s> is not lost

children.translated_text: The four analytical knowledges of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are incomparable —

children.text: paryāye lakṣaṇe vākye jñāne jñānāc ca tā matāḥ || AMsa_18.34 ||
children.translated_text: in synonyms, in characteristics, in speech, and in knowledge — and they arise from knowledge. // AMsa_18.34 //

body.translated_text: The first,
'in synonyms,'

body.text: jñānam ekaikasyārthastha yāvanto nāma paryāyāḥ | dvitīyā
body.translated_text: is the knowledge of all the synonym-terms for each individual meaning. The second,
'in characteristics,'
is [the knowledge of] the name corresponding to each meaning. The third,
'in speech,'
is the languages [spoken] in each individual region. The fourth,
'in knowledge,'

body.text: svayaṃ yat pratibhānaṃ | idaṃ pratisaṃvidāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ |
body.translated_text: is one's own spontaneous eloquence. This is the characteristic of the analytical knowledges.

children.text: deśanāyāṃ prayuktasya yasya yena ca deśanā |
children.translated_text: Of one engaged in teaching: that which [is taught], and by what means — the teaching

children.text: dharmārthayor dvayor vācā jñānenaiva ca deśanā || AMsa_18.35 ||
children.translated_text: of both <s>Dharma</s> and meaning is by speech and by knowledge itself. // AMsa_18.35 //
From the synopsis and detailed exposition of <s>Dharma</s>, from conveying both [<s>Dharma</s> and meaning] in all ways,
and from the full comprehension and removal of objections — the fourfold analytical knowledge. // AMsa_18.36 //
For one engaged in teaching,
[there is] that which [is taught] and by what means.
Therein,
'by knowledge'
— for whom, then, is
the teaching?
Of <s>Dharma</s> and

children.text: rthasya | kena deśanā vacanena jñānena ca | tatra
children.translated_text: of meaning. By what means is the teaching? By words and by knowledge. Therein,
the teaching of <s>Dharma</s> and meaning [is]:
'from the synopsis and detailed exposition of <s>Dharma</s>'
— by words, the teaching of those two
'from conveying [them] in all ways.'

children.text: | jñānena deśanā codyānāṃ pariharaṇāt | ato yac ca yena ca deśyate tajjñānāt catasraḥ pratisaṃvido vyavasthāpitāḥ |
children.translated_text: By knowledge, the teaching is from removing objections. Therefore, from what is taught and by what means it is taught, and from the knowledge thereof, the four analytical knowledges are established.

body.translated_text: Thus [is stated] the reason for the fourfold [division].

children.translated_text: Having individually reached equality, the subsequent communication
is proclaimed as analytical knowledge, for the destruction of all doubts. // AMsa_18.37 //

body.text: etena pratisaṃvidāṃ nirvacanaṃ karam ca darśitaṃ |

children.translated_text: 'Individually' —
having reached the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> through supramundane knowledge,
'equality' [means]
<s>tathatā</s> (suchness).
Having reached [that], in the subsequent
time, through the knowledge obtained subsequently [to the supramundane],
'the communication'
of synonyms and so forth is the analytical knowledge — this is the etymology.
'For the destruction of all doubts'

children.text: pareṣām iti karma | saṃsāravibhāge carvāraḥ ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: of others — this is the function. On the division of accumulations (<s>saṃbhāra</s>), four verses:

body.translated_text: By this, the etymology and function of the analytical knowledges are shown.

children.translated_text: The accumulation of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, consisting of merit and knowledge, is incomparable;
one is for prosperity in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the other is for undefiled transmigration. // AMsa_18.38 //
accumulation

children.text: yad arthaṃ ca saṃdarśayati | dvividhaḥ saṃbhāraḥ | tatra
children.translated_text: and for what purpose — this he shows. The accumulation is twofold. Therein,
the merit
accumulation
conduces to prosperity in <s>saṃsāra</s>.
The knowledge
accumulation
[conduces to] transmigration without defilement.

body.translated_text: What

children.text: dānaṃ śīlaṃ ca puṇyasya prajñā jñānasya saṃbhṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Generosity and morality are the accumulation of merit; wisdom is the accumulation of knowledge;

children.text: trayaṃ cānyad dvayasyāpi pañcāpi jñānasaṃbhṛtiḥ || AMsa_18.39 ||
children.translated_text: the other three are [accumulations] of both; and all five are also accumulations of knowledge. // AMsa_18.39 //

body.translated_text: By this, the inclusion of both accumulations through the perfections is [shown]. For through the power of patience, vigor, and meditation,

body.text: hy ubhayaṃ kriyate | tasmād dvayasaṃbhāratrayaṃ bhavati | punaḥ prajñāyāṃ pariṇāmanāt sarvāḥ pañca pāramitā jñānasaṃbhāro veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: both are accomplished. Therefore, the three [perfections] become [accumulations] of both. Furthermore, through the dedication [of all] in wisdom, all five perfections should be understood as the accumulation of knowledge.

children.text: saṃtatyā bhāvanām etya bhūyo bhūyaḥ śubhasya hi |
children.translated_text: That which, by continuity, having reached cultivation, is again and again the nourishment of virtue —

children.text: āhāro yaḥ sa saṃbhāro vīdhīre sarvārthasādhakaḥ || AMsa_18.40 ||
children.translated_text: that is the accumulation for the steadfast, accomplishing all purposes. // AMsa_18.40 //

body.text: etat saṃbhāranirvacanaṃ karma ca | sam iti

children.translated_text: 'by continuity.'
'Bhā' [means]
having reached 'cultivation.'
'Ra' [means]
'again and again'
— nourishment.
'Accomplishing all purposes'
— this is the function, from accomplishing one's own and others' purposes.

body.translated_text: This is the etymology and function of 'accumulation.' 'Sam' [means]

children.translated_text: The accumulation increases for the steadfast — for entry [into the stages], for the signless,
for effortlessness, for consecration, and for the final [attainment]. // AMsa_18.41 //
the stages.

children.text: | ṣaṭsu bhūmiṣv animittāya saptamībhūmisaṃgṛhītāya | tasyāṃ nimittasamudācārāt | saptamyāṃ bhūmāv anābhogāya tadanybhūmidvayasṃgṛhītāya | tayoḥ saṃbhārābhiṣekāya daśamībhūmisaṃgṛhītāya | tasyāṃ saṃbhāro niṣṭhāgamanāya buddhabhūmisaṃgṛhītāya | smṛtyupasthānavibhāge trayaḥ ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: On the six stages, for signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), which is included in the seventh stage — because on that stage signs still arise in practice; on the seventh stage, for effortlessness (<s>anābhoga</s>), which is included in the other two stages [eighth and ninth]; on those, the accumulation for consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), which is included in the tenth stage; on that stage, the accumulation for final completion, which is included in the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. On the division of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), three verses:

body.translated_text: This is the division [of the accumulation] according to <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therein, on the stage of devotional practice (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), the accumulation is for entry into

children.translated_text: Through fourteen aspects, the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness —

children.text: dhīmatām asamatvāt sā tadanyebhyo viśiṣyate || AMsa_18.42 ||
children.translated_text: of the wise, through its inequality with that of others, is distinguished. // AMsa_18.42 //
fourteen?

body.translated_text: Through which

children.text: niśrayāt pratipakṣāc ca avatārāt tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: From the basis, from the antidote, and from the entry likewise,
and from the object, mental attention, and attainment, it is distinguished. // AMsa_18.43 //
From conformity and following, from full comprehension and arising,
from the degree, from the supremacy, and from the accomplishment of cultivation. // AMsa_18.44 //

body.text: ity ebhiś caturdaśabhir ākārair bodhisatvānāṃ smṛtyupastānabhāvanā viśiṣyate | katham
body.translated_text: By these fourteen aspects, the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is distinguished. How
from the basis

body.text: to mahāyāne śrutacintābhāvanāmayīṃ prajñām āśritya | kathaṃ
body.translated_text: ? By relying on the wisdom arising from learning, reflection, and cultivation in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. How
from the antidote

body.text: taḥ caturviparyāsapratipakṣāṇām apy aśuciduḥkhānityānātmasaṃjñānaṃ pratipakṣatvāt kāyādidharmanairātmyapraveśataḥ | katham
body.translated_text: ? Because even the perceptions of impurity, suffering, impermanence, and non-self — which are antidotes to the four errors (<s>viparyāsa</s>) — serve as antidotes, through entering the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> regarding the body and the rest. How
from entry

body.text: taḥ | caturbhiḥ smṛtyupasthānair yathākramaṃ duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgasatyāvatārāt svayaṃ pareṣāṃ cāvatāraṇāt | yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text: ? Through the four foundations of mindfulness, respectively, entry into the truths of suffering, origination, cessation, and path — entering oneself and causing others to enter. As stated
in the <s>Madhyāntavibhāga</s>. How
from the object
? From taking as object the body and the rest of all beings. How
from mental attention
? From the non-apprehension of the body and the rest. How
from attainment

body.text: kāyādīnāṃ na visaṃ yogāya nāvasaṃyogāya | kathaṃ
body.translated_text: ? Neither for the disjunction nor the conjunction of the body and the rest. How
from conformity
? Through conformity with the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), by being antidotes to their opponents. How
from following

body.text: taḥ laukikānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ cānuvṛttyā tadupasaṃhitasmṛtyupasthānabhāvanāt tebhyas tadupadeśārthaṃ | kathaṃ
body.translated_text: ? Through following along with worldly beings, <s>śrāvakas</s>, and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — from cultivating the foundations of mindfulness associated with them, for the purpose of instructing them. How
from full comprehension

body.text: taḥ kāyasya māyopamatvaparijñayā tathaivābhūtarūpasaṃprakhyānāt | vedanāyāḥ | svapnopamatvaparijñayā tathaiva mithyānubhavāt | cittasya prakṛtiprabhāsvaratvapraijñayā ākāśavat | dharmāṇām āgantukakatvaparijñayā ākāśāganturajodhūmābhranīhāropakleśavat | katham
body.translated_text: ? Through the full comprehension of the body as being like an illusion, from its likewise manifesting as unreal forms; of feeling, through the full comprehension of its being like a dream, from its likewise experiencing falsely; of mind, through the full comprehension of its luminous nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvaratva</s>), like space; of <s>dharmas</s>, through the full comprehension of their adventitious nature, like the defilements of dust, smoke, clouds, and mist upon space. How
from arising

? In intentional birth in existence, for one who has become a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) and the like, in the excellent endowments of body, feeling, and the rest, from non-defilement thereby. How
from the degree

body.text: taḥ mṛdvā api smṛtyupasthānabhāvanāyās tad anyebhyo adhimātratvāt | prakṛtitīkṣṇendriyatayā | kataṃ
body.translated_text: ? Because even a mild cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness surpasses that of others in intensity, through having naturally sharp faculties. How
from the supremacy
? From the effortless, mixed, and unstained cultivation of those who have perfected [it]. How
from cultivation

body.text: taḥ atyantaṃ tadbhāvanāt nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇe 'pi tadakṣayāt | kathaṃ
body.translated_text: ? From cultivating it utterly, since even in <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>), it is inexhaustible. How
from accomplishment

body.text: taḥ | daśasu bhūmiṣu buddhatve ca samudāgamāt | samyakprahāṇavibhāge pañca ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: ? From the accomplishment on the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) and in <s>Buddhahood</s>. On the division of right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), five verses:

children.translated_text: The right effort of the steadfast is unequal to [that of] all beings;
it is cultivated through the antidote to the faults of the foundations of mindfulness. // AMsa_18.45 //

body.text: yāvatyaḥ smṛtyupasthānabhāvanā uktāḥ tadvipakṣāṇāṃ pratipakṣeṇa samyakprahāṇabhāvaneti samastaṃ samyakprahāṇalakṣaṇaṃ | prabhedena punaḥ |
body.translated_text: Whatever cultivations of the foundations of mindfulness have been stated, the cultivation of right effort through the antidote to their opponents — this is the complete characteristic of right effort. In detail, furthermore:

children.translated_text: In the enjoyments of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and in the abandonment of the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>),

children.text: manaskārasya ca tyāge praveśe caiva bhūmiṣu || AMsa_18.46 ||
children.translated_text: and in the abandonment of [inferior] mental attention, and in the entry into the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>); // AMsa_18.46 //

body.translated_text: in the abiding in signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), and in the attainment of the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>),

body.text: satvānāṃ paripāke ca abhiṣeke ca dhīmatāṃ || AMsa_18.47 ||
body.translated_text: and in the maturation of beings, and in the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) of the wise; // AMsa_18.47 //

children.text: kṣetrasya ca viśuddhyarthaṃ niṣṭhāgamana eva ca |
children.translated_text: and for the purpose of the purification of the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field, and in the final completion itself —
the right effort of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is cultivated through the antidote to [each] opponent. // AMsa_18.48 //

body.translated_text: This is the division of the cultivation of right effort.
In the enjoyments of <s>saṃsāra</s> —
defiled
enjoyments,
in [worldly] prosperities. The five
hindrances are to be abandoned.
The mental attention of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>
is to be abandoned.
Entry into the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>).
Abiding in signlessness (<s>animittavihāra</s>)
on the seventh stage.
Attainment of the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>).
Maturation of beings
on the ninth [stage].
And the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>)
on the tenth [stage].
For the purpose of purification of the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field
on all three [stages] as well.
And in the final completion
on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. Those
who are
the opponents —
through their
antidote,
the cultivation of right effort should be understood. This is its division.

children.translated_text: Relying on aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), the cultivation of yoga is accompanied by signs;
the antidote in all right efforts is declared. // AMsa_18.49 //
'aspiration' (<s>chanda</s>)

children.text: janayati | vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhate | cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | samyak pradadhāti | ity eṣāṃ padānām arthanirdeśaḥ | chandaṃ hi
children.translated_text: — one generates [it]. One strives, one arouses vigor. One takes hold of the mind. One rightly applies [it]. This is the explanation of the meaning of these terms. For relying on
aspiration,
one cultivates the yoga called <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight)
— the yoga
— thus one strives. And that
cultivation
is cultivated together with the signs of calm (<s>śamatha</s>), holding (<s>pragraha</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Therefore it is
accompanied by signs.

children.text: | kathaṃ punar bhāvyate | yac chamathapragrahopakleśayor layāuddhatyayoḥ
children.translated_text: How then is it cultivated? With the antidote to the defilements of calm and holding — namely, dullness (<s>laya</s>) and excitement (<s>auddhatya</s>) —
through the antidote,

children.text: vīryam ārabhate | cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti pradadhāti ca | śamathe samaprāpte copekṣāyāṃ pradadhāti | eṣā yogabhāvanā yathoktaprabhedeṣu
children.translated_text: one arouses vigor; one takes hold of the mind and applies [it]. And when calm is achieved, one applies [oneself] in equanimity. This is the cultivation of yoga — in all right efforts of the stated divisions,
the antidote is declared.
On the division of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), five verses:

body.translated_text: By this,

children.translated_text: The four bases of supernatural power of the steadfast, having the foremost characteristics,

children.text: sarvārthasiddhau jāyante ātmanaś ca parasya ca || AMsa_18.50 ||
children.translated_text: arise for the accomplishment of all aims, of oneself and of others. // AMsa_18.50 //
The accomplishment of all aims

children.text: laukikī lokottarā ca veditavyā ca | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ |
children.translated_text: should be understood as both mundane and supramundane. The rest is self-evident.

children.text: niśrayāc ca prabhedāc ca upāyād abhinirhṛteḥ |
children.translated_text: From the basis, from the division, from the means, and from the accomplishment —
the determination of the bases of supernatural power of the wise is accepted in every way. // AMsa_18.51 //

body.translated_text: This is the explanation of the remainder of the summary.

children.translated_text: Relying on the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), the division is fourfold;

children.text: upāyaś cābhinirhāraḥ ṣaḍvidhaś ca vidhīyate || AMsa_18.52 ||
children.translated_text: and the means, and the accomplishment is sixfold — thus it is established. // AMsa_18.52 //
The perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is the basis. The fourfold division is
through the distinction of aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), mind (<s>citta</s>), and investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>) <s>samādhis</s>.
The means
is also fourfold.
The accomplishment is sixfold.
What is the fourfold means?
'The first is that of resolve, the second is that of benevolence,

children.text: naibandhikas tṛtīyaś ca caturthaḥ prātipakṣikaḥ || AMsa_18.53 ||
children.translated_text: the third is that of binding, and the fourth is that of antidoting.' // AMsa_18.53 //
the means of resolve —
the means of one who has faith, who desires, and who exerts. Pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) is
the means of benevolence.
Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) are
the means of binding —

children.text: | ekena cittasyālambanāvismarāt | dvitīyena visāraprajñānāt | cetanā copekṣā ca prātipakṣika upāyaḥ | layāuddhatyopakleśayoḥ kleśānāṃ ca
children.translated_text: by the first, through not forgetting the object of the mind; by the second, through the knowledge of what is erroneous. Volition (<s>cetanā</s>) and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) are the means of antidoting, because of being
the antidote
to the defilements of dullness and excitement, and to the afflictions. What is the sixfold accomplishment?

body.translated_text: Among the eight formations of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasaṃskāra</s>): aspiration (<s>chanda</s>) and exertion (<s>vyāyāma</s>) and faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) are

children.translated_text: 'The accomplishment of vision, of instruction, of abiding and display,

children.text: praṇidher vaśitāyaś ca dharmaprāpteś ca nirhṛtiḥ || AMsa_18.54 ||
children.translated_text: of aspiration, of mastery, and of the attainment of <s>dharmas</s>.' // AMsa_18.54 //
vision

children.text: cakṣuḥ pañcavidhaṃ māṃsacakṣuḥ divyaṃ cakṣuḥ āryaṃ prajñācakṣuḥ dharmacakṣuḥ buddhacakṣuś ca |
children.translated_text: is the fivefold eye: the fleshly eye, the divine eye, the noble eye, the wisdom eye, the <s>dharma</s>-eye, and the <s>Buddha</s>-eye.
Instruction

children.text: ṣaḍabhijñā yathākramaṃ | tābhir upasaṃkramya bhāṣā cittaṃ cāgatiṃ ca gatiṃ ca viditvā niḥsaraṇāyāvavadanāt |
children.translated_text: is the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>), respectively. Through them, having approached [beings], knowing their speech, mind, past existence, and future destiny, one instructs [them] for the purpose of liberation.
Abiding and display —
because <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have manifold displays of <s>samādhi</s> through emanations and the like.
Aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>) —

children.text: yena praṇidhijñānena praṇidhānabalikā bodhisatvāḥ praṇidhānavaiśeṣikatayā vikrīḍanti | yeṣāṃ na sukaraṃ saṃkhyā kartuṃ kāyasya vā prabhāyā vā svarasasya veti vistareṇa yathā daśabhūmike sūtre |
children.translated_text: the aspiration-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>) through which <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, empowered by their aspirations, display [wonders] through the distinction of their aspirations — of whom it is not easy to count the [displays] of body, radiance, or vocal sound — and so forth in detail, as in the <s>Daśabhūmika Sūtra</s>.
Mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) —
as therein [in the <s>Daśabhūmika Sūtra</s>] the ten masteries are taught.
The attainment of <s>dharmas</s> —

<s>samādhi</s> is for the purpose of the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkriyā</s>)
of the pacification of that. On the division of the summaries of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmoddāna</s>), [two] verses:

body.translated_text: Emptiness is for the purpose of complete knowledge (<s>parijñā</s>)

children.translated_text: 'As proximate causes of <s>samādhi</s>, the four summaries of <s>Dharma</s>
have been taught to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, out of the desire for the benefit of beings.' // AMsa_18.80 //

body.text: tatra saṃskārā anityāḥ sarvasaṃskārā duḥkhāḥ ity apraṇihitasya

children.translated_text: proximate cause of the wishless

children.text: bhāvena deśitaṃ | sarvadhamrā anātmāna ity śūnyatāyāḥ | śāntaṃ nirvāṇam iti ānimittasya samādheḥ | kaḥ punar anityārtho yāvac chāntārthaḥ ity āha |
children.translated_text: samādhi. 'All dharmas are without self' — [this is the proximate cause] of emptiness. 'Peaceful is nirvāṇa' — [the proximate cause] of the signless samādhi. What then is the meaning of 'impermanent' up to the meaning of 'peaceful'? He says:

body.translated_text: Therein, 'conditioned things (saṃskāras) are impermanent' and 'all conditioned things are suffering' — these are taught as the

children.translated_text: 'The meaning of non-existence, the meaning of non-conceptualization, the meaning of mere imagination,

children.text: vikalpopaśamārthaś ca dhīmatāṃ tac catuṣṭayam || AMsa_18.81 ||
children.translated_text: and the meaning of the pacification of conceptualization — that fourfold [meaning] is for the wise.' // AMsa_18.81 //
the meaning of non-existence

children.text: 'nityārthaḥ | yan nityaṃ nāsti tad anityaṃ teṣāṃ yat parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: is the meaning of 'impermanent' — that which is permanent does not exist; that is impermanent — [this refers to] their imagined characteristic (<s>parikalpitalakṣaṇa</s>).
The meaning of unreal
conceptualization
is the meaning of 'suffering' — [this refers to] the dependent characteristic (<s>paratantralakṣaṇa</s>).
The meaning of mere
imagination
is the meaning of 'without self.'
The word 'indeed' (eva)

children.text: śabdenāvadhāraṇaṃ parikalpata ātmā nāsti parikalpamātraṃ tv astīti parikalpitalakṣaṇasyābhāvārtho 'nātmārtha ity uktaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: serves as a restriction: the imagined self does not exist, but mere imagination does exist — thus the meaning of 'without self' is stated as the meaning of the non-existence of the imagined characteristic.
The meaning of the pacification of conceptualization

children.text: pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ | kṣaṇabhaṅgārtho 'py anityārtho veditavyaḥ paratantralakṣaṇasya | atas tatsādhanārthaṃ kṣaṇikatvavibhāge daśa ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: is the perfected characteristic (<s>pariniṣpannalakṣaṇa</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The meaning of 'impermanent' should also be understood as the meaning of momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) of the dependent characteristic. Therefore, for the purpose of establishing that, on the division of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>), ten verses:

body.translated_text: For <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.translated_text: 'From the impossibility [of continuity], from arising from causes, from opposition, from non-abiding by itself,
from non-existence, from the invariability of characteristics, from conformity, and from cessation; // AMsa_18.82 //
from the perception of transformation, from being the cause and the fruit of that,
from having been taken up, from dominance, and from the conformity of pure beings.' // AMsa_18.83 //

body.text: tatra kṣaṇikaṃ sarvaṃ saṃskāram iti paścād vacanād iyaṃ pratijñā veditavyā | tat punaḥ kathaṃ sidhyati | kṣaṇikatvam antareṇa saṃskārāṇāṃ pravṛtter
body.translated_text: Therein, 'all conditioned things are momentary' — this thesis should be understood from the later statement. How then is it established? Because without momentariness, the operation of conditioned things would be
impossible (ayoga).

body.text: | prabandhena hi vṛttiḥ pravṛttiḥ | sā cāntareṇa pratikṣaṇam utpādanirodhau na yujyate | atha kālāntaraṃ sthitvā pūrvottaranirodhotpādataḥ prabandheneṣyate vṛttiḥ | tadanantaraṃ pravṛttir na syāt prabandhābhāvāt naiva cotpannasya vinā prabandhena kālāntaraṃ bhāvo yujyate | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ
body.translated_text: For continuity (prabandha) is the operation. And that is not possible without arising and ceasing at every moment. Now, if one holds that [things] abide for some time and then cease and arise in succession, and [thus] continuity is accepted as operation — then there would be no immediate operation, because of the absence of continuity. And it is not possible for something that has arisen to exist for a further period without continuity. For what reason?
Because of arising from causes (hetu) —

body.text: utpattiḥ | hetuto hi sarvaṃ saṃskṛtam utpadyate bhavatīty arthaḥ | tad yadi bhūtvā punar uttarakālaṃ bhavati tasyāvaśyaṃ hetunā bhavitavyaṃ | vināhetunā ādita ivābhāvāt | na ca tat tenaiva hetunā bhavitum arhati tasyopayuktahetukatvāt | na cānyo hetur uplabhyate | tasmāt pratikṣaṇam avaśyaṃ pūrvahetukam anyad bhavatīti veditavyaṃ | evaṃ vinā prabandhenotpannasya kālāntaraṃ bhāvo no yujyate | atha apy evam iṣyata notpannaṃ punar utpadyate yad arthaṃ hetunā bhavitavyaṃ syād utapannaṃ tu kālāntareṇa paścān nirudhyate notpannamātram eveti | tatpaścāt kena nirudhyate | yad utpādahetunaiva tad ayuktaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | utpādnirodhayor
body.translated_text: Arising: for everything conditioned arises from a cause — this is the meaning, 'it comes into being.' If, after having come into being, it exists at a later time, it must necessarily exist through a cause — because without a cause it would be non-existent, as in the beginning. And it cannot exist through that very same cause, because that cause has been exhausted. Nor is any other cause apprehended. Therefore, it must be understood that at every moment something different, having a prior cause, comes into being. Thus, without a continuum, the existence of something that has arisen at a later time is not tenable. Now even if it is accepted that what has arisen does not arise again — for which purpose it would need to exist through a cause — but what has arisen is subsequently destroyed after an interval, not at the mere moment of arising, then: by what is it subsequently destroyed? If by the very cause of arising — that is untenable. For what reason? Because of the mutual contradiction of arising and destruction

body.text:
| na hi virodhayos tulyo hetur upalabhyate | tad yathā chāyātapayoḥ śītoṣṇayoś ca |
kālāntaranirodhasyaiva
body.translated_text:
for a single cause of two contradictories is not apprehended, just as with shade and sunlight, and cold and heat.
And because of the contradiction with destruction at a later time

body.text: ca virodhāt | kena virodhāt | āgamena ca | yad uktaṃ bhagavatā | māyopamās te bhikṣo saṃskārā āpāyikās tāvat kālikā itvarapratyupasthāyina iti | manaskāreṇa ca yogināṃ | te hi saṃskārāṇām udayavyayau manasikurvantaḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ teṣāṃ nirodhaṃ paśyanti | anyathā hi teṣām api nirvidvirāgavimuktayo na syur yathānyeṣāṃ maraṇakālādiṣu nirodhaṃ paśyantāṃ | yadi cotpannaḥ saṃskāraḥ kālāntaraṃ tiṣṭhet sa
body.translated_text: itself. With what contradiction? With scripture as well — for the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'O monk, conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are like illusions — they pertain to calamity, are temporal, and swiftly present.' And through the mental attention of yogins — for they, mentally attending to the arising and passing away of conditioned phenomena, see their destruction at every moment. Otherwise, they too would not have disenchantment, dispassion, and liberation, just like others who see destruction only at the time of death and so forth. And if a conditioned phenomenon, having arisen, were to persist for an interval, it
would either persist
by itself,
being

body.text: eva sthātuṃ samarthaḥ | sthitikāraṇena vā kenacit | svayaṃ tāvad avasthānam ayuktaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | paścāt
body.translated_text: capable of persisting by itself, or through some cause of persistence. Persisting by itself, to begin with, is untenable. For what reason? Because subsequently
it does not persist by itself

body.text: | kkena vā so 'nte punaḥ sthātuṃ na samarthaḥ | sthitikāraṇenāpi na yuktaṃ tasyā
body.translated_text: — why then would it not be capable of persisting by itself at the end? And [persisting] through a cause of persistence is also untenable, because of the non-existence
of that

body.text: | na hi tat kiṃcid upalabhyate | athāpi syād vināpi sthitikāraṇena vināśakāraṇābhāvāt avatiṣṭhate | labdhe tu vināśakāraṇe paścād vināśayati agnineva śyāmateti | tad ayuktaṃ tasyābhāvāt | na hi vināśakāraṇaṃ paścād api kiṃcid asti | agnināpi śyāmatā vināśayatīti suprasiddhaṃ | visadṛśotpattau tu tasya sāmārthyaṃ prasiddhaṃ | tathā hi tatsaṃbandhāt śyāmatāyāḥ saṃtatir visadṛśī gṛhyate ma tu sarvathaivāpravṛttiḥ | apām api kvathyamānānām agnisaṃbandhād alpataratamotpattito 'timandyād ante punar anutpattir gṛhyate |
body.translated_text: — for no such [cause of persistence] is apprehended. Now one might say: even without a cause of persistence, it persists because of the absence of a cause of destruction; but when a cause of destruction is obtained, it is subsequently destroyed — just as fire [destroys] dark color. That is untenable, because of the non-existence of that [cause of destruction] — for there is no cause of destruction even subsequently. That fire destroys dark color is well-established — but its power is established in producing a dissimilar arising. For it is observed that through contact with fire, the continuum of dark color becomes dissimilar, but there is not a complete cessation in every respect. Even in water being boiled, through contact with fire, from the arising of ever-lesser [quantities], through extreme diminution, at the end, non-arising is observed.
Because of the invariability of the characteristic

body.text: | ekāntikaṃ hy saṃskṛtalakṣaṇam uktaṃ bhagavatā yad uta saṃskṛtasyānityatā | tad yadi notpannamātraṃ vinaśyet | kaṃcit kālam asyānityatā na syād iti anaikāntikam anityatālakṣaṇaṃ prasahyate | athāpi syāt pratikṣaṇam apūrvotpattau tad evedam iti pratyabhijñānaṃ na syād iti | tad bhavaty eva sādṛśasya
body.translated_text: — for the <s>Bhagavān</s> stated the invariable characteristic of the conditioned, namely the impermanence of the conditioned. If what has just arisen were not to perish [immediately], its impermanence would not obtain for some period of time, and thus the characteristic of impermanence would not be invariable. Now one might object: in the case of a novel arising at every moment, there would be no recognition 'this is that very thing.' But that [recognition] does occur, because of the continuation of what is similar

body.text: māyākārapalakavat | sādṛśyāt tatbuddhir na tadbhāvād iti | kathaṃ gamyate |
body.translated_text: like the actor's mask. The cognition 'this is that' is due to similarity, not due to identity. How is this ascertained?
From destruction

body.text: | na hi tathaivāvasthitasyānte nirodhaḥ syād ādilakṣaṇanirviśiṣṭatvāt | tasmān na tat tad evety avadhāryate ante
body.translated_text: — for there would be no destruction at the end of something that has remained just as it was, since it would be indistinguishable from its initial characteristic. Therefore, it is ascertained that it is not that very same thing. And because
transformation is apprehended

body.text: | pariṇāmo hi nāmānyathātvaṃ | tad yadi nādita evārabdhaṃ bhaved ādhyātmikabāhyānāṃ bhāvānām ante pariṇāmo nopalabhyeta | tasmād ādita evānyathātvam ārabdhaṃ yat krameṇābhivardhamānam ante vyaktim āpadyante kṣīrasyeva dadhyavasthāyāṃ | yāvat tu tad anyathātvaṃ sūkṣmatvān na paricchidyate | tāvat sādṛśyānuvṛttes tad evedam imi jñāyata iti siddhaṃ | tataś ca pratikṣaṇam anyathātvāt | kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasiddhaṃ | kutaś ca prasiddhaṃ |
body.translated_text: — for transformation means becoming otherwise. If that [change] had not begun from the very start, transformation of internal and external entities would not be apprehended at the end. Therefore, the becoming-otherwise has begun from the very start, and increasing gradually, becomes manifest at the end — like milk in the state of curds. But as long as that becoming-otherwise is not discerned due to its subtlety, so long, because of the continuation of similarity, it is known as 'this is that very thing' — this is established. And therefore, because of the becoming-otherwise at every moment, momentariness is established. And from what else is it established?
From being the cause and the effect of that
— from being the cause of what is momentary, and from being the effect of what is momentary — this is the meaning.

body.text: kṣaṇikaṃ hi cittaṃ prasiddhaṃ tasya cānye saṃskārāś cakṣūrūpādayo hetutaḥ | tasmāt te 'pi kṣaṇikā iti siddhaṃ | na tv akṣaṇikāt kṣaṇikaṃ bhavitum arhati yathā nityād anytyatam iti | cittsya khalv api sarve saṃskārāḥ phalaṃ | katham idaṃ gamyate |
body.translated_text: For mind is well-established as momentary, and the other conditioned phenomena — eye, form, and the like — are its causes. Therefore, they too are established as momentary. For a momentary [effect] cannot arise from what is not momentary, just as an impermanent [thing cannot arise] from what is permanent. Moreover, all conditioned phenomena are the effect of mind. How is this ascertained?
Because they are appropriated, because of [mind's] sovereignty, and because of the conformity of pure beings

body.text:
ca | cittena hi sarve saṃskārāś cakṣurādayaḥ sādhiṣṭhānā upāttāḥ sahasaṃmūrchnāḥ tadanugrahānuvṛttitaḥ | tasmāt te cittasya phalaṃ cittasya cādhipatyaṃ saṃskāreṣu | yathoktaṃ bhagavatā | cittenāyaṃ loko nīyate cittena parikṛṣyate cittasyotpannasyotpannasya vaśe vartate iti | tathā viñānapratyayaṃ nāma rūpam ity uktaṃ | tasmāc cittasya phalaṃ | śuddhacittānuvṛttitaś ca | śuddhaṃ hi yogināṃ cittaṃ saṃskārā anuvartante | yathoktaṃ | dhyāyī bhikṣuḥ ṛddhimāṃś cittavaśe prāpta imaṃ dāruskandhaṃ sacet suvarṇam adhimucyate tad apy asya tahaiva syād iti | tasmād api cittaphalaṃ saṃskārāḥ | satvānuvṛttitaś ca | tathā hi pāpakāreṣu satveṣu bāhyā bhāvā hīnā bhavanti | puṇyakāreṣu ca praṇītāḥ | atas taccittānuvartanāt cittaphalatvaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ siddhaṃ | tataś ca teṣāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ | na hi kṣaṇikasyākṣaṇikaṃ phalaṃ yujyate tadanuvidhāyitvāt | evaṃ tāvad aviśeṣeṇa saṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ dvābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ sādhitaṃ |
ādhyātmikānāṃ punaḥ sādhanārthaṃ pañca ślokā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text:
— for all conditioned phenomena — eye and the like — are appropriated by mind, co-arising with it, existing in its domain, because of the conformity of its sustenance. Therefore, they are the effect of mind, and mind has sovereignty over conditioned phenomena. As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This world is led by mind, dragged by mind; it is subject to the power of mind when it has arisen.' Likewise it was said: 'Name-and-form is conditioned by consciousness.' Therefore, [conditioned phenomena] are the effect of mind. And also because of the conformity of pure mind — for conditioned phenomena conform to the pure mind of yogins. As stated: 'A monk who meditates, possessing supernatural power, who has gained mastery over the mind — if he resolves that this piece of wood is gold, it would indeed become so for him.' Therefore too, conditioned phenomena are the effect of mind. And also because of the conformity of beings — for when beings perform evil, external entities become inferior; and when they perform merit, [external entities become] excellent. Thus, because of conformity with their minds, the status of conditioned phenomena as effects of mind is established. And therefore their momentariness [is established] — for a non-momentary effect of what is momentary is untenable, because it conforms to it. Thus, the momentariness of conditioned phenomena in general has been established by two verses.
For the establishment [of momentariness] of internal [phenomena] in particular, five verses should be understood:

children.translated_text: The first [type of arising], even by degrees, by accumulation, by being a basis,
by transformation and ripening, likewise by inferior and superior [status]. // AMsa_18.84 //
By [being] luminous and non-luminous, by traveling to another place,
by [being] with seed and without seed, and by [being] a reflection — thus there is arising. // AMsa_18.85 //
In the fourteen types of arising, [each] has a cause, without exception;

children.text: cayāyāpārthād ayogāc ca āśrayatva asaṃbhavāt || AMsa_18.86 ||
children.translated_text: because of the purposelessness of accumulation, because of logical impossibility, and because of the impossibility of being a basis. // AMsa_18.86 //
Because of the impossibility of something that persists at the end, from [the argument of] non-destruction at the beginning and transformation,
likewise in inferior and superior [states], and also in the luminous and non-luminous. // AMsa_18.87 //
Because of the absence of [actual] going, because of the illogicality of persistence, because of the impossibility of a final [state],

children.text: anuvṛtteś ca cittasya kṣaṇikaṃ sarvasaṃskṛtam || AMsa_18.88 ||
children.translated_text: and because of the conformity of mind — all that is conditioned is momentary. // AMsa_18.88 //

body.translated_text: 'The first, even by degrees'
up to
'all that is conditioned is momentary.'

body.text: iti | katham eṣām ebhiḥ kṣaṇikatvaṃ sidhyati | ādyātmikānāṃ hi saṃskārāṇāṃ caturdaśavidha utpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: How is the momentariness of these established by these [arguments]? For the arising of internal conditioned phenomena is of fourteen types:
The 'first'
arising is the initial production of the bodily existence.
'By degrees'
refers to that which is beyond the initial birth-characteristic [i.e., growth].
'By accumulation'
refers to the increase through food, sleep, celibacy, and attainment.
'By being a basis'
refers to [the arising] of eye-consciousness and the like through their bases such as the eye and so forth.
'By transformation'
refers to the change in complexion and the like through desire and the like.
'By ripening'
refers to the stages of embryo, infant, youth, young adult, middle-aged, and elderly.
'By inferior status'
'and by superior status'
refer to [the arising] of those born in bad destinies and [good destinies], respectively.
'By luminous [status]'

body.text: yo nirmitakāmeṣu parinirmitakāmeṣu rūpārūpyeṣu copapannānāṃ | cittamātrādīnatvāt |
body.translated_text: refers to [the arising] of those born among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, and in the form and formless realms — because of being governed by mind alone.
'By non-luminous [status]'
refers to that of those born elsewhere.
'By traveling to another place'
refers to the arising in another place upon cessation in one place.
'By having seed'
refers to [the arising] of the <s>Arhat</s>, excluding the final aggregates.
'By being without seed'
refers to those very final [aggregates] of the <s>Arhat</s>.
'By being a reflection'

body.text: | yo aṣṭavimokṣadhyāyināṃ samādhivaśena pratibimbānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ utpādaḥ | etasyāṃ
body.translated_text: refers to the arising of conditioned phenomena as reflections through the power of <s>samādhi</s> for those who meditate on the eight liberations. In this
fourteenfold arising
of internal conditioned phenomena, momentariness [is established]
'because it has a cause, without exception'

body.text: dibhiḥ kāraṇair veditavyaṃ | ādyotpāde tāvat hetuviśeṣāt | yadi hi tasya hetutvena viśeṣo na syāt tad uttarāyāḥ saṃskārapravṛtter uttarottaraviśeṣo nopalabhyeta hetvaviśeṣāt | viśeṣe ca sati taduttarebhyas tasyānyatvāt | kṣaṇikatvasiddhiḥ | taratamotpāde mānaviśeṣāt | mānaṃ pramāṇam ity arthaḥ | na hi pratikṣaṇaṃ vinā 'nyatvena parimāṇaviśeṣo bhavet | upacayotpāde
body.translated_text: and so forth — through these reasons it should be understood. In the case of the first arising, to begin with — because of the distinctiveness of its cause. For if that [first arising] had no distinctiveness as a cause, then no successive distinctiveness in the subsequent operation of conditioned phenomena would be apprehended, due to the absence of causal distinctiveness. But when there is distinctiveness, since [the first arising] is different from those subsequent [moments], the establishment of momentariness [follows]. In the case of arising by degrees — because of the distinctiveness of measure. 'Measure' means size. For without there being otherness at every moment, there would be no distinctiveness of size. In the case of arising by accumulation —
because of the purposelessness of accumulation

body.text: | upastambho hi cayaḥ | tasyāpārthyaṃ syād antareṇa kṣaṇikatvaṃ tathaivāvasthitatvāt |
body.translated_text: — for accumulation means nourishment. Its purposelessness would follow if there were no momentariness, since [things] would remain just as they are.
And because of the logical impossibility

body.text: copacayasyaiva | na hi pratikṣaṇaṃ vinā puṣṭatarotpattyā yujyetopacayaḥ |
body.translated_text: of accumulation itself — for without [change] at every moment, accumulation could not be consistent with the arising of something more nourished.
In the case of arising through a basis
(<s>āśraya</s>) — because of the impossibility of what is supported

body.text: | na hi tiṣṭhaty āśraye ca tadāśritasyānavasthānaṃ yujyate | yena tiṣṭhati ta ārūḍhānavasthānavad anyathā hy āśrayatvaṃ na saṃbhavet | vikārotpattau paripākotpattau ca
body.translated_text: [existing while the support does not persist] — for if the basis persists and the non-persistence of what is supported by it is untenable — in that [the supported persists] when [the basis] persists, like the non-persistence of one mounted on a vehicle — otherwise, being a basis would be impossible. In the case of arising through transformation and through ripening —
because of the impossibility of something that persists
[at the end].
Because of [the argument of] non-destruction at the beginning and transformation

body.text: | ma hi tathāsthitasyaiva rāgādibhir vikāraḥ saṃbhavati | na cāvasthāntareṣu paripāka ādāv avināśe saty ante vikārābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: — for transformation through desire and the like is not possible for something that remains just as it was. Nor is ripening in different stages possible if there is no destruction at the beginning, because of the absence of change at the end.
Likewise, in the case of arising by inferior and superior

body.text: tpattau kaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ yathā vikāraparipākotpattau | na hi tahtāsthiteṣv eva saṃskāreṣu karmavāsanā vṛttiṃ labhate yato durgatau vā syād utpattiḥ sugatau vā | krameṇa hi saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣāt vṛttilābho yujyate |
body.translated_text: [status], momentariness should be understood just as in the case of arising through transformation and ripening — for the <s>karmic</s> imprint does not gain operation in conditioned phenomena that remain just as they are, such that there would be arising in bad or good destinies. Rather, it is tenable that operation is gained through the gradual differentiation of the transformation of the continuum.
In the case of arising by luminous and non-luminous [status]
too, momentariness is tenable in the same way.
In the case of the luminous
— to begin with, because of the impossibility of something remaining as it was, since its operation depends on mind.
In the case of the non-luminous
too — because of the impossibility of change at the end without destruction at the beginning. In the case of arising through traveling to another place —
because of the absence of [actual] going

body.text: | na hi saṃskārāṇāṃ deśāntarasaṃkrāntilakṣaṇā gatir nāma kācit kriyā yujyate | sa hy utpannā vā saṃskāraṃ deśāntaraṃ gamayed anutpannā vā | yad utpannā tena gatikāle na kaṃcid gata iti sthitasyaiva gamanaṃ nopapadyate | athānutpannā tena asatyāṃ gatau gata iti na yujyate | sā ca kriyā yadi taddeśastha eva saṃskāre kāritraṃ karoti na yujyate | sthitasyānyadeśāprāpteḥ | athānyadeśasthe na yujyate | vinā kriyayānyadeśāprāpteḥ | na ca kriyā tatra vā anyatra vā deśe sthitā saṃskārād anyopalabhyate | tasmān nāsti saṃskārāṇāṃ deśāntarasaṃtatyutpādād anyā gatiḥ | tadabhāvāc ca siddhiṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ | deśāntaranirantarautpattilakṣaṇā gatir vibhavadbhiḥ kāraṇair veditavyā | asti cittavaśena yathā caṅkramaṇādyavasthāsu | asti pūrvakarmāvedhena yathāntarābhavaḥ | asty abhighātavaśena yathā kṣiptasyeṣoḥ | asti saṃbandhavaśena yathā yānanadīplavāruḍhānāṃ |
body.translated_text: — for no action called 'going,' characterized by the transfer of conditioned phenomena to another place, is tenable. For either an arisen [action] would cause the conditioned phenomenon to go to another place, or an un-arisen one would. If arisen — then since at the time of going it has not gone anywhere, the going of something that remains [where it is] is untenable. And if un-arisen — then since there is no going when [the action] does not exist, it is not tenable that 'it has gone.' And if that action produces its effect on the conditioned phenomenon while it remains in that very place — it is untenable, because what remains has not reached another place. And if [it acts] on [something] in another place — it is untenable, because without the action, [the phenomenon] has not reached another place. And no action is apprehended as existing in either that place or another place, separate from the conditioned phenomenon. Therefore, there is no 'going' of conditioned phenomena other than the arising of a continuum in another place. And because of the absence of that [actual going], momentariness is established. Going, characterized as the immediate arising in another place, should be understood through various causes: there is [going] through the power of mind, as in the states of walking meditation and the like; there is [going] through the momentum of past <s>karma</s>, as in the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>); there is [going] through the force of impact, as with a hurled arrow; and there is [going] through the force of connection, as with those mounted on vehicles, boats, and the like.

body.text: asti nodanavaśena yathā vāyupreritānāṃ tṛṇādīnāṃ | asti svabhāvavaśena yathā vāyos tiryaggamanam agner ūrdhvaṃ jvalanam apāṃ nimne syandanaṃ | asty anubhāvena yathā mantrāuṣadhānubhāvena | keṣāṃcid ayaskāntānubhāvenāyasāṃ | ṛddhyanubhāvena ṛddhimatāṃ | sabījābījabhāvenotpattau kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: There is [movement] by the force of impulsion, as in the case of grass and the like impelled by wind. There is [movement] by the force of [its own] nature, as in the case of wind's horizontal movement, fire's upward burning, and water's downward flowing. There is [movement] by the force of potency, as in the case of the potency of mantras and medicines; for some, by the potency of a magnet upon iron; by the potency of supernatural power, for those endowed with such power. Momentariness in arising, whether with or without seed, should be understood.
Because of the impossibility of remaining, and because of the impossibility of a final [moment having seed-nature] —

body.text: ca | na hi pratikṣaṇaṃ hetubhāvam antareṇa tathāsthitasyānyasmin kāle punar bījabhāvo yujyate | nirbījatvaṃ vā carame kṣaṇe | na ca śakyaṃ pūrvaṃ sabījatvaṃ carame kṣaṇe nirbījatvam abhyupagantuṃ | tadabhāve
body.translated_text: for without functioning as a cause at each moment, it is not reasonable for what remains as such to again become a seed at another time; nor is there seedlessness at the final moment. And it is not possible to accept that what was previously possessed of seed-nature becomes seedless at the final moment — in the absence of that,
because the final [moment] would be impossible.

body.text: | tathā hi caramatvam eva na saṃbhavati | pratibimbotpattau kṣaṇikatvaṃ
body.translated_text: For indeed, a final moment itself would be impossible. Momentariness in the arising of reflections should be understood
from following the mind —

body.text: veditavyaṃ | pratikṣaṇaṃ cittavaśena tadutpādāt | ekāntāt sādhitam ādhyātmikaṃ
body.translated_text: because at each moment they arise under the control of the mind. Thus, from a single [line of argument], it has been established that all internal
conditioned phenomena are momentary.

body.text: iti | bāhyasyedānīṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ tribhiḥ ślokaiḥ sādhayati |
body.translated_text: Now he establishes the momentariness of the external by three verses:

children.translated_text: The momentariness of the four great elements and the sixfold object is established:

children.text: śoṣavṛddheḥ prakṛtyā ca calatvād vṛddhihānitaḥ || AMsa_18.89 ||
children.translated_text: from drying and increase, from natural motility, from increase and decrease, // AMsa_18.89 //
from arising from those, from the fourfold transformation of earth,
and from the equality of color, smell, taste, and touch — likewise that. // AMsa_18.90 //
From dependence on fuel, from the perception of gradation,

children.text: cittānuvṛtteḥ pṛcchātaḥ kṣaṇikaṃ bāhyam apy ataḥ || AMsa_18.91 ||
children.translated_text: from following the mind, and from inquiry — therefore the external too is momentary. // AMsa_18.91 //

body.text: kiṃ punas tad bāhyaṃ | catvāri mahābhūtāni | ṣaḍvidhaś cārthaḥ | varṇagandharasasparśaśabdā dharmāyatanikaṃ ca rūpaṃ | ato
body.translated_text: What, then, is that external? The four great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>). And the sixfold object: color, smell, taste, touch, sound, and the form belonging to the <s>dharmāyatana</s>. Therefore,
'the momentariness of the elements and the sixfold object'
'is established.'
How is it established? First, for water,
'from drying and increase' —

body.text: | utsaras taḍāgādiṣv apāṃ krameṇa vṛddhiḥ | śoṣaś copalabhyate | tac cobhayam antareṇa pratikṣaṇaṃ pariṇāmaṃ na syāt paścād viśeṣakāraṇābhāvāt | vāyoḥ
body.translated_text: in springs, ponds, and the like, the gradual increase and drying up of water is perceived. And without transformation at each moment, that twofold [increase and decrease] would not occur, because subsequently there would be no special cause. For wind,
'from natural motility and from increase and decrease' —

body.text: ca | na hy avasthitasya calatvaṃ syāt tatsvabhāvād iti prasādhitam etat | na ca vṛddhihrāsau tathaivāvasthitvāt |
body.translated_text: for what is stationary could not have motility; since it is of that nature, this is established. And increase and decrease [would not occur] if it remained the same.
For earth, 'from arising from those, and from the fourfold transformation' —

body.text: | tac chabenāpaś ca gṛhyante vāyuś ca | adbhyo hi vāyusahitābhyaḥ pṛthivī saṃbhūtā vivartakāle | tasmāt tatphalatvāt sāpi kṣaṇikā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: by the word 'those,' water and wind are also included. For earth arose from water combined with wind at the time of cosmic formation (<s>vivartakāla</s>). Therefore, being the effect of those, it too should be understood as momentary.
And the fourfold
transformation

body.text: pṛthivyā upalabhyate | karmakṛtaḥ satvānāṃ karmaviśeṣāt | upakrtamakṛtaḥ prahādibhiḥ | bhūtakṛto 'gnyādibhiḥ | kālakṛtaḥ kālāntarapariṇāmataḥ | sa cāntareṇa pratikṣaṇaṃ anyotpattiṃ na yujyate vināśakāraṇābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: of earth is observed: produced by <s>karma</s>, due to the distinct <s>karma</s> of beings; produced by secondary causes, such as plowing and the like; produced by the elements, such as fire and the like; produced by time, from transformation over time. And without the arising of a different [state] at each moment, that [transformation] would be impossible, because of the absence of a cause of destruction.
For color, smell, taste, and touch —
because they share the same
cause
as earth and the like,
their momentariness should be understood in the same way. The momentariness of fire, moreover,
[is established] from its dependence on fuel.

body.text: na hi tejasy utpanne tejaḥsahotpannam indhanaṃ tathaivāvatiṣṭhate | na ca dagdhendhanaṃ tejaḥ sthātuṃ samarthaṃ | mā bhūd ante 'py anindhanasyāvasthānam iti | ślokabadhānurodhād varṇādīnāṃ pūrvam abhidhānaṃ paścāt tejasaḥ | śabdaḥ punar yo 'pi kālāntaram upalabhyate ghaṇṭhādīnāṃ tasyāpi kṣaṇikatvaṃ veditavyaṃ
body.translated_text: For when fire has arisen, the fuel that arose simultaneously with the fire does not remain as it was. And fire whose fuel has been consumed is not able to remain. Lest there be the objection that even at the end, fireless [fuel] could remain. Because of following the verse order, color and the like are mentioned first, fire afterward. Sound, moreover — even that which is perceived over a period of time, such as the sound of bells and the like — should be understood as momentary,
'from the perception of gradation' —

body.text: na hy asati kṣaṇikatve pratikṣaṇamandataratamopalabdhiḥ syāt | dharmāyatanikasyāpi rūpasya kṣaṇikatvaṃ prasiddham eva
body.translated_text: for without momentariness, the perception of gradually diminishing [sound] at each moment would not occur. The momentariness of form belonging to the <s>dharmāyatana</s> is also well-established,
'from following the mind,'
as previously stated. Therefore,
'the momentariness of the external too'
is established.
One may further ask:

body.text:
