khalv api sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ sidhyati kathaṃ kṛtvā |
idaṃ tāvad ayam akṣaṇikavādī praṣṭavyaḥ | kasmād bhavān anityatvam icchati na saṃskārārāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ necchatīti | yady evaṃ vadet pratikṣaṇam anyatvasyāgrahaṇād iti sa idaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ | prasiddhakṣaṇikabhāveṣv api pradīpādiṣu niścalāvasthāyāṃ tadagrahaṇād akṣaṇikatvaṃ kasmān neṣyate | yady evaṃ vadet pūrvavat paścād agrahaṇād iti | sa idaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ | saṃskārāṇām api kasmād evaṃ neṣyate | yady evaṃ vadet vilakṣaṇatvāt pradīpāditadanyasaṃskārāṇām iti | sa idaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ | dvidhaṃ hi vailakṣaṇyaṃ svabhāvavailakṣaṇyaṃ vṛttivailakṣaṇyaṃ ca | tad yadi tāvat svabhāvavailakṣaṇyam abhipretam ata eva dṛṣṭāntatvaṃ yujyate | na hi tatsvabhāva eva tasya dṛṣṭānto bhavati yathā pradīpaḥ pradīpasya gaur vā gor iti | atha vṛttavailakṣaṇyam ata eva dṛṣṭāntatvaṃ pradīpapradīpānāṃ prasiddhatvāt | kṣaṇikatvānuvṛtteḥ punaḥ sa idaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ | kaccid icchasi yāne tiṣṭhati yānāruḍho gacched iti | yadi no hīti vadet | sa idaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ | cakṣurādiṣu tiṣṭhatsu tad āśritaṃ vijñānaṃ prabandhena gacchatīti na yujyate | yady evaṃ vadet nanu ca dṛṣṭaṃ vartisaṃniśrite pradīpe prabandhena gacchati vartyā avathānam iti | sa idaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ | na dṛṣṭaṃ tatprabandhena vartyā pratikṣaṇaṃ vikārotpatter iti | yady evaṃ vadet sati kaṇikatve saṃskārāṇāṃ kasmāt pradīpād iva kṣaṇikatvaṃ na siddham iti | sa idaṃ vacanīyaḥ viparyāsavastutvāt | sadṛśasaṃtatiprabandhavṛttyā hi kṣaṇikatvam eṣāṃ na prajñāyate | yataḥ saty apy aparāparatve tad evedam iti viparyāso jāyate | itarathā hi anityanityaviparyāso na syāt tadabhāve saṃkleśo na syāt kutaḥ punar vyavadānam ity evaṃ paryanuyogato 'pi kṣaṇikatvaṃ sarvasaṃskārāṇāṃ prasiddhaṃ | pudgalanairātmyaprasādhanārthaṃ nairātmyavibhāge dvādaśa ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text:
how indeed is the momentariness of all conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāras</s>) established?
First, this proponent of non-momentariness should be asked: Why does your honor accept impermanence of <s>saṃskāras</s> but not their momentariness? If he answers: 'Because the difference [of each moment] is not apprehended at each moment' — he should be told this: Even in cases where momentariness is well-established, such as a lamp and the like, when it appears to remain still, since that [difference] is not apprehended, why is non-momentariness not accepted? If he answers: 'Because previously it was the same but later it is not apprehended [being the same]' — he should be told: Why is it not accepted likewise for [other] <s>saṃskāras</s>? If he answers: 'Because the <s>saṃskāras</s> other than lamps and the like are of a different character' — he should be told: The difference of character is twofold: difference of essential nature and difference of mode of operation. If, first, a difference of essential nature is intended — that is precisely why it serves as an example, for the example of a thing is never of the very same nature, just as a lamp cannot be an example for a lamp, nor a cow for a cow. If, however, a difference of mode of operation is intended — that is precisely why it serves as an example, since the [momentariness of] lamps among lamps is well-established; [the example works] because momentariness is what is being carried over. Furthermore, he should be asked: Do you accept that someone mounted on a vehicle that is standing still would move? If he says 'No indeed' — he should be told: Then it is unreasonable that consciousness, which depends on the sense-faculties such as the eye, should proceed in a continuum while those [sense-faculties] remain stationary. If he says: 'But is it not observed that in a lamp based on a wick, the [flame] proceeds in a continuum while the wick remains?' — he should be told: It is not observed so, for in the wick, a transformation arises at each moment. If he then says: 'If the <s>saṃskāras</s> are momentary, why is their momentariness not established like that of a lamp?' — he should be told: Because they are the object of error (<s>viparyāsa</s>). For because of the mode of operation through a continuum of a similar series, their momentariness is not discerned; since, even though there is succession, the error arises: 'This is that very same thing.' For otherwise, there would be no error of [grasping] the impermanent as permanent; in the absence of that, there would be no defilement; whence then would there be purification? Thus, through this line of inquiry too, the momentariness of all conditioned phenomena is established. For the purpose of establishing the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>), on the division of selflessness, twelve verses:

children.text: prajñaptyastitayā vācyaḥ pudgalo dravyato na tu |
children.translated_text: The person (<s>pudgala</s>) is to be spoken of as existing by way of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), but not in terms of substance (<s>dravya</s>);
because of non-apprehension, because of error, because of defilement, and because of a defiled cause. // AMsa_18.92 //
He is to be spoken of neither as identical with nor as different [from the aggregates]; because of two faults,
because of the consequence that the aggregates would be a self, and because of the consequence that it [the person] would be a substance. // AMsa_18.93 //

children.text: dravyasan yady avācyaś ca vacanīyaṃ prayojanaṃ |
children.translated_text: If it exists as a substance yet is inexpressible, the purpose [of asserting this] must be stated;
one who is inexpressible in terms of identity or difference is unreasonable and purposeless. // AMsa_18.94 //

children.text: lakṣaṇāl lokadṛṣṭāc ca śāstrato 'pi na yujyate |
children.translated_text: From the defining characteristic, from what is seen in the world, and from the scriptures too, it is unreasonable;

children.text: indhanāgnyor avācyatvam upalabdher dvayena hi || AMsa_18.95 ||
children.translated_text: the inexpressibility of fuel and fire, for it is apprehended through both. // AMsa_18.95 //

children.text: dvaye sati ca vijñānasaṃbhavāt pratyayo na saḥ |
children.translated_text: And when the two exist, because consciousness arises [from them], that [person] is not a condition;

children.text: nairarthakyād ato draṣṭā yāvan moktā na yujyate || AMsa_18.96 ||
children.translated_text: because of purposelessness — therefore, from the seer up to the liberated one, [a person] is unreasonable. // AMsa_18.96 //

children.text: svāmitve sati cānityam aniṣṭaṃ na pravartayet |
children.translated_text: And if it were a master, the impermanent and the unwanted would not occur;

children.text: tatkarmalakṣaṇaṃ sādhyaṃ saṃbodho bādhyate tridhā || AMsa_18.97 ||
children.translated_text: its defining characteristic of action would have to be proved; [the doctrine of] awakening is contradicted in three ways. // AMsa_18.97 //

children.text: darśanādau ca tadyatnaḥ svayaṃbhūr na trayād api |
children.translated_text: And in seeing and the like, the effort for that — [whether the person is] self-arisen — is not [possible] from the three either;
and the conditionality of that effort, and seeing and the like being effortless — // AMsa_18.98 //
because of non-agency, because of impermanence, because of a single occurrence — [hence] from non-occurrence,

children.text: darśanādiṣu yatnasya svayaṃbhūtvaṃ na yujyate || AMsa_18.99 ||
children.translated_text: the self-arising of effort in seeing and the like is unreasonable. // AMsa_18.99 //

children.text: tathā sthitasya naṣṭasya prāg abhāvād anityataḥ |
children.translated_text: Likewise, of one who remains thus, of one who has perished, because of prior non-existence, because of impermanence,

children.text: tṛtīyapakṣābhāvāc ca pratyayatvaṃ na yujyate || AMsa_18.100 ||
children.translated_text: and because of the absence of a third alternative — conditionality is unreasonable. // AMsa_18.100 //
All <s>dharmas</s> are without self; in the ultimate sense, [this is] emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>);

children.text: ātmopalambhe doṣaś ca deśito yata eva ca || AMsa_18.101 ||
children.translated_text: and the fault in apprehending a self has been taught — from which [teaching itself follows]. // AMsa_18.101 //
In defilement and purification, the states that are distinguished by cutting —
indeed, the difference of mode and continuum has been shown by [the word] 'person.' // AMsa_18.102 //
The view of self is not to be produced; the habituation is from beginningless time;

children.text: ayatnamokṣaḥ sarveṣāṃ na mokṣaḥ pudgalo 'sti vā || AMsa_18.103 ||
children.translated_text: effortless liberation for all, or no liberation — [results] if a person exists. // AMsa_18.103 //

body.text: pudgalaḥ kim astīti vaktavyo nāstīti vaktavyaḥ | āha |
body.translated_text: Is the person (<s>pudgala</s>) to be said to exist, or to be said not to exist? He says:

body.text: prajñaptyastitayā vācyaḥ pudgalo dravyato na tu |
body.translated_text: 'The person is to be spoken of as existing by way of designation, but not in terms of substance.'

body.text: yataś ca prajñaptito 'stīti vaktavyo dravyato nāstīti vaktavyaḥ | evam anekāṃśavādaparigrahe naivāstitve doṣāvakāśo na nāstitve | sa punar dravyato nāstīti kathaṃ veditavyaḥ | nopalambhāt | na hi sa dravyata upalabhyate rūpādivat upalabdhir hi nāma buddhyā pratipattiḥ | na ca pudgalaṃ buddhyā na pratipadyante pudgalavādinaḥ | uktaṃ ca bhagavatā | dṛṣṭa eva dharme ātmānam nupalabhate prajñāpayatīti kathaṃ nopalabdhā bhavati | na sa evam upalabhyamāno dravyata upalabdho bhavati | kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | viparyāsāt tathā hy anātmany ātmeti viparyāsa ukto bhagavatā | tasmād ya evaṃ pudgalagrāho viparyāsaḥ saḥ | katham idaṃ gamyate | saṃkleśāt | satkāyadṛṣṭikleśalakṣaṇo hy eṣa saṃkleśo yad uta ahaṃ mameti | na ca viparyāsaḥ saṃkleśo bhavitum arahati | na caiṣa saṃkleśa iti kathaṃ veditavyaṃ | kliṣṭahetutaḥ | tathā hi tadhetukāḥ kliṣṭā
body.translated_text: Since it is to be said to exist designationally, but to be said not to exist substantially — thus, in the adoption of the multi-faceted position, there is no opening for fault either in existence or in non-existence. How, then, should its non-existence as a substance be understood? Because of non-apprehension. For it is not apprehended as a substance, like form and the like — for apprehension means cognitive ascertainment. And the proponents of the person (<s>pudgalavādins</s>) do not fail to cognize the person. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has also stated: 'In this very life, one does not apprehend the self but designates it' — how then does non-apprehension occur? One who is apprehended in this way is not apprehended as a substance. For what reason? Because of error (<s>viparyāsa</s>). For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has stated the error: 'Self in what is not self.' Therefore, such grasping of a person is an error. How is this known? Because of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>). For this defilement, characterized by the affliction of the view of a personal aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) — namely, 'I' and 'mine' — [arises from that error]. And an error cannot not be a defilement. And how should one understand that this is a defilement? Because of a defiled cause (<s>kliṣṭahetu</s>). For defiled [states] such as desire (<s>rāga</s>) and the like arise, caused by that.

body.text: yatra punar vastuni rūpādisaṃjñake prajñaptiḥ pudgala iti tasmāt kim ekatvena pudgalo vaktavya āhosvid anyatvena | āha |
body.translated_text: Regarding that entity designated by form and the like on the basis of which the designation 'person' is made — is the person to be spoken of as identical with or as different from that? He says:
'He is to be spoken of as neither identical with nor different [from the aggregates].'
For what reason? Because of two faults. What are the two faults?
'Because of the consequence that the aggregates would be a self, and because of the consequence that it would be a substance.'

body.text: ekatve hi skandhānām ātmatvaṃ prasajyate pudgalasya ca dravyasatvaṃ | athānyatve pudgalsya dravyasatyaṃ | evaṃ hi pudgalsya prajñaptito 'stitvād avaktavyatvaṃ yuktaḥ | tenāvyākṛtavastusiddhaḥ |
body.translated_text: For in the case of identity, it would follow that the aggregates are a self, and that the person is a substantial entity. In the case of difference, [it would follow that] the person is a substantial reality. Thus, because the person exists only designationally, its inexpressibility is reasonable. Thereby, the inexpressible entity is established.

body.text: ye punaḥ śāstuḥ śāsanam atikramya pudgalsya dravyato 'stitvam icchanti ta idaṃ syur vacanīyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Those, however, who transgress the teaching of the Teacher and wish to accept the person as existing substantially — they should be told this:

body.text: dravyasan yady avācyaś ca vacanīyaṃ prayojanaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'If it exists as a substance yet is inexpressible, the purpose [of asserting this] must be stated.'
For what reason?
'One who is inexpressible in terms of identity or difference is unreasonable and purposeless.'

body.text: atha dṛṣṭāntamātrāt pudgalasyāvaktavyatvam iccheyuḥ | yathāgnir andhanān nānyo nānyo vaktavya iti | ta idaṃ syur vacanīyāḥ |
body.translated_text: If they wish to accept the inexpressibility of the person merely from an analogy — saying 'Just as fire is to be said to be neither identical with nor different from fuel' — they should be told this:

body.text:
lakṣaṇāl lokadṛṣṭāc ca śāstrato 'pi na yujyate |
indhanāgnyor avācyatvam upalabdher dvayena hi |
body.translated_text:
'From the defining characteristic, from what is seen in the world, and from the scriptures too, it is unreasonable;
the inexpressibility of fuel and fire, for it is apprehended through both.'

body.text: ekatvenānyatvena ca agnir hi nāma tejodhātur indhanaṃ śeṣāṇi bhūtāni | teṣāṃ ca bhinnaṃ lakṣaṇam ity anya evāgnir indhanāt | loke ca vināpy agninā dṛṣṭam indhanaṃ kāṣṭād vināpi cendhanenāgnir iti siddham anyatvaṃ | śāstre ca bhagavatā na kvacid agnīndhanayor avācyatvam uktam ity ayuktam etat | vinā punar indhanenāgnir astīti katham idaṃ vijñāyate | upalabdhes tathā hi vāyunā vikṣiptaṃ dūram api jvalat paraiti | athāpi syād vāyus tatrendhanam iti ata evāgnīndhanayor anyatvam it siddhiḥ | kitaḥ | dvayena hi upalabdher iti prakṛtaṃ | dvayaṃ hi tatropalabhyate arcir vāyuś cendhanatvena | asty eva pudgalo ya eṣa draṣṭā yāvad vijñāntā kartā bhoktā jñātā moktā
body.translated_text: As for [the refutation through] unity and otherness: fire is, by name, the heat-element; fuel is the remaining elements. Their characteristics are distinct, so fire is indeed other than fuel. And in the world, fuel is seen without fire, and fire without fuel (wood) — thus otherness is established. And in the treatise, the Bhagavān has never stated the inexpressibility of fire and fuel — so this [position of inexpressibility] is unjustified. But how is it known that fire exists without fuel? From observation — for indeed, blown by wind, it goes far even while burning. And if one says 'the wind there is the fuel' — precisely this establishes the otherness of fire and fuel. From what? From dual observation — for the subject is established. For two things are observed there: the flame, and the wind as fuel. [Regarding the person:] 'There exists a person who is this seer, up to knower, doer, experiencer, cognizer, and liberator.'

body.text: ca | na sa draṣṭā yujyate | nāpi yāvan moktā | sa hi darśanādisaṃjñakānāṃ vijñānānāṃ pratyayabhāvena vā kartā bhavet svāmitvena vā |
body.translated_text: He cannot properly be the seer, nor up to the liberator. For he would be the doer of those cognitions designated as seeing and so forth, either as their condition or as their owner.

body.text:
tatra tāvat |
dvayaṃ pratītya vijñānasaṃbhavāt pratyayo na saḥ |
body.translated_text: With respect to the first: 'Since cognition arises dependent on a pair [of conditions], he is not the condition.'

body.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ | nairarthakyāt | na hi tatra kiṃcit sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ |
body.translated_text: For what reason? Because of purposelessness — for no efficacy is seen there.

body.text: svāmitve sati cānityam aniṣṭaṃ na pravartayet |
body.translated_text: 'And if he were the owner, he would not set in motion what is impermanent and undesired.'

body.text: sa hi vijñānapravṛttau svāmībhavann aniṣṭaṃ vijñānam anityaṃ na pravartayet | aniṣṭaṃ ca | naiva tasmād ubhayathāpy asaṃbhāvāt | asau draṣṭā yāvan moktā na yujyate |
body.translated_text: For if he were the owner over the arising of cognition, he would not set in motion impermanent cognition, nor undesired [cognition]. Therefore, from the impossibility in both ways, he cannot properly be the seer, up to the liberator.
Moreover, if the person exists substantially,
'its action-characteristic must be established.'

body.text: yadi dravyato 'sti tasya karmāpy upalabhyate | yathā cakṣurādīnāṃ darśanādilakṣaṇaṃ ca rūpaprasādādi | na caivaṃ pudgalasya | tasmān na so 'sti dravyataḥ | tasmiṃś ca dravyata iṣyamāṇe buddhasya bhagavataḥ
body.translated_text: If it exists substantially, its action too must be observable — just as the characteristic of seeing and so forth of the eye and so on, and form and clarity and so forth. But this is not the case for the person. Therefore he does not exist substantially. And if he is accepted as existing substantially, then the <s>Buddha Bhagavān's</s>
'awakening is invalidated in three ways.'

body.text: gambhīrābhisaṃbodhaḥ | asādhāraṇābhisaṃbodhaḥ | lokottarābhisaṃbodhaḥ | ni hi pudgalābhisaṃbodhe kiṃcid gambhīram abhisaṃbuddhaṃ bhavati | na tīrthyāsādhāraṇāṃ | na lokānucitaṃ | tathā hy eṣa grāhaḥ sarvalokagamyaḥ | tīrthyābhiniviṣṭaḥ | dīrghasaṃsārocitaś ca | api khalu pudgalo draṣṭā bhavan yāvad vijñātā darśanādiṣu saprayatno vā bhaven niṣpratyatno vā |
body.translated_text: The profound awakening, the uncommon awakening, and the supramundane awakening. For in the awakening to a person, nothing profound has been realized; it is not uncommon to the <s>tīrthikas</s>; and it is not unprecedented for the world. For this grasping is accessible to all worldly beings, is held by <s>tīrthikas</s>, and is habituated through long <s>saṃsāra</s>. Moreover, if the person were the seer, up to the knower, in seeing and so forth — would he have effort or be without effort?

body.text: saprayatnasya vā punar asau prayatnaḥ svayaṃbhūr vā bhaved ākasmikaḥ | tatpratyayo
body.translated_text: If with effort, would that effort be self-arisen or accidental? That being his condition —

body.text: darśanādau ca tadyatnaḥ svayaṃbhūr na trayād api |
body.translated_text: 'And the effort of that [person] in seeing and so forth is not self-arisen, [as will be shown] from three [faults].'
And from those very three faults about to be stated,
'its being the condition of that effort'

body.text: neti vartate | niṣprayatnasya vā punaḥ sataḥ siddhaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: — [the reading] continues as 'is not.' Or if [the person exists] without effort, it is established that
'seeing and so forth are effortless' —

body.text: ity asati vyāpare pudgalasya darśanādau katham asau draṣṭā bhavati |
body.translated_text: and if the person has no activity in seeing and so forth, how can he be the seer?

body.text: yāvad vijñātā doṣatrayād ity uktaṃ katamasmād doṣatrayāt |
body.translated_text: 'Up to the knower — from the three faults.' What are the three faults?

children.translated_text: 'From non-agency, from impermanence, and from non-arising [for one who has arisen] once' —
the self-arisen nature of effort in seeing and so forth is not justified.

body.text: yadi darśanādiṣu prayatna ākasmiko yato darśanādīni | na tarhi teṣāṃ pudglaḥ karteti katham asau draṣṭā bhavati yāvad vijñātā sati vākasmikatve nirapekṣatvāt na kadācit prayatno na syād anityo na syāt | nitye ca prayatne darśnādīnāṃyugapac ca nityaṃ ca pravṛrtiḥ syād iti doṣaḥ | tasmān na yujyate darśnādiṣu prayatnasya svayaṃbhūtvaṃ |
body.translated_text: If the effort in seeing and so forth were accidental — from which seeing and so forth [arise] — then the person would not be their agent, so how could he be the seer, up to the knower? And if there were accidentality, because of independence, the effort would never not exist; it would never be impermanent. And with permanent effort, seeing and so forth would arise simultaneously and always — this is the fault. Therefore, the self-arisen nature of effort in seeing and so forth is not justified.

body.text:
tathā sthitasya naṣṭasya prāg abhāvād anityataḥ |
tṛtīyapakṣābhāvāc ca pratyayatvaṃ na yujyate |
body.translated_text: 'Of one established, or of one perished, from prior non-existence, from impermanence, and from the absence of a third alternative — being a condition is not justified.'

body.text: atha pudgalaprayatnaḥ prayatnaḥ syāt | tasya tathā sthitasya prayatnatvaṃ na yujyate | prāg abhāvāt | sati hi tatprayatnatve na kadācit pudgalo nāstīti | kim arthaṃ prāk prayatno na syād yadā notpannaḥ | vinaṣṭasyāpi pratyayatvaṃ na yujyate pudgalasyānityatvaprasaṅgāt | tṛtīyaś ca kaścitpakṣo nāsti yan na sthito na vinaṣṭaḥ syād iti | tatpratyayo 'pi prayatno na yujyate | evaṃ tāvad yuktima āśritya dravyataḥ pudgalo nopalabhyate |
body.translated_text: Now, if the person's effort were [accepted as] his condition — [even then,] its being the condition of one established is not justified, because of prior non-existence. For if it were his condition, the person would never not exist — so why would the effort not exist previously, when [the person] is unborn? Nor is being a condition of one perished justified, because of the consequence of the person's impermanence. And there is no third alternative — that he would neither be established nor perished. So effort as his condition is not justified either. Thus, relying on reasoning, the person is not found substantially.

children.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self; ultimately, emptiness;

children.text: ātmopalambhe doṣaś ca deśito yata eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and the fault in apprehending a self has been taught — for these very reasons.'

body.text: dharmoddāneṣu hi bhagavatā sarve dharmā anātmāna iti deśitaṃ paramārthaśūnyatāyām asti karmāsti vipākaḥ kārakas tu nopalabhyate ya imaṃś ca skhandān nikṣipati anyāṃś ca skhandān pratisaṃdadhāti | anyatra dharmasaṃketād iti deśitaṃ | pañcakeṣu pañcādīnavā ātmopalambha iti dśitā | ātmadṛṣṭir bhavati jīvadṛṣṭiḥ nirviśeṣo bhavati tīrthikaiḥ | unmārgapratipannao bhavati | śūnyatāyām asya cittaṃ na praskandati na prasīdati na saṃtiṣṭhate nādhimucyate | āryadharmā asya na vyvadāyante | evam āgamato 'pi na yujyate | pudgalo 'pi hi bhagavatā tatra tatra deśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught in the <s>Dharmottāra</s>: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without self.' In the ultimate emptiness [scripture]: 'There is action, there is fruition, but no agent is found who casts off these aggregates and takes up other aggregates — except through the convention of <s>dharmas</s>.' In the groups of five, five disadvantages of apprehending a self are taught: 'The view of self arises; the view of a living being arises; one becomes undifferentiated from <s>tīrthikas</s>; one has entered a wrong path; one's mind does not leap forward, is not clear, does not settle, and does not have conviction regarding emptiness; the noble <s>dharmas</s> do not become pure for him.' Thus, from scripture too, it is not justified. But the person has been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> here and there —

body.text: parijñātāvī bhārahāraḥ śraddhānusāryādipudgalavyavasthānata ity asati dravyato 'stitve kasmād deśitaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The one who fully knows,' 'the burden-bearer,' and the establishment of persons such as 'the faith-follower' and so forth — if he does not exist substantially, why was he taught?

children.translated_text: 'In defilement and purification, which differ by state and by discontinuity,
the distinction of occurrence and continuity is shown through the [designation of] person.'

body.text: avasthābhinne hi saṃkleśavyavadāne chedabhinne ca | pudgalaprajñaptim antareṇa tadvṛttibhedaḥ saṃtānabhedaś ca deśayituṃ na śakyaḥ | parijñāsūtre parijñeyā dharmāḥ saṃkleśaḥ parijñā vyavadānaṃ | bhārahārasūtre | bhāro bhārādānaṃ ca saṃkleśaḥ | bhāranikṣepaṇaṃ vyavadānaṃ | tayor vṛttibhedaḥ saṃtānabhedaś cāntareṇa parijñātāvībhārahārapudgalaprajñaptiṃ na śakyeta deśayituṃ | bodhipakṣāś ca dharmā bahudhāvasthāḥ prayogadarśanabhāvanāniṣṭhāmārgaviśeṣabhedataḥ | teṣāṃ vṛttibhedaḥ saṃtānabhedaś cāntareṇa śraddhānusāryādipudgalaprajñaptiṃ na śakyeta deśayituṃ | yenāsati dravyato 'stitve pudgalo deśita ity ayam atra nayo veditavyaḥ | itarathā hi pudgaladeśanā niṣprayojanā prāpnoti |
body.translated_text: For in defilement and purification, which differ by state and by discontinuity, without the designation of a person, the distinction of their occurrence and the distinction of continuum cannot be taught. In the sūtra on full knowledge: the <s>dharmas</s> to be fully known are defilement; full knowledge is purification. In the burden-bearer sūtra: the burden and the taking up of the burden are defilement; the laying down of the burden is purification. The distinction of their occurrence and the distinction of continuum cannot be taught without the designation of the person as 'the one who fully knows' and 'the burden-bearer.' And the <s>dharmas</s> that are wings of awakening are of many states — from the distinctions of the paths of application, seeing, cultivation, and completion. The distinction of their occurrence and the distinction of continuum cannot be taught without the designation of persons such as 'the faith-follower' and so forth. This is the method to be understood here — the reason why the person is taught even though he does not exist substantially. For otherwise, the teaching of a person would be purposeless.

body.text: na hi tāvad asāv ātmadṛṣṭyutpādanārthaṃ yujyate yasmāt
body.translated_text: For it cannot be justified that [the person was taught] for the purpose of producing the view of self, because

body.text: ātmadṛṣṭir anutpādyā pūrvam evotpannatvāt | nāpi tadabhyāsārthaṃ yasmād ātmadṛṣṭer abhyāso 'nādikālikaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'the view of self is not to be produced, since it has already arisen previously.' Nor for the purpose of habituating it, because the habituation of the view of self is beginningless.

body.text: yadi cātmadarśanena mokṣa ity asau deśyeta | evaṃ sati syāt
body.translated_text: And if it were taught that liberation comes through the view of self, then

body.text: ayatnamokṣaḥ sarveṣāṃ tathā hi sarveṣāṃ na dṛṣṭasatyānām ātmadarśanaṃ vidyate | naiva vā mokṣo 'stīti
body.translated_text: 'liberation without effort [would follow] for all' — for all who have not seen the truths possess the view of self. Or [it would follow that] there is no liberation at all,

body.text:
prāpnoti | na hi pūrvam ātmānam anātmato gṛhītvā satyābhisamayakāle kaścid ātmato gṛhṇāti |
yathā duḥkhaṃ duḥkhataḥ pūrvam agṛhītvā paścād gṛhṇātīti yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścād api mokṣo na syāt | sati cātmany avaśyam ahaṃkāramamakārābhyām ātmatṛṣṇayā cānyaiś ca tannidānaiḥ | kleśair bhavitavyam iti ato 'pi mokṣo na syāt | na vā pudgalo 'stīti abhyupagantavyaṃ | tasmin hi sati niyatam ete doṣāḥ prasajyante |
body.translated_text: for no one, having previously grasped the self as non-self, grasps it as self at the time of realization of the truths. Just as one does not first grasp suffering as suffering and then later grasp it [differently] — so liberation would not exist later either, just as before. And if there were a self, there would necessarily be the conceit 'I' and 'mine,' craving for self, and other afflictions having that as their basis — therefore too, there would be no liberation. Or else it must be admitted that the person does not exist — for if he did, these faults would necessarily follow.

children.text: evam ebhir guṇair nityaṃ bodhisatvāḥ samanvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, endowed always with these qualities, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>

children.text: ātmārthaṃ ca na riñcanti parārthaṃ sādhayanti ca || AMsa_18.104 ||
children.translated_text: do not abandon their own purpose and accomplish the purpose of others. // AMsa_18.104 //

body.translated_text: The function of the qualities beginning with moral shame and fortitude is stated in summary.
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the eighteenth chapter on the wings of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) is complete.

CHAPTER XIX
The nineteenth chapter.
On the division of wonders (<s>āścarya</s>), three verses:

children.translated_text: The abandonment of one's own body, and of prosperity in [its fullest] extent;

children.text: durbaleṣu kṣamā kāye jīvite nirapekṣiṇaḥ || AMsa_19.1 ||
children.translated_text: patience toward the weak, without regard for body or life; // AMsa_19.1 //

children.text: vīryārambho hy anāsvādo dhyāneṣu sukha eva ca |
children.translated_text: the undertaking of vigor without relishing, and happiness indeed in meditations (<s>dhyāna</s>);

children.text: niṣkalpanā ca prajñāyām āścaryaṃ dhīmatāṃ gataṃ || AMsa_19.2 ||
children.translated_text: and non-conceptualization in wisdom — these are accepted as the wonder of the wise. // AMsa_19.2 //
Birth in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, obtaining prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>),

children.text: abhiṣekasya ca prāptir bodheś cāścaryam iṣyate || AMsa_19.3 ||
children.translated_text: attaining consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), and awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — these are accepted as wonders. // AMsa_19.3 //
practice
is stated, beginning with the six perfections. For through generosity,
the abandonment of one's own body
is a wonder; through the moral restraint of discipline, the abandonment of noble
prosperity

children.text: tyāgaḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | tṛtīyena ślokena phalā
children.translated_text: [is a wonder]. The rest has been explained. By the third verse, the wonder of
fruit

children.text: uktaṃ catvāri bodhisatvaphalāny ārabhya prathamāyām aṣṭabhyāṃ daśabhyāṃ trīṇi śaikṣāṇi phalāni buddhabhūmau caturtham aśaikṣam atra phalaṃ | anāścaryavibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: is stated, beginning with the four fruits of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: on the first, the eighth, and the tenth [stages] are the three trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) fruits; on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage is the fourth, the beyond-training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) fruit. On the division of non-wonder, a verse:

body.translated_text: By these two verses, the wonder of

children.text: vairāgyaṃ karuṇāṃ caitya bhāvanāṃ paramām api |
children.translated_text: Dispassion, compassion, and supreme cultivation,

children.text: tathaiva samacittatvaṃ nāścaryaṃ tāsu yuktatā || AMsa_19.4 ||
children.translated_text: and likewise equal-mindedness — engagement in those [perfections] is no wonder. // AMsa_19.4 //
'In those'
means in the perfections.
'Dispassion' —
relying on [this], the engagement in generosity
is no wonder.
'Compassion' —
relying on [this], [the engagement] in morality and patience [is no wonder].
'Supreme cultivation' —
relying on [this], on the eighth stage, the engagement of vigor and the rest without conceptual construction and effort
is no wonder.
Relying on self-other
equal-mindedness,
the engagement in all the perfections
is no wonder —

children.text: artha iva parārthe khedābhāvāt | samacittatāyāṃ trayaḥ ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: because of the absence of weariness in the purpose of others, as in one's own purpose. On equal-mindedness, three verses:
The love of beings toward themselves, their spouses, children, friends, and relatives

children.text: satvānāṃ pragataḥ sneho yathā satveṣu dhīmatāṃ || AMsa_19.5 ||
children.translated_text: does not reach the extent of the love of the wise toward [all] beings. // AMsa_19.5 //
Impartiality toward supplicants; never breaking morality;

children.text: kṣāntiḥ sarvatra satvārthaṃ sarvārthaṃ vīryārambho mahān api || AMsa_19.6 ||
children.translated_text: patience everywhere; great undertaking of vigor for the purpose of all beings; // AMsa_19.6 //

children.text: dhyānaṃ ca kuśalaṃ nityaṃ prajñā caivāvikalpikā |
children.translated_text: and meditation that is always wholesome, and wisdom that is non-conceptual —

children.text: vijñeyā bodhisatvānāṃ tāsv eva samacittatā || AMsa_19.7 ||
children.translated_text: these should be known as the equal-mindedness of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in those very [perfections]. // AMsa_19.7 //

body.text: ekaḥ ślokaḥ satveṣu samacittatāyāṃ | dvau pāramitāsu |

children.translated_text: For
the love of beings toward self
and the rest

children.text: samatayā anugato na cātyantaṃ | tathā hi
children.translated_text: does not follow with equality, nor to the utmost degree. For indeed,
themselves

children.text: api kadācin mārayanti | bodhisatānāṃ tu sarva
children.translated_text: too they sometimes kill. But <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [have love] toward all
beings

children.text: samatayā atyantaṃ ca pāramitāsu punar dāne samacittatvam
children.translated_text: with equality and to the utmost degree. In the perfections, equal-mindedness in generosity is
from impartiality toward supplicants.
In morality —
never, even of the slightest [precept],
breaking [it].
'Patience everywhere'
means non-discrimination among beings. In vigor —
from undertaking vigor for the purpose of beings,

children.text: svaparārthaṃ samaṃ prayogāt sarvakuśalārthaṃ ca | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | upakāritvavibhāge ṣoḍaśa ślokāḥ |
children.translated_text: from equal engagement for one's own and others' purposes, and for the purpose of all wholesome [qualities]. The rest has been explained. On the division of beneficence (<s>upakāritva</s>), sixteen verses:

body.translated_text: One verse is on equal-mindedness toward beings; two are on [equal-mindedness] in the perfections.

children.text: sthāpanā bhājanatve ca śīleṣv eva ca ropaṇaṃ |
children.translated_text: Establishing [beings] in receptivity, and planting [them] precisely in moral disciplines;
tolerating harm, and engaging in activity for [their] purpose; // AMsa_19.8 //
attracting [them] to this teaching, and cutting their doubts —

children.text: satveṣu upakāritvaṃ dhīmatām etad iṣyate || AMsa_19.9 ||
children.translated_text: this is the beneficence of the wise toward beings. // AMsa_19.9 //

body.text: ābhyāṃ ślokābhyāṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhir yathopakāritvaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ tatparidīpitaṃ | dānena hi satvānāṃ
body.translated_text: By these two verses, the beneficence of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> through the six perfections is illuminated. For through generosity, they
establish beings in receptivity
to wholesome activity.
Through meditation, they
attract [beings]

body.text: prabhāvaviśeṣayogāt | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | śeṣaiḥ ślokaiḥ mātrādisādharmyeṇo
body.translated_text: because of the endowment with extraordinary power. The rest is self-explanatory. By the remaining verses, the quality of being a benefactor is shown through the analogy of a mother and the like.

children.translated_text: Those who, with a benevolent intention, always sustain beings,

children.text: janayanty āryabhūmau ca kuśalair vardhayanti ca || AMsa_19.10 ||
children.translated_text: and give them birth on the noble stage, and increase them with wholesome [qualities] — // AMsa_19.10 //
and protect them from wrongdoing, and train them in learning —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like mothers to beings. // AMsa_19.11 //
to beings.'

children.text: | mātā hi putrasya pañcavidham upakāraṃ karoti | garbheṇa
children.translated_text: A mother performs fivefold benefit for her child: she carries [the child] in the womb
gives birth
; suckles, nourishes, and
raises [the child]
protects from danger
; and teaches speech. By analogy with those, these
five
<s>Bodhisattva</s>
actions
should be understood. The noble stage should be understood as the noble <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: Those who are like mothers of beings are 'like mothers

children.translated_text: Because of always implanting faith in all beings,
and because of engaging [them] in the training of higher moral discipline and the like, and in liberation — // AMsa_19.12 //
and because of supplicating the <s>Buddhas</s> on their behalf, and because of removing their obscurations —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like fathers to beings. // AMsa_19.13 //
A father

children.text: hi putrāṇāṃ pañcavidham upakāraṃ karoti | bījaṃ teṣām
children.translated_text: performs fivefold benefit for his children: he
plants the seed
for them;
trains [them in] a craft
engages [them]

children.text: | anṛṇaṃ karoti yathā na paitṛkam ṛṇaṃ dāpyate | tatsādharmyeṇa bodhisatvānām etāni pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni |
children.translated_text: with suitable spouses; and frees them from debt, so that they are not made to pay the paternal debt. By analogy with those, these five actions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood.
For faith
is the seed for beings' attainment of a noble
bodily
existence. The trainings are the craft.
Liberation
is the spouse — the experience of the joy and happiness of liberation. The <s>Buddhas</s> are the spiritual friends. The obscurations are the site of [debt].

children.text: anarhadeśanāṃ ye ca satvānāṃ gūhayanti hi |
children.translated_text: Those who conceal from beings the teachings they are unfit [to receive],

children.text: śikṣāvipattiṃ nindanti śaṃsanty eva ca saṃpadam || AMsa_19.14 ||
children.translated_text: and who censure failure in the training and praise its success — // AMsa_19.14 //

children.text: avavādaṃ ca yacchanti mārān āvedayanti hi |
children.translated_text: and who give instruction and disclose the <s>Māras</s> —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like relatives to beings. // AMsa_19.15 //

body.text: bandhavo hi bandhūnāṃ pañcavidham upakāraṃ kurvanti | guhyaṃ
body.translated_text: For relatives perform fivefold benefit for their kin: they conceal
secrets
; they censure bad conduct; they
praise
[good conduct]; they come to their aid
in tasks
; and they prevent [them] from places of misfortune. By analogy with those, these
five actions
of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood.

body.text: anarthebhyo gambhīradharmadeśanāvinigūhanāt śikṣāvipattisaṃpattyor yathākramaṃ nindanāt praśaṃsanāc ca | adhigamāyāvavādanāt mārakarmavedanāc ca |
body.translated_text: [Protecting] from harm by concealing the teaching of profound <s>dharmas</s>; and from censuring failure and praising success in training, respectively; and from giving instruction for the sake of realization; and from disclosing the works of <s>Māra</s>.

children.translated_text: Those who, with unwearied minds regarding defilement and purification,

children.text: yacchanti laukikīṃ kṛtsnāṃ saṃpadaṃ cātilaukikīm || AMsa_19.16 ||
children.translated_text: give the entire worldly prosperity and the supramundane as well — // AMsa_19.16 //

children.text: sukhe hite cābhinnā akheditvād abhinnā ye sadā sukhahitaiṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: and who are undivided regarding happiness and benefit, unwearied, always seeking happiness and benefit —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like friends to beings. // AMsa_19.17 //

body.text: tad dhi mitraṃ yan mitrasya hite ca sukhe cāparyastaṃ | sukhaṃ copasaṃharati hitaṃ cābhidyaṃ ca bhavati | hitasukhaiṣi ca nityaṃ | tathā bodhisatvāḥ satvānāṃ

children.translated_text: like friends to beings through these five actions.

children.text: veditavyāḥ | laukikī hi saṃpat sikhaṃ | tayā sukhānubhavāt | lokottarā hitaṃ kleśavyādhipratipakṣatvāt |
children.translated_text: For worldly prosperity is happiness — because of the experience of happiness through it. The supramundane is benefit — because of being the antidote to the disease of defilements.

body.translated_text: For a friend is one who is not perverse regarding both the benefit and the happiness of his friend — who brings happiness, who acts for benefit, who is trustworthy, and who always seeks benefit and happiness. Likewise, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as

children.translated_text: Those who are always striving in the maturation of beings,
who teach the correct way of progress, who are patient with transgressions — // AMsa_19.18 //
who give the twofold prosperity and are skilled in the means thereof —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like servants to beings. // AMsa_19.19 //
A servant
indeed
conducts himself properly through five actions:

children.text: samyag vartate | utthānasaṃpanno bhavati kṛtyeṣu | avisaṃvādako bhavati | kṣamo bhavati | paribhāṣaṇatāḍanādīnāṃ | nipuṇe bhavati sarvakāryakaraṇāt | vicakṣaṇaś ca bhavati upāyajñaḥ | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni pañca karmāṇi bodhisatvānāṃ veditavyāni |
children.translated_text: he is diligent in rising for tasks; he is reliable; he is patient with scoldings, beatings, and the like; he is skillful in accomplishing all tasks; and he is discerning — knowing the means. By analogy with those, these five actions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood.
The twofold prosperity
should be understood as worldly and supramundane.

children.text: anutpattikadharmeṣu kṣāntiṃ prāptāś ca ye matāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are considered to have attained the patience regarding the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>),
who teach all vehicles, who engage [disciples] in the accomplished practice — // AMsa_19.20 //
who are pleasant-faced, and who are without expectation of reciprocation or of ripening —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like teachers to beings. // AMsa_19.21 //

body.text: pañcavidhena karmaṇā śiṣyāṇām upakārī bhavati | svayaṃ suśikṣito bhavati | sarvaṃ śikṣayati | kṣipraṃ śikṣayati |

children.translated_text: he is pleasant-faced

children.text: bhavati suratajātīyaḥ | nirāmiṣacittaś ca bhavati | tatsādharmyeṇaitāni bodhisatvānāṃ pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni |
children.translated_text: — of a joyful disposition; and he has a selfless mind. By analogy with those, these five actions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood.

body.translated_text: A [teacher] benefits his students through fivefold action: he is himself well-trained; he teaches everything; he teaches quickly;

children.translated_text: Those who are striving for the welfare of beings, who fulfill the accumulations,

children.text: saṃbhṛtān mocayanty āśu vipakṣaṃ hāpayanti ca || AMsa_19.22 ||
children.translated_text: who quickly liberate those who have gathered [the accumulations], who cause the abandonment of opponents — // AMsa_19.22 //
and who connect [beings] with the various ornaments of worldly prosperity —
through these five actions, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are like preceptors (<s>upādhyāya</s>) to beings. // AMsa_19.23 //

body.text:
upādhyāyaḥ pañcavidhena karmaṇā sārdhaṃ vihāriṇām upakārī bhavati | pravrājayati upasaṃpādayati |
anuśāsti doṣaparivarjane | āmiṣeṇa saṃgṛhṇāti dharmeṇa ca tatsādharmyeṇaitāni bodhisatvānāṃ pañca karmāṇi veditavyāni | pratikāravibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text:
A preceptor benefits his co-dwellers through fivefold action: he grants ordination; he grants full ordination;
he instructs in the avoidance of faults; he sustains them with material things and with the <s>Dharma</s>. By analogy with those, these five actions of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood. On the division of reciprocation, two verses:

children.text: asaktyā caiva bhogeṣu śīlasya ca na khaṇḍanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By non-attachment to enjoyments, and by not violating moral discipline,

children.text: kṛtajñatānuyogāc ca pratipattau ca yogataḥ || AMsa_19.24 ||
children.translated_text: and by the pursuit of gratitude, and by engagement in practice — // AMsa_19.24 //

children.text: ṣaṭsu pāramitāsv eva vartamānā hi dehinaḥ |
children.translated_text: beings who are engaged in the six <s>pāramitās</s> themselves
become reciprocators to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> accordingly. // AMsa_19.25 //
'Accordingly'

children.text: ti yathā teṣāṃ bodhisatvā upakāriṇaḥ | tatra
children.translated_text: means just as the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are benefactors to them. Therein,
by non-attachment to enjoyments
they are engaged in generosity;
by not violating moral discipline
[they are engaged] in moral discipline;
by the pursuit of gratitude

children.text: kṣāntau | upakāribodhisatvasya kṛtajñatayā te hi kṣāntipriyā iti |
children.translated_text: [they are engaged] in patience — because, out of gratitude to the benefactor <s>Bodhisattva</s>, they are fond of patience.
By engagement in practice
[they are engaged] in vigor and the remaining [<s>pāramitās</s>] — considering both that by which they practice and that in which
they practice.
A verse on the division of aspiration:

children.text: vṛddhiṃ hāniṃ ca kāṅkṣanti satvānāṃ ca prapācanaṃ |
children.translated_text: They aspire to the increase and decrease among beings, and to their maturation,

children.text: viśeṣagamanaṃ bhūmau bodhiṃ cānuttarāṃ sadā || AMsa_19.26 ||
children.translated_text: and to advancing to a higher stage, and always to unsurpassed awakening. // AMsa_19.26 //
increase
of the <s>pāramitās</s>; the
decrease
of their opponents;
the maturation of beings
advancing to a higher stage
and unsurpassed
perfect awakening. A verse on the division of unfailing endeavor:

body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> always aspire to five things: the

children.translated_text: In dispelling fear, in the arising [of <s>bodhicitta</s>], in cutting through doubt,
and in the instruction of practice — the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are always unfailing. // AMsa_19.27 //

body.text: caturvidhe satvārthe bodhisatvānām abandhyaḥ prayogo veditavyaḥ | gambhīrodāradharma
body.translated_text: The endeavor of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be understood as unfailing in four types of benefit to beings: in the practice of
dispelling fear
regarding profound and sublime <s>Dharma</s>
; in the
arising
of <s>bodhicitta</s>; in
cutting through doubt
for those who have generated <s>bodhicitta</s>; and in
the instruction of practice
of the <s>pāramitās</s>. On the division of correct endeavor, two verses:

children.translated_text: Giving of one without expectation of reciprocation, of one without longing for rebirth;

children.text: śīlaṃ kṣāntiś ca sarvatra vīryaṃ sarvaśubhodaye || AMsa_19.28 ||
children.translated_text: moral discipline and patience everywhere; vigor in the arising of all wholesome [qualities] — // AMsa_19.28 //

children.text: vinā rūpyaṃ tathā dhyānaṃ prajñā copāyasaṃhitā |
children.translated_text: free from form, likewise meditation; and wisdom accompanied by skillful means —
this is the correct endeavor of the steadfast in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. // AMsa_19.29 //

body.text: yathoktaṃ ratnakūṭe | vipāko 'pratikaṅkṣiṇo dāneneti vistaraḥ | parihāṇiviśeṣabhāgīyadharmavibhāge dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s>: 'The ripening [result] of one without expectation of reciprocation through giving' — and so forth in detail. On the division of <s>dharmas</s> leading to decline and to distinction, two verses:

children.translated_text: Attachment to enjoyments, having breaches [in moral conduct], conceit, and self-indulgence,

children.text: āsvādanaṃ vikalpaś ca dhīrāṇāṃ hānihetavaḥ || AMsa_19.30 ||
children.translated_text: savoring [meditative states], and conceptualization — these are the causes of decline for the steadfast. // AMsa_19.30 //
For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who stand in the antidotes to those,
the <s>dharmas</s> leading to distinction should be known — from the reversal of those. // AMsa_19.31 //

body.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ vipakṣā hānibhāgīyāḥ | tatpratipakṣā viśeṣabhāgīyā veditavyāḥ | pratirūpakabhūtagauṇavibhāge dvau ślokau | ekaḥ ṣaḍpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: The opponents of the six <s>pāramitās</s> are the factors leading to decline. Their antidotes should be understood as the factors leading to distinction. On the division of the counterfeit, the genuine, and the secondary, two verses — one with six lines:

children.translated_text: The invitation [to ask for correction] too, and hypocrisy, and the display of a pleasant countenance,

children.text: lobhatvena tathā vṛttiḥ śāntavākkāyatā tathā || AMsa_19.32 ||
children.translated_text: and conduct motivated by greed, likewise peaceful speech and body — // AMsa_19.32 //
and excellence of fine speech devoid of practice —
these have been taught as [indicating] the inauthenticity of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;
from the reversal [of these], for those who are engaged [correctly], their authenticity has been taught. // AMsa_19.33 //

body.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ pratirūpakāḥ ṣaḍ bodhisatvaguṇāḥ pravāraṇādayo veditavyāḥ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | vinayavibhāge ślokaḥ |
body.translated_text: The six counterfeit qualities of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> corresponding to the six <s>pāramitās</s> — beginning with the invitation [to point out faults] — should be understood. The rest is self-explanatory. A verse on the division of disciplining [beings]:

children.translated_text: They discipline beings through the application of generosity and the like,

children.text: ṣaṭprakāraṃ vipakṣaṃ hi dhīmantaḥ sarvabhūmiṣu || AMsa_19.34 ||
children.translated_text: [overcoming] the sixfold opponent with wisdom, on all the stages. // AMsa_19.34 //

body.translated_text: The sixfold opponent: avarice, immorality, anger, laziness, distraction, and wrong understanding — the opponents of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, respectively.

children.translated_text: The prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of the wise is twofold, by the distinction of time and person;

children.text: bodhau vyākaraṇe caiva mahāc cānyad udāhṛtaṃ || AMsa_19.35 ||
children.translated_text: and regarding awakening too there is a prediction, and also one called 'great,' different [from the ordinary]. // AMsa_19.35 //
Through the attainment of the patience of the non-arising [of <s>dharmas</s>], through the abandonment of conceit and conceptualization,
and through coming into oneness with all <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of the <s>Jina</s> — // AMsa_19.36 //

children.text: kṣetreṇa nāmnā kālena kalpanāmnā ca tatpunaḥ |
children.translated_text: by field, by name, by time, by the name of the <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: parivārānuvṛtyā ca saddharmasya tad iṣyate || AMsa_19.37 ||
children.translated_text: and by retinue and succession — that is desired regarding the true <s>Dharma</s>. // AMsa_19.37 //
prediction by distinction of person
— from the prediction of persons who possess the lineage, who have generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, and who are face-to-face;
by distinction of time
— from the prediction over limited and unlimited periods of time. Furthermore,
there is prediction regarding awakening

children.text: bhavati | vyākaraṇaṃ vā evaṃnāmā tathāgata evam amuṣmin kāle vyākariṣyatīti |
children.translated_text: — either: 'A <s>Tathāgata</s> of such a name will make such a prediction at such a time.'
But there is another
'great'
prediction, which occurs on the eighth stage,
through the attainment of the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>
; through the abandonment of [the thought] 'I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>' —
through the abandonment of conceit
; through the abandonment of the enjoyment of all signs; and
through coming into oneness
with all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — because the differentiation of one's own continuum is not perceived. Furthermore,
prediction by field
and the like: 'In such a <s>Buddha</s>-field, with such a
name,
in such a
period of time,
he will become a <s>Buddha</s>; in the <s>kalpa</s>
of such a name,
and such will be his
retinue.'
A verse on the division of the inevitable fall [into definite attainment], with six lines:

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: The inevitable fall of the wise into [the certainty of] prosperity, rebirth, determination,
and unweariness, and into continuity of cultivation,

children.text: kṛtyasiddhāv anābhoge kṣāntilābhe ca sarvathā || AMsa_19.38 ||
children.translated_text: and into the non-loss of <s>samādhi</s>, and into the accomplishment of the task, and into effortlessness, and into the attainment of patience in every way — // AMsa_19.38 //

body.translated_text: This sixfold inevitable fall has been taught in accordance with the six <s>pāramitās</s>.
The inevitable fall into prosperity
— from the constant attainment of excellent and abundant enjoyments.
The inevitable fall into [favorable] rebirth
— from the constant taking of rebirth as desired.
The inevitable fall into unweariness
— from constant unweariness amid the sufferings of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
The inevitable fall into continuity of cultivation
— from the constant continuity of cultivation.
The inevitable fall into the non-loss of <s>samādhi</s> and the accomplishment of the task

body.text: ca niyatipāto nityaṃ samādhyaparihāṇitaḥ satkṛtyasādhanataś ca |
body.translated_text: — from the constant non-decline of <s>samādhi</s> and from the accomplishment of what is truly to be done.
And the inevitable fall into effortless
[attainment of] the patience of the non-arising
of <s>dharmas</s>

body.text: niyatipātaś ca nityam anābhoganirvikalpajñānavihārāt | avaśyakaraṇīyavibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaḍpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: — from the constant abiding in effortless, non-conceptual knowledge. A verse on the division of what must necessarily be done, with six lines:

children.translated_text: Worship, undertaking of the training, compassion, cultivation of wholesome [qualities],
diligence in the forest, and insatiability for learning and its meaning —
on all stages, these are what must necessarily be done by the steadfast. // AMsa_19.39 //
<s>pāramitās</s>.
The verse is self-explanatory. On the division of what must be done with continuity, two verses:

body.translated_text: This sixfold [list of] what must necessarily be done pertains to the six

children.translated_text: Knowledge of the danger in sense-pleasures (<s>kāmas</s>), attention to one's lapses,

children.text: duḥkhādhivāsanā caiva kuśalasya ca bhāvanā || AMsa_19.40 ||
children.translated_text: and the endurance of suffering, and the cultivation of the wholesome. // AMsa_19.40 //
And non-savoring of happiness, and non-conceptualization of signs (<s>nimittas</s>),
these are what the wise must do continuously on all stages. // AMsa_19.41 //

body.text: ṣaḍparamitāpariniṣpādanārthaṃ ṣaḍ sātatyakaraṇīyāni | gatārthau ślokau | pradhānavastuvibhāge ślokaḥ ṣaḍpādaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the completion of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, there are six things to be done continuously. The two verses are self-evident. A six-quarter verse on the division of principal objects:

children.translated_text: The gift of <s>Dharma</s>, purity of morality, the patience of non-arising,
effort initiated in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the final abiding with compassion,

children.text: prajñā pāramitānāṃ ca pradhānaṃ dhīmatāṃ matam || AMsa_19.42 ||
children.translated_text: and wisdom — these are considered the principal [forms] of the <s>pāramitās</s> for the wise. // AMsa_19.42 //

body.text: ṣaṭsu pāramitāsv etat ṣaḍvidhaṃ pradhānaṃ | tatra

children.translated_text: 'purity of morality'
is the morality beloved by the noble ones (<s>āryakānta śīla</s>).
'The final abiding with compassion'

children.text: caturthaṃ karuṇā 'pramāṇayuktaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | prajñaptivyavasthānavibhāge catvāraḥ ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: — the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>], connected with the immeasurable of compassion. The rest is self-evident. On the division of the establishment of designations, four verses:

body.translated_text: In the six <s>pāramitās</s>, this is the sixfold principal. Therein,

children.translated_text: The establishment of fields of knowledge, and from the differentiation of forms such as <s>sūtras</s> and the like,
the establishment of <s>dharmas</s> should be known by the wise on all stages. // AMsa_19.43 //

body.text: caturdhā ca tridhā caiva yuktiyānavyavasthitiḥ || AMsa_19.44 ||
body.translated_text: And the establishment of reasoning and vehicle is fourfold and threefold. // AMsa_19.44 //

children.translated_text: Methodical mental attention, right view endowed with fruit,
investigation through valid means of knowledge, and the inconceivable — these should be known as the fourfold reasoning. // AMsa_19.45 //

children.text: āśayād deśanāc caiva prayogāt saṃbhṛter api |
children.translated_text: From intention, from teaching, from practice, from accumulation,

children.text: samudāgamabhedāc ca trividhaṃ yānam iṣyate || AMsa_19.46 ||
children.translated_text: and from the distinction of attainment — the vehicle is accepted as threefold. // AMsa_19.46 //

body.translated_text: The establishment of designations is fourfold, from the distinction of the establishments of <s>dharma</s>, truth, reasoning, and vehicle. Therein,
the five
fields of knowledge are the establishment of <s>dharma</s>,
to be understood
through the forms of <s>sūtra</s>,
<s>geya</s>,
and the like in their differentiations.

body.text: | tadantarbhūtāny eva tadanyāni vidyāsthānāni mahāyāne bodhisatvebhyo deśyante |
body.translated_text: The other fields of knowledge, which are included within these, are taught to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
The establishment of truth
however,
[is based on] the seven
-fold
<s>tathatā</s> (suchness), depending on

body.text: pravṛttitathatāṃ lakṣaṇatathatāṃ vijñaptitathatāṃ saṃniveśatathatāṃ mithyāpratipattitathatāṃ samyakpratipattitathatāṃ ca |
body.translated_text: the <s>tathatā</s> of occurrence, the <s>tathatā</s> of characteristics, the <s>tathatā</s> of cognition, the <s>tathatā</s> of arrangement, the <s>tathatā</s> of wrong practice, and the <s>tathatā</s> of right practice.
The establishment of
the designation of
reasoning

body.text: caturvidhaṃ | apekṣāyuktiḥ | kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ | upapattisādhanayuktiḥ | dharmatāyuktiś ca |
body.translated_text: is fourfold: the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>), the reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>), the reasoning of proof by argument (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>), and the reasoning of the nature of reality (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>).
The establishment of
the designation of
vehicle

body.text: trividhaṃ | śrāvakayānaṃ | pratyekabuddhayānaṃ | mahāyānaṃ | tatrāpekṣāyuktis triṣv api yāneṣu
body.translated_text: is threefold: the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Therein, the reasoning of dependence, in all three vehicles, is
methodical mental attention (<s>yoniśomanaskāra</s>)

body.text: | tam apekṣya tena pratyayena lokottarāyāḥ samyagdṛṣṭer utpādāt | kārakāraṇāyuktiḥ
body.translated_text: — because, depending on it as a condition, supramundane right view arises. The reasoning of cause and effect is
right view
endowed
with fruit.
The reasoning of proof by argument is investigation through
valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇas</s>) —
examination. The reasoning of the nature of reality is
the inconceivable

body.text: sthānaṃ | siddhā hi dharmatā na punaś cintyā kasmāt | yoniśomanaskārāt samyagdṛṣṭir bhavati | | tato vā kleśaprahāṇaṃ phalam ity evam ādi | yānatrayavyavasthānaṃ pañcabhir ākārair veditavyaṃ | āśayato deśanātaḥ prayogataḥ saṃbhārataḥ samudāgamataś ca | tatra hīnaṃ āśayadeśanāprayogasaṃbhārasamudāgamāḥ śrāvakayānaṃ madhyāḥ pratyekabuddhayānaṃ uttamā mahāyānaṃ | yathā
body.translated_text: domain. For the nature of reality, once established, is not to be further thought about — [for instance] why right view arises from methodical mental attention, or why the abandonment of defilements is the fruit thereof, and so on. The establishment of the vehicle is to be understood through five aspects: from intention, from teaching, from practice, from accumulation, and from attainment. Therein, the inferior intention, teaching, practice, accumulation, and attainment are the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>; the middling are the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>; the superior are the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For according to
the intention —
that is, according to the aim — the <s>Dharma</s>
teaching
comes about. According to the teaching, so is
the practice;
according to the practice, so is
the accumulation;
and according to the accumulation, so is the awakening-
attainment.
A verse on the division of investigation:

children.translated_text: The investigation of the adventitious nature of name and thing in each other,
and the investigation of the mere-designation-nature of both types of designation. // AMsa_19.47 //

body.text: caturvidhā paryeṣaṇā dharmāṇāṃ | nāmaparyṣaṇā vastuparyeṣaṇā | svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā | viśeṣaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇā ca | tatra

children.translated_text: the investigation of the adventitious nature of
name in
thing
should be understood as the investigation of name.
The investigation of the adventitious nature of
thing in
name
should be understood as the investigation of thing. In the connection of those two, the investigation of the mere-designation-nature of the designations of essential nature and distinction is
the investigation of the mere
-designation-
nature,
[i.e.,] the investigation of the designation of essential nature and
distinction.
On the division of realization as it truly is, ten verses:

body.translated_text: The investigation of <s>dharmas</s> is fourfold: investigation of name, investigation of thing, investigation of the designation of essential nature, and investigation of the designation of distinction. Therein,

children.translated_text: From the non-apprehension of everything, fourfold true knowledge
arises for the courageous on all stages, for the accomplishment of all purposes. // AMsa_19.48 //

body.text: caturvidhaṃ yathābhūtaparijñānaṃ dharmāṇāṃ nāmaparyeṣaṇāgatam | vastuparyeṣaṇāgataṃ | svabhāvaprajñaptiparyeṣaṇāgataṃ | viśeṣaparjñaptiparyeṣaṇāgataṃ ca | tac ca
body.translated_text: The fourfold realization of <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are: that arrived at through the investigation of name, that arrived at through the investigation of thing, that arrived at through the investigation of the designation of essential nature, and that arrived at through the investigation of the designation of distinction. And that
is to be understood from the non-apprehension of all
this
— name and the like —
non-apprehension.
By the latter half, he shows the greatness of the function of the realization as
it
truly
is.

children.translated_text: The sign of the basis, of enjoyment, and of seed — these are the signs of bondage;

children.text: sāśrayāś cittacaittās tu badhyante 'tra sabījakāḥ || AMsa_19.49 ||
children.translated_text: mind and mental factors, with their support and seeds, are bound therein. // AMsa_19.49 //
the 'sign of the basis'
is the container world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>).
The 'sign of enjoyment'
is the five objects — form and the like.
The 'sign of seed'

children.text: yat teṣāṃ bījam ālayavijñānaṃ | yatra tirvidhe nimitte
children.translated_text: is that which is their seed — the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness). In those three signs,
'mind and mental factors, with their support, are bound.'

children.text: | yac ca teṣāṃ bījam ālayavijñānaṃ | āśrayāḥ punaś cakṣurādayo veditavyāḥ |
children.translated_text: And that which is their seed is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. The supports, moreover, should be understood as the eye and the like.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.text: purataḥ sthāpitaṃ yac ca nimittaṃ yat sthitaṃ svayaṃ |
children.translated_text: That which has been placed before [the mind] as a sign, and that which stands by itself —

children.text: sarvaṃ vibhāvayan dhīmān labhate bodhim uttamām || AMsa_19.50 ||
children.translated_text: clearly understanding all of this, the wise one attains supreme awakening. // AMsa_19.50 //
'the sign that has been placed before' is that which
has been made an object and conceived through the application of learning, reflection, and cultivation.
'That which stands by itself'
that which
has become an object by its very nature, conceived effortlessly. The
'clear understanding'

children.text: dhigamo nālambanībhāvaḥ | akalpanā tadupāyo nimittapratipakṣaḥ | tac cobhayaṃ kramād bhavati | pūrvaṃ hi sthāpitasya paścāt svayaṃsthitasya | tatra caturviparyāsānugataṃ pudaglanimittaṃ vibhāvayan yogī śrāvakabodhiṃ pratyekabodhiṃ vā
children.translated_text: thereof is realization — the state of being no [longer] an object — non-conceptualization, which is the means and the antidote to signs. Both of these occur in sequence: first of that which has been placed [before], then of that which stands by itself. Therein, the <s>yogin</s> who clearly understands the sign of a person, which is accompanied by the four errors (<s>viparyāsas</s>), obtains <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening or <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-awakening
; the one who clearly understands the sign of all <s>dharmas</s> obtains great
awakening.

children.text: | etena yathātatvaṃ parijñāya mokṣāya saṃvartate yathābhūtaṃ parijñānaṃ | tat paridīpitaṃ |
children.translated_text: By this, it is illuminated that realization as it truly is leads to liberation through knowing things as they truly are. That has been shown.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: Knowledge that has <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as its object, free from the grasping of duality,
directly perceiving the body of impurity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), and for its cessation — this is what the wise consider. // AMsa_19.51 //

body.text: etena yathāsvabhāvatrayaparijñānāt paratantrasvabhāvakṣayāya saṃvartate | tat paridīpitaṃ |

children.translated_text: 'By having <s>tathatā</s> as its object' —
having realized the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s>).
'By being free from the grasping of duality' —
the imagined [nature] (<s>parikalpita</s>).
'By directly perceiving the body of impurity' —

children.text: paratantraṃ | tasyaiva kṣayāya saṃvartate dauṣṭhulyakāyasyālayavijñānasya tatkṣayārthaṃ
children.translated_text: the dependent [nature] (<s>paratantra</s>). It leads to the cessation of that very body of impurity — the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> — for the purpose of its cessation:
'for its cessation.'

body.translated_text: By this, it is shown that through the realization of the three natures as they truly are, it leads to the cessation of the dependent nature (<s>paratantra svabhāva</s>). That has been shown:

children.translated_text: Knowledge that has <s>tathatā</s> as its object, cultivated without manifold aspects,
is said to be directly perceiving the existent and non-existent objects, and sovereign over conceptualization. // AMsa_19.52 //

body.translated_text: 'Cultivated without manifold aspects' —

body.text: nitmittatathatayor anānātvadarśanāt | etena śrāvakānimittatvād bodhisatvānimittatvasya viśeṣaḥ paridīpitaḥ | te hi nitmittānimittayor nānātvaṃ paśyantu | sarvanimittānām amanasikārād animittasya ca
body.translated_text: from seeing the non-difference of sign and suchness. By this, the distinction of the <s>Bodhisattva's</s> signlessness from the <s>Śrāvaka's</s> signlessness has been illuminated. For those [<s>Śrāvakas</s>] see a difference between sign and signlessness; through not mentally attending to all signs and through mentally attending to the signless

body.text: dhātor manasikārād animittaṃ samāpadyante | bodhisatvās tu tathatāvyatirekeṇa nimittam apaśanto nimittam evānimittaṃ paśyanty atas teṣāṃ
body.translated_text: element, they enter the signless. <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, however, not seeing signs as other than <s>tathatā</s>, see signs themselves as signless; therefore, for them,
that knowledge is cultivated through mental attention to it.
And regarding the existent object —
i.e., signs —
it is 'directly perceiving and sovereign over conceptualization.'
Because of attaining sovereignty over conceptualization, all purposes are accomplished according to [their] conceptualization.

children.text: tatvaṃ saṃcchādya bālānām atatvaṃ khyāti sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Concealing reality, unreality appears everywhere to the childish;

children.text: tatvaṃ tu bodhisatvānāṃ sarvataḥ khyāty apāsya tat || AMsa_19.53 ||
children.translated_text: but reality appears everywhere to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having cast that aside. // AMsa_19.53 //
the childish,
spontaneously
unreality
alone
appears —
the sign, not
reality,
[i.e., not] <s>tathatā</s> — so for
<s>Bodhisattvas</s>,
spontaneously, reality alone
appears,
not unreality — this has been shown.

body.translated_text: By this, just as for

children.translated_text: The non-appearance and the appearance, respectively, of the unreal object and the real object should be known;
the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) — that is liberation, because of acting freely. // AMsa_19.54 //
and the appearance of the real object — <s>tathatā</s> —
should be understood from the transformation of the basis.

children.text: veditavyā tayā hi tadakhyānaṃ ca | saiva
children.translated_text: For through that [transformation], there is both the non-appearance and [the appearance] of that. That itself
is liberation,
to be understood. For what reason?
'Because of acting freely' —

children.text: | tadā hi svatantro bhavati svacittavaśavartī prakṛtyaiva nimittāsamudācārāt |
children.translated_text: for then one becomes autonomous, operating under the control of one's own mind, because signs do not arise by their very nature.

body.translated_text: The non-appearance of the unreal object — the sign —

children.text: anyonyaṃ tulyajātīyaḥ khyāty arthaḥ sarvato mahān |
children.translated_text: Objects of the same kind appear everywhere as great, one upon another;
therefore, they create obstacles — having fully understood this, one should abandon them. // AMsa_19.55 //
which is great, operating
one upon another,
'appears as of the same kind' —

children.text: sa evāyam iti | sa caivaṃ khyānād
children.translated_text: as 'this is that very same thing.' And because it appears in this way,
'it creates obstacles'
for the purification of the Buddha-field.
Therefore,
'having fully understood this obstacle-creating [object],
one should abandon it' —
its appearing thus. A verse on the division of the immeasurable:

body.translated_text: This is the realization as it truly is regarding the means of purifying the [Buddha-]field. The object of the container world,

children.text: paripācyaṃ viśodhyaṃ ca prāpyaṃ yogyaṃ ca pācane |
children.translated_text: That which is to be ripened, that which is to be purified, that which is to be attained, that which is fit for ripening,
and the object of right teaching — these are immeasurable for the wise. // AMsa_19.56 //
immeasurable:
'That which is to be ripened' —
the realm of beings (<s>satvadhātu</s>), in particular.
'That which is to be purified' —
the world-realm (<s>lokadhātu</s>), comprised of the container world.
'That which is to be attained' —
the realm of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmadhātu</s>).
'That which is fit for ripening' —
the realm of those to be trained (<s>vineyadhātu</s>).
'The object of right teaching' —
the realm of the means of training (<s>vinayopāyadhātu</s>). On the division of the power of teaching, two verses:

body.translated_text: The objects of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are fivefold and

children.translated_text: The arising of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind) and the patience of non-arising,

children.text: cakṣuś ca nirmalaṃ hīnam āśravakṣaya eva ca || AMsa_19.57 ||
children.translated_text: and the stainless eye, the inferior [eye], and the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (outflows). // AMsa_19.57 //
The long abiding of the true <s>Dharma</s>, learning, cutting of doubt, and enjoyment —

children.text: deśanāyāḥ phalaṃ jñeyaṃ tatprayuktasya dhīmataḥ || AMsa_19.58 ||
children.translated_text: these should be known as the fruits of teaching for the wise one engaged therein. // AMsa_19.58 //
the eightfold
fruit of teaching
should be understood. Among the listeners, some
generate <s>bodhicitta</s>;
some
attain the patience of the non-arising
of
<s>dharmas</s>;
some generate the stainless, purified
<s>Dharma</s>-
eye
regarding <s>dharmas</s>,
comprised in the inferior
vehicle; some
attain the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s>.
The true <s>Dharma</s>
abides for a long
time
through successive transmission. For those who have not learned,
there is learning of the meaning;
for those who have doubts,
the cutting of doubt
occurs; for those who have certainty,
the enjoyment of the true <s>Dharma</s>

children.text: bhavati anavadyo prītirasaḥ | mahāyānamahatvavibhāge dvau ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: occurs — a blameless savor of joy. On the division of the greatness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, two verses:

body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> engaged in teaching,

children.translated_text: Greatness of object, and of practice in both [one's own and others' purpose], likewise

children.text: jñānasya vīryārambhasya upāye kauśalasya ca || AMsa_19.59 ||
children.translated_text: of knowledge, of the initiation of effort, and of skill in means, // AMsa_19.59 //
greatness of attainment, and greatness of the activity of a <s>Buddha</s> —

children.text: etan mahatvayogād dhi mahāyānaṃ nirucyate || AMsa_19.60 ||
children.translated_text: because of the connection with this [sevenfold] greatness, it is called the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). // AMsa_19.60 //
greatness,
it is called the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
'Greatness of object' — because of the connection with <s>Dharma</s> of immeasurable and vast <s>sūtras</s> and the like.
'Greatness of practice' —
of twofold practice:
for one's own purpose and for others' purpose.
'Greatness of

children.text: mahatvena dvayor jñānātmapudgalanairātmyasya dharmanairātmyasya ca prativedhakāle |
children.translated_text: knowledge' — of twofold knowledge, [namely] the selflessness of the person and the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, at the time of penetration.
'Greatness of the initiation of
effort' — three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), because of continuous and respectful application.
'Greatness of skill in
means' — because of not abandoning <s>saṃsāra</s> without defilement.
'Greatness of attainment' —
from the accomplishment of the powers (<s>bala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.
The <s>Buddha</s>'s activity —
through its greatness, from repeatedly displaying the great awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhi</s>) and the great final <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>mahāparinirvāṇa</s>).

body.translated_text: Because of the connection with the sevenfold

children.translated_text: 'The lineage (<s>gotra</s>), aspiration for the <s>Dharma</s>, and the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>),

children.text: dānādipratipattiś ca nyāyām āvakrāntir eva ca || AMsa_19.61 ||
children.translated_text: the practice of generosity and the rest, and entry into the correct [path]; // AMsa_19.61 //

children.text: satvānāṃ paripākaś ca kṣetrasya ca viśodhanā |
children.translated_text: the maturation of beings, and the purification of the [<s>Buddha</s>-]field,

children.text: apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ bodhiḥ śreṣṭhā ca darśanāt darśanā || AMsa_19.62 ||
children.translated_text: non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), and the supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — from the display [of these].' // AMsa_19.62 //

body.text: etena daśavidhena vastunā kṛtsnaṃ mahāyānaṃ saṃgṛhītaṃ |
body.translated_text: By these ten topics, the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> is encompassed.
The maturation of beings
should be understood as [pertaining to one] established on the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), up to the seventh stage.
The purification of the
[<s>Buddha</s>-]
field, and non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>)
[pertain to] the threefold irreversible stage (<s>avinivartanīyā bhūmi</s>).
The supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>)
[pertains to] the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. And on that very [stage], the display of the great awakening and the great final <s>nirvāṇa</s>
[takes place].
The rest is self-evident. On the division of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, ten verses:

children.translated_text: 'One who practices through aspiration (<s>ādhimokṣika</s>), and another who has pure superior intention (<s>śuddhādhyāśayika</s>);

children.text: nimitte cānimitte ca cāry apy anabhisaṃskṛte |
children.translated_text: and one who practices with signs (<s>nimitta</s>), one without signs (<s>animitta</s>), and one in the unconditioned (<s>anabhisaṃskṛta</s>) —

children.text: bodhisatvā hi vijñeyāḥ pañcaite sarvabhūmiṣu || AMsa_19.63 ||
children.translated_text: these five types of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should be known across all stages.' // AMsa_19.63 //
one who practices with signs (<s>nimittacārī</s>)
[applies] from the second stage up to the sixth.
One who practices without signs (<s>animittacārī</s>)
[applies] on the seventh.
One who practices in the unconditioned (<s>anabhisaṃskāracārī</s>)
[applies] on the subsequent [stages]. The rest is self-evident.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.text: kāmeṣv asaktas triviśuddhakarmā krodhābhibhūmyaṃ guṇatatparaś ca |
children.translated_text: 'Unattached to sensual pleasures, with threefold pure action, conquering anger, devoted to virtues,

children.text: dharme 'calas tatvagabhīradṛṣṭir bodhau spṛhāvān khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.64 ||
children.translated_text: unwavering in the <s>Dharma</s>, with a view into the profound reality, and aspiring to awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.64 //

body.text: etena ṣaḍpāramitāpratipattito mahābodhipraṇidhānataś ca bodhisatvalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ |
body.translated_text: By this, the characteristic of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is illuminated through the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the aspiration for great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Desiring to help, with a view to non-harm, forbearing when others inflict harm,

children.text: dhīro 'pramattaś ca bahuśrutaś ca parārthayuktaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.65 ||
children.translated_text: steadfast, diligent, learned, and devoted to the welfare of others — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.65 //
'steadfast' (<s>dhīra</s>) —
one who has aroused vigor, from not becoming dejected through sufferings.
'Diligent' (<s>apramatta</s>) —
unattached to the pleasures of meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). The rest is self-evident.

body.translated_text: Therein, in the commentary on 19.65,

children.text: ādīnavajñaḥ svaparigraheṣu bhogeṣv asakto hy anigūḍhavairaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Knowing the dangers in one's own possessions, unattached to enjoyments, without concealed enmity,

children.text: yogī nimitte kuśalo 'kudṛṣṭir adhyātmasaṃsthaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.66 ||
children.translated_text: a yogin, skilled in signs, free from wrong views, established inwardly — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.66 //
'unattached to enjoyments' —
one who, having renounced them, goes forth into homelessness.
'Skilled in signs' (<s>nimittakuśala</s>) —
from skill in the three signs: calm (<s>śamatha</s>) and the rest.
'Established inwardly' (<s>adhyātmasaṃstha</s>) —

children.text: mahāyānāvikampanāt | mahāyānaṃ hi bodhisatvānām adhyātmaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ |
children.translated_text: from being unshaken in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the innermost [essence] of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The rest is self-evident.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: 'Endowed with compassion, possessed of the quality of moral shame (<s>hrī</s>), unattached to personal happiness through forbearing suffering,

children.text: smṛtipradhānaḥ susamāhitātmā yānāvikāryaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.67 ||
children.translated_text: predominant in mindfulness, well-concentrated in mind, unwavering in the vehicle — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.67 //
