Therein, 'predominant in mindfulness' —
one who possesses meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), from concentrating the mind through the power of mindfulness.
'Well-concentrated in mind' (<s>susamāhitātmā</s>) —
one who possesses non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpajñāna</s>). The rest is self-evident.

children.text: duḥkhāpaho duḥkhakaro na caiva duḥkhādhivāso na ca duḥkhabhītaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One who removes suffering, yet does not create suffering; who forbears suffering, yet does not fear suffering;

children.text: duḥkhād vimukto na ca duḥkhakalpo duḥkhābhyupetaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.68 ||
children.translated_text: who is liberated from suffering, yet does not conceptualize suffering; who has taken on suffering — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.68 //
'liberated from suffering' —
one who possesses meditation, from liberation from the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) through dispassion toward the desire realm.
'Who has taken on suffering' (<s>duḥkhābhyupeta</s>) —
from accepting [rebirth in] <s>saṃsāra</s>. The rest is self-evident.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.text: dharme rato 'dharmarataḥ dharme 'rato 'dharmarataḥ prakṛtyā dharme jugupsī dharamābhiyuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Delighting in <s>Dharma</s>, not delighting in non-<s>dharma</s>; pleased in <s>Dharma</s>, not pleased in non-<s>dharma</s>; by nature repelled by [certain] <s>dharmas</s>, yet devoted to <s>Dharma</s>; master of <s>Dharma</s>, without darkness in <s>Dharma</s>, with <s>Dharma</s> as foremost — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.69 //

children.text: dharme vaśī dharmanirandhakāro dharmapradhānaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.69 ||

children.translated_text: 'repelled by [certain] <s>dharmas</s>' (<s>dharme jugupsī</s>) —
from being repelled by impatience.
'Master of <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>dharme vaśī</s>) —
in meditative attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>).
'With <s>Dharma</s> as foremost' (<s>dharmapradhāna</s>) —
one whose highest [aim] is great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). Here, '<s>dharma</s>' itself
is called '<s>dharma</s>'
through the continuation of usage [in different senses]. The rest is self-evident.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: 'Diligent regarding enjoyments, diligent regarding discipline, diligent regarding protection, diligent regarding the wholesome,

children.text: sukhāpramatto dharamāpramatto yānāpramatto khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.70 ||
children.translated_text: diligent regarding happiness, diligent regarding <s>Dharma</s>, diligent regarding the vehicle — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.70 //
'diligent regarding protection' (<s>rakṣāpramatta</s>) —
one who possesses patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), from guarding one's own and others' minds.
'Diligent regarding <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>dharmāpramatta</s>) —
from knowing <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. The rest is self-evident.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: 'Ashamed of contempt, ashamed of minor faults, ashamed of intolerance, ashamed of decline,

children.text: viśālavisāralajjas tanudṛṣṭilajjaḥ yānānyalajjaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.71 ||
children.translated_text: ashamed of extensive distraction, ashamed of narrow views, ashamed of other vehicles — such indeed is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' // AMsa_19.71 //
'ashamed of contempt' (<s>vimānalajja</s>) —
one who does not treat suppliants with contempt.
'Ashamed of minor faults' (<s>tanudoṣalajja</s>) —

children.text: 'ṇumātreṣv avadyeṣu bhyadarśī | tanudṛṣṭilajjo dharmanairātmyaprativedhī | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | sarvair ebhiḥ ślokaiḥ paryāyāntareṇa ṣaḍpāramitāpratipattito mahābodhipraṇidhānataś ca bodhisatvalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ |
children.translated_text: one who perceives danger even in the slightest faults. 'Ashamed of narrow views' (<s>tanudṛṣṭilajja</s>) — one who has penetrated the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>. The rest is self-evident. By all these verses, the characteristic of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has been illuminated, in alternative terms, through the practice of the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the aspiration for great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: 'Through equanimity here and hereafter, through the yoga of formations, through attainments of sovereignty,

children.text: śamopasamaupadeśena mahāphalena anugrahe vartati bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.72 ||
children.translated_text: and through the teaching of calm and tranquility which bears great fruit — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> engages in benefiting [beings].' // AMsa_19.72 //

body.translated_text: Here
[the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] engages in benefiting beings in this very [life] through generosity (<s>dāna</s>).
Hereafter —
through morality (<s>śīla</s>), having attained an excellent rebirth.
'Through the yoga of formations' —
that is, through the yoga of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>).
'Bearing great fruit' —
that is, through <s>Buddhahood</s>. The rest is self-evident. By this,

body.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhir mahābodhipraṇidhānena ca yathā satvānugrahe bodhisatvo vartate tat paridīpitaṃ | bodhisatvasāmānyanāmavibhāge aṣṭau ślokāḥ |
body.translated_text: it is illuminated how the <s>Bodhisattva</s> engages in benefiting beings through the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the aspiration for great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>). On the division of common names of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, eight verses:

children.translated_text: '<s>Bodhisattva</s>, <s>mahāsattva</s>, the wise one, one of supreme radiance,
son of the <s>Jina</s>, support of the <s>Jina</s>, conqueror, and sprout of the <s>Jina</s>; // AMsa_19.73 //
the heroic, the supremely wondrous, the caravan-leader, the greatly renowned,

children.text: kṛpāluś ca mahāpuṇya īśvaro dhārmikas tathā || AMsa_19.74 ||
children.translated_text: the compassionate, the greatly meritorious, the sovereign, and the righteous.' // AMsa_19.74 //

body.translated_text: These are the sixteen common names of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [given] in accordance with their meanings.

children.translated_text: 'Through awakening to true being, through awakening to great purpose, through awakening to all purposes too, through constant awakening,

children.text: upāyabodhaiś ca viśeṣaṇena tenocyate hetuna bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.75 ||
children.translated_text: and through awakening to skillful means — by way of distinction, one is therefore called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for these reasons.' // AMsa_19.75 //

body.text: pañcavidhena bodhaviśeṣeṇa bodhisatva ity ucyate | pudgalanairātmyabodhena | sarvākārasarvārthabodhena akṣayāvabdhena parinirvāṇasaṃdarśane 'pi | yathāvidhenāyaṃ ca vinayopāyabodhena |
body.translated_text: Through a fivefold distinction of awakening (<s>bodha</s>), one is called a <s>Bodhisattva</s>: through awakening to the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>); through awakening to all aspects and all purposes; through inexhaustible awakening, even in displaying <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; and through the awakening to whatever methods of discipline are appropriate.

children.translated_text: 'Through awakening to the self, through awakening to subtle views, through awakening to varied cognitions,

children.text: sarvasya cābhūtavikalpabodhāt tenocyate hetuna bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.76 ||
children.translated_text: and through awakening to the unreal conceptualization of everything — one is therefore called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for these reasons.' // AMsa_19.76 //

body.text: atra punaś caturvidhabodhiviśeṣaṃ darśayati cittamanovijñānabodhataḥ | teṣāṃ cābhūtaparikalpatvāvabodhataḥ | tatra cittam ālayavijñānaṃ | manas tadālambanam ātmadṛṣṭyādisaṃyuktaṃ | vijñānaṃ ṣaḍvijñānakāyāḥ
body.translated_text: Here, he again shows a fourfold distinction of awakening, through awakening to mind (<s>citta</s>), mentation (<s>manas</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), and through awakening to their nature as unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>). Therein, 'mind' (<s>citta</s>) is the storehouse consciousness (<s>ālayavijñāna</s>); 'mentation' (<s>manas</s>) is that which takes it as object, associated with the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest; 'consciousness' (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the six consciousness-groups.

children.translated_text: 'Through awakening to non-awakening, through awakening to subsequent awakening, through awakening to non-existence, through subsequent awakening to origination,

children.text: abodhabodhapratibodhataś ca tenocyate hetuna bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.77 ||
children.translated_text: and through counter-awakening to non-awakening — one is therefore called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for these reasons.' // AMsa_19.77 //

body.text: atra punaḥ pañcavidhaṃ bodhaviśeṣaṃ darśayati | avidyābodhāt | vidyābodhāt | parikalpitādisvabhāvatrayabodhāc ca | tatrāvabodhatvena bodhipratibodhāt pariniṣpannasvabhāvabodho veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, he again shows a fivefold distinction of awakening: through awakening to ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); through awakening to knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>); and through awakening to the three natures — the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and the rest. Therein, through the nature of realization (<s>avabodhatva</s>), the awakening to the perfected nature (<s>pariniṣpannasvabhāva</s>) should be understood as counter-awakening to <s>bodhi</s> [itself].

children.translated_text: 'Through awakening to non-purpose, through awakening to the ultimate purpose (<s>paramārtha</s>), through awakening to everything, through awakening to the complete purpose,
and through awakening to the basis of what is to be awakened — one is therefore called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for these reasons.' // AMsa_19.78 //

body.text: atra pañcavidhaṃ bodhiviśeṣaṃ darśayati | paratantralakṣaṇabodhāt | pariniṣpannabodhāt | sarvajñeyasarvākārabodhāt | bodhyavabodhatrimaṇḍalapariśuddhibodhāc ca |
body.translated_text: Here, he shows a fivefold distinction of awakening: through awakening to the dependent characteristic (<s>paratantralakṣaṇa</s>); through awakening to the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>); through awakening to all aspects of all that is knowable; and through awakening to the threefold purity of what is to be awakened.

children.translated_text: 'Through awakening to the perfected, through awakening to the station, through awakening to the womb, through the awakening of seeing the stages,

children.text: bodhād bhṛśaṃ saṃśayahānibodhāt tenocyate hetuna bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_19.79 ||
children.translated_text: and through the awakening of the utter destruction of doubt — one is therefore called a <s>Bodhisattva</s> for these reasons.' // AMsa_19.79 //
'awakening to the perfected' (<s>niṣpannabodha</s>) —
<s>Buddhahood</s>.
'Awakening to the station' (<s>padabodha</s>) —
by which one dwells in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven.
'Awakening to the womb' (<s>garbhānubodha</s>) —
by which one descends into the mother's womb.
'Awakening of seeing the stages' (<s>kramadarśane bodha</s>) —

children.text: yena garbhān niṣkramaṇaṃ kāmaparibhogaṃ pravrjyāṃ duṣkaracaryām abhisaṃbodhiṃ ca darśayati |
children.translated_text: by which one displays the emergence from the womb, the enjoyment of sensual pleasures, the going forth, the practice of austerities, and the full awakening.
'The awakening of the utter destruction of doubt' (<s>bhṛśaṃ saṃśayahānibodha</s>) —
by which, in order to cut through all doubts of beings, one turns the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.text: lābhī hy alābhī dhīsaṃsthitaś ca boddhānuboddhā pratideśakaś ca |
children.translated_text: 'One who has gained, yet not gained; one established in wisdom; one who awakens and causes others to awaken; one who teaches;

children.text: nirjalpabuddhir hatamānamānī hy apakkasaṃpakkamatiś ca dhīmān || AMsa_19.80 ||
children.translated_text: one whose understanding is free from idle talk; one who has destroyed pride; and one whose mind is [both] unripe and ripe — [such is] the wise one.' // AMsa_19.80 //
'One who has gained, one who has not gained, and one established in wisdom' —
correspond to the past, future, and present, respectively.
'One who awakens' (<s>boddhā</s>) —
from self-awakening.
'One who causes others to awaken' (<s>anuboddhā</s>) —
from awakening through others. By this, he shows the internal and external [aspects of] awakening.
'One who teaches' and 'one whose understanding is free from idle talk' —
show the coarse and the subtle.
'One who has pride' and 'one who has destroyed pride' —
show the inferior and the excellent.
'One whose mind is unripe and ripe' —
shows the distant and the near [aspects of] awakening.

body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is illuminated through an elevenfold awakening pertaining to the past and so forth. Therein,
In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, the nineteenth chapter on qualities (<s>guṇādhikāra</s>) is completed.

CHAPTERS XX–XXI
The twentieth and twenty-first chapters.
On the division of signs (<s>liṅga</s>), two verses:

children.translated_text: 'Compassion, kind speech, steadfastness, open-handedness,
and the liberation of the profound intention — these are the signs of the wise.' // AMsa_20-21.1 //
'In gathering [beings], in aspiration achieved, in unwearied effort, in the twofold gathering,

children.text: āśayāc ca prayogāc ca vijñeyaṃ liṅgapañcakaṃ || AMsa_20-21.2 ||
children.translated_text: and from intention and from practice — the fivefold signs should be known.' // AMsa_20-21.2 //

body.text: tatra prathamena ślokena pañca bodhisatvaliṅgani darśayati | dvitīyena teṣāṃ
body.translated_text: Therein, by the first verse, five signs of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> are shown. By the second, their
function and summary inclusion [are shown]. Therein,
compassion (<s>anukampā</s>) —
for the purpose of gathering beings through the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>).
Kind speech (<s>priyākhyāna</s>) —
for the purpose of beings attaining aspiration for the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching.
Steadfastness (<s>dhīratā</s>) —
for the purpose of unwearied [effort] in difficult practices and the like.
Open-handedness (<s>muktahastatā</s>) and the liberation of the profound intention (<s>gambhīrasaṃdhinirmokṣa</s>) —

body.text: ca dvayena saṃgrahārtham āmiṣeṇa dharmeṇa yathākramaṃ | eṣāṃ pañcānāṃ
body.translated_text: for the purpose of the twofold gathering — through material [gifts] and through <s>Dharma</s>, respectively. Of these five
signs,
compassion should be understood as from intention (<s>āśaya</s>). The rest
[should be understood] from practice (<s>prayoga</s>).
On the division into the householder and renunciant classes, three verses:

children.translated_text: '<s>Bodhisattvas</s>, being constantly universal monarchs (<s>cakravartins</s>),

children.text: prakurvanti hi satvārthaṃ gṛhiṇaḥ sarvajanmasu || AMsa_20-21.3 ||
children.translated_text: accomplish the welfare of beings as householders in all births.' // AMsa_20-21.3 //
'The going forth that is obtained through undertaking, and another that comes through the nature of <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: nidarśikā ca pravrajayā dhīmatāṃ sarvabhūmiṣu || AMsa_20-21.4 ||
children.translated_text: and also the going forth that is for the purpose of example — these are [the types] of the wise across all stages.' // AMsa_20-21.4 //

children.text: aprameyair guṇair yuktaḥ pakṣaḥ pravrajitasya tu |
children.translated_text: 'The class of the renunciant, however, is endowed with immeasurable qualities;

children.text: gṛhiṇo bodhisatvād dhi yatis tasmād viśiṣyate || AMsa_20-21.5 ||
children.translated_text: since the renunciant is [superior] to a householder <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the ascetic is therefore distinguished.' // AMsa_20-21.5 //
householder
class in which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> abides [is shown], and how one
accomplishes the welfare of beings

children.text: karoti tatparidīpitaṃ | dvitīyena yādṛśe pravrajitapakṣe | tatra trividhā
children.translated_text: is illuminated thereby. By the second, the kind of renunciant class [is shown]. Therein, the threefold
going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>)
should be understood: that obtained through undertaking;
that obtained through the nature of <s>dharmas</s>

children.text: labdhā | nidarśakā ca nirmāṇaiḥ | tṛtīyena gṛhapakṣāt pravrajitapakṣasya
children.translated_text: (<s>dharmatā</s>); and that which serves as an example, through emanations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>). By the third, the
distinction
of the renunciant class over the householder class is illuminated. On the division of superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>), a verse of six feet:

body.translated_text: By this verse, the kind of

children.translated_text: 'The desire for the wished-for fruit hereafter, and for wholesome conduct here in this very [life],

children.text: nirvāṇecchā ca dhīrāṇāṃ satveṣv āśaya iṣyate |
children.translated_text: and the desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the intention toward beings accepted for the steadfast;

children.text: aśuddhaś ca viśuddhaś ca suviśuddhaḥ sarvabhūmiṣu || AMsa_20-21.6 ||
children.translated_text: impure, pure, and thoroughly pure — across all stages.' // AMsa_20-21.6 //
'the desire for the wished-for fruit hereafter' —
the intention toward welfare;
'here in this very [life]' —
the desire for engaging in wholesome [action];
'the desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s>' —
the intention for both [happiness and welfare] — and no other should be understood.
The impure
and other three [types of] superior intentions belong to those who have not entered [the stages];
to those who have entered the stages;

children.text: praviṣṭānāṃ | avinivartanīyabhūmiprāptānāṃ ca yathākramaṃ veditavyāḥ | parigrahavibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: and to those who have attained the irreversible stage — to be understood in sequence. On the division of embracing [beings], a verse:

body.translated_text: By this, the fivefold superior intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is illuminated in summary: the intention toward happiness;

children.translated_text: From aspiration, from equal mind, from sovereignty — the embracing

children.text: gaṇasya karṣaṇatvāc ca dhīmatāṃ sarvabhūmiṣu || AMsa_20-21.7 ||
children.translated_text: of a retinue through attracting — this belongs to the wise on all stages. // AMsa_20-21.7 //

body.translated_text: The fourfold embracing of beings by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>:
the embracing through aspiration (<s>praṇidhānaparigraha</s>)
should be understood as the embracing of all beings through the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>).
The embracing through equal-mindedness (<s>samacittatāparigraha</s>)
is from attaining equality of self and others at the time of realization.
The embracing through sovereignty (<s>ādhipatyaparigraha</s>)
is that of one who has become master, over those whose master he is.
The embracing through attracting
a retinue
is from taking on a group of disciples. On the division of birth (<s>upapatti</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: From the sovereignty of action, and another from aspiration,

children.text: samādheś ca vibhutvasya cotpattir dhīmatāṃ matā || AMsa_20-21.8 ||
children.translated_text: and from concentration, and from pervasiveness — the birth of the wise is accepted. // AMsa_20-21.8 //
by the sovereignty of action —
the birth in a desired place by the power of action for those abiding on the stage of devotional practice;
by the power of aspiration —
the birth in inferior places such as the animal realm and so forth, for those who have entered the stages, for the purpose of ripening all beings;
by the sovereignty of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) —
the birth in the desire-realm by turning away from the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyāna</s>);
by the sovereignty of pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>) —

children.text: dhipatyena yā nirmāṇais tuṣitabhavanādyupapattisaṃdarśanāt | vihārabhūmivibhāge triṃśat ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: the display of birth in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and so forth through emanations. On the division of abiding and stages, thirty verses:

body.translated_text: The fourfold birth of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>:

children.translated_text: By characteristic, by person, by the completion of the training-aggregates, by signs,

children.text: nirukteḥ prāptitaś caiva vihāro bhūmir eva ca || AMsa_20-21.9 ||
children.translated_text: by etymology, and by attainment — the abidings and the stages [are to be known]. // AMsa_20-21.9 //

body.translated_text: Beginning with the division by characteristic, five verses:

children.translated_text: The emptiness of the supreme self; stability in the non-destruction of action;

children.text: vihṛtya sasukhair dhyānair janma kāme tataḥ param || AMsa_20-21.10 ||
children.translated_text: having dwelt with blissful meditations, birth in the desire[-realm]; and beyond that, // AMsa_20-21.10 //
the dedication of the wings of awakening within <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: vinā ca cittasaṃkleśaṃ satvānāṃ paripācanā || AMsa_20-21.11 ||
children.translated_text: and the ripening of beings without mental defilement; // AMsa_20-21.11 //
and in [intentional] birth, the deliberate guarding of defilement;
connected to the one-way path, the exclusively signless path; // AMsa_20-21.12 //
and even in the signless, effortlessness; and the purification of the [Buddha-]field;

children.text: satvapākasya niṣpattir jāyate ca tataḥ param || AMsa_20-21.13 ||
children.translated_text: and the accomplishment of the ripening of beings arises beyond that; // AMsa_20-21.13 //
and the purity of concentrations and <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, and of awakening itself —

children.text: etasmāc ca vyavasthānād vijñeyaṃ bhūmilakṣaṇam || AMsa_20-21.14 ||
children.translated_text: from this arrangement, the characteristics of the stages should be known. // AMsa_20-21.14 //

body.text: ekādaśa vihārā ekādaśa bhūmayaḥ | teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ | prathamāyāṃ bhūmau
body.translated_text: There are eleven abidings and eleven stages. Their characteristics: on the first stage,
supreme emptiness
is the characteristic at realization, from the realization of the selflessness of the person. On the second,
the non-destruction
of actions
and stability — from knowing the diversity of wholesome and unwholesome action-paths and their fruits. On the third, having dwelt with
blissful
<s>Bodhisattva</s>
meditations that are supreme,
birth in the desire-
realm even having withdrawn from those. On the fourth, even though one dwells abundantly in the wings of awakening,
the dedication of the wings of awakening within <s>saṃsāra</s>.
On the fifth, through dwelling abundantly in the four noble truths,
without
mental defilement, the ripening of beings
through composing various treatises and arts. On the sixth, through dwelling abundantly in the arising of dependent origination,
in deliberate birth in [various] existences,
therein
the guarding of defilement.
On the seventh, through being connected
to the one-way path
in a mixed and unmixed manner — the exclusively signless
path. On the eighth,
even in the signless, effortlessness —
from dwelling in the signless without effort, and the purification of the <s>Buddha-</s>
field.
On the ninth, through mastery of the analytical knowledges,
the accomplishment of the ripening of beings —
from the ability to ripen in all aspects. On the tenth,
the purity of the gateways of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>)
and of the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s>.
On the eleventh — the <s>Buddha-</s>
stage —
the purity of awakening
is the characteristic,

body.text: sarvajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt | bhūmiṣṭhe ca pudgalavibhāgam ārabhya dvau ślokau |
body.translated_text: from the abandonment of all knowledge-obstructions. Beginning with the division of persons established on the stages, two verses:

children.translated_text: Of purified vision, of thoroughly purified morality, concentrated, whose pride in the abundance of <s>Dharma</s> has ceased,
emanating in the distinction of continuum-defilement and purification, with wisdom attained in a single moment. // AMsa_20-21.15 //

children.text: upekṣakaḥ kṣetraviśodhakaś ca syāt satvapāke kuśalo maharddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Equanimous, purifying the field, skilled in the ripening of beings, of great power,

children.text: saṃpūrṇakāyaś ca nidarśane ca śakto 'bhiṣiktaḥ khalu bodhisatvaḥ || AMsa_20-21.16 ||
children.translated_text: with a complete body, capable of displaying — indeed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is consecrated. // AMsa_20-21.16 //

body.text: daśasu bhūmiṣu daśa bodhisatvā vyavasthāpyate | prathamāyāṃ

children.translated_text: 'of purified vision' —
from obtaining the knowledge that is the antidote to the views of person and <s>dharma</s>. On the second,
'of thoroughly purified morality' —
from the absence even of the occurrence of subtle faults and stumbling. On the third,
'concentrated' —
from obtaining unshakeable meditation and concentration. On the fourth,
'whose pride in the abundance of <s>Dharma</s> has ceased' —
from the cessation of pride in the diversity of <s>dharmas</s> such as sūtras and the rest. On the fifth,
'emanating in the distinction of continuums' —
from entering the equality of all continuums through ten kinds of
purity of
mental intention. On the sixth,
'emanating in the distinction of defilement
and purification' —

children.text: pratītyasamutpādatathatābahulavihāritayā kṛṣṇaśuklapakṣābhyāṃ tathatāyāḥ saṃkleśvyavadānādarśanāt | prakṛtiviśuddhitām upādāya | saptamyām
children.translated_text: from seeing defilement and purification of <s>tathatā</s> through the dark and bright sides, through dwelling abundantly in the suchness of dependent origination — taking its natural purity as basis. On the seventh,
'with wisdom attained in a single moment' —
from the ability of dwelling in the signless, [and] from cultivating the thirty-seven wings of awakening moment by moment. On the eighth,
'equanimous and purifying the field' —
from dwelling without effort in the signless, and from engaging in mixed and unmixed practice by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have entered the irreversible stage. On the ninth,
'skilled in the ripening of
beings' —
as before. On the tenth — the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage — the <s>Bodhisattva</s>
'of great power'
is established — from obtaining great superknowledges.
'With a complete body' —
from the manifestation of immeasurable gateways of concentration and <s>dhāraṇī</s> in the basis [of his being].
'Capable of displaying' —
is established from the display of emanations such as dwelling in the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven and so forth.
'Consecrated' —

body.translated_text: On the ten stages, ten <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are established. On the first,

and thereafter, the purification of the concentration and wisdom aggregates. // AMsa_20-21.22 //

children.text: ca buddhabhūmau | yenānyeṣāṃ jñeye jñānaṃ pratihanyate | buddhānāṃ to tadvimokṣāt sarvatrāpratihataṃ jñānaṃ | śeṣaṃ gatārthaṃ | niṣpattivyavasthānam ārabhya trayaḥ ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: — on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. By which the knowledge of others regarding the knowable is obstructed — but for <s>Buddhas</s>, from liberation from that, knowledge is unobstructed everywhere. The rest has been explained. Beginning with the arrangement of accomplishment, three verses:
Unaccomplished and accomplished — all the stages should be known;

from knowing that [establishment] is mere conceptualization, and through non-conceptualization of that very [thing]. // AMsa_20-21.25 //

When one knows that this stage-arrangement is mere conceptualization, and does not further conceptualize even that as mere conceptualization — thus, from attaining the knowledge of non-conceptualization of grasped and grasper, the complete accomplishment of the stages is stated. children.text: nānyeṣāṃ | bhūmipratiṣṭhasya liṅgavibhāgam ārabhya dvau ślokau |
children.translated_text: not of others. Beginning with the division of signs of one established on the stages, two verses:

body.translated_text: Therein, the stage of devotional practice is

children.text: adhimuktir hi sarvatra sālokā liṅgam iṣyate |

non-contraction, non-despondency, and not depending on others; // AMsa_20-21.27 //
and penetration everywhere, equal-mindedness everywhere,
knowledge of the means of attracting and not attracting, and birth in the assembly (<s>maṇḍala</s>). // AMsa_20-21.28 //

body.text: etadbhūmipraviṣṭasya bodhisatvasya daśavidhaṃ liṅgaṃ sarvāsu bhūmiṣu veditavyaṃ | yāṃ bhūmiṃ praviṣṭas tatra

children.translated_text: 'accompanied by light';
on what one has not entered,
'conviction' —
this is one

'Non-contraction'

'Non-despondency'
— in difficult practices.
'Not depending on others'

'Penetration of all stages' —
from skill in accomplishing that. 'Equal-mindedness
toward all beings as toward oneself.'
'Not led away' —

non-apprehension [of anything], from knowledge of the means to Buddhahood.
And birth in the assemblies (<s>maṇḍalas</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>

children.text: copapattiḥ sarvakālam ity etāni aparāṇi liṅgāni bodhisatvasya | bhūmiṣu pāramitālābhaliṅgavibhāge dvau ślokau |
children.translated_text: at all times — these are the other signs of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Beginning with the division of signs of attaining the perfections on the stages, two verses:

body.translated_text: The tenfold sign of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has entered the stages should be known on all stages. On the stage one has entered,

children.text: nācchando na ca lubdhahrasvahṛdayo na krodhano nālaso nāmaitrīkarūṇāśayo na kumatiḥ kalpair vikalpair hataḥ |
children.translated_text: Not without aspiration, not greedy nor mean-hearted, not wrathful, not lazy, not without the intention of friendliness and compassion, not of poor understanding — destroyed by [wrong] conceptualizations and [false] imaginings;

children.text: no vikṣiptamatiḥ sukhair na ca hato duḥkhair na vā vyāvartate satyaṃ mitram upāśritaḥ śrutaparaḥ pūjāparaḥ śāstari || AMsa_20-21.29 ||
children.translated_text: not with distracted mind, not defeated by pleasures, nor turning away from sufferings — relying on true friends, devoted to learning, devoted to worship of the Teacher. // AMsa_20-21.29 //

body.text: sarvaṃ puṇyasamuccayaṃ suvipulaṃ kṛtvānyasādhāraṇaṃ saṃbodhau pariṇāmayaty aharaharyo hy uttamopāyavit |
body.translated_text: 'Having gathered all meritorious accumulations, vast and uncommon, one who always knows the supreme means dedicates [them] day by day toward awakening;

body.text: jātaḥ svāyatane sadā śubhakaraḥ krīḍaty abhijñāguṇaiḥ sarveṣām uparisthito guṇanidhir jñeyaḥ sa buddhātmanaḥ || AMsa_20-21.30 ||
body.translated_text: born in one's own domain, always performing wholesome [deeds], playing with the qualities of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), a treasury of qualities surpassing all — such should be known as one of the nature of a <s>Buddha</s>.' // AMsa_20-21.30 //

body.text: daśapāramitālābhino bodhisatvasya ṣoḍaśavidhaṃ liṅgaṃ darśayati | ṣoḍaśavidaṃ liṅgaṃ | sadā pāramitāpratipatti

children.translated_text: the practice

children.text: virahitatvaṃ | ṣaḍpāramitāvipakṣaiś ca rahitatvaṃ pratyekaṃ | anyayānamanasikāreṇā
children.translated_text: of the <s>pāramitās</s>. Being free from the opponents of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, individually. Not being
distracted
by attention to other vehicles. Non-attachment to the
pleasures
of prosperity. Not being turned back from the practice of difficult conduct by the
sufferings
of adversity. Reliance on a spiritual
friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>).
Devotion to learning (<s>śruta</s>).
Devotion to honoring
the Teacher.
Proper
dedication —
through the <s>pāramitā</s> of skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>).
Birth in one's own
domain — through the <s>pāramitā</s> of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>), from being born in places never separated from <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.
Always performing wholesome [deeds] —
through the <s>pāramitā</s> of power (<s>bala</s>), from not being mixed with <s>dharmas</s> opposed to it.
Playing with the qualities of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) —
through the <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). Therein,
loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>)
is the antidote to ill-will, with the intention of bringing happiness —
compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>)
is the antidote to harmfulness, with the intention of removing suffering.
Imagination of [things having their] own nature (<s>svabhāvakalpana</s>)
is conceptualization (<s>kalpa</s>).
Imagination of distinction (<s>viśeṣakalpana</s>)
is conceptual proliferation (<s>vikalpa</s>),
it should be understood. Therein, on the division of benefits, a verse:

body.translated_text: This shows the sixteenfold sign of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained the ten <s>pāramitās</s>. The sixteenfold sign: never being separated from the desire for

children.translated_text: 'In calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>) and insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), the benefit is considered fivefold for both,

children.text: dhīmatām anuśaṃso hi sarvathā sarvabhūmiṣu || AMsa_20-21.31 ||
children.translated_text: for the wise, in every way on all stages.' // AMsa_20-21.31 //
on all stages,
for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the benefit in every way

children.text: | pañcavidho veditavyaḥ | pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvaduaṣṭhulyāśrayaṃ drāvayati | nānātvasaṃjñāvigatiṃ dharmārāmaratiḥ pratilabhate | aparicchinnākāraṃ ca sarvato 'pramāṇaṃ dharmāvabhāsaṃ saṃjānīte | avikalpitāni cāsya viśuddhibhāgīyāni nimittāni samudācaranti | dharmakāyaparipūripariniṣpattaye ca uttarād uttarataraṃ hetusaṃparigrahaṃ karoti | tatra prathamadvitīyau
children.translated_text: should be understood as fivefold: at every moment, one melts away the basis of all <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (unwholesomeness); one attains the departure from the perception of diversity and delight in the <s>Dharma</s>-park; one perceives the <s>Dharma</s>-illumination in all its unlimited and uninterrupted forms; the purified signs that partake of purification arise without conceptualization; and one progressively embraces the causes for the completion and fulfillment of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. Therein, the first and second
pertain to the side of calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>),
it should be understood. The third and fourth
pertain to the side of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>).

children.translated_text: The remaining pertains to both sides. On the division of the etymologies of the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), nine verses:

'From the purity of freedom from the stain of immorality, it is called the Stainless (<s>Vimalā</s>) stage.'

body.translated_text: 'And from producing a great illumination of <s>Dharma</s>, it is called Radiant (<s>Prabhākarī</s>).' // AMsa_20-21.33 //

body.text: tathā hi tasyāṃ samādhibalenāpramāṇadharmaparyeṣaṇadhāraṇāt mahāntaṃ dharmāvabhāsaṃ pareṣāṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: For on that [stage], through the power of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), from retaining the pursuit of immeasurable <s>Dharma</s>, one produces a great illumination of <s>Dharma</s> for others.

children.translated_text: 'Since the <s>dharmas</s> that are the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>) have become flames and are burning,

the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>)

body.translated_text: The wisdom that has

even though devoted to the maturation

body.translated_text: Therein,

children.translated_text: 'From facing both — <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — here,

children.text: uktā hy abhimukhī bhūmiḥ prajñāpāramitāśrayāt || AMsa_20-21.36 ||
children.translated_text: it is called the Facing (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) stage, from the basis of the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).' // AMsa_20-21.36 //
through the basis of the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom,
faces both <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>saṃsāra</s>,
from non-abiding
in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: For it,
'From connection with the one-way path, it is considered the Far-Going (<s>Dūraṃgamā</s>) stage.'

children.translated_text: The one-way path (<s>ekāyanapatha</s>)
was previously taught; from connection
with that, it has gone far,
from going to the end of the path of practice.

body.translated_text: 'From non-deviation from the twofold perception, it is called Immovable (<s>Acalā</s>).' // AMsa_20-21.37 //

children.translated_text: From non-deviation from the two perceptions:
the perception of signs (<s>nimittasaṃjñā</s>) and the perception of effortless signlessness (<s>animittābhogasaṃjñā</s>).

body.translated_text: 'From the excellence of the intellect of analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the stage is considered Good Intelligence (<s>Sādhumatī</s>).'

children.translated_text: From the excellence of the intellect of analytical knowledges —
meaning from its predominance.

body.translated_text: '<s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>), from pervading the twofold, like a cloud over the space of <s>Dharma</s>.' // AMsa_20-21.38 //

children.translated_text: From pervading the twofold —
meaning from pervading with the gateways of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>, like a cloud over
space —
of the <s>Dharma</s> that has been learned, established in the basis,
it is called <s>Dharmameghā</s>
(Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>).
'From always dwelling with delight in the varied accomplishment of wholesome [deeds],
the stages of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are considered in all [respects] as abodes (<s>vihāra</s>).' // AMsa_20-21.39 //
From the varied
wholesome
accomplishment —
its sign —

abodes (<s>vihāras</s>).
'Again and again, in these immeasurable [stages], from the yoga of ascending upward,

children.text: bhūtāmitābhayārthāya ta eveṣṭā hi bhūmayaḥ || AMsa_20-21.40 ||
children.translated_text: for the purpose of removing the fear of immeasurable beings — those very [stages] are desired as stages (<s>bhūmis</s>).' // AMsa_20-21.40 //

children.text: bhūyo bhūyo 'mitāsv āsu ūrdhvaṃgamanayogād bhūtāmitābhayārthāya ta eva
children.translated_text: Again and again, in these immeasurable [stages], from the yoga of ascending upward, for the purpose of removing the fear of immeasurable beings — those very
abodes are again [called]
stages (<s>bhūmis</s>),
it is said.
'Immeasurable' —

from the yoga of going to higher stages.

children.translated_text: for the purpose of abandoning the fear of immeasurable beings. On the abode of attainment, a verse:
'From the attainment of stages, from conviction, and from engagement in practices,

children.translated_text: from penetration and from the accomplishment of stages — it is fourfold.' // AMsa_20-21.41 //

from conviction as stated, on the stage of conduct through conviction (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>). Attainment through practice — from engagement in the ten <s>Dharma</s>-
practices,
on that very [stage]. Through ultimate
penetration,
upon entering the
stages.
And attainment through accomplishment —
upon entering the irreversible stage. On the division of conduct, a verse of six quarters:

body.translated_text: The attainment of stages is fourfold:

children.translated_text: 'For those with conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and for beings in the inferior vehicle,
for the purpose of attracting and disciplining both —
the four conducts of the steadfast are taught, in accordance with the <s>sūtras</s>.' // AMsa_20-21.42 //

body.translated_text: Therein, the conduct of the <s>pāramitās</s>
is taught for the purpose of those with conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
The <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct [is taught] for those with conviction in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. The conduct of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>)
is for both —
those with conviction in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and the inferior vehicle — through its power, for the purpose of
attraction.
The conduct of maturing beings is for both, for the purpose of maturation.
For maturation here is
disciplining.

body.text: ca deśitāḥ | buddhaguṇavibhāge bahavaḥ ślokāḥ | apramāṇavibhāge tad buddhastotram ārabhhyaikaḥ |
body.translated_text: These are taught. On the division of the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, many verses. On the division of the immeasurables, beginning with the praise of the <s>Buddha</s>, one [verse]:

children.translated_text: 'O compassionate one toward beings, whose intention is the union [with happiness] and removal [of suffering],
whose intention is non-separation [from happiness], whose intention is well-being and benefit — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.43 //
The compassionate nature toward beings

children.translated_text: is shown. The intention of well-being, moreover, [is shown] through loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), as the intention of union with happiness; through compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), as the intention of separation from suffering;
through sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), as the intention of non-separation
from happiness;
and the intention of benefit,

children.text: tvam upekṣayā | sā punar niḥkleśatāśayalakṣaṇā veditavyā | vimokṣābhibhvāyatanakṛtsnāyatanavibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: through equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). That, moreover, should be understood as having the characteristic of the intention toward freedom from afflictions. On the division of liberations, stations of mastery, and totality-bases, a verse:
'O sage, freed from all obstructions, master over all worlds,

children.text: jñānena jñeyaṃ vyāptaṃ te muktacitta namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.44 ||
children.translated_text: whose knowledge pervades all that is knowable, O one whose mind is liberated — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.44 //
through being freed from all
affliction and knowledge
obstructions.
The special quality of the stations of mastery [is shown]
through being master over all worlds —

from the sovereignty of one's own mind, through the power of creating objects at will, transforming, and establishing [them]. The special quality of the totality-bases [is shown] through the unobstructed [nature] of knowledge of all
that is knowable.
Precisely because of being freed from the opponents of the qualities of liberation and so forth, [he is]
one whose mind is liberated.
On the division of the [quality of being] free from conflict (<s>araṇā</s>), a verse:

body.translated_text: Here, the special quality of liberation of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is shown

children.translated_text: 'O one who completely destroys all afflictions of all beings,
O striker of afflictions, O one compassionate toward the afflicted — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.45 //
remainder,
of the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
from subduing the afflictions of all beings,

children.text: vinayanād utpāditakleśeṣv api ca tatkleśapratipakṣavighānāt kliṣṭajanānukampayā saṃdarśayati | anye hy araṇāvihāriṇaḥ satvānāṃ kasyacid eva tadālambanasya kleśasyotpattipratyayamātraṃ pratiharanti | na tu kleśasaṃtānād apanayanti | praṇidhijñānaviśeṣe ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: and from obstructing the opponents of the afflictions even in those whose afflictions have been produced, through compassion for the afflicted — [this quality] is shown. For other dwellers in the state free from conflict merely remove the mere condition for the arising of a particular affliction of a particular being as its object, but they do not remove [the affliction] from the continuum of afflictions. On the special quality of knowledge from aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), a verse:

body.translated_text: Here, without

children.translated_text: 'O effortless one, O unattached one, O unobstructed one, O concentrated one,

children.text: sadaiva sarvapraśnānāṃ visarjaka namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.46 ||
children.translated_text: O one who forever resolves all questions — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.46 //

body.text: atra pañcabhir ākārair praṇidhijñānaviśeṣaṃ bhagavataḥ saṃdarśayati |

from unattached
presentation; from the unobstructed [nature regarding] all that is knowable;
from being always concentrated;
Msa 185)

children.text: arvasaṃśayachedanataś ca satvānāṃ | anye hi praṇidhjñānaṃ saṃmukhīkurvanti | na cāsaktaṃ samāpattipraveśāpekṣatvāt | na cāvyāhataṃ pradeśajñānāt | na ca sadā samāhitā bhavanti | na ca sarvasaṃśayāṃś chindanti | pratisaṃvidvibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: and from cutting through all doubts of beings. For others make the knowledge from aspiration present, but it is not unattached, because of depending on entry into meditative attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>); it is not unobstructed, because of being partial knowledge; they are not always concentrated; and they do not cut through all doubts. On the division of analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), a verse:

body.translated_text: Here, by five aspects, the special quality of the knowledge from aspiration of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is shown:

children.text: āśraye 'thāśrite deśye vākye jñāne ca deśike |
children.translated_text: 'Regarding the support, the supported, what is to be taught, the utterance, the knowledge, and the teaching —

children.text: avyāhatamate nityaṃ sudeśika namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.47 ||
children.translated_text: O one of ever-unobstructed intellect, O excellent teacher — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.47 //

body.text: atra samāsato yac ca deśyate yena deśyate tatra

children.translated_text: through having an ever-unobstructed intellect —

children.text: tvenabhagavataś catasraḥ pratisaṃvido deśitāḥ | tatra dvayaṃ deśyate
children.translated_text: the four analytical knowledges of the <s>Bhagavān</s> are taught. Therein, what is taught is twofold:
the support —
<s>Dharma</s>; and what is
supported —
the meaning. By what it is taught is twofold:
by speech and by knowledge.
Through being an excellent teacher —

children.text: tvena tāsāṃ karma saṃdarśitaṃ | abhijñāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: the function of those [analytical knowledges] is shown. On the division of superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), a verse:

body.translated_text: Here, in brief, regarding what is taught and by what it is taught —

children.text: upetya vacanais teṣāṃ carijña āgatau gatau |
children.translated_text: 'O one who knows the conduct [of beings], who approaches with words to them, [who knows] their coming and going,

children.text: niḥsāre caiva satvānāṃ svavavāda namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.48 ||
children.translated_text: and the leading forth of beings from the essenceless [<s>saṃsāra</s>] — O one of excellent instruction, homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.48 //

body.text: atra ṣaḍbhir abhijñābhiḥ samyagavavādatvaṃ bhagavato darśitaṃ |

children.translated_text: approaching
the presence of those to be trained through the superknowledge of miraculous powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>);
in their

children.text: bhāṣayā divyaśrotrābhijñayā cittacaritraṃ jñātvā cetaḥparyāyābhijñayā yathā pūrvāntād ihā
children.translated_text: language, through the superknowledge of the divine ear; knowing the conduct of their minds, through the superknowledge of reading others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>); [knowing] how they came
here from the past,
and how to lead them forth
from <s>saṃsāra</s> —
therein, one gives
instruction

children.text: dadāty avaśiṣṭābhistotṛbhir abhijñābhir yathākramaṃ | lakṣaṇānuvyañjanavibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: through the remaining three superknowledges, respectively. On the division of marks and minor marks, a verse:

body.translated_text: Here, through the six superknowledges, the quality of giving excellent instruction of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is shown:

children.translated_text: 'All embodied beings, seeing you, become convinced of your great personhood (<s>mahāpuruṣatva</s>);

children.text: dṛṣṭamātrāt prasādasya vidhāyaka namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.49 ||
children.translated_text: O one who produces faith from the mere sight — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.49 //
faith from mere seeing,
through the conviction of great personhood. On the division of complete purity, a verse:

body.translated_text: Here, of the marks and minor marks of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the function is shown: producing

children.translated_text: 'In taking up, establishing, relinquishing, and transforming through emanation —
O one who has attained mastery of <s>samādhi</s> and knowledge — homage to you!' // AMsa_20-21.50 //

body.text: atra bhagavataś caturvidhayā vaśitayā sarvākārāś catasraḥ pariśuddhayaḥ paridīpitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, through the fourfold mastery of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, all four complete purities are illuminated.
The purity of the basis — through the mastery of
taking up and establishing and relinquishing
one's own existence. The purity of objects — through the mastery of
transforming through emanation.
The purity of mind — through the mastery of all forms of
<s>samādhi</s>.
The purity of wisdom — through the mastery of all forms of
knowledge.
On the division of powers (<s>bala</s>), a verse:

children.translated_text: Regarding skillful means, regarding refuge, regarding purity, and regarding the disputation of beings,

children.text: mahāyāne ca niryāṇe mārabhañja namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.51 ||
children.translated_text: and regarding the progress in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — O crusher of <s>Māra</s>, homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.51 //
<s>Māra</s> [who causes]
disputation —
the action of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s ten powers has been shown as
crushing

children.text: katvena bhagavato daśānāṃ balānāṃ karma saṃdarśitaṃ | yad utasugatidurgatigamanādy
children.translated_text: that [<s>Māra</s>]: regarding the disputation concerning the
means
of going to good and bad destinies; regarding the disputation concerning
refuge
— [taking] refuge in gods and the like [instead of the true refuge]; regarding the disputation concerning
purity
— [settling] merely for purity with outflows (<s>sāśrava</s>);
and regarding the disputation concerning the progress in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

children.text: vipravādane ca | sthānāsthānajñānabalena hi bhagavān prathame 'rthe
children.translated_text: Through the power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñāna</s>), the <s>Bhagavān</s> should be understood as
the crusher of <s>Māra</s>

children.text: ko veditavyaḥ | karmavipākajñānabalena dvitīye | dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattijñānabalena tṛtīye | indriyaparāparatvādijñānabalena caturthe | hīnānīndriyādīni varjayitvā śreṣṭhasaṃniyojanāt | vaiśāradyavibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: in the first matter; through the power of knowledge of the ripening of <s>karma</s>, in the second; through the power of knowledge of <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments, in the third; and through the power of knowledge of the superiority and inferiority of faculties and the like, in the fourth — from the engagement with the best, excluding the inferior faculties and the like. A verse on the division of the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>):

body.translated_text: Herein, regarding the disputation of beings in four matters,

children.translated_text: Knower, abandoner, teacher of the means of progress and of obstacles —
unassailable by non-Buddhist teachers in the purpose of self and others — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.52 //
as the knower and the abandoner
[he serves] his own purpose;
as the teacher of the means of progress and of obstacles
[he serves] others' purpose.
Because he is unassailable
by non-Buddhist teachers,

children.text: bhagavato yathākramaṃ caturvidhaṃ vaiśāradyam udbhāvitaṃ | ārakṣasmṛtyupasthānavibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s fourfold fearlessness has been illuminated, in due order. A verse on the division of the guardlessnesses and the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>):

body.translated_text: Herein,

children.translated_text: Speaker in debate within assemblies, free from the defilement of the two [partiality and aversion],

children.text: nirārakṣa asaṃmoṣa gaṇakarṣa namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.53 ||
children.translated_text: guardless, unforgetting, attractor of assemblies — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.53 //

body.text: anena trīṇy arakṣāṇi trīṇi ca smṛtyupasthānāni bhagavataḥ paridīpitāni | teṣāṃ ca karma

children.translated_text: being the attractor
of
assemblies.
For through these, in due order,
he is a speaker in debate
within assemblies, because of being guardless
and free from the defilement of the two [partiality and aversion]
— because of the absence of favor and hostility;
and unforgetting
— because his mindfulness is always predominantly present. A verse on the division of the eradication of latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>):

body.translated_text: By this, the three guardlessnesses and the three foundations of mindfulness of the <s>Bhagavān</s> have been illuminated. And their function is

children.translated_text: In conduct and in dwelling, everywhere, there is no action not [befitting] an omniscient one;

children.text: sarvadā tava sarvajña bhūtārthika namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.54 ||
children.translated_text: always, O Omniscient One, O one whose [purpose] is reality — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.54 //

body.translated_text: By this,
in conduct and in dwelling,
or
everywhere,
or always,
because of the absence of any action not [befitting] an omniscient one
on the part of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,

body.text: sarvakleśavāsanāsammudghātaḥ paridīpitaḥ | asarvajño hi kṣīṇakleśo 'py asamudghātitatvād vāsanāyā ekadā bhrāntena hastinā sārdhaṃ samāgacchati bhrāntena rathenety evamādikam
body.translated_text: the eradication of all latent tendencies of defilements has been illuminated. For even a non-omniscient one whose defilements are destroyed, because the latent tendencies have not been eradicated, sometimes encounters a maddened elephant or a maddened chariot, and performs
actions not [befitting] an omniscient one
of such kinds. As stated in the <s>Māṇḍavya-sūtra</s>. But that
[quality of being] an omniscient one whose [purpose] is reality
does not exist [in such cases]. A verse on the division of non-forgetfulness:

children.translated_text: In all acts for the welfare of all beings, you never let the [right] time pass;

children.text: abandhyakṛtya satatam asaṃmoṣaḥ namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.55 ||
children.translated_text: your work is always fruitful — O unforgetting one, homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.55 //
being
whatever
purpose
is to be accomplished, at whatever
time
— because of not letting that time pass,
the work is always fruitful
for the <s>Bhagavān</s> — thus
the non-forgetful

children.text: dharmatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ karmataś ca saṃdarśitaṃ | mahākaruṇāvibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: nature has been shown both in terms of its essential nature and in terms of its function. A verse on the division of great compassion:

body.translated_text: By this, for whichever

children.translated_text: Six times each day and night you survey the entire world;

children.text: mahākaruṇayā yukta hitāśaya namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.56 ||
children.translated_text: endowed with great compassion, O one of benevolent intention — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.56 //

body.text: atra mahākaruṇā bhagavataḥ karmataḥ svabhāvataś ca paridīpitā |

children.translated_text: With great compassion,
the <s>Bhagavān</s>
six times
each day and night
surveys the world —

children.text: ko hīyate ko vardhate ity evamādi | tadyogāc ca bhagavataḥ sarvasatveṣu nityaṃ
children.translated_text: 'who is declining, who is progressing' and so forth. And because of that practice, the <s>Bhagavān</s> always has a
benevolent intention
toward all beings. A verse on the division of the exclusive qualities:

body.translated_text: Herein, the great compassion of the <s>Bhagavān</s> has been illuminated in terms of its function and essential nature.

children.translated_text: In conduct, in attainment, in knowledge, and in action —
supreme among all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.57 //

body.translated_text: Herein,
through those comprised in conduct
— six exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>;
through those comprised in attainment
— six;
through those comprised in knowledge

body.text: saṃgṛhītais tribhiḥ | karmasaṃgṛhītaiś ca tribhiḥ |tadanyasatvottamānām api
body.translated_text: — three; and through those comprised in action — three. The supremacy of the <s>Bhagavān</s> over all beings, even those supreme among
<s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,
has been illuminated as his
supremacy

body.text: tvena sarvasatvottamatvaṃ paridīpitaṃ | tatra nāsti tathāgatasya skhalitaṃ | nāsti ravitaṃ | nāsti muṣitā smṛtiḥ | nāsty asamāhitaṃ cittaṃ | nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā | nāsty apratisaṃkhyāyopekṣeti
body.translated_text: over all beings. Therein: the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no stumbling; he has no idle chatter; he has no lapse of mindfulness; he has no unconcentrated mind; he has no perception of multiplicity; and he has no indiscriminate equanimity — these are the
six exclusive <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> comprised in conduct,

body.text: saṃgṛhītāḥ ṣaḍāveṇikā buddhadharmā ye buddhasyaiva saṃvidyante nānyeṣāṃ | nāsti chandaparihāṇir nāsti vīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāvimuktiparihāṇir ity
body.translated_text: which exist in the <s>Buddha</s> alone and not in others. There is no decline of zeal; there is no decline of vigor, mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s>, wisdom, or liberation — these are the six
comprised in attainment.

body.text: saṃgṛhītāḥ ṣaḍ | atīte adhvani tathāgatasyāsaṅgam apratihataṃ jñānaṃ | anāgate pratyutpanne adhvani tathāgatasyāsaṅgam apratihataṃ jñānam iti | jñānasaṃgṛhītās trayaḥ | sarvaṃ tathāgatasya
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge regarding the past is unobstructed and unhindered; the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge regarding the future and the present is unobstructed and unhindered — these are the three comprised in knowledge. All the bodily action of the <s>Tathāgata</s>

body.text: kāyakarma jñānapūrvaṃgamaṃ jñānānuparivarti | sarvaṃ vākkarma sarvaṃ manaskarmeti
body.translated_text: is preceded by knowledge and follows upon knowledge; all verbal action and all mental action likewise — these are the three
comprised in action.
A verse on the division of omniscience in all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>):

children.translated_text: Through three bodies, you have attained great awakening in all its aspects;

children.text: sarvatra sarvasatvānāṃ kāṅkṣāchida namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.58 ||
children.translated_text: cutter of doubt of all beings everywhere — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.58 //
through three
bodies, because of attaining awakening in all aspects,

children.text: tvāt sarvajñeyasarvākārajñānāc ca sarvākārajñatā bhagavataḥ paridīpitā | trayaḥ kāyāḥ svābhāvikaḥ sāṃbhogiko nairmāṇikaś ca | sarvajñeyasarvākārajñānaṃ punar atra
children.translated_text: and because of knowledge of all knowables in all aspects, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s omniscience in all aspects has been illuminated. The three bodies are: the essential body (<s>svābhāvikakāya</s>), the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s>), and the emanation body (<s>nairmāṇikakāya</s>). The knowledge of all knowables in all aspects, moreover, is here indicated by its function of
cutting through all doubts

children.text: devamanuṣyādīnāṃ sarvasaṃśayacchedena karmaṇā nirdiṣṭaṃ | pāramitāparipūrivibhāge ślokaḥ |
children.translated_text: of all beings — gods, humans, and the like. A verse on the division of the perfection of the <s>pāramitās</s>:

body.translated_text: By this,

children.translated_text: Without grasping, without fault, without turbidity, unestablished,

children.text: āniṅkṣya sarvadharmeṣu niṣprapañca namo 'stu te || AMsa_20-21.59 ||
children.translated_text: irresistible in all <s>dharmas</s>, without conceptual proliferation — homage to you! // AMsa_20-21.59 //

body.text: anena sakalaṣaḍpāramitāvipakṣanirmuktatayā ṣaḍpāramitāparipūrir bhagavata udbhāvitā | tatrā

children.translated_text: being without grasping
should be understood from his non-grasping of enjoyments;
being without fault
— from his bodily and other actions being stainless;
being without turbidity
— from the non-turbidity of his mind through worldly <s>dharmas</s> and suffering;
being unestablished
— from his non-establishment in the mere attainment of a minor degree of obscuration [removal];
being irresistible
— from his non-distraction;
being without conceptual proliferation
— from the non-occurrence of the proliferation of all conceptualization. On the division of the characteristics of a <s>Buddha</s>, two verses:

body.translated_text: By this, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s perfection of all six <s>pāramitās</s> has been illuminated through his freedom from all their opponents. Therein,

children.translated_text: You have accomplished the ultimate reality; you have emerged from all stages;
you have attained supremacy over all beings; you are the liberator of all beings. // AMsa_20-21.60 //

children.text: akṣayair asamair yukto guṇair lokeṣu dṛśyase |
children.translated_text: Endowed with inexhaustible, incomparable qualities, you are seen in the worlds;

children.text: maṇḍaleṣv apy adṛśyaś ca sarvathā devamānuṣaiḥ || AMsa_20-21.61 ||
children.translated_text: yet you are unseen by gods and humans in all respects and in all assemblies. // AMsa_20-21.61 //

body.text: atra ṣaḍbhiḥ svabhāvahetuphalakarmayogavṛttyarthair buddhalakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitaṃ | tatra viśuddhā tathatā
body.translated_text: Herein, the characteristic of a <s>Buddha</s> has been illuminated through the six aspects of essential nature, cause, fruit, action, application, and mode. Therein, purified <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is
the accomplished ultimate reality
— and that is the essential nature of <s>Buddhas</s>.
Having emerged from all
<s>Bodhisattva</s>
stages
is the cause.
Having attained supremacy over all beings
is the application.
Being seen in various
world-realms
through the emanation body
; being seen in
assemblies
through the enjoyment body;
and
being unseen
in all respects through the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — this is the threefold mode of division.

In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s>, spoken by the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> at the time of purification,
the twenty-first chapter, called 'Conduct and Establishment,' [is completed].
And the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra</s> is completed.
